Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) were interpreted using prespecified thresholds of 1.30, 1.50, and 1.70 m/s (∼5, 7, and 9 kPa, respectively). We assessed whether risk-factor-based criteria would have identified participants with elevated stiffness, and evaluated the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) against LSM thresholds. Of 692 adults offered participation, 610 enrolled (88.2% acceptance); one was excluded for decompensated heart failure. Reliable LSM was obtained in 578 of 609 (94.9%). Ultrasound-defined steatosis was identified in 55.5%. LSM exceeded 1.30 m/s in 25.3%; 9.0% and 5.0% met thresholds consistent with significant fibrosis (≥1.50 m/s) and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (≥1.70 m/s), respectively. Among participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s, exposure profiles were metabolic in 63.5%, mixed metabolic-alcohol in 21.2%, and alcohol-related in 15.4%. Risk-factor criteria were met by 76.6% and captured 46/52 participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s. At this threshold, FIB-4 showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.682); sensitivity decreased from 0.706 using a single threshold to 0.529 using age-adjusted thresholds. Opportunistic liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy was feasible, well accepted, and identified previously undetected steatosis and elevated LSM.

papers.title: Impact of mixed nut consumption on faecal lipid content and gut microbiota composition in healthy adults.
papers.abstract: Nuts are a source of dietary fibre and are considered a nutritious snack despite their high fat content. The effects of nut consumption on the microbiota and the role of nut-derived lipids in altering the large intestinal microbial community remain poorly understood. This study examined changes in faecal characteristics and microbiota composition in 15 healthy volunteers consuming unrestricted diets during a cross-over dietary intervention consisting of three weeks of daily mixed-nut consumption (30 g almonds, macadamias and pistachios) and three weeks of nut abstinence. Microscopic examination of faecal samples revealed lipid-containing nut particles following nut consumption, which were not observed during the nut abstinence. Mixed nut consumption was associated with a significant increase in total faecal lipid content compared with nut abstinence ( P < 0.05), suggesting incomplete digestion and absorption of nut-derived lipids. In contrast, faecal pH, dry matter, ash content, short-chain fatty acids and ammonium concentrations were not significantly altered by the intervention. 16S rRNA gene sequence analysis demonstrated substantial inter-individual variation in gut microbial community composition, with only modest differences associated with nut consumption. Predicted functional profiling suggested variation in pathways related to lipid metabolism between intervention periods. Overall, the findings indicate that a portion of consumed nut cells likely reaches the large intestine intact. Upon degradation of the nut cell wall, encapsulated lipids may become available to the colonic microbiota, potentially contributing to microbial metabolism and community responses observed.

papers.title: Gut microbiome-related plasma metabolites and risk of colorectal cancer.
papers.abstract: Perturbations in gut microbiome composition and altered levels of related metabolites may be related to colorectal cancer (CRC). This study assessed whether pre-diagnostic, circulating, microbiome-related metabolite concentrations were associated with CRC risk. We undertook a nested case-control study of 739 participants in the Colon Cancer Family Registry Cohort (312 cases, 427 controls). Median follow-up time from blood draw to diagnosis was 7 years. Pre-diagnostic plasma concentrations of 70 metabolites were quantified by targeted liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Odds ratios (ORs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were estimated for metabolite concentrations and CRC risk using multivariable conditional logistic regression models. Stratified analyses were conducted by sex, Lynch syndrome diagnosis, and age at tumor onset. The primary bile acids, cholate and chenodeoxycholate, were positively associated with CRC incidence, overall and among females. The odds of CRC were higher in individuals in the highest compared with the lowest quartiles of cholate (ORQ4vQ1=1.61, 95% CI=1.05-2.49) and chenodeoxycholate (ORQ4vQ1=1.60, 95% CI=1.03-2.50). Two short-chain fatty acids (caproate, valerate) and three metabolites involved in phenylalanine and tyrosine metabolism (cinnamoylglycine, phenylpropionate, 4-ethylphenylsulfate) were suggested to be associated, positively and negatively, respectively, with incident CRC but these associations did not withstand correction for multiple comparisons. In stratified analyses, some differences were observed according to sex, Lynch syndrome diagnosis, and age at tumor onset. Circulating microbiome-related metabolites, including bile acids and short-chain fatty acids, may be associated with CRC risk. These findings provide insight into potential pathways linking the gut microbiome to colorectal carcinogenesis.

papers.title: Linking the fine structural characteristics of cereal β-glucans to their differential protective effects against colitis.
papers.abstract: Although cereal β-glucans exert protective effects against experimental colitis, the relationship between their fine structural and physicochemical properties and differential in vivo responses remains unclear. This study directly compared highland barley β-glucan (BBG) and oat β-glucan (OBG), two high-purity mixed-linkage β-(1 → 3)/(1 → 4)-D-glucans, under identical experimental conditions. BBG had a higher cellotriosyl-to-cellotetraosyl (DP3/DP4) ratio than OBG (2.33 vs. 1.51) and a lower weight-average molecular weight. In dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis mice, both β-glucans alleviated clinical signs of disease, while BBG showed greater protection at the tissue and biochemical levels. BBG preserved colon length at 4.88 cm, compared with 4.46 cm for OBG. It reduced myeloperoxidase activity, nitric oxide, and malondialdehyde levels to 1226 U g -1 , 0.42 μmol g -1 , and 78.8 nmol mg -1 , respectively, and fully restored Claudin-1 expression. BBG was also associated with enrichment of Ligilactobacillus , Limosilactobacillus , Romboutsia , and Turicibacter and suppression of Escherichia-Shigella . Fecal metabolomics showed higher levels of selected indole derivatives and taurine-conjugated bile acids, accompanied by lower uric acid and prostaglandin-related inflammatory metabolites. These in vivo differences were accompanied by distinct physicochemical behaviors. BBG showed faster self-aggregation, with a shorter lag time than OBG (112.9 vs . 256.0 min), accompanied by a markedly higher storage modulus (360 vs. 66 Pa). BBG also showed stronger intestinal-phase reassembly under simulated gastrointestinal conditions, approximately threefold greater bile acid retention during dynamic dialysis, and higher DPPH radical-scavenging activity (11.8% vs. 4.8%). Overall, the differential intestinal responses to BBG and OBG were accompanied by distinct physicochemical, microbial, and metabolic profiles, supporting a potential aggregation between cereal β-glucan fine structure, supramolecular behavior, and protective effects against colitis.

papers.title: Myrica rubra juice attenuates DSS-induced colitis and is associated with changes in the gut microbiota-metabolite-host axis.
papers.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is characterized by chronic intestinal inflammation and impaired mucosal barrier function. Myrica rubra contains polyphenols and flavonoids, but the mechanisms underlying its potential protective effects in colitis remain unclear. We evaluated Myrica rubra juice (MRJ) in a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced mouse model of colitis and a TNF-α-injured colonic organoid model. The study combined 16S rRNA gene sequencing, untargeted serum and fecal metabolomics, and molecular docking. MRJ treatment attenuated disease severity and was associated with increased expression of occludin and MUC2 in DSS-treated mice. MRJ also altered microbial diversity and taxonomic composition in a taxon-specific manner. Serum and fecal metabolomic profiles differed after MRJ treatment, including pathways related to amino acid and bile acid metabolism. Integrated analyses identified associations among microbial taxa, putatively annotated metabolites, and host inflammatory and barrier-related variables. Direct exposure to 20% (v/v) whole MRJ increased occludin immunofluorescence in TNF-α-injured colonic organoids cultured without a gut microbial community. This single-marker result is consistent with an epithelial response to whole MRJ under the applied in vitro conditions. Molecular docking generated predicted poses and docking scores for selected parent compound-protein pairs. These calculations did not demonstrate physical binding, functional inhibition, or target engagement in vivo . Together, the findings support a direct epithelial response and identify concurrent microbiota-associated changes. However, the present design could not determine whether these microbial changes contributed to protection. It also could not separate or quantify the host-directed and microbiota-mediated contributions or identify the active chemical species.

papers.title: Case Report: When cardiomyopathy is the clue: late-presenting propionic acidemia manifesting as acute heart failure.
papers.abstract: Propionic acidemia (PA) is a rare inborn error of metabolism that typically presents in infancy; however, late-onset variants may manifest with atypical features, including cardiac involvement. Dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM) is an uncommon but serious complication. A 15-year-old with no prior medical history but a significant maternal family history of cardiomyopathy of unknown etiology from an Amish background presented with altered mental status, increased work of breathing, and progressive edema in the context of preceding viral illness. Evaluation revealed severe biventricular dysfunction, chamber dilation, and findings consistent with chronic DCM. Despite supportive management, her course was complicated by ventricular arrhythmias and clinical deterioration. Metabolic workup demonstrated elevated propionylcarnitine and increased urinary 2-methylcitric acid, confirming late-onset variant PA. She was treated with intravenous carnitine and a specialized metabolic formula; however, cardiac function remained severely impaired. In accordance with family wishes, she was discharged home on hospice care. Late-onset PA can present as isolated cardiomyopathy in adolescence. Early consideration of metabolic etiologies is essential in unexplained DCM, particularly in high-risk populations.

papers.title: SGLT2 Inhibitors' Effects on Biomarkers of Myocardial Injury: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: There is a lack of clinical data regarding sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors' effects on myocardial injury, a common clinical condition that deteriorates patient prognosis. Hence, this systematic review aims to investigate the effects of SGLT2 inhibitors on myocardial injury, using the cardiac injury biomarkers, particularly high-sensitivity cardiac troponin (hs-cTn). We performed a literature review on Embase, MEDLINE (PubMed), and the Cochrane Library, up to May 27, 2025. All potentially relevant randomized clinical trials (RCTs) assessing the effects of SGLT2 inhibitors on myocardial injury in individuals with diabetes or cardiovascular diseases were identified. The outcome measures were the most relevant cardiac injury biomarkers, including hs-cTnT and hs-cTnI, creatine kinase (CK)-MB, heart-type fatty acid-binding protein (H-FABP), myoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase (LDH), ischemia-modified albumin, and glycogen phosphorylase BB. In total, 1770 articles were identified through the literature search. After eliminating duplicates and screening articles, 10 studies involving 10440 participants were included. Of them, 6 studies evaluated hs-cTnT and 4 studies evaluated hs-cTnI. Among individuals with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), four of six trials showed significant attenuation in hs-cTn rise with SGLT2 inhibitors. In contrast, studies on HFrEF populations reported no significant change in hs-cTn levels. One study, including patients with acute myocardial infarction, also did not demonstrate a significant effect on hs-cTnI. The outcomes of this systematic review may suggest the potential effects of SGLT2 inhibitors in reducing myocardial injury by lowering hs-cTn levels in T2DM individuals. However, more studies are recommended to provide robust evidence.

papers.title: Comment on "Mechanisms of gut microbiota metabolite-mediated gut-heart Axis in heart failure: An integrative study based on network pharmacology".
Combined assessment of fibrinogen-to-platelet ratio and ApoB/ApoA1 ratio for pre-angiographic risk stratification of severe multivessel coronary disease in NSTEMI.
papers.abstract: Residual inflammation and dysregulated lipid metabolism are closely associated with the extent of severe multivessel coronary disease (MVD) in patients with non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI). The fibrinogen-to-platelet ratio (FPR) and the apolipoprotein B/apolipoprotein A1 (ApoB/ApoA1) ratio reflect these two residual risk pathways, respectively, whereas the clinical value of their combined assessment for pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD remains to be evaluated. To evaluate the incremental value of combining FPR with the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio for pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD in patients with NSTEMI and to develop an adjunctive risk-stratification model. This single-center retrospective study included 580 patients with NSTEMI who underwent coronary angiography. Correlation analyses, logistic regression, and restricted cubic spline models were used to assess the associations between the two biomarkers and MVD. The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), continuous net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were used to evaluate the incremental value of the biomarkers. A nomogram was developed and internally validated using bootstrap resampling. Decision curve analysis (DCA) was performed to assess net clinical benefit, and subgroup analyses were conducted. FPR remained independently and positively associated with severe MVD, with an approximately linear dose-response relationship; the association of the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio was attenuated after full adjustment, although it showed complementary value in patients with a very high coronary lesion burden. With the combined model, the AUC increased from 0.683 to 0.719, while the continuous NRI and IDI were 0.488 and 0.037, respectively; adding the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio to the model containing FPR did not significantly improve the AUC ( P  = 0.266) but yielded further improvements in NRI and IDI. Potential effect modification by diabetes status was observed ( P for interaction = 0.025). FPR is an important adjunctive biomarker for the pre-angiographic identification of severe MVD in patients with NSTEMI, whereas the ApoB/ApoA1 ratio provides complementary reclassification information. The nomogram incorporating both biomarkers may facilitate pre-angiographic risk stratification.

papers.title: Dynamics of ventriculo-arterial coupling and peripheral tissue perfusion during early resuscitation of septic shock.
papers.abstract: Left ventriculo-arterial coupling (LVAC), the ratio of arterial elastance to left ventricular end-systolic elastance, is a dimensionless index that depicts the interaction between arterial load and cardiac contractility, reflecting energy transmission from the heart to the proximal arterial tree. Nevertheless, how dynamic variations of LVAC may impact tissue perfusion remains unclear. We evaluated the dynamic relationship between LVAC and capillary refill time (CRT), a peripheral perfusion surrogate, during early resuscitation of septic shock. Adult patients were prospectively included within 4-h of meeting Sepsis-3.0 septic shock criteria. LVAC was estimated at inclusion and 6-hours later by combining transthoracic echocardiography with arterial pressure monitoring, while CRT was simultaneously assessed. Patients were classified as uncoupled when LVAC > 1.36. Variations in CRT between baseline and 6-h were compared across four groups defined by LVAC evolution: (1) coupled-to-coupled; (2) coupled-to-uncoupled; (3) uncoupled-to-coupled; (4) uncoupled-to-uncoupled. Additionally, paired measurements before/after fluid loading and/or dobutamine initiation were analyzed. CRT differences among groups were compared using Kruskal-Wallis testing, followed by Dunn's post-hoc test for pairwise comparisons. Paired-Wilcoxon tests assessed CRT variations before/after interventions according to pre-intervention LVAC status. Eighty-four patients were included. CRT variation between baseline and 6-h differed significantly among groups (Kruskal-Wallis, p = 0.013), with CRT improvement in uncoupled-to-coupled (-33.8 [-53.1 to -1.2]%, p = 0.013) and worsening in coupled-to-uncoupled patients (17.5 [7.1-31.3]%, p = 0.013). Persistently coupled and uncoupled groups exhibited heterogeneous CRT responses at 6-h. Thirty-one fluid loads and thirty-two inotrope interventions were also analyzed. CRT decreased after dobutamine in initially uncoupled patients (-26.2%, p = 0.007) but not after fluid loading (-9.5%, p = 0.656) despite both interventions significantly increasing stroke volume in uncoupled LVAC condition (+14.0%, p = 0.021 and +14.2%, p < 0.001, for fluids and dobutamine, respectively). CRT did not change after either intervention in patients already coupled. Although LVAC improvement was associated with recovery of peripheral perfusion in some patients, and its deterioration with CRT prolongation in others, this relationship proved to be weak. Indeed, inconsistent CRT behavior among persistently coupled or uncoupled patients, and the heterogeneous response to resuscitative interventions suggest peripheral perfusion often evolves independently of energy transmitted from the heart to proximal arterial tree.

papers.title: Understanding the change in calcium ion-binding, protein dynamics, and hydration behavior from the wild type for two pathogenic mutants (D3V and G34R) of troponin-C : molecular dynamics simulation and network analysis.
papers.abstract: The protein Troponin-C is an important player in muscle contraction, and mutations in Cardiac Troponin-C (cTnC) have been associated with inherited cardiomyopathies. Till now, eight mutants of the N-domain of cTnC have been listed in the ClinVar database as pathogenic or likely pathogenic. Understanding the molecular mechanisms of these mutations is crucial for mitigating their effects. Previous work studied mutations A8V, A31S, and I4M and found that changes in the conformational landscape are a key feature of these mutations. In the current work, our focus is on two mutations, D3V and G34R, the only ones out of the eight mentioned that undergo a change of charge on mutation. We have performed molecular dynamics simulation and network analysis to calculate binding affinity between Ca 2+ and mutants vis-à-vis the wild type, the change of Ca 2+ coordination shell, the effect of water, protein dynamics, and the communication path from the mutation site to the binding site. Our findings show that both electrostatics and the location of the mutation are the key factors for the difference between WT and the two mutants. D3V, in a disordered region, disrupts long-range allostery through electrostatic and hydration changes, whereas G34R, near the binding site, induces local electrostatic and structural perturbations. The changed conformational landscape, as found for the previously studied mutants, is a general feature for these two mutations also; however, specific effects found here illustrate the diversity present in different mutants.

papers.title: Pre-sleep milk-derived proteins do not impair sleep or recovery in elite female athletes.
papers.abstract: Sleep is essential for athlete recovery and performance, yet athletes frequently experience restricted or poor-quality sleep. Pre-sleep feeding (PSF) has emerged as a strategy to support recovery, but randomized, double-blinded, crossover trials comparing PSF macronutrient options on objective and subjective sleep outcomes in elite female athletes remain limited. Twenty-five National Collegiate Athletic Association (NCAA) Division I female athletes (18-25 years old) were recruited; 21 completed the trial. In a randomized, double-blinded, placebo controlled, crossover design conducted over 4-8 weeks, participants consumed four treatments for three consecutive nights each: 40 g casein protein (CAS; 160 kcal), 40 g α -lactalbumin protein (ALA; 160 kcal), 40 g carbohydrate (CHO; 160 kcal), and 40g of a placebo (PLA; 5 kcal), with a minimum three-day washout between conditions. Supplements were consumed ~2 h after the final meal and ~30 min before bedtime as the last caloric intake of the day. Objective outcomes were obtained from the WHOOP 4.0 device (total sleep time (TST), sleep onset latency (SOL), sleep efficiency (SE), resting heart rate (RHR), and heart rate variability (HRV)). Subjective outcomes were assessed each morning via questionnaires (subjective sleep quality (SSQ), subjective sleep onset latency (SSOL), and subjective recovery (SREC)). Nocturnal interstitial glucose was assessed via blinded continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) in a subset ( n  = 6). Sleep and recovery variables were analyzed using one-way repeated-measures analysis of variance (ANOVA) to evaluate treatment effects across the four supplementation conditions. For CGM data, a two-way repeated-measures ANOVA was used to evaluate main effects of treatment and time, as well as the treatment × time interaction. Tukey's post hoc testing was used with significance set at p  < 0.05. No significant treatment effects were observed for TST, SOL, SE, RHR, or HRV ( p  > 0.05). TST ranged from 7.47-7.62 h, SE from 91.5-92.0%, RHR from 53.5-54.1 bpm, and HRV from 98.2-103.9 ms across conditions. No significant treatment effects were detected for SSQ, SSOL, or SREC ( p  > 0.05); SSQ ranged from 69-75%, SSOL from 16-20 min, and SREC from 61-66%. In the CGM sub-analysis, a main effect of time was observed for nocturnal glucose ( p  = 0.008), but no differences among treatments ( p  = 0.187) or a time × treatment interaction ( p  = 0.550) were detected. In NCAA Division I female athletes, three consecutive nights of pre-sleep ingestion of CAS, ALA, or CHO did not impair objective or subjective measures of sleep or recovery compared with PLA. These findings demonstrate that pre-sleep feeding, regardless of macronutrient type, can be incorporated without negatively affecting sleep quality or recovery metrics. ClinicalTrials.gov (Identifier: STUDY00004409).

papers.title: Early Changes in Left Atrial Mechanics During Sodium-Glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor Therapy in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
papers.abstract: Conventional echocardiographic improvements after sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitor therapy have been reported in heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), but data on novel composite indices of atrial mechanics, particularly the left atrial (LA) stiffness index and the left atrioventricular coupling index (LACI), remain poorly characterized. The authors evaluated early changes in conventional diastolic parameters and atrial mechanics following initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy. In this prospective, single-center observational cohort study, patients with HFpEF in sinus rhythm who were naive to SGLT2 inhibitors received empagliflozin or dapagliflozin. Clinical assessment, laboratory testing, and comprehensive echocardiography were performed at baseline and after 3 months. Echocardiographic evaluation included LA reservoir and pump strain, the LA stiffness index (E/e'/LA reservoir strain), and LACI (minimum LA volume/LV end-diastolic volume ×100). Fifty patients completed follow-up (70% women; mean age, 63.9 ± 8.1 years). New York Health Association functional class improved and N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide levels decreased significantly (347 [134.8-524.8] vs. 257 [161.3-427.5] pg/mL; P = .007). Left atrial volume index and E/e' decreased significantly (34.6 ± 5.5 to 32.6 ± 5.7 mL/m2 and 12.1 ± 3.2 to 9.8 ± 2.8, respectively; both P < .001). Left atrial reservoir and pump strain increased, whereas the LA stiffness index and LACI decreased significantly (all P < .001). In this prospective observational cohort of patients with HFpEF, initiation of SGLT2 inhibitor therapy was associated with early changes in conventional diastolic parameters and LA mechanics. Composite atrial indices, particularly the LA stiffness index and LACI, changed in parallel with established clinical and echocardiographic markers, suggesting that they may provide complementary information for monitoring early atrial remodeling during SGLT2 inhibitor therapy.

papers.title: Heart Failure Risk Phenotypes Based on a 2-Dimensional Tree Structure Derived from Clinical Characteristics and Associations with Disease Prevalence and Cardiovascular Mortality in the General Population.
papers.abstract: Using the Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction Tree (DDRTree) algorithm, a 2-dimensional tree model was constructed based on conventional clinical indicators to identify heart failure (HF) risk phenotypes with different pathophysiological characteristics from the general adult population and evaluate their association with HF prevalence and cardiovascular mortality risk. A representative sample of 24 205 general US adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2018 was analyzed. Eleven routine clinical indicators from multiple physiological dimensions were fed into the DDRTree algorithm to project each of them in a 2-dimensional space. The resulting tree structure revealed distinct HF risk phenotypes whose links to outcome HF prevalence and cardiovascular mortality risk were quantified with weighted logistic regression and Cox proportional-hazard models. Discriminant Dimensionality Reduction Tree identified 3 HF risk phenotypes: normal, metabolic (characterized by upregulated glucose-metabolism markers), and inflammatory (characterized by abnormalities in inflammatory and hepatic-renal markers). After fully adjusting for confounding factors, the metabolic phenotype was significantly associated with the risk of HF compared with the normal phenotype (odds ratio [OR] = 1.96, P < .001, 95% CI: 1.47-2.62), whereas it showed no significant correlation with the risk of cardiovascular death (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.92, P = .539, 95% CI: 0.70-1.20). In contrast, the inflammatory phenotype was significantly correlated with both HF risk (OR = 3.95, P < .001, 95% CI: 2.94-5.33) and cardiovascular mortality risk (HR = 1.47, P = .002, 95% CI: 1.16-1.87). This study elucidates potential risk phenotypes influencing HF and cardiovascular mortality, providing new insights for precise HF risk stratification and targeted preventive interventions in the general population.

papers.title: Effects of ChatGPT Use on Self-care Cardiac Rehabilitation Adherence in Patients with Coronary Artery Disease.
papers.abstract: To clarify the possible effects of ChatGPT use on self-care cardiac rehabilitation (CR) adherence in patients with coronary artery disease (CAD). Patients in the ChatGPT group participated in a standard cardiac rehabilitation program supplemented with personalized digital support via ChatGPT (n=48). The control group participated in conventional cardiac rehabilitation only, without AI-based support (n=48). Both groups completed a 6-month structured rehabilitation program supervised by a multidisciplinary team. Baseline demographic and clinical data, patient satisfaction assessed using a Likert scale, physical activity levels assessed using the International Physical Activity Questionnaire (IPAQ), and metabolic equivalent of task (MET) values were recorded. The postrehabilitation MET score was 1537 in the ChatGPT group and 1413 in the control group (P = 0.001). Similarly, the change in MET score after rehabilitation was greater in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (1029 vs. 875, P = 0.001). SF-36 parameters, including physical functioning, role-physical, mental health, bodily pain, and general health, were significantly higher in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (P < 0.05 for all). Program compliance was higher in the ChatGPT group than in the control group (91.7% vs. 75.0%, P = 0.028). Patient satisfaction was also higher in the ChatGPT group (4.5 vs. 3.8, P = 0.001). ChatGPT use during CR was associated with higher patient compliance rates. Moreover, ChatGPT-supported CR was associated with higher physical activity levels, greater patient satisfaction, and better selected quality-of-life scores.

papers.title: Renin-Angiotensin System Activation Drives Early Cardiorenal Dysfunction in Normotensive Prediabetes.
papers.abstract: Prediabetes is increasingly recognised as a stage at which cardiovascular and renal dysfunction begin to develop despite the absence of overt metabolic disease. The mechanisms underlying these early alterations remain poorly understood. Because adipose tissues surrounding blood vessels and kidneys can locally generate components of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), we hypothesised that subclinical RAS activation contributes to early cardiorenal dysfunction in prediabetes. Using a pre-established normotensive, non-obese rat model of prediabetes induced by 12 weeks of mild hypercaloric feeding, we examined the impact of systemic angiotensin II (AngII) elevation and angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibition on cardio-, cerebro- and renovascular function by invasive hemodynamics, ex vivo pressure myography, and ex vivo renal perfusion experiments, respectively. Prediabetic rats exhibited impaired parasympathetic baroreceptor sensitivity and altered renovascular endothelium-dependent vasodilation despite preserved blood pressure and cardiac function. Systemic AngII infusion further exacerbated autonomic and renovascular dysfunction. In contrast, treatment with a non-hypotensive dose of the ACE inhibitor captopril restored baroreceptor sensitivity, improved renovascular endothelial function, reduced brainstem inflammation, and attenuated renal tubular fibrosis. Examination of perivascular and perirenal adipose tissues revealed significantly higher protein concentration of ACE1 in prediabetic rats compared to controls. These findings are consistent with an early activation of RAS contributing to subclinical cardiovascular and renal dysfunction during prediabetes independently of hypertension. Targeting RAS signalling at this early stage may therefore represent a strategy to limit progression of cardiorenal complications along the continuum from prediabetes to diabetes.

papers.title: Tirzepatide for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Trial Evidence, Cardiometabolic Effects, and Implications for Cardiovascular Practice.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea affects approximately one billion adults worldwide and is associated with hypertension, atrial fibrillation, heart failure, and stroke. Obesity is its dominant reversible cause, yet positive airway pressure therapy splints the pharyngeal airway without addressing the adiposity that narrows it, and randomized trials have not shown that it reduces cardiovascular events. In December 2024, the United States Food and Drug Administration approved tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist, as the first drug for moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea in adults with obesity. We summarize the pharmacology of tirzepatide and the anatomic basis by which weight reduction improves upper airway patency, notably reduction of tongue and parapharyngeal fat. We then review the SURMOUNT-OSA program: two parallel 52-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 trials enrolling 469 adults with obesity and an apnea-hypopnea index of at least 15 events per hour, one conducted without positive airway pressure and one during established positive airway pressure use. Tirzepatide reduced the apnea-hypopnea index by an estimated 20.0 and 23.8 events per hour relative to placebo, with concurrent reductions in sleep apnea-specific hypoxic burden, body weight, systolic blood pressure, and high-sensitivity C-reactive protein.

papers.title: Left ventricular myxoma diagnosed by multimodal cardiac imaging with postoperative recurrence: a case report.
papers.abstract: Left ventricular myxoma is a rare benign cardiac tumour. Diagnosis relies on multimodal imaging, and postoperative recurrence is uncommon. A middle-aged woman with a two-week history of recurrent chest tightness and dyspnoea upon exertion was admitted to our hospital. Transthoracic and transoesophageal echocardiography revealed an irregular, hypoechoic mass (approximately 61 mm × 24 mm) in the left ventricular outflow tract. The mass had a broad base attached to the inferior and posterior walls of the left ventricle, involving the posterior mitral valve leaflet, partial chordae tendineae, and papillary muscles. It exhibited significant deformation and extensive mobility during the cardiac cycle, prolapsing towards the aortic valve orifice during systole and returning to the left ventricular inflow tract during diastole. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging revealed a mass on the inferior and posterior walls of the left ventricle that involved the posterior mitral leaflet, partial chordae tendineae, and papillary muscles. The mass showed no significant enhancement, suggesting a benign lesion, with myxoma as the primary consideration. Whole-body positron emission tomography/computed tomography revealed a slightly hypodense patchy shadow within the left ventricular cavity adjacent to the mitral valve area, accompanied by calcification and mildly increased fluorodeoxyglucose metabolism. Therefore, malignancy could not be entirely excluded. Owing to the unusual location, extensive involvement, high mobility and deformability of the mass close to the aortic orifice, and the consequent risk of embolism, surgical resection of the cardiac myxoma along with mitral valve replacement was performed. At the six-month postoperative follow-up, tumour recurrence was detected by echocardiography. This case highlights the importance of multimodal cardiac imaging in the diagnosis of left ventricular myxoma, with echocardiography being the most frequently utilised modality. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is highly specific for distinguishing between benign and malignant tumours. Echocardiography plays a critical role in the postoperative follow-up of patients with cardiac tumours.

papers.title: Circadian clock and its potential as a therapy for ischemic heart disease.
papers.abstract: According to an epidemiological survey, myocardial infarction, ischemia-reperfusion injury, and aortic rupture usually occur in the morning and summer and are characterized by more severe symptoms and poorer prognosis. The occurrence, development, treatment difficulties, and poor prognosis of ischemic heart disease are closely related to circadian rhythm disorders and the abnormal transcription of circadian clock genes. Normal circadian rhythms regulate neurohumoral regulation and energy metabolism, thereby playing a protective or modulatory role in ischemic heart disease (IHD). HIF1α links the IHD and circadian signaling pathways through the hypoxia response element (HRE) and Per-Arnt-Sim (PAS) domains in gene promoters and enhancers.

papers.title: Preclinical carotid atherosclerosis is independently associated with cardiovascular events and mortality in type 1 diabetes.
papers.abstract: To evaluate whether carotid atherosclerosis predicts future cardiovascular events (CVE) and mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) in primary prevention. Cohort study in adults with T1D participating in a cardiovascular risk assessment program that included carotid ultrasound. Eligibility criteria included age ≥ 40 years, diabetic kidney disease regardless of age or diabetes duration, or type 1 diabetes duration ≥ 10 years in the presence of at least one additional cardiovascular risk factor.The primary endpoint was the first CVE. A secondary endpoint was a composite of CVE plus all-cause mortality. Carotid plaque burden and outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models. 701 individuals were followed for a mean of 5.85 years (mean age 48.5 years; T1D duration 27 years; 51.9% males). Carotid plaques were identified in 40.4%. During follow-up, 45 CVE occurred (18 coronary artery disease, 14 peripheral artery disease, 6 stroke, 3 heart failure, 4 deaths) along with 5 non-cardiovascular deaths. Event-free survival declined progressively with increasing plaque burden (log-rank p < 0.001). In unadjusted analyses, the presence of any plaque was associated with increased risk of CVE (HR 3.14, 95%C I 1.69-5.84) and of the composite endpoint (HR 3.07, 95% CI 1.71-5.51). After multivariable adjustment for demographic, metabolic, and microvascular factors, a high plaque burden (≥ 3 plaques) remained associated with CVE (HR 3.38, 95% CI 1.37-8.38) and with the composite endpoint (HR 2.64, 95% CI 1.13-6.21). Preclinical carotid atherosclerosis in adults with T1D was independently associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events and mortality. These findings support the potential role of carotid ultrasound as a complementary tool for cardiovascular risk assessment in individuals with T1D.

papers.title: High-Frequency Electrograms Abolition as a Valuable Target for Remap During Ventricular Tachycardia Ablation. The HF REMAP Study.
papers.abstract: peak frequency (PF) analysis has recently emerged as a novel tool to assess electrogram properties through their frequency spectrum. PF is an indirect marker of local myocardial activity, and its reduction after radiofrequency ablation reflects effective tissue modification. our study aims to evaluate PF analysis as an objective method to validate lesion efficacy during ventricular tachycardia (VT) ablation. we retrospectively analyzed 43 (out of 247) consecutive patients who underwent VT ablation between January 2023 and December 2024, using the EnSite X mapping system with Advisor HD Grid catheter (Abbott, Minneapolis, USA). Complete pre- and post-ablation high-density sinus rhythm maps were obtained. PF analysis was applied offline to quantify the residual high-frequency (HF) electrogram burden, expressed as a percentage of the ablated area. Patients were stratified according to residual HF burden, and outcomes were assessed with Kaplan-Meier survival analysis and Cox regression analysis. During a median follow-up of 372 days, 11 patients reached the primary endpoint (VT recurrence or arrhythmic storm). Patients with <70% residual HF post-ablation had significantly higher VT-free survival (≈90% at 12 months) compared to those with ≥70% residual HF (≈25%; log-rank p<0.001). Cox regression confirmed residual HF ≥70% as an independent predictor of recurrence (HR 13.36; 95% CI 3.52-50.7; p<0.001). PF analysis during re-mapping provides an operator-independent, reproducible tool to validate lesion efficacy. A low post-ablation residual HF burden is associated to a significantly increased VAs-free survival rate.

papers.title: Effects of LBBAP Pacing-Site Position under a Modelled Proximal LBBB: A 24-Model Electrophysiological Simulation Study.
papers.abstract: Left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) may recruit the distal left-sided conduction &#xD;system, but the electrical effect of pacing-site position along the left bundle branch (LBB) &#xD;remains incompletely defined. We evaluated this effect in 24 four-chamber virtual heart &#xD;anatomies using a Reaction-Eikonal finite-element model with rule-based myocardial &#xD;fibres and algorithmically generated His-Purkinje networks. A modelled proximal His&#xD;to-LBB disconnection preserved the distal LBB-Purkinje network while interrupting its &#xD;proximal connection. Six conditions were simulated in each anatomy: a sinoatrial-node &#xD;(SAN)-initiated left bundle branch block (LBBB) control, right ventricular apical pacing, &#xD;right ventricular outflow-tract pacing and a modelled non-selective LBB capture &#xD;configuration at proximal, nominal and distal positions. The primary outcome was &#xD;BiV_TAT95, the 95th percentile of activation times across left-ventricular, right&#xD;ventricular and interventricular-septal nodes. The control-versus-paced analysis used a &#xD;common simulation-clock origin and was interpreted as contextual benchmarking, &#xD;whereas the positional analysis used matched direct ventricular stimulation. In the &#xD;matched positional analysis, median BiV_TAT95 was 104.5, 93.5 and 88.5 ms for &#xD;proximal, nominal and distal LBBAP, respectively (Friedman chi-square = 48.000, P < &#xD;0.001, Kendall's W = 1.000); every anatomy followed distal < nominal < proximal. In &#xD;three selected anatomies, a 20% decrease or increase in the prescribed myocardial &#xD;conduction speeds altered absolute activation times but preserved this ordering in all &#xD;nine anatomy-by-speed combinations. Under the tested homogeneous substrate and &#xD;modelled non-selective capture configuration, the distal tested position produced the &#xD;lowest simulated BiV_TAT95; this does not imply superiority for every activation metric. &#xD;This conditional prediction requires validation against patient-specific electrical data.

papers.title: Engineered ZFP36-overexpressing AC16 cell-derived extracellular vesicles attenuate ferroptosis-related endothelial injury and functionalize NiTi vascular interfaces.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) is associated with persistent myocardial injury and vascular dysfunction despite advances in reperfusion therapy. Delayed endothelial recovery, inflammation, and vascular remodeling remain important challenges during post-MI repair and vascular intervention. Here, we investigated whether extracellular vesicles (EVs) derived from ZFP36-overexpressing AC16 cells could attenuate ferroptosis-related endothelial injury, improve cardiac function after MI, and be integrated into a bioactive NiTi surface for vascular repair. Bioinformatic screening identified ZFP36 as an MI-associated candidate linked to ferroptosis-related processes; increased expression was subsequently observed in the mouse MI model. ZFP36-overexpressing AC16 cells were generated, and the released EVs were designated ZFP36 OE -EV. In RSL3-treated HUVECs, ZFP36 OE -EV improved cell viability, reduced oxidative stress, preserved mitochondrial membrane potential, and partially restored ferroptosis-related molecular changes. In a mouse MI model, intramyocardial delivery of ZFP36 OE -EV improved cardiac function and reduced myocardial fibrosis. To explore the use of the same engineered EV preparation for vascular interface functionalization, ZFP36 OE -EV was immobilized onto a polydopamine/hyaluronic acid (PDA/HA)-modified NiTi surface to generate the NPH@Z-EV coating. The coating supported EV loading and gradual particle release in vitro. Under direct cell-material contact conditions, the NPH@Z-EV coating exhibited endothelial protective activity under ferroptosis-related stress. In a rat femoral artery injury model, the NPH@Z-EV coating supported vascular repair, with improved endothelial recovery, reduced local inflammatory activation, attenuated lipid peroxidation-associated vascular injury, and a VSMC marker pattern consistent with reduced phenotypic switching. These findings support further evaluation of engineered EVs as a strategy for functionalizing NiTi vascular interfaces to improve vascular healing after implantation.

papers.title: Quadruple Boronic Acid-Functionalized Lanthanide MOFs Enable Deep and Unbiased Spatial Proteomics from Ultra-Trace Laser-Captured Microtissues.
papers.abstract: Spatial proteomics of laser capture microdissection (LCM) specimens is fundamentally constrained by protein loss during processing of ultra-trace samples, limiting proteomic depth and biological insight. Here, we report the integration of a quadruple metal-organic framework (qMOF)-enhanced surfactant-assisted one-pot sample preparation (MSOP) workflow for deep proteomic profiling of micro-scale tissues. The qMOF composite, featuring high-density boronic acid functionalities, acts as a potent protein capture vehicle, drastically minimizing surface adsorption losses. Applied to LCM-isolated mouse myocardial sections as small as 100 × 100 μm (∼20 cells), the MSOP workflow approximately doubled the number of confidently identified proteins, compared to the conventional surfactant-assisted one-pot sample preparation (SOP) method (mean of 2238 vs. 1116), while exhibiting lower quantification variance and preserving unbiased coverage of the proteome's physicochemical landscape. We further demonstrate the workflow's utility by resolving spatially distinct proteomic signatures in perivascular regions of aged cardiac tissue, identifying molecular hallmarks of aging characterized by impaired cytoskeletal stability and dysregulated mitochondrial functions. Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified Rack1 as a potential key node in cardiac aging, which was further validated by immunohistochemistry. This MSOP-assisted platform provides a robust, cost-effective, and highly sensitive chemical strategy to significantly enhance the depth of discovery-driven spatial proteomics.

papers.title: Physiological Responses, Exercise Intensity, and Enjoyment During Ring Fit Adventure in Adults With Chronic Diseases: Single-Arm, Pre-Post Experimental Study.
papers.abstract: Physical inactivity and insufficient muscle-strengthening exercise remain important public health concerns among adults with chronic diseases. Active video games may offer an accessible way to support exercise participation, but many may not provide sufficient exercise intensity to produce meaningful physiological responses. Ring Fit Adventure (RFA) is an active video game that combines aerobic and resistance-based exercise. However, little is known about its physiological demands among adults with chronic diseases. This pilot study aimed to examine the acute physiological responses, exercise intensity, perceived exertion, and enjoyment during RFA gameplay in adults with stable chronic diseases. A single-arm, pre-post experimental study was conducted among 20 adults aged 40 to 65 years with at least one chronic disease. Participants were recruited through convenience and snowball sampling from a hospital-based setting and public recruitment channels. After baseline assessment and familiarization, participants completed 2 stages of RFA gameplay. Heart rate (HR) was continuously monitored, while blood pressure (BP), capillary blood glucose (BG), and the rate of perceived exertion were measured at baseline and immediately after each stage. Enjoyment was assessed using the Exergame Enjoyment Questionnaire (EEQ). All 20 participants completed the study, with no adverse events or missing data. The mean age was 54.3 (95% CI 51.25-57.25) years, and 10 participants were male. Hypertension was the most common condition (n=14, 70%), followed by hyperlipidemia (n=11, 55%), obesity (n=8, 40%), and diabetes (n=5, 25%). The mean continuous HR during gameplay was 111.6 (95% CI 102.6-120.6) bpm, corresponding to 67.2% of the age-predicted maximum HR, while peak HR reached 138.6 (95% CI 128.9-148.3) bpm, corresponding to 83.5% of the age-predicted maximum HR. HR increased significantly after World 1 by 16.7 (95% CI 11.42-21.88; P <.001) bpm and after World 2 by 20.7 (95% CI 13.28-28.12; P <.001) bpm. Rate of perceived exertion also increased significantly after World 1 by 2.83 (95% CI 2.32-3.33; P <.001) points and after World 2 by 3.75 (95% CI 3.18-4.32; P <.001) points. Capillary BG decreased after World 1 by 1.4 (95% CI -1.95 to 0.78; P <.001) mmol/L and after World 2 by 1.6 (95% CI -2.46 to -0.80; P =.01) mmol/L, with no hypoglycemic events. No significant changes were observed in systolic or diastolic BP. The mean enjoyment score was 77.6 out of 100 (95% CI 74.7-80.5). RFA elicited moderate average exercise intensity with periods of vigorous intensity, reductions in capillary BG, stable postexercise BP, and high enjoyment among adults with stable chronic diseases. These findings suggest that RFA may be a feasible and engaging home-based exercise option for this population. However, the small, heterogeneous sample, absence of a control condition, and single-session design limit generalizability. Larger controlled longitudinal studies are needed to determine its effects on exercise adherence, physical activity levels, and cardiometabolic outcomes.

papers.title: Cardiac Effects of Combined Versus Individual Interventions of Mediterranean Diet and Exercise in Adults with the Hypertriglyceridemic Waist Phenotype: A Randomized Trial.
papers.abstract: The hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype, combining abdominal obesity and elevated serum triglycerides, is associated with adverse cardiovascular prognosis. The combination of dietary and exercise programs has the potential to improve outcomes with regard to adverse cardiac remodeling and dysfunction associated with poor metabolic health. We tested the hypothesis that the combination of a Mediterranean Diet (MedDiet) and exercise interventions improves cardiac structure and function more than the sum of each individual intervention. We performed a randomized 2 × 2 factorial design trial that included adults with the hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype (triglycerides ≥1.50 mmol/L, waist circumference ≥80 cm in women or ≥94 cm in men). Participants were randomly assigned to one of four 16-week interventions: (1) MedDiet alone, (2) exercise alone, (3) MedDiet + exercise, or (4) control group. The MedDiet groups received education, counseling, and key food items from the MedDiet. The exercise groups participated in a structured exercise program designed to achieve 150 min of moderate-intensity aerobic exercise per week. Data were collected during the screening, baseline, and post-intervention visits. In mixed-effects models, we compared the post-intervention echocardiographic measurements of left ventricular (LV) structure and function per intervention group after adjusting for age, sex, and baseline values. We calculated an interaction ratio between MedDiet and exercise to assess their combined effect. Of the 200 recruited, 185 participants (76% women) had available echocardiographic data. LV measurements were within normal range for most participants. After the intervention, the posterior wall thickness (LV structure) was higher in the MedDiet groups (0.04 [95% CI: 0.01-0.07] cm), and the septal mitral annular tissue Doppler e' velocity (diastolic function) was higher in the exercise groups (0.4 [95% CI: 0.0-0.8] cm/s). No significant interactions between interventions were identified with respect to LV measurements. No interaction between the MedDiet and exercise interventions on LV structure and function was observed among adults with the hypertriglyceridemic waist phenotype. Further research is needed to ascertain whether the combination of these interventions can prevent the development of adverse LV remodeling over the long term or in participants with more advanced cardiac alterations.

papers.title: Integrating Non-Invasive Liver Assessment into Screening Colonoscopy: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Steatotic liver disease is underdiagnosed despite guideline recommendations for risk-based case-finding. Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening colonoscopy engages a prevention-oriented, healthcare-seeking population in whom liver disease may go undetected. We assessed the feasibility, acceptance, and yield of non-invasive liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy visits. This prospective cross-sectional study enrolled adults aged ≥50 years attending screening colonoscopy. Individuals with known chronic liver disease were excluded. Participants underwent hepatic ultrasound and point shear wave elastography. Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) were interpreted using prespecified thresholds of 1.30, 1.50, and 1.70 m/s (∼5, 7, and 9 kPa, respectively). We assessed whether risk-factor-based criteria would have identified participants with elevated stiffness, and evaluated the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) against LSM thresholds. Of 692 adults offered participation, 610 enrolled (88.2% acceptance); one was excluded for decompensated heart failure. Reliable LSM was obtained in 578 of 609 (94.9%). Ultrasound-defined steatosis was identified in 55.5%. LSM exceeded 1.30 m/s in 25.3%; 9.0% and 5.0% met thresholds consistent with significant fibrosis (≥1.50 m/s) and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (≥1.70 m/s), respectively. Among participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s, exposure profiles were metabolic in 63.5%, mixed metabolic-alcohol in 21.2%, and alcohol-related in 15.4%. Risk-factor criteria were met by 76.6% and captured 46/52 participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s. At this threshold, FIB-4 showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.682); sensitivity decreased from 0.706 using a single threshold to 0.529 using age-adjusted thresholds. Opportunistic liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy was feasible, well accepted, and identified previously undetected steatosis and elevated LSM.

papers.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Multi-hormone Receptor Modulators for Kidney Protection in Nondiabetic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), together with newer multi-hormone receptor modulators that target glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon and amylin, have emerged as promising therapies for chronic kidney disease. This review examines the mechanisms through which these agents may protect the kidney and summarizes the emerging clinical evidence in populations without diabetes. Kidney protection appears to arise through complementary direct and indirect routes. Direct effects include natriuresis through inhibition of the sodium-hydrogen exchanger (NHE)-3, modulation of glomerular hemodynamics through effects on afferent arteriolar tone and vasoconstrictor pathways, and attenuation of renal inflammation; mechanisms that are largely independent of glucose lowering. Indirect mechanisms include reductions in the metabolic, hemodynamic and cardiac burden on the kidney through weight loss, blood pressure lowering, and improvement of heart failure. Beyond selective GLP-1R-agonism, the added hormonal components of multi-hormone receptor modulators engage distinct physiological pathways whose interactions may be additive, synergistic or counteracting, but remain incompletely understood. The efficacy of GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone receptor modulators in people without diabetes is currently supported by results from secondary kidney endpoints in phase-3 obesity and cardiovascular outcome trials, including reductions in albuminuria and preservation of estimated glomerular filtration rate. Several dedicated outcome studies of GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone receptor modulators are now underway and will determine whether these therapies become a new pillar of care in nondiabetic kidney disease.

papers.title: Severe Hypoxic-ischaemic Encephalopathy and Takotsubo Cardiomyopathy Following Accidental Butane Exposure: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Butane is a highly lipophilic aliphatic hydrocarbon widely used as a domestic fuel and aerosol propellant. Acute exposure in enclosed environments may cause severe neurological and cardiovascular toxicity through oxygen displacement, respiratory depression, myocardial sensitisation to catecholamines, and potentially direct toxic effects. A 45-year-old woman was found unconscious in a small, closed studio apartment, while her husband was found deceased in the same environment. Subsequent inspection by the judicial authorities identified deterioration of the gas tubing associated with a gas leak. The patient presented in deep coma (Glasgow Coma Scale score 5) and required tracheal intubation and mechanical ventilation. Initial carboxyhaemoglobin was 16.9% and progressively normalised during oxygen therapy. Brain imaging demonstrated extensive cortical, deep grey matter, brainstem, cerebellar, and white-matter abnormalities consistent with severe hypoxic-ischaemic injury. Cardiac evaluation showed mild ST-segment elevation, increased cardiac biomarkers, and severe transient Left Ventricular Systolic Dysfunction (LVEF 25%) with a pattern highly suggestive of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy; LVEF subsequently improved to 44%. Severe neurological impairment persisted, and the patient was transferred to neurological rehabilitation. She died approximately six months after the index event; reliable documentation of the precise cause of death was unavailable. This case illustrates the severe neurological and cardiovascular consequences that may follow accidental butane exposure in an enclosed environment. The coexistence of extensive hypoxic- ischaemic brain injury and transient stress-related ventricular dysfunction highlights the importance of integrated neurological, cardiological, and toxicological assessment.

papers.title: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC.
papers.abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold standard treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure and survival after transplantation has substantially improved over recent decades. As a consequence, the number of long-term HTx recipients continues to increase, and these patients are now frequently encountered in routine practice outside specialized transplant centers. Their management remains complex due to the use of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-specific complications, and a growing burden of comorbidities in the perspective of increasing longevity. Non-transplant cardiologists, general practitioners, and other healthcare professionals are therefore increasingly involved in their care but often have limited experience of post-transplant management. This clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC provides practical support and a structured framework for healthcare providers involved in the care of HTx recipients outside dedicated transplant centers. The document reviews key aspects of post-transplant management, including outlining principles of care according to time from transplantation, essential knowledge around immunosuppressive therapy and drug monitoring, recognition and initial management of rejection, infection prophylaxis and treatment, and surveillance of long-term complications such as cardiac allograft vasculopathy, malignancy, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. In addition, specific clinical situations frequently encountered in practice-including fertility and pregnancy, non-cardiac surgery, rehabilitation, and palliative care-are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the organization of shared-care models between transplant centers and community providers and on identifying clinical scenarios requiring early referral. Through providing practical recommendations and a structured framework for follow-up, this document aims to support non-specialist clinicians in the safe management of HTx recipients and to facilitate timely collaboration with transplant centers.

papers.title: Association between waist-to-height-haemoglobin A1c index and subclinical myocardial injury in individuals with and without hypertension.
papers.abstract: Recently, a novel metabolic indicator, the Waist-to-Height-Haemoglobin A1c (WHH) index, has been shown to be associated with diabetes risk. This study investigated the association of WHH with the Cardiac Infarction/Injury Score (CIIS) and the risk of subclinical myocardial injury (SC-MI), stratified by hypertension status. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of 5,597 adults aged ≥40 years from the Third National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey who were free of CVD. The WHH index was calculated as waist circumference/height × HbA1c. SC-MI was defined as a CIIS ≥10 on a 12-lead electrocardiogram. Using weighted generalised linear and logistic regression models, we examined the associations of WHH with CIIS and SC-MI. Nonlinear relationships were assessed using restricted cubic spline (RCS) models. The WHH index was not associated with SC-MI among adults without hypertension (odds ratio [OR], 0.95; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73-1.24 per SD increase), but was positively associated among adults with hypertension (OR, 1.37; 95% CI, 1.08-1.72; P interaction = 0.007). For the CIIS, each 1-SD higher WHH index was positively associated only among those with hypertension (β = 0.81; 95% CI, 0.12 to 1.63; P interaction = 0.020). RCS analysis confirmed a linear relationship between WHH and SC-MI risk among individuals with hypertension. These findings demonstrate a significant association between the WHH index and subclinical myocardial injury, particularly among adults with hypertension.

papers.title: Pyrophosphatase 2 Deficiency: Clinical Presentation, Diagnosis and Management.
papers.abstract: PPA2 (pyrophosphatase 2) deficiency is a relatively newly recognized condition caused by biallelic variants in the PPA2 gene. The gene encodes the mitochondrial enzyme PPA2, involved in the production of orthophosphate in the mitochondrial matrix. Affected individuals typically present with sudden cardiac death or acute heart failure following common viral illnesses in infants and toddlers, or following exposure to small amounts of alcohol as teenagers. The condition has a high mortality rate in these situations. Here, we explore the clinical presentations and current management of these patients with a view to guiding future emergency clinical management of cases. Case records from published and unpublished affected individuals diagnosed with PPA2 deficiency were compiled in a retrospective cohort study of genotypes, phenotypes and clinical management protocols in individuals with biallelic (likely) pathogenic PPA2 variants. We collated 93 affected individuals from 53 families, 14 of which have not previously been reported. Patient presentation is invariably acute, often associated with fatigue, vomiting, seizures and collapse. Generally, presenting individuals received standard emergency management with cardiopulmonary resuscitation and appropriate management of arrhythmia, and here we present compiled clinical management protocols for emergency and ongoing treatment of PPA2-deficient patients. A pronounced inheritance rate of pathogenic alleles from carrier parents is noted, and further research is warranted to confirm and investigate any selective advantage for gametes carrying pathogenic PPA2 variants. PPA2 deficiency has a high mortality rate following exposure to common childhood viruses in children around and under the age of 3 and in teenagers exposed to ethanol. We have presented current therapeutic approaches gathered from a worldwide survey of clinicians treating their patients, possible pathogenic mechanisms and inheritance peculiarities of the condition and provide a comprehensive review of the current recommendations surrounding patients' clinical management.

papers.title: Comprehensive cardiac, vascular, and pulmonary characterization of a cardiometabolic HFpEF model.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which translational progress is limited by experimental models that insufficiently reflect the cardiometabolic phenotype while affecting endogenous endothelial function. We aimed to characterize a cardiometabolic "two-hit" HFpEF model combining metabolic stress (db/db) with chronic mineralocorticoid excess (d-aldosterone), focusing on integrated cardiac, vascular, and pulmonary phenotyping. Female db/db mice received 4-week d-aldosterone (0.3 µg/h) or vehicle via osmotic minipumps. Metabolic profiling, high-resolution echocardiography including strain and left atrial mechanics, invasive right-heart catheterization, and thoracic aortic wire myography were performed. Aldosterone-treated db/db mice developed cardiac hypertrophy and pulmonary congestion with preserved LVEF but marked diastolic dysfunction, left atrial remodeling with increased stiffness, and impaired global longitudinal LV strain. Pulmonary hypertension with right ventricular dysfunction was evidenced by elevated RVSP/estimated mPAP, reduced PAT/PET, and reduced TAPSE. Thoracic aortae from untreated db/db mice already showed impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation, which was further aggravated by aldosterone, whereas maximal endothelium-independent relaxation remained largely preserved. The db/db+d-aldosterone model recapitulates key features of cardiometabolic HFpEF across the cardiac-vascular-pulmonary axis and provides a translational platform for mechanistic and therapeutic studies targeting endothelial and ventricular-vascular dysfunction in HFpEF. New & Noteworthy: Current HFpEF animal models often limit the investigation of vascular dysfunction, a central component of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We provide a comprehensive functional characterization of a db/db+d-aldosterone two-hit model demonstrating obesity, diabetes, diastolic dysfunction, atrial remodeling, endothelial dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, and right ventricular impairment. By preserving endogenous endothelial nitric oxide signaling, this model offers a translational platform for studying vascular and cardiopulmonary mechanisms in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

papers.title: Lipid metabolism remodeling in human cardiomyocyte differentiation and maturation.
papers.abstract: Cardiac development involves extensive metabolic remodeling, yet dynamic changes of endogenous lipid species during human cardiomyocyte (CM) differentiation remain poorly characterized. In this study, we systematically performed high-coverage lipidomic profiling across five consecutive CM differentiation stages, using high-performance liquid chromatography. MYL2 expression confirmed ventricular lineage specification in late-stage CMs. Ceramide levels peaked at the cardiac progenitor cell (CPC) stage, suggesting a stage-specific association with the mesendoderm (MES)-to-CPC transition. Meanwhile, lipid categories such as monosialodihexosylganglioside, phosphatidylcholine (PC), lysophosphatidylcholine, and lysophosphatidic acid were markedly elevated in mature CMs. Integrated transcriptomic and chromatin accessibility analyses further delineated the temporal regulatory landscape underlying stage-dependent lipid remodeling during cardiogenic differentiation. Functional assays revealed that PC promotes the expression of mature CM marker genes and improves CM viability. Collectively, these findings establish a comprehensive, high-resolution dynamic lipidomic atlas of in vitro hESC-derived CM differentiation, providing a valuable resource for understanding lipid-associated mechanisms in heart development.

papers.title: Acute and Chronic Resistance Training Differentially Modulate Myocardial Angiogenesis-Related Gene Expression in Wistar Rats.
papers.abstract: Myocardial angiogenesis contributes to the maintenance of myocardial perfusion and cardiac function. Resistance training (RT) induces cardiovascular adaptations, but the myocardial transcriptional responses to acute RT (ART) and chronic RT (CRT) remain incompletely understood. This study compared the expression of angiogenesis- and metabolic adaptation-related genes in the left ventricle following a single RT bout and 8 weeks of repeated RT in healthy male Wistar rats. Twenty-four rats were randomized to three groups: sedentary control (CON) ( n  = 8), ART (one ladder-climbing session), or CRT (ladder-climbing 5 days/week for 8 weeks). RT was performed on a 1-m ladder inclined at 80° using progressive loads attached to the tail. Left-ventricular tissue was collected 1 h after the exercise bout in ART and 1 h after the final training session in CRT. Compared to CON, ART showed significantly higher HIF-1 α and FSTL1 expression, whereas PGC-1 α and VEGF did not differ significantly. CRT also showed significantly higher HIF-1 α and FSTL1 expression than CON, together with significantly higher PGC-1 α and VEGF expression. No significant differences were observed between ART and CRT for any of the genes examined. These findings demonstrate distinct myocardial transcriptional profiles following ART versus CRT, characterized by an HIF-1α- and FSTL1-associated response after a single bout and a PGC-1α- and VEGF-associated response following CRT.

papers.title: Targeting NLRP3 Inflammasome Signaling After Myocardial Infarction: Mechanistic Rationale, Regulatory Networks, and Translational Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction (MI) remains a major cause of death and heart failure despite advances in reperfusion and secondary prevention. Sterile inflammation triggered by ischemic myocardial injury is increasingly recognized as a determinant of infarct expansion, adverse ventricular remodeling, and subsequent clinical outcomes. The NOD-like receptor protein 3 (NLRP3) inflammasome integrates danger-associated molecular patterns, mitochondrial dysfunction, ionic disturbance, metabolic stress, and innate immune signaling. Following activation, caspase-1 processes interleukin-1β and interleukin-18 and cleaves gasdermin D to generate the pore-forming GSDMD-N fragment, thereby promoting pyroptosis and inflammatory amplification. After MI, NLRP3 activity is shaped by extracellular adenosine triphosphate and P2X7 signaling, potassium efflux, reactive oxygen species, mitochondrial DNA release, lysosomal and endoplasmic reticulum stress, and cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes signaling. Importantly, these responses are temporally and cell-type dependent: cardiomyocytes, macrophages, endothelial cells, and fibroblasts contribute differently to injury, debris clearance, vascular dysfunction, scar formation, and repair. This review differs from earlier pathway-centered summaries by integrating temporal regulation and cell-specific biology with emerging crosstalk among mitochondrial quality control, STING signaling, ferroptosis, pyroptosis, and immunometabolism. Translational evidence is considered alongside mechanism, including interleukin-1-directed studies such as CANTOS and the Virginia Commonwealth University Anakinra Remodeling Trial program, while emphasizing that clinical benefit from selective NLRP3 inhibition itself remains to be established. Direct inflammasome inhibitors, colchicine, metabolic modulators, RNA-based approaches, targeted delivery systems, and traditional Chinese medicine-derived compounds are critically discussed with attention to evidence level and limitations. We further examine biomarker-guided patient selection and unresolved questions concerning therapeutic timing, cell specificity, long-term safety, and preservation of reparative inflammation.

papers.title: Beyond Ocular Symptoms: Chronic Progressive External Ophthalmoplegia With Coexisting Facial Palsy and T-wave Inversion.
papers.abstract: Chronic progressive external ophthalmoplegia (CPEO) exists on a wide phenotypic continuum. The systemic propagation of cellular metabolic impairment frequently precipitates a heterogeneous spectrum of neurogenic, myopathic, and cardiovascular manifestations, clinically designated as CPEO-plus. Beyond the highly susceptible extraocular muscles, other metabolically intensive muscular tissues remain vulnerable to compromised function. Diagnosing CPEO remains challenging because its ocular signs overlap significantly with other conditions. Furthermore, CPEO-plus must be distinguished from Kearns-Sayre syndrome. This case report documents a 43-year-old female patient exhibiting classic ocular manifestations of CPEO, supported by a positive family history and elevated serum lactate levels. The clinical presentation is complicated by atypical features, including mild unilateral facial palsy and signs of cardiac electrical remodeling (T-wave inversion), illustrating the significant phenotypic heterogeneity characteristic of CPEO-plus syndromes.

papers.title: Proprotein Convertase Subtilisin/Kexin Type 9: From Biology to Therapeutic Targeting in Cardiovascular Disease.
papers.abstract: Proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) is a pivotal regulator of cholesterol homeostasis, primarily known for inducing the degradation of the low-density lipoprotein receptor (LDLR). Beyond this classical pathway, PCSK9 exerts complex pleiotropic effects and interacts with various lipoproteins, contributing to cardiovascular and metabolic pathologies. This review synthesizes current knowledge on PCSK9 biology, its multi-organ implications and evolving therapeutic strategies. This narrative review summarizes current evidence from experimental, translational and clinical studies on PCSK9 biology and therapeutics. The literature examined includes studies on PCSK9 transcriptional regulation, post-translational modifications, interactions with lipoproteins and the clinical development of established and emerging PCSK9-targeting therapies. PCSK9 activity is modulated by several transcription factors (e.g., SREBP2, HNF1α) and post-translational processes such as furin cleavage and sulfation. Clinically, elevated PCSK9 levels are linked to atherosclerosis progression, heart failure and adverse outcomes in infectious diseases and certain malignancies. Monoclonal antibodies (alirocumab, evolocumab) and siRNA (inclisiran) consistently reduce LDL-C by 50%-60%. Emerging approaches include oral inhibitors which may broaden access to PCSK9-targeting therapy, and CRISPR-based gene-editing strategies (e.g., VERVE-102), which aim to achieve sustained LDL-C lowering after a single treatment. PCSK9 is a multifaceted protein with roles extending far beyond LDL-C regulation. Understanding its diverse interactions is crucial for optimizing treatment in cardiovascular disease and potentially expanding its therapeutic application to metabolic and infectious conditions.

papers.title: Baduanjin Exercise Across Clinical Conditions: An Umbrella Review.
papers.abstract: Baduanjin (BDJ) is a traditional Chinese mind-body exercise increasingly evaluated in rehabilitation and chronic disease care. The growth of systematic reviews has made the literature difficult to interpret because review volume, methodological quality, certainty of evidence, and overlap of primary trials are rarely considered together. This umbrella review aimed to map the clinical condition spectrum of BDJ research and to appraise the credibility and redundancy of the existing review evidence. Eight English and Chinese databases were searched from inception to April 2026 for systematic reviews and meta-analyses in which BDJ was a standalone or separable intervention. Eligible reviews were mapped by clinical condition. Representative core reviews were selected using prespecified hierarchical criteria. Methodological quality, certainty of evidence, and primary-trial overlap were assessed using A Measurement Tool to Assess Systematic Reviews 2 (AMSTAR 2), grading of recommendations assessment, development and evaluation (GRADE), and corrected covered area (CCA), respectively. A total of 261 reviews were included. Thirty-one core reviews underwent AMSTAR 2 appraisal, 21 condition-outcome pairs underwent GRADE assessment, and 10 review clusters underwent CCA analysis. Review activity was concentrated in cardiovascular/cardiac rehabilitation, musculoskeletal pain, cognitive/neurological rehabilitation, endocrine/metabolic disorders, psychological/sleep/emotional conditions, oncology/postoperative rehabilitation, and respiratory disease. AMSTAR 2 ratings were moderate in one review, low in 18, and critically low in 12. Nineteen condition-outcome pairs were rated low certainty and 2 very low certainty. Several clusters showed high or very high primary-trial overlap. BDJ has been reviewed widely, but the evidence is methodologically uneven, frequently overlapping, and of low or very low certainty. Current findings should be interpreted as uncertain evidence signals rather than practice recommendations.

papers.title: Sex differences in the association of uric acid to HDL-cholesterol ratio (UHR) with subclinical cardiovascular damage.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of global mortality, with risk increasing significantly in women post-menopause. Identifying accessible biomarkers for subclinical risk stratification is a clinical priority. The uric acid to HDL-cholesterol ratio (UHR) has emerged as a composite marker reflecting metabolic burden and reduced vascular protection. This study investigates the independent association between UHR and subclinical organ damage, exploring sex-specific differences. We analyzed 1,198 Caucasian subjects. Subclinical cardiovascular damage was evaluated via carotid intima-media thickness (c-IMT) and left ventricular mass index (LVMI). Multivariate linear regression and formal interaction analyses were employed to assess the independent association of UHR with organ damage, adjusting for traditional cardiometabolic risk factors. UHR correlated significantly with adiposity, insulin resistance, blood pressure, and lipid profiles. In the total population, UHR was independently associated with both c-IMT (β = 0.093, p = 0.003) and LVMI (β = 0.194, p < 0.0001). A significant sex-UHR interaction was observed for LVMI (p = 0.024). Sex-stratified analyses revealed that UHR was linked to LVMI in women, particularly those postmenopausal, but not in males. In postmenopausal women, UHR remained an independent determinant of LVMI (β = 0.164, p = 0.033). UHR is independently associated with subclinical cardiovascular damage, displaying a sex-specific relationship with myocardial remodeling after menopause. As an inexpensive and easily accessible biomarker, UHR may represent a practical tool to combat clinical inertia and improve the early selection of postmenopausal women warranting targeted diagnostic workups. Heart disease is the leading cause of death worldwide, and women face a particularly sharp rise in risk after menopause. To prevent cardiovascular events, it is vital to find simple ways to spot early, hidden signs of trouble before a person even feels sick. In our study, we looked at an accessible tool called the Uric Acid to HDL-Cholesterol Ratio (UHR). This is a simple value that doctors can easily calculate at no extra cost using two common markers found in routine blood tests: uric acid and HDL (“good”) cholesterol.We studied nearly 1,200 individuals to see if a high UHR score was associated with early, subclinical damage to the heart muscle and the arteries in the neck.
