Our results showed that while a higher score is generally linked to poorer artery health across the entire population, it has a very specific meaning for women. Indeed, the link between this blood marker and an enlarged heart is remarkably strong in women who have gone through menopause, whereas no such significant association was detected in men.This discovery is important because it suggests that menopause triggers metabolic changes that make the female heart more vulnerable to certain types of stress. By using this simple blood test ratio as an early biochemical indicator, doctors may more easily recognize postmenopausal women who exhibit silent changes in their heart structure, allowing clinicians to facilitate early intervention and prioritize them for deeper diagnostic checkups. Because this calculation is inexpensive and easily accessible, it offers a highly practical way to help women protect their heart health as they age.

papers.title: Analysis of myocardial work in different obesity phenotypes and its association with epicardial adipose tissue.
papers.abstract: To evaluate subclinical cardiac dysfunction across distinct obesity phenotypes using myocardial work (MW) indices, and to investigate the moderating role of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) on MW impairment. One hundred ninety-two participants were categorized by BMI and metabolic status into four groups: metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically healthy obesity (MHO), metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), and metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO). MW indices were measured using speckle-tracking echocardiography. EAT volume was quantified from ECG-gated CT scans. Associations were analyzed using ANCOVA and regression models. Despite no significant differences in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) among the groups, MUNW and MUO individuals exhibited significantly impaired MW, characterized by lower global work index (GWI), global constructive work (GCW), and global work efficiency (GWE), alongside higher global waste work (GWW), compared with MHNW controls. MHO patients showed significantly better MW profiles than MUNW and MUO groups. EAT volume was increased in all obesity phenotype groups. Although no direct association was found between EAT volume and MW indices, EAT volume significantly moderated the relationship between Metabolically Unhealthy (MUH) and both GWE and GWW. MW detects subclinical dysfunction earlier than LVEF across obesity phenotypes, with impairment progressively worsening from MHO to MUNW to MUO. In metabolically unhealthy individuals with increased EAT volume, more pronounced reductions in GWE and elevations in GWW were observed. This study has been registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry under the registration number ChiCTR2500100754 (registration date: April 15, 2025).

papers.title: Restoration of cyclin A2 by glabridin reverses pathological cell cycle arrest and drives cardiac repair in HFpEF.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a pervasive clinical syndrome characterized by complex and elusive pathogenic mechanisms. In this study, we identify aberrant cardiomyocyte cell cycle arrest as a previously unrecognized pathological driver of HFpEF that hinders tissue repair. Using in vivo and in vitro models, we further demonstrate that Glabridin (Gla), a bioactive isoflavone, can induce cardiac repair and alleviate myocardial hypertrophy and fibrosis in HFpEF by targeting the cell cycle arrest pathway. Mechanistically, Gla exerts its protective effects by specifically inhibiting the degradation of Cyclin A2 (CCNA2) and mitigating cardiomyocyte oxidative damage. This stabilization of CCNA2 effectively abrogates cell cycle arrest and drives cardiomyocyte cell cycle re-entry, an effect that was successfully recapitulated by CCNA2 gain-of-function experiments. This reparative response is intrinsically coupled with the restoration of metabolic homeostasis and the attenuation of oxidative stress, as evidenced in both cardiac and hepatic cells. Collectively, our findings define cell cycle arrest as a novel target and position Gla as a potent inducer of CCNA2-mediated cardiac repair for HFpEF treatment.

papers.title: Doxorubicin-induced Cardiotoxicity in Dogs: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Doxorubicin, an anthracycline widely used in both human and veterinary oncology, is highly effective against a variety of malignancies in dogs, including lymphomas, sarcomas and carcinomas. Despite its efficacy, doxorubicin exposure can be associated with cardiotoxicity, which may present acutely or chronically, potentially leading to severe cardiac arrhythmia and congestive heart failure. Mechanisms underlying cardiotoxicity are multifactorial, including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, DNA damage via topoisomerase IIβ, inflammation and dysregulated cell death pathways such as apoptosis, pyroptosis and ferroptosis. In dogs, known risk factors include higher cumulative dose, breed predisposition to idiopathic dilated cardiomyopathy, and higher body weight. Cardiac biomarkers, electrocardiography, echocardiography and other advanced imaging techniques have been employed to detect cardiac changes that can be seen also in the absence of clinical signs. However, current evidence is predominantly derived from experimental and retrospective research, highlighting the need for large prospective clinical studies to strengthen recommendations for monitoring and prevention. A deeper understanding of doxorubicin-induced cardiotoxicity in dogs is needed to identify factors influencing individual susceptibility, clarify the progression from subclinical damage to clinical cardiac dysfunction, and guide future research. Emerging approaches, including advanced echocardiography, microRNAs, proteomic biomarkers and pharmacokinetic modelling, may help improve early detection and guide more individualised dosing to minimise toxicity.

papers.title: Menstrual Health in Children, Adolescents, and Young Adults with Cardiac Disease: An Underrecognized Component of Heart Failure, Mechanical Circulatory Support, and Transplant Care.
papers.abstract: Menstrual abnormalities, including heavy menstrual bleeding, amenorrhea, and dysmenorrhea, are frequently encountered among children, adolescents, and young adults with congenital and acquired heart disease, yet remain underrecognized in routine cardiovascular care. Anticoagulation, thrombosis risk, heart failure physiology, and limited high-quality evidence complicate management and contribute to substantial variation in practice. The Advanced Cardiac Therapies Improving Outcomes Network convened a multidisciplinary working group of cardiologists, hematologists, gynecologists, adolescent medicine specialists, and allied health providers. Following a literature search, the group met monthly via virtual meetings to synthesize current evidence and clinical experience and develop consensus guidance. The consensus emphasizes routine, developmentally appropriate menstrual screening and recognition that traditional definitions of heavy menstrual bleeding may underestimate its clinical impact in patients with heart disease. Management requires individualized assessment of bleeding risk, thrombotic risk, cardiac physiology, and patient preferences. Menstrual abnormalities may warrant broader evaluation for changes in overall health, cardiac status, or energy availability. Menstrual health is integral to comprehensive cardiovascular care. Integrating screening and individualized management into cardiology practice may reduce morbidity, improve quality of life, and support equitable, sex-informed care. Further research and culturally responsive, multidisciplinary implementation are needed to strengthen the evidence base and improve care consistency.

papers.title: Network Analysis of Chronic Disease Diagnosis Co-documentation in Insurance Claims Among Older Arkansans.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity among older adults presents growing clinical and economic challenges, particularly in medically underserved states such as Arkansas. However, it remains unclear whether chronic conditions documented in routine healthcare encounters exhibit structured patterns of diagnosis co-documentation or primarily reflect incidental co-documentation. Understanding these patterns may inform future studies of multimorbidity and healthcare utilization. To characterize statewide, sex-stratified patterns of claim-level diagnosis co-documentation among Arkansas adults aged ≥65 years using administrative claims data. We analyzed 2024 IQVIA administrative claims for Arkansas residents aged ≥65 years (1,408,707 claims from 35,253 unique patients). Analyses were conducted at the claim level; therefore, individuals could contribute multiple claims, and results reflect utilization-weighted diagnosis co-documentation rather than patient-level disease prevalence or multimorbidity. Twenty-five chronic condition categories were defined using ICD-10-CM codes. Pairwise diagnosis co-documentation was quantified using Lewontin's standardized disequilibrium coefficient (D'), which compares observed joint documentation with the expectation under statistical independence. Sex-stratified D' matrices, disease connectedness metrics, and hierarchical clustering were used to characterize patterns of diagnosis co-documentation. Hypertension was the most frequently documented chronic condition among claims for both females (22.2%) and males (23.7%) and exhibited the highest positive connectedness in both sex-stratified analyses. Among females, the strongest diagnosis co-documentation patterns involved hypertension with dyslipidemia, coronary artery disease (CAD), obesity, thyroid disorders, and heart failure (D' = 0.46-0.69). Among males, the strongest diagnosis co-documentation patterns involved hypertension with dyslipidemia (D' = 0.73), obesity (D' = 0.64), CAD (D' = 0.57), and thyroid disorders (D' = 0.56). Females demonstrated relatively greater diagnosis co-documentation among musculoskeletal, endocrine, and mental health conditions, whereas males showed more concentrated diagnosis co-documentation among cardiometabolic and organ dysfunction conditions. Negative D' values identified disease pairs that were infrequently co-documented within the same claims (e.g., autoimmune disease-chronic gastrointestinal disease among males, D' = -1.00), reflecting absent or infrequent claim-level joint documentation. In this claim-level analysis of Arkansas adults aged ≥65 years represented in the IQVIA administrative claims database, diagnosis co-documentation exhibited structured, sex-specific patterns, with hypertension demonstrating the highest positive connectedness among the 25 chronic conditions. These utilization-weighted findings provide a descriptive basis for hypothesis generation and support future longitudinal, patient-level studies to evaluate temporal disease relationships and the potential role of cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CVRM) risk management.

papers.title: Phasic metabolic remodeling coordinates cardiac myofibroblast differentiation and function.
papers.abstract: Fibroblast differentiation into matrix-producing, contractile myofibroblasts is accompanied by metabolic reprogramming, but whether these changes precede differentiation or arise from the activated phenotype remains unclear. We integrated time-resolved extracellular flux analysis, transcriptomics, stable isotope-resolved metabolomics, and metabolic interventions to define the relationship between metabolism and myofibroblast differentiation in adult mouse cardiac fibroblasts stimulated with transforming growth factor-β (TGFβ). TGFβ increased glycolysis within 1.5 h, before broad transcriptional remodeling and induction of periostin and α-smooth muscle actin. Mitochondrial respiration initially declined but increased at 48 h as the phenotype emerged, accompanied by smaller, less elongated mitochondria and greater respiratory capacity. [U- 13 C 6 ]-glucose tracing revealed progressive incorporation of glucose-derived carbon into glycolytic intermediates, nucleotide sugars, and glycerol 3-phosphate, followed later by increased labeling of tricarboxylic acid cycle intermediates. TGFβ-treated fibroblasts also demonstrated enhanced insulin-stimulated glycolysis. Replacing glucose with galactose attenuated collagen and periostin induction, whereas glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase inhibition prevented induction of collagen, periostin, and α-smooth muscle actin. Conversely, glucose transporter 1 or mutant PFK2 (Glyco Hi ) overexpression increased glycolysis without inducing myofibroblast markers. Together, these loss- and gain-of-function studies indicate that glycolytic activity is required for complete differentiation but is not sufficient to initiate the phenotype. Inhibition of mitochondrial Complex I or ATP synthase preferentially reduced collagen abundance, while glycolytic and Complex I inhibition diminished TGFβ-induced collagen gel contraction. These findings define a phasic metabolic program in which early glycolytic activation precedes transcriptional and phenotypic remodeling, whereas mitochondrial respiratory capacity increases later and distinct metabolic nodes selectively regulate collagen abundance and contractile behavior.

papers.title: A Micropeptide Component of the OGDH Complex Modulates ATP Production in the TCA Cycle.
papers.abstract: Since its elucidation, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle has been regarded as a fully defined enzymatic pathway. Here, we report the discovery of a previously unrecognized micropeptide component of this central metabolic system. Through analyzing ribosome profiling data from the mouse sORFs.org database, we discovered APPM (ATP production-promoting micropeptide), a 29-amino acid peptide encoded by a non-canonical small open reading frame within the mouse Ctsb gene. APPM localizes to the mitochondrial matrix and inner membrane, where it directly binds to the E1 subunit (OGDH) of the α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (OGDHc). This interaction modulates OGDHc enzymatic activity, thereby regulating NADH and ATP production. We identified tyrosine-13 as the critical residue mediating the APPM-OGDH interaction and functional activation. Exogenous APPM administration increased ATP levels in vivo and, in a mouse model of heart failure, restored cardiac function, outperforming the reference drug trimetazidine. Collectively, our findings identify APPM as the first micropeptide regulator of the OGDH complex, expanding the known repertoire of the TCA cycle and presenting a potential therapeutic strategy for diseases characterized by bioenergetic insufficiency.

papers.title: Association of peripartum cardiomyopathy with psychiatric disorders - a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) is a myocardial disease characterized by a decrease in left ventricular ejection fraction below 45%, developing at the end of pregnancy or within a few months after its termination. It is a condition with multifactorial etiology that remains incompletely elucidated. Presumed pathophysiological mechanisms include excessive oxidative stress and abnormal prolactin and tryptophan metabolism. These mechanisms may also underlie the development of psychiatric disorders, which occur more frequently in patients with PPCM than in women without the condition. Studies show that PPCM patients are characterized by mental deterioration and a higher risk of diseases such as depression and schizophrenia. Since bromocriptine indirectly inhibits prolactin secretion, the important role of this drug in the treatment of PPCM is highlighted. Recent studies also highlight the potential risks of using psychiatric drugs in patients with cardiovascular burden resulting from PPCM. This article provides an overview of current knowledge on the relationship between peripartum cardiomyopathy and psychiatric disorders.

papers.title: Epicardial adipose tissue radiomics complement calcium scoring in black adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Conventional markers of risk such as coronary artery calcium (CAC) scores are lower and less predictive in Black adults, despite a high prevalence of Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and Metabolic Syndrome We evaluated whether incorporation of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) features capture prognostic signal beyond CAC and social deprivation index, in predicting major adverse cardiovascular events. Adults with T2DM undergoing non-contrast CT calcium scoring from the CLARIFY registry (NCT04075162), including 1024 non-Hispanic Black participants and 3072 propensity-matched non-Hispanic White participants were included. EAT was automatically segmented and radiomic features were extracted and selected using survival-based machine learning. Cox proportional hazards models were constructed using CAC, Social Deprivation Index (SDI), and EAT features alone and in combination. The primary endpoint was 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-3P), defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke. Model discrimination, reclassification, and calibration were assessed. During a median follow-up of approximately 5 years, 206 (20%) Black participants and 422 (14%) matched White participants experienced MACE-3P In Black participants, the SDI+CAC+EAT model demonstrated the highest discrimination (C-index 0.62) and significantly improved reclassification compared with CAC alone (NRI) of 0.29 (95% CI 0.15-0.56; p < 0.0007). In contrast, the SDI+CAC+EAT model showed no improvement in discrimination when compared to CAC alone (C-index 0.67 v. 0.67) in the White cohort. In adults with T2DM, EAT may serve as a complimentary imaging marker when combined with CAC scores to provide incremental prognostic information or refine risk characterization.

papers.title: Use of an AI metabolomics score to predict cardiovascular risk among patients with Psoriasis in the MGB and UK Biobanks.
papers.abstract: Systemic inflammation in psoriasis accelerates atherosclerosis and confers excess cardiovascular risk that is not fully captured by traditional clinical predictors. Metabolomic profiling may identify disease-specific metabolic signatures associated with cardiovascular events and enhance risk prediction beyond conventional factors. To determine whether plasma metabolomic profiling improves cardiovascular risk prediction in patients with psoriasis and to develop and externally validate an artificial intelligence-driven metabolomic risk score (MetaPsoAI) for incident cardiovascular events. We analyzed 1086 individuals with psoriasis and no prior coronary artery disease from the Mass General Brigham (MGB) Biobank who underwent nuclear magnetic resonance-based quantification of 168 circulating metabolites. Associations between metabolites and incident all-cause death or myocardial infarction were assessed. An extreme gradient boosting algorithm was used to develop MetaPsoAI for prediction of myocardial infarction or stroke. External validation was performed in the UK Biobank ( n = 274,000), stratified by psoriasis status. Multiple metabolites, particularly HDL subfractions and amino acid metabolites, were associated with cardiovascular outcomes. MetaPsoAI stratified risk across quartiles, with individuals in the highest quartile demonstrating a 3.6-fold higher risk of myocardial infarction or stroke in the MGB cohort. In the UK Biobank, the highest quartile was associated with a 1.9-fold increased risk among psoriasis patients, with stronger effect sizes compared with non-psoriasis controls. Our findings highlight the potential of AI-driven metabolomics to refine cardiovascular risk prediction in immune-mediated diseases and enable precision prevention strategies for patients with psoriasis.

papers.title: Blockade of EP3 attenuates cardiac fibrosis by suppressing TGF-β1-Smad2/3 signaling through the Smurf2-mediated Smad7 ubiquitination.
papers.abstract: Sustained β-adrenergic activation induces cardiac fibrosis, which is characterized by excessive deposition of extracellular matrix (ECM) secreted by activated cardiac fibroblasts (CFs). Prostaglandin E 2 (PGE 2 ) is a dominant cyclooxygenase metabolite of arachidonic acid and exerts important biological actions by activating four G-protein-coupled receptors, including E-type prostanoid receptors 1-4 (EP1-EP4). The present study aimed to investigate the role of the EP3 receptor in isoproterenol (ISO)-induced cardiac fibrosis. To elucidate the role of EP3 in cardiac fibrosis, the global EP3 gene knockout mice (EP3 -/- ) and the LoxP-Cre system-based CF-specific EP3 gene knockout mice (EP3 cKO ) or cardiomyocyte (CM)-specific EP3 gene knockout mice (EP3 mKO ) were subcutaneously injected with ISO [5 mg/(kg·d)] for 7 d to establish a cardiac fibrosis model. In parallel, the EP3 agonist sulprostone and the EP3 antagonists DG041 and L798106 were used to elucidate the underlying mechanisms. Finally, the therapeutic potential of the EP3 antagonist DG041 was evaluated in the context of cardiac fibrosis. Echocardiography assay showed that both EP3 -/- and EP3 cKO mice exhibited a significant improvement in cardiac diastolic function. Histological staining revealed that EP3 -/- and EP3 cKO , but not EP3 mKO , exhibited a significant attenuation of ISO-induced CF activation and ECM accumulation. Further investigation uncovered that EP3 was highly expressed in the CFs rather than CMs. Inhibition of EP3 in the CFs suppressed transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)-triggered phosphorylation of small mother against decapentaplegic (Smad)2/3 and the production of ECM proteins. Mechanistically, the blockade of EP3 in the CFs activated the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase (PI3K)/protein kinase B (Akt) pathway, which promoted the degradation of Smad ubiquitination regulatory factor 2 (Smurf2) and subsequently suppressed the ubiquitination of Smad7, an inhibitory Smad, leading to an increase in the protein level of Smad7. Furthermore, the administration of an EP3 antagonist, DG041, markedly improved ISO-induced cardiac diastolic dysfunction and fibrosis. This study demonstrates that CF-EP3 contributes to β-adrenergic activation-induced cardiac fibrosis and target of EP3 represents a potential therapeutic strategy for the treatment of cardiac fibrosis.

papers.title: Cardiometabolic Risk Factors, Obesity Phenotypes, and Novel Anthropometric Indices in Patients With Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Hospital-Based Case-Control Study in Central India.
papers.abstract: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) is the most severe manifestation of cardiovascular disease and disproportionately affects South Asians at a younger age than Western populations. Body mass index (BMI) inadequately reflects visceral adiposity, particularly in Indian populations. Obesity phenotypes, which combine BMI with metabolic status, and novel anthropometric indices may improve cardiovascular risk assessment, but data from Indian ACS patients remain limited. To evaluate the association between cardiometabolic risk factors, obesity phenotypes, and novel anthropometric indices with ACS, and to quantify these associations using odds ratios (ORs). This case-control study enrolled 50 patients with confirmed ACS (unstable angina, Non-ST-elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), or ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI)) and 50 age-, sex-, and weight-matched healthy controls at a tertiary care hospital. Sociodemographic, clinical, anthropometric, and biochemical data were recorded. Participants were classified into four obesity phenotypes - metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), metabolically healthy overweight/obese (MHO), and metabolically unhealthy overweight/obese (MUO) - based on BMI and presence of hypertension, diabetes, and/or dyslipidemia. Five novel indices were calculated: A body shape index (ABSI), body roundness index (BRI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and abdominal volume index (AVI). Continuous variables were compared using t-tests and categorical variables using chi-square/Fisher's exact test; unadjusted ORs with 95% CIs were calculated. p<0.05 was significant. ST-elevation myocardial infarction Results: Cases and controls were comparable for age and sex (p>0.05). Hypertension (60% vs 36%), diabetes (52% vs 28%), dyslipidemia (56% vs 32%), and smoking (44% vs 24%) were more common among cases (all p<0.05). Per 1-SD increase, BMI was not significantly associated with ACS (Exp(B) 1.208, 95% CI 0.816-1.790, Wald 0.89, p=0.345), whereas waist circumference, waist-to-hip ratio, and neck circumference were each significantly associated with ACS. Each of the five novel indices was significantly associated with ACS per 1-SD increase (all p<0.001; e.g., WHtR Exp(B) 2.473, 95% CI 1.638-3.732, Wald 18.59); because each index reflects a different geometric construct even when expressed per 1-SD, indices are not ranked by strength of association. Using MHNW as reference, MUO showed significantly increased odds of ACS (OR 3.33, 95% CI 1.10-10.12); MUNW showed a similar point estimate (OR 3.33, 95% CI 0.89-12.49) that did not reach significance (p=0.074), and MHO was not significantly associated with ACS (OR 1.50, 95% CI 0.48-4.65). All ORs are unadjusted. In this unadjusted, cross-sectional comparison, metabolic health and central fat distribution were associated with ACS, whereas BMI was not. Obesity phenotyping and novel anthropometric indices warrant further evaluation in larger, multivariable-adjusted, prospective studies as potential adjuncts to cardiovascular risk stratification in South Asian populations.

papers.title: Telerehabilitation vs. centre-based cardiac rehabilitation after acute coronary syndrome: results of the pragmatic TELECOR randomized trial.
papers.abstract: Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) improves cardiovascular outcomes after acute coronary syndrome (ACS), but access remains suboptimal. Telerehabilitation may overcome barriers, yet evidence from real-world, public health systems is limited. This randomized controlled trial study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of a structured telerehabilitation programme compared with standard centre-based CR in patients after ACS, focussing on cardiovascular risk factor control and lifestyle adherence. TELECOR is a pragmatic, open-label, randomized trial conducted at a tertiary public hospital. Adults with recent ACS were randomized 1:1 to an 8 week structured telerehabilitation or a centre-based CR programme. The primary outcome was achievement of a composite target (≥4 of 7 predefined cardiovascular and lifestyle goals) at 8 weeks. Secondary outcomes included changes in functional capacity, medication adherence, quality of life, psychological status, satisfaction, and cardiovascular events at 6 months. A total of 129 patients were randomized (65 telerehabilitation, 64 centre-based). At 8 weeks, 86% of telerehabilitation vs. 79.7% of centre-based participants met the composite target ( P = 0.37). At 6 months, this was 87% vs. 80.4% ( P = 0.34). Both groups showed similar improvements in functional capacity (≈+1 metabolic equivalent of tasks), adherence (>84%), and satisfaction (>91/100). No between-group differences were observed in clinical events or psychological outcomes. In a real-world public hospital setting, telerehabilitation was non-inferior to conventional CR in achieving cardiovascular risk factor control and improving functional capacity. These results support the broader integration of digital CR models into routine secondary prevention care.

papers.title: Early Life Adversity Produces Enduring Molecular and Functional Disruption of Developing Vagal Circuits.
papers.abstract: Early life adversity (ELA) is a leading preventable contributor to morbidity and mortality, increasing risk for mental and physical illness later in life. However, mechanisms linking ELA to comorbid outcomes within both the brain and body remain poorly understood. We tested whether ELA disrupts functional and molecular development of vagal circuitry, a key pathway for brain-body communication, using the limited bedding and nesting (LBN) mouse model of unpredictable maternal care. We measured vagally mediated autonomic stress responses longitudinally using three noninvasive measures of heart rate variability (HRV). This is the first time the development of the vagally-mediated autonomic stress response has been measured in mice. We also performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing of the vagal medulla immediately after LBN and in adulthood, followed by spatial mapping of high-confidence differentially expressed genes. ELA altered trajectories of all HRV measures, with pronounced sex differences. ELA females showed precocious maturation followed by adult declines, whereas males initially exhibited blunted responses but recovered to control levels. Transcriptomic changes were also sex dependent, with female neurons exhibiting signatures of mitochondrial dysfunction, while males showed adaptive mitochondrial responses. Spatial mapping revealed rostro-caudal organization, localizing adaptive male responses to the rostral and intermediate vagal medulla and maladaptive female responses to the intermediate vagal medulla and loose nucleus ambiguus. These findings demonstrate enduring, sex-specific alterations in vagal circuit development centered on mitochondrial pathways.

papers.title: Channelrhodopsin ion selectivity determines mechanisms and efficacy of optogenetic defibrillation in human atria and ventricles.
papers.abstract: Cardiac re-entrant arrhythmias are a major cause of sudden cardiac death. Optogenetic defibrillation has emerged as a promising anti-arrhythmic strategy based on photoactivation of channelrhodopsins, yet the efficacy and potential adverse consequences of activating different classes of light-gated ion channels have not been systematically evaluated. Previous studies assessed either cation (e.g. ChR2) or anion (e.g. GtACR1) non-selective channels, both of which depolarize resting cardiomyocytes. Recently identified light-gated K + channels (e.g. WiChR) suppress cardiomyocyte activity while maintaining the membrane potential near its resting state, but their defibrillation potential remains unexplored. We used computational simulations to compare ChR2, GtACR1 and WiChR. Single-cell simulations showed that ChR2 and GtACR1 markedly increased diastolic intracellular Ca 2+ (by 42.6% and 52.6%, respectively), whereas WiChR induced only minimal changes (by 4.0%), suggesting lower pro-arrhythmogenic risk. WiChR, however, slightly increased intracellular Na + (by 15.1% vs. 0.1% and 3.4% for ChR2 and GtACR1), consistent with the residual Na + permeability of currently available K + -conducting channelrhodopsins. Simulations in human ventricles and atria showed that GtACR1 most effectively terminated re-entrant arrhythmias at low light intensities, whereas WiChR achieved comparable efficacy at ≥5 mW/mm 2 . Complementary tissue-scale simulations revealed that defibrillation occurs through depolarization within the excitable gap followed by fast Na + channel inactivation (ChR2 and partly GtACR1), or through reduced membrane resistance at sufficiently high light intensities (large-conductance channels GtACR1 and WiChR). Overall, we demonstrate that channelrhodopsin ion selectivity is a key determinant of both optogenetic defibrillation efficacy and its underlying mechanisms. TRANSLATIONAL PERSPECTIVE: Re-entrant arrhythmias are a leading cause of sudden cardiac death. Standard therapies, including the activation of implantable cardioverter-defibrillators, carry burdens such as pain and myocardial injury. Optogenetic defibrillation has been suggested as a potentially gentler alternative, replacing high-voltage electrical shocks by photoactivation of light-gated ion channels expressed in cardiac cells. Determining which light-gated ion channel optimally balances efficacy and adverse effects on cardiac electrophysiology is critical for clinical translation. We addressed this question using computational simulations and validation experiments in zebrafish hearts. We identify ion selectivity as a key determinant of both the success rate for arrhythmia termination and the underlying mechanisms: non-selective cation- and anion-conducting channels terminate re-entry efficiently while promoting intracellular Ca 2+ accumulation, a plausible substrate for pro-arrhythmic side effects that could undermine therapeutic safety. K + -conducting channels largely avoid this pro-arrhythmic risk by holding cardiomyocytes near their resting potential, albeit at the cost of requiring transmural illumination, while also causing mild Na + accumulation attributable to residual Na + permeability. Together, these trade-offs define clear clinical implications: K + -conducting channels may provide the safest option for optogenetic defibrillation, particularly once variants with further enhanced K + selectivity and red-shifted activation spectra for improved operation within blood-perfused myocardium become available. KEY POINTS: We use computational simulations to compare cation non-selective (ChR2), anion non-selective (GtACR1) and K + -selective (WiChR) channelrhodopsins for optogenetic termination of re-entrant arrhythmia. Single-cardiomyocyte simulations suggest that ChR2 and GtACR1 activation can cause progressive accumulation of intracellular Ca 2+ , which is minimized when using WiChR. Intracellular microelectrode recordings from hearts of transgenic adult zebrafish validate the simulated voltage dynamics seen with ChR2, GtACR1 or WiChR activation. Simulations of human left ventricles and atria indicate that GtACR1 is most effective in terminating re-entrant arrhythmia at low light intensities, whereas WiChR becomes similarly effective at higher intensities. Tissue-scale simulations indicate distinct defibrillation mechanisms: excitable gap extinction by de novo action potential initiation followed by inactivation of fast Na + channels for depolarizing channelrhodopsins (ChR2, GtACR1), and reduction in membrane resistance for the large-conductance channels (GtACR1, WiChR), effectively clamping the membrane potential at each channel's reversal potential at high light levels.

papers.title: Metabolic memory in diabetic complications: evidence for persistent cellular states and limits of therapeutic reversal.
papers.abstract: Metabolic memory is defined here as an exposure-history-dependent cellular phenotype that persists beyond immediate carry-over after verified withdrawal of the initiating exposure, principally high glucose and is accompanied by a specified functional impairment or an altered response to the same defined secondary stimulus. This operational definition separates cellular memory from clinical legacy effects, continuing local stimulation and residual structural injury. We critically examine evidence from longitudinal clinical studies, human biospecimens, animal models and controlled cell experiments, distinguishing molecular persistence, measured signaling activity, causal maintenance and treatment-free durability. DCCT/EDIC and UKPDS establish lasting benefits of earlier glycemic management but do not independently identify cellular memory as the mechanism. Experimental evidence supports selected endothelial redox circuits, epigenetic regulation and hematopoietic progenitor training; human causal evidence is substantially more limited. Persistent chromatin marks do not necessarily imply continuously active signaling, and latent priming may become apparent only after rechallenge. In kidney, cardiovascular, retinal and wound disease, candidate cellular memory coexists with hypoxic or inflammatory niches and structural loss. Pancreatic β-cell plasticity is considered a comparative endocrine model rather than an established complication-memory circuit. The proposed interactions among epigenetic, mitochondrial, metabolic and inflammatory mechanisms remain a framework supported by selected local feedback loops, not a universally demonstrated network. Therapeutic evidence is organized into prevention, modification or suppression of established abnormalities, and sustained molecular and functional recovery after treatment cessation after intervention withdrawal. The latter remains unestablished in patients for the mechanisms reviewed. Early glycemic and multifactorial management remains essential, while mechanistic translation requires explicit recovery, perturbation and post-treatment follow-up designs.

papers.title: Simple renal cysts are associated with ischemic stroke in young adults: a case-control study.
papers.abstract: The incidence of ischemic stroke among young patients is increasing, and ischemic stroke has become a major cause of death and disability in young adults. The key to alleviating this problem is to identify the risk factors and causes of stroke to optimize treatment. The current study aims to assess whether simple renal cysts are associated with the occurrence of ischemic stroke among young adults. Data from patients with acute ischemic stroke aged 18-50 years and age- and sex-matched controls who underwent medical examinations at the Affiliated Changsha Central Hospital, Hengyang Medical School, University of South China, from October 2022 to September 2025 were retrospectively collected. Potential risk factors (including blood pressure, fasting blood glucose, dyslipidemia, homocysteine, and simple renal cysts) were compared between young patients with stroke and controls. Binary logistic regression analysis was conducted to identify risk factors for ischemic stroke among young patients. A total of 219 young patients with acute ischemic stroke and 219 controls were enrolled for analysis. Patients with elevated blood pressure, elevated blood glucose, and concurrent simple renal cysts had a higher risk of ischemic stroke. Simple renal cysts were associated with a higher risk of ischemic stroke in young adults, but they did not correlate with greater stroke severity. Simple renal cysts are associated with ischemic stroke in young adults and thus merit clinical awareness. Prospective multicenter cohort studies are expected to confirm this association and clarify potential mechanisms.

papers.title: Incident Type 2 Diabetes in Individuals With CKD: The REGARDS Study.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and diabetes are comorbid metabolic diseases that share common factors such as insulin resistance. Few studies have examined the association between CKD and incident diabetes, with limited consensus and associated risk factors. We conducted an analysis of participants in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in stroke study to investigate incident diabetes among participants with CKD compared with non-CKD participants. A prospective cohort study. Total of 7,511 participants who completed 10 years of follow-up were included in the analysis, of whom 994 had CKD (an estimated glomerular filtration rate <60 mL/min/1.73m 2 or albumin-to-creatinine ratio >30mg/g) at baseline. CKD. Incident diabetes. Logistic regression analysis was performed to estimate the odds of incident diabetes among CKD participants, with odds ratio (OR) and 95% CI. Risk factors for incident diabetes among CKD participants were also examined. After 10 years of follow-up, 11.0% (717) of non-CKD participants and 15.8% (157) of CKD participants developed diabetes. Incident diabetes was higher among CKD participants than in non-CKD participants using creatinine-based equations, which was not seen when using a creatinine-based and cystatin C-based equation for CKD. Several risk factors such as race, prediabetes, age, body mass index, hypertension, current smoking, and exercise ≥ 4 times/week increased the odds of incident diabetes, whereas current alcohol use had a lower risk of incident diabetes. Prediabetes had the highest risk of incident diabetes (OR = 4.94, 95% Cl: 4.22-5.78; P < 0.01). Attrition bias, limited generalizability, and limited diagnostic classification. The association between CKD and incident diabetes depends on how CKD is defined. These findings highlight the need for future studies to explore how renal function is assessed when determining adverse outcomes related to CKD. Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and diabetes are common chronic diseases that might share similar causes for their development. Our study looked at 7,511 participants in the Reasons for Geographic and Racial Differences in Stroke study to look at the odds of developing diabetes in participants with CKD versus those without CKD within 10 years. The odds of developing diabetes changed based on how CKD was calculated. Prediabetes was the strongest risk factor, but others included body mass index, hypertension, current smoking, and exercise. Interestingly, individuals who drink alcohol had a lower odds of developing diabetes. Our study suggests that how CKD is defined plays a big role in determining future outcomes related to CKD.

papers.title: Randomized Clinical Trial of Ringer's Lactate Versus Chloride-Reduced Saline-Dextrose in Postoperative Kidney Transplantation.
papers.abstract: Normal saline administration induces hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis, potentially impairing kidney allograft recovery. The comparative efficacy of balanced crystalloids against actively chloride-reduced saline protocols remains unclear. This randomized, open-label trial compared Ringer's Lactate Solution (RLS) with a dynamic dual-infusion protocol of normal saline and 5% dextrose (NSS + D5W) in adult kidney transplant recipients. Using a prespecified modified intention-to-treat analysis, 134 patients who received ≥2 L of study fluid were evaluated. Fluids were strictly titrated to hourly urine output. The primary outcome was day-4 serum bicarbonate. Secondary outcomes evaluated the overall treatment strategy, including protocolized rescue bicarbonate requirements, 1-month estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) as an indicator of early functional recovery, and exploratory mechanistic biomarkers (urine neutrophil gelatinase-associated lipocalin [NGAL] and serum cytokines). On postoperative day 4, the RLS group maintained significantly higher serum bicarbonate (19.39 vs. 17.31 mEq/L; P < 0.001) and required substantially less rescue bicarbonate therapy (17.9% vs. 58.2%; P < 0.001) compared with the NSS + D5W group. Serum chlorides were comparable between groups on day 4. RLS was associated with more favorable early allograft function, evidenced by a higher 1-month eGFR (61.63 vs. 53.18 ml/min per 1.73 m 2 ; P = 0.028). Among the deceased-donor recipients, a lower proportion of RLS group had high urine NGAL (>100 ng/ml) and elevated interferon-γ; however, the continuous NGAL comparison was not significant and other cytokines (tumor necrosis factor [TNF]-α, interleukin [IL]-6, and IL-10) did not differ. These exploratory biomarker findings are hypothesis-generating. RLS effectively reduces early postoperative metabolic acidosis and was associated with better short-term allograft functional recovery compared with a chloride-reduced saline regimen. These benefits are most applicable to allografts exhibiting immediate or early function that permits standard volume expansion.

papers.title: Case Report: When muscle edema is not a myositis flare: Legionella pneumonia complicated by rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury in long-standing polymyositis.
papers.abstract: Legionella pneumophila is an important cause of severe community-acquired pneumonia and can produce extrapulmonary manifestations that obscure the primary diagnosis. Diagnostic error is especially likely in patients with established idiopathic inflammatory myopathy, because fever, myalgia, weakness, creatine kinase elevation and muscle edema may be attributed to autoimmune flare. We report a 70-year-old woman with a 25-year history of polymyositis receiving long-term corticosteroids and azathioprine who developed high fever, severe bilateral thigh pain and progressive proximal weakness after recent travel. On transfer, she had anuria with bladder distension, dark urine, diffuse posterior-thigh muscle edema, pneumonia, hyponatremia, metabolic acidosis, myoglobinemia and acute kidney injury. Legionella pneumonia with rhabdomyolysis and multifactorial acute kidney injury was suspected clinically, and Legionella-active antimicrobial therapy, hydration, urinary drainage and urine alkalinization were started before microbiological confirmation. A targeted sequencing-based respiratory pathogen assay on sputum collected on Day +4 detected L. pneumophila (145 sequences; estimated concentration <10^3 copies/mL) and respiratory syncytial virus A (266,036 sequences; 10^5 copies/mL), raising the possibility of viral-bacterial coinfection. Legionella urinary antigen, targeted PCR and culture were not documented. After infection and renal injury stabilized, methylprednisolone and intravenous immunoglobulin were used because residual inflammatory myopathy activity remained in the differential. However, creatine kinase and myoglobin had already declined, so subsequent improvement cannot be attributed specifically to immunomodulation. Creatinine fell from 538 μmol/L on Day 0 to 110 μmol/L on Day +9 and 78 μmol/L on Day +30; follow-up chest CT on Day +14 showed marked improvement. This case shows that muscle MRI edema is contextual rather than etiologic. In immunosuppressed myositis patients, pneumonia plus hyponatremia, myoglobinuria and renal injury should prompt early Legionella-active treatment while autoimmune activity is reassessed after infection control.

papers.title: Beyond canonical homeostasis: Dynamic, plastic, and intermittently unregulated physiology as the norm.
papers.abstract: Homeostasis is often taught as steady-state regulation keeping internal variables within narrow limits-reflecting a mammalian bias. Yet, canonical homeostasis is far from universal. In many animals, including humans, normal physiological states allow some variables to fluctuate cyclically or stochastically while others remain tightly controlled. Indeed, across non-mammalian species, broad physiological variability is frequently normal rather than exceptional. Here we present case studies showing that plastic, variable regulation-sometimes approaching randomness-is both common and adaptive. Examples include intermittent breathing during diving, episodic feeding and digestion, pulsatile hormone release, variable sleep cycles, irregular gastric emptying, fluctuating renal blood flow, and stochastic immune responses. These complex regulatory patterns represent evolved strategies-not failures of homeostasis-allowing organisms to function efficiently in dynamic environments. Such flexible regulation, including unregulated intervals, may minimize energetic costs compared with continuous tight control, enhancing evolutionary fitness. We propose that variable degrees of physiological regulation have evolved as energy-efficient solutions shaped by natural selection. Expanding the concept of homeostasis to include intermittent and stochastic forms will improve our understanding of physiological adaptation, with significant implications for ecology and evolutionary biology. We further advocate new experimental approaches to distinguish adaptive variability from true regulatory failure.

papers.title: Heart Failure Risk Phenotypes Based on a 2-Dimensional Tree Structure Derived from Clinical Characteristics and Associations with Disease Prevalence and Cardiovascular Mortality in the General Population.
papers.abstract: Using the Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction Tree (DDRTree) algorithm, a 2-dimensional tree model was constructed based on conventional clinical indicators to identify heart failure (HF) risk phenotypes with different pathophysiological characteristics from the general adult population and evaluate their association with HF prevalence and cardiovascular mortality risk. A representative sample of 24 205 general US adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2018 was analyzed. Eleven routine clinical indicators from multiple physiological dimensions were fed into the DDRTree algorithm to project each of them in a 2-dimensional space. The resulting tree structure revealed distinct HF risk phenotypes whose links to outcome HF prevalence and cardiovascular mortality risk were quantified with weighted logistic regression and Cox proportional-hazard models. Discriminant Dimensionality Reduction Tree identified 3 HF risk phenotypes: normal, metabolic (characterized by upregulated glucose-metabolism markers), and inflammatory (characterized by abnormalities in inflammatory and hepatic-renal markers). After fully adjusting for confounding factors, the metabolic phenotype was significantly associated with the risk of HF compared with the normal phenotype (odds ratio [OR] = 1.96, P < .001, 95% CI: 1.47-2.62), whereas it showed no significant correlation with the risk of cardiovascular death (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.92, P = .539, 95% CI: 0.70-1.20). In contrast, the inflammatory phenotype was significantly correlated with both HF risk (OR = 3.95, P < .001, 95% CI: 2.94-5.33) and cardiovascular mortality risk (HR = 1.47, P = .002, 95% CI: 1.16-1.87). This study elucidates potential risk phenotypes influencing HF and cardiovascular mortality, providing new insights for precise HF risk stratification and targeted preventive interventions in the general population.

papers.title: Advanced Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Risk and Risk-Factor Control in Patients With Type 2 Diabetes Without Established Cardiovascular Disease.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) risk stratification may identify patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) who require more intensive primary prevention, but real-world data from Vietnam are limited. We aimed to describe advanced CKM risk and risk-factor control in Vietnamese patients with T2DM without established cardiovascular disease (CVD). This multicenter cross-sectional study enrolled 1436 adults with T2DM without CVD in Vietnam. Advanced CKM risk was defined as 10-year total CVD risk ≥ 20% or eGFR < 60 mL/min/1.73 m 2 . Guideline-based control of HbA1c, blood pressure, LDL-C, triglycerides, and non-HDL-C was evaluated. Logistic regression assessed associations between advanced CKM risk and target achievement. Advanced CKM risk was identified in 551 patients (38.4%). Despite a relatively low prevalence of BMI ≥ 25 kg/m 2 (26.9%), hypertriglyceridemia was the most common metabolic abnormality, affecting 88.0% of participants. Risk-factor control was generally low, with 33.3% achieving glycemic control, 33.5% blood pressure control, 18.8% LDL-C control, 12.0% triglyceride control, and 21.1% non-HDL-C control. After adjustment, advanced CKM risk was associated with poorer blood pressure control (adjusted OR = 0.466, 95% CI = 0.359-0.603, p < 0.001) and triglyceride control (adjusted OR = 0.677, 95% CI = 0.473-0.969, p = 0.033), but not with achievement of HbA1c, LDL-C, non-HDL-C, or combined lipid control. Advanced CKM risk was common among Vietnamese patients with T2DM without established CVD and was consistently associated with poorer blood pressure control. CKM-based risk assessment may identify high-risk patients earlier and support guideline-directed risk-factor management. Frequent hypertriglyceridemia with relatively low obesity supports a CKM-based strategy tailored to this metabolic risk pattern.

papers.title: Body Composition Phenotypes and Their Metabolic Associations in Treatment-Naïve Patients With Newly Diagnosed Type 2 Diabetes: A DXA-Based Cluster Analysis.
papers.abstract: We characterized body-composition heterogeneity in treatment-naive type 2 diabetes (T2DM) using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA), and assessed whether cluster-metabolic associations persisted after accounting for sex-related body-composition differences. K-means clustering of 50 DXA-derived body-composition variables classified 185 treatment-naive T2DM patients. Variance decomposition, sex-stratified analyses, sex-stratified clustering, sex-specific standardization clustering and multiple imputation (20 datasets) addressed sex confounding and missing data. Four exploratory body-composition clusters were identified: Low Fat-Low Muscle, Male-Predominant Central Obesity (98.6% male), Female-Predominant Low-Muscle High-Adiposity (98.0% female) and High Fat-High Muscle. Two clusters showed strong sex predominance; sex-specific normalization reduced sex-cluster dependence while preserving metabolic associations. In multiple-imputation-adjusted models, Clusters 2 and 4 had markedly higher MASLD odds (OR = 9.69 and 8.55, respectively), while Cluster 4 had lower osteoporosis (OR = 0.16) and higher hyperuricemia (OR = 6.36) odds versus Cluster 1. Bone turnover markers, diabetic retinopathy and diabetic kidney disease showed no significant associations. DXA-based body-composition clusters are associated with distinct metabolic and comorbidity profiles-particularly MASLD, osteoporosis and hyperuricemia-that persisted after sex-specific standardization and multiple imputation. Given the sex-cluster overlap and modest silhouette width, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require prospective validation.

papers.title: Renin-Angiotensin System Activation Drives Early Cardiorenal Dysfunction in Normotensive Prediabetes.
papers.abstract: Prediabetes is increasingly recognised as a stage at which cardiovascular and renal dysfunction begin to develop despite the absence of overt metabolic disease. The mechanisms underlying these early alterations remain poorly understood. Because adipose tissues surrounding blood vessels and kidneys can locally generate components of the renin-angiotensin system (RAS), we hypothesised that subclinical RAS activation contributes to early cardiorenal dysfunction in prediabetes. Using a pre-established normotensive, non-obese rat model of prediabetes induced by 12 weeks of mild hypercaloric feeding, we examined the impact of systemic angiotensin II (AngII) elevation and angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibition on cardio-, cerebro- and renovascular function by invasive hemodynamics, ex vivo pressure myography, and ex vivo renal perfusion experiments, respectively. Prediabetic rats exhibited impaired parasympathetic baroreceptor sensitivity and altered renovascular endothelium-dependent vasodilation despite preserved blood pressure and cardiac function. Systemic AngII infusion further exacerbated autonomic and renovascular dysfunction. In contrast, treatment with a non-hypotensive dose of the ACE inhibitor captopril restored baroreceptor sensitivity, improved renovascular endothelial function, reduced brainstem inflammation, and attenuated renal tubular fibrosis. Examination of perivascular and perirenal adipose tissues revealed significantly higher protein concentration of ACE1 in prediabetic rats compared to controls. These findings are consistent with an early activation of RAS contributing to subclinical cardiovascular and renal dysfunction during prediabetes independently of hypertension. Targeting RAS signalling at this early stage may therefore represent a strategy to limit progression of cardiorenal complications along the continuum from prediabetes to diabetes.

papers.title: Real-world observational study evaluating metabolic and kidney outcomes in patients living with chronic kidney disease and type 2 diabetes mellitus with obesity prescribed tirzepatide.
papers.abstract: Obesity and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) accelerate chronic kidney disease (CKD) progression. Tirzepatide, a dual glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) and glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP) receptor agonist, has demonstrated metabolic and potential renoprotective benefits in clinical trials. There have been limited reports of the implications of prescribing tirzepatide in a real-world cohort of patients with advanced CKD. This observational study includes a multi-ethnic cohort of 62 adults with CKD stages 1-5 who initiated tirzepatide indicated for T2DM with concurrent obesity in a general nephrology clinic between June 2024 and October 2025. Patients were followed for a median of 21.4 weeks. Clinical outcomes including weight, glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR), urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (uACR), blood pressure, lipid profile and insulin requirements were collected. Tirzepatide significantly reduced median weight (103-100 kg; p < 0.0001), HbA1c (63 [7.9%] to 54 [7.1%] mmol/mol; p = 0.002) and uACR (111-44 mg/mmol; p = 0.008), while eGFR remained stable. Significant improvements were also observed in triglycerides, total cholesterol, LDL cholesterol and total daily insulin dose. Gastrointestinal symptoms and decreased serum bicarbonate were the most common adverse events. In this real-world, multi-ethnic cohort, including patients with advanced CKD, tirzepatide was associated with clinically meaningful improvements in weight, glycaemic control, albuminuria, lipid profile and insulin requirements without adversely affecting kidney function. The introduction of tirzepatide to patients with CKD should be guided by a multidisciplinary team.

papers.title: Frailty transitions and the risk of multisystem burden of chronic disease: a prospective cohort study in China.
papers.abstract: Frailty, defined by a decline in physiological reserve, is a key determinant of adverse health outcomes in older populations. While baseline frailty has been shown to predict the development of chronic diseases, the impact of changes in frailty status over time, particularly in rapidly ageing populations like China, remains poorly understood. This study aimed to assess how baseline frailty and its longitudinal transitions influence the incidence of chronic diseases across multiple organ systems. We analysed data from 17,708 adults (aged ≥ 40) in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) collected between 2011 and 2018. Frailty was assessed using the Rockwood Frailty Index at baseline and at two-year follow-up, categorised as stable, improved, or worsened. We applied Cox proportional hazards models to estimate hazard ratios (HRs) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for the onset of 13 major chronic diseases spanning cardiovascular, metabolic, respiratory, neurological, psychiatric, digestive, renal, and musculoskeletal systems. The study included 9,807 to 16,882 participants across 13 disease-specific subgroups, with a median follow-up period of 6.2-6.8 years for baseline frailty status and 4.4-5.0 years for frailty transitions. Frail individuals were typically older, more likely to be female, unmarried, with lower education, higher BMI, and reported fewer hours of sleep. Baseline frailty was associated with significantly higher risks for all 13 chronic diseases, with the strongest association observed for psychiatric problems (HR 5.17, 95% CI 3.24-8.24). Worsening frailty over time was linked to elevated risks, particularly for asthma (HR 3.91, 95% CI 1.28-11.91), while improvements in frailty showed reduced risks, notably for kidney diseases (HR 0.37, 95% CI 0.22-0.63). The association was particularly strong in adults aged 40-65 years, indicating greater potential for risk modification in midlife. Frailty is a dynamic and modifiable predictor of multisystem chronic disease risk. Changes in frailty status offer valuable insights into future disease development, especially among middle-aged adults. Routine frailty monitoring in clinical settings may offer a strategic opportunity to delay or prevent the onset of chronic diseases through timely interventions. These findings emphasize the need for incorporating frailty-targeted strategies into public health and clinical care policies to enhance ageing-related disease prevention.

papers.title: Preclinical carotid atherosclerosis is independently associated with cardiovascular events and mortality in type 1 diabetes.
papers.abstract: To evaluate whether carotid atherosclerosis predicts future cardiovascular events (CVE) and mortality in adults with type 1 diabetes (T1D) in primary prevention. Cohort study in adults with T1D participating in a cardiovascular risk assessment program that included carotid ultrasound. Eligibility criteria included age ≥ 40 years, diabetic kidney disease regardless of age or diabetes duration, or type 1 diabetes duration ≥ 10 years in the presence of at least one additional cardiovascular risk factor.The primary endpoint was the first CVE. A secondary endpoint was a composite of CVE plus all-cause mortality. Carotid plaque burden and outcomes were analyzed using Kaplan-Meier curves and Cox regression models. 701 individuals were followed for a mean of 5.85 years (mean age 48.5 years; T1D duration 27 years; 51.9% males). Carotid plaques were identified in 40.4%. During follow-up, 45 CVE occurred (18 coronary artery disease, 14 peripheral artery disease, 6 stroke, 3 heart failure, 4 deaths) along with 5 non-cardiovascular deaths. Event-free survival declined progressively with increasing plaque burden (log-rank p < 0.001). In unadjusted analyses, the presence of any plaque was associated with increased risk of CVE (HR 3.14, 95%C I 1.69-5.84) and of the composite endpoint (HR 3.07, 95% CI 1.71-5.51). After multivariable adjustment for demographic, metabolic, and microvascular factors, a high plaque burden (≥ 3 plaques) remained associated with CVE (HR 3.38, 95% CI 1.37-8.38) and with the composite endpoint (HR 2.64, 95% CI 1.13-6.21). Preclinical carotid atherosclerosis in adults with T1D was independently associated with an increased risk of cardiovascular events and mortality. These findings support the potential role of carotid ultrasound as a complementary tool for cardiovascular risk assessment in individuals with T1D.

papers.title: Longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and their association with cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity risk in postmenopausal women: evidence from the CHARLS study.
papers.abstract: To investigate the association between longitudinal sleep duration trajectories and the risk of cardio-renal-metabolic multimorbidity (CRMM) in a population of postmenopausal women. A total of 2,859 postmenopausal women from the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study (CHARLS) were included, with 4 repeated measurements of night sleep duration collected from 2011 to 2018. Group-based trajectory modeling was adopted to identify distinct sleep duration trajectory patterns. Multivariable logistic regression was used to examine the associations between sleep trajectories and incident CRMM ascertained between 2018 and 2020. Subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses were further conducted to validate the robustness of the findings. Three sleep duration trajectory patterns were identified: normal-stable (33.9% of the cohort), normal-fluctuating decline (52.0%), and short-rapid decline (14.1%). During a median follow-up of 2 years, the primary outcome (incident CRMM) occurred in 108 participants (3.8%). Compared with normal-stable group, those in normal-fluctuating decline and short-rapid decline groups had an increased risk of CRMM (ORs of 2.30 [95%CI, 1.35-3.91] and 3.75 [95%CI, 1.99-7.07], respectively) after adjustment for multiple covariates. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these associations, which were independent of key baseline characteristics and missing data. In postmenopausal women, short and declining sleep duration trajectories are strong, independent risk factors for CRMM. Public health and clinical interventions should prioritize maintaining stable, adequate sleep to mitigate multimorbidity risk in this population.

papers.title: Implementation of the Cardiovascular-Kidney-Metabolic Syndrome Framework in Contemporary Cardiology: A Nationwide Survey of the Hellenic Society of Cardiology.
Sleep duration and risk of microvascular complications in type 2 diabetes: A prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Longitudinal evidence on sleep duration's effects on type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) microvascular outcomes, particularly in Asian populations, remains limited. This study investigated the prospective association between sleep duration and microvascular complication incidence in T2DM patients. This prospective cohort included 1236 T2DM adults, free of microvascular complications at baseline from National Metabolic Management Centre Ningbo Branch (2018-2023). Self-reported sleep duration was categorized into 5 groups (<7, 7-8, 8-9, 9-10, or ≥10h). Incident diabetic kidney disease (DKD), retinopathy (DR), and peripheral neuropathy (DPN) were ascertained. Cox regression and restricted cubic spline analyses estimated hazard ratio (HRs) and dose-response relationships. In 2459 person-years, 237 participants developed microvascular complications. A U-shaped association emerged between sleep duration and composite microvascular complications (P < 0.001) and DPN (P = 0.039), with lowest risk at 7-8h. Compared to 7-8h, shorter (<7h) and longer (≥10h) durations significantly increased composite microvascular complication risks (HR = 1.71, P = 0.018; HR = 1.87, P = 0.005). No statistically significant interactions were observed between sleep duration and age, BMI, sedentary time, or sleep quality (all P for interaction >0.05). Both insufficient and excessive sleep increase T2DM microvascular complication risks. Maintaining 7-8 h of sleep daily may be a vital behavioral target in comprehensive T2DM management, potentially reducing microvascular complication burden.

papers.title: Key safety outcomes of SGLT2 inhibitors versus DPP-4 inhibitors in general and vulnerable participants with T2DM: A target trial emulation study.
papers.abstract: Sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT2i), a class of oral hypoglycaemic agents (OHAs), have demonstrated cardiovascular and renal benefits. However, safety concerns may hinder their broader adoption, particularly among frail populations. We evaluated key safety outcomes associated with SGLT2i compared with dipeptidyl peptidase-4 inhibitors (DPP4i), an OHA class with low risks of complications. We conducted a target trial emulation (TTE) study using Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database (NHIRD) and enrolled participants with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). Eligible participants were categorized according to newly initiated SGLT2i (n = 224,510) or newly initiated DPP4i (n = 698,012) with continuous use for at least 30 days. Propensity score overlap weighting (PSOW) was used to balance baseline characteristics. In the intention-to-treat analysis, the SGLT2i group showed significantly lower incidence rate (per person-years) of several safety outcomes than the DPP4i group, including urinary tract infection (UTI) (23.84‰ vs. 27.88‰; hazard ratio [HR], 0.86; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.84-0.87), fractures or falls (16.55‰ vs. 17.79‰; HR, 0.93; 95% CI, 0.91-0.95), acute kidney injury (AKI) (1.06‰ vs. 1.91‰; HR, 0.55; 95% CI, 0.51-0.59), bullous pemphigoid (0.02‰ vs. 0.07‰; HR, 0.35; 95% CI, 0.23-0.54), and all-cause mortality (13.05‰ vs. 19.72‰; HR, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.65-0.67). Conversely, the risk of genital infection was higher in the SGLT2i group (2.96‰ vs. 2.05‰; HR, 1.44; 95% CI, 1.38-1.51). These findings remained consistent in the per-protocol analysis, across most vulnerable subgroups and individual SGLT2i and DPP4i agents. SGLT2i, compared with DPP4i, demonstrated a favourable safety profile across most evaluated outcomes, except for genital infections.

papers.title: Selective Systemic Responses During Aeromonas salmonicida Subsp. Salmonicida Infection in Northern Snakehead (Channa argus).
papers.abstract: Northern snakehead (Channa argus) is a bimodal air-breathing fish in which erythrocyte-associated parameters remain relatively stable during physiological challenges such as aerial exposure. However, whether this characteristic is maintained during systemic infection remains unclear. In this study, temporal host responses were characterized following experimental Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida infection by integrating haematological, leukocyte morphological, biochemical, and multi-tissue transcriptional analyses. Most erythrocyte-associated indices, including RBC, HGB, HCT, MCV, MCH, and RDW, showed no significant temporal changes, whereas MON, GRA, and PLT exhibited significant responses. Morphologically abnormal leukocytes increased from approximately 7% in healthy fish to 56% at 6 days post-infection and remained above 50% through 8 days, indicating persistent leukocyte-associated cellular alterations during infection. Biochemical responses were also selective, with changes primarily in protein- and metabolism-associated parameters. Transcriptional responses differed among peripheral blood, head kidney, spleen, and liver, including sustained casp7 suppression in the head kidney and distinct inflammatory and apoptosis-associated responses across tissues. Two-way ANOVA further identified significant tissue × time interactions for casp8, tnfα, and casp3. Collectively, A. salmonicida infection in northern snakehead was characterized by comparatively limited temporal variation in most erythrocyte-associated indices, alongside selective leukocyte, biochemical, and tissue-dependent transcriptional responses. These findings highlight a contrasting blood response characterized by persistent leukocyte alterations despite comparatively limited temporal variation in most erythrocyte-associated indices during bacterial infection in northern snakehead.

papers.title: Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Multi-hormone Receptor Modulators for Kidney Protection in Nondiabetic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), together with newer multi-hormone receptor modulators that target glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP), glucagon and amylin, have emerged as promising therapies for chronic kidney disease. This review examines the mechanisms through which these agents may protect the kidney and summarizes the emerging clinical evidence in populations without diabetes. Kidney protection appears to arise through complementary direct and indirect routes. Direct effects include natriuresis through inhibition of the sodium-hydrogen exchanger (NHE)-3, modulation of glomerular hemodynamics through effects on afferent arteriolar tone and vasoconstrictor pathways, and attenuation of renal inflammation; mechanisms that are largely independent of glucose lowering. Indirect mechanisms include reductions in the metabolic, hemodynamic and cardiac burden on the kidney through weight loss, blood pressure lowering, and improvement of heart failure. Beyond selective GLP-1R-agonism, the added hormonal components of multi-hormone receptor modulators engage distinct physiological pathways whose interactions may be additive, synergistic or counteracting, but remain incompletely understood. The efficacy of GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone receptor modulators in people without diabetes is currently supported by results from secondary kidney endpoints in phase-3 obesity and cardiovascular outcome trials, including reductions in albuminuria and preservation of estimated glomerular filtration rate. Several dedicated outcome studies of GLP-1 RAs and multi-hormone receptor modulators are now underway and will determine whether these therapies become a new pillar of care in nondiabetic kidney disease.

papers.title: Antidiabetic medications in the pipeline.
papers.abstract: There is an extensive pipeline of therapies for diabetes mellitus. It has been known for the past three decades that obesity is a key pathophysiological player, involving inflammation, insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction leading to type 2 diabetes and to significant cardiovascular, renal and hepatic complications, all central to the metabolic syndrome. On the basis of this knowledge and the disposition of drugs with multiple effects on different disease components, the diabetes therapeutic paradigm has shifted from merely glucocentric to multitargeted against these interconnected pathways.Much more recently, incretin-based multi-agonists have been developed that deliver unprecedented glycemic and weight benefits as well as weekly insulins and oral GLP-1 agonists that are able to reduce the burden of injectable therapies. An antibody-peptide conjugate that acts as a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor modulator has also shown promising results. Today, novel insulin sensitizers are modulating metabolic pathways towards higher energy expenditure with fewer side effects. Adjunctive agents for type 1 diabetes are improving glucose control while reducing hypoglycemia risk. Finally, drugs designed to restrain the inevitable muscle mass loss caused by antiobesity treatments are being tested. The diabetes pipeline is rich and there is hope that in the next few years, the therapeutic landscape will be further transformed with even more efficacious and individualized treatments.

papers.title: tRF-15:31-Arg-CCT-3-1 Improves Diabetic Kidney Disease by Reducing AATF and Alleviating Mesangial Cell Oxidative Stress and Inflammation.
papers.abstract: Diabetic kidney disease (DKD), a primary contributor to end-stage renal disease, involves a complex interplay between oxidative stress and inflammation. Given the reported involvement of apoptosis-antagonizing transcription factor (AATF) in cellular stress and inflammatory responses, we investigated whether the anti-inflammatory effects of tRF-15:31-Arg-CCT-3-1 (tRF-15:31) are mediated through the regulation of AATF expression. The expression and biological effects of tRF-15:31 were investigated in streptozotocin (STZ)-induced DKD mice and high-glucose (HG)-treated renal mesangial cells. The involvement of AATF was examined through tRF-15:31 and AATF overexpression and siRNA-mediated knockdown of AATF. Reduced expression of tRF-15:31 was observed in both STZ-induced DKD mice and HG-treated renal mesangial cells and was associated with aggravated intrarenal inflammation and oxidative stress. Overexpression of tRF-15:31 in diabetic mice significantly reduced serum creatinine levels and 24-h urinary protein excretion and alleviated renal pathological injury. Both in vivo and in vitro, tRF-15:31 overexpression markedly downregulated pro-inflammatory and oxidative stress markers, including IL-6, MCP-1, TNF-α, and malondialdehyde (MDA), while upregulating antioxidant factors such as glutathione (GSH) and glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4). AATF expression was significantly elevated in STZ-induced DKD mice, whereas this upregulation was markedly suppressed by tRF-15:31 overexpression. In HG-treated mesangial cells, co-overexpression of tRF-15:31 and AATF reversed the protective effects of tRF-15:31 overexpression alone. Furthermore, siRNA-mediated knockdown of AATF significantly attenuated HG-induced inflammation and oxidative stress. Collectively, these findings suggest that tRF-15:31 attenuates inflammation and oxidative stress in the STZ-induced DKD model, at least in part through regulation of AATF expression. These findings provide additional mechanistic evidence for tRF-mediated regulation in DKD and support further investigation of the biological significance of the tRF-15:31-AATF regulatory relationship.

papers.title: Management of Heart transplant recipients for the non Heart Transplant health care provider. A Clinical Consensus Statement of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC.
papers.abstract: Heart transplantation (HTx) remains the gold standard treatment for selected patients with advanced heart failure and survival after transplantation has substantially improved over recent decades. As a consequence, the number of long-term HTx recipients continues to increase, and these patients are now frequently encountered in routine practice outside specialized transplant centers. Their management remains complex due to the use of chronic immunosuppression, transplant-specific complications, and a growing burden of comorbidities in the perspective of increasing longevity. Non-transplant cardiologists, general practitioners, and other healthcare professionals are therefore increasingly involved in their care but often have limited experience of post-transplant management. This clinical consensus statement from the Heart Failure Association (HFA) and the Association of Cardiovascular Nursing & Allied Professions (ACNAP) of the ESC provides practical support and a structured framework for healthcare providers involved in the care of HTx recipients outside dedicated transplant centers. The document reviews key aspects of post-transplant management, including outlining principles of care according to time from transplantation, essential knowledge around immunosuppressive therapy and drug monitoring, recognition and initial management of rejection, infection prophylaxis and treatment, and surveillance of long-term complications such as cardiac allograft vasculopathy, malignancy, chronic kidney disease, and metabolic disorders. In addition, specific clinical situations frequently encountered in practice-including fertility and pregnancy, non-cardiac surgery, rehabilitation, and palliative care-are discussed. Particular emphasis is placed on the organization of shared-care models between transplant centers and community providers and on identifying clinical scenarios requiring early referral. Through providing practical recommendations and a structured framework for follow-up, this document aims to support non-specialist clinicians in the safe management of HTx recipients and to facilitate timely collaboration with transplant centers.

papers.title: Chronic kidney disease as a systemic disorder: filtration phenotypes, inflammation and cardiovascular risk in the cardio-kidney metabolic era.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder driven by metabolic dysfunction, vascular injury, inflammation, and emerging filtration phenotypes. In the cardio-kidney-metabolic (CKM) era, renal biomarkers such as estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) and albuminuria provide essential insight into early metabolic-renal stress and cardiovascular (CV) vulnerability. This narrative review synthesizes contemporary evidence linking CKD to cardiovascular disease (CVD), emphasizing the multidimensional interactions among filtration impairment, glomerular barrier injury, metabolic dysfunction, and inflammatory pathways. Novel filtration phenotypes defined through creatinine-cystatin C (Cr-CysC) eGFR (including glomerular hyperfiltration and selective hypofiltration) highlight the limitations of classical staging and underscore the need for refined risk assessment. The integration of kidney markers into the AHA PREVENT equations represents a major advance, enabling absolute CVD risk estimation across the CKM continuum. Simulation-based analyses of 5000 virtual patients visually demonstrate the nonlinear and synergistic effects of eGFR, albuminuria, age, hypertension, diabetes, and lipid abnormalities on CV risk. Furthermore, disease-modifying therapies such as SGLT2 inhibitors, finerenone, GLP-1 receptor agonists, and anti-obesity interventions provide multisystem benefits that align with CKM pathophysiology.
