Together, these developments support a unified, continuum-based approach to CKD detection, risk stratification, and prevention, positioning CKD as a central driver of long-term CV outcomes.

papers.title: Phytodiab® in subjects with metabolic syndrome and early type 2 diabetes: a 12-week observational registry study.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes associated with increased weight is a common metabolic condition that may progress to chronic disease. This pilot observational registry evaluated the effects of Phytodiab ® , a multi-component natural extract formulation, on metabolic and oxidative parameters in subjects with mild-to-moderate type 2 diabetes managed with diet and lifestyle measures. Sixty adults with type 2 diabetes, moderately overweight, without diabetic complications and not receiving pharmacological treatment, were included. Subjects followed standard lifestyle management (SM) alone (N.=30) or Phytodiab ® plus SM once daily before the main meal (N.=30) for 12 weeks. Outcomes included body weight, fat mass, fasting glucose, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and plasma oxidative stress measured in Carr units. Safety, tolerability, compliance, and routine blood parameters were monitored. The two groups were comparable at baseline for age, sex distribution, and clinical profile. There were no dropouts and no tolerability problems. Compliance was high, with 96% of tablets correctly used. At 12 weeks, subjects receiving Phytodiab ® showed significant reductions in weight, fat mass, fasting glucose, HbA1c, and oxidative stress compared with controls (P<0.05). Routine laboratory parameters, including kidney and liver function, blood count, coagulation, and platelet activity, remained normal and unchanged. In this 12-week observational registry, Phytodiab ® plus SM was well tolerated and associated with improvements in metabolic and oxidative parameters in otherwise healthy subjects with mild-to-moderate type 2 diabetes managed with lifestyle measures. These findings are exploratory and support further controlled evaluations in larger populations.

papers.title: Epimeric Vitamin D is Not Associated With Arterial Stiffness or Cardiovascular Outcomes in Patients With Advanced CKD.
papers.abstract: 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 , an epimeric form of 25(OH)D 3 generated by C-3 epimerization, declines with advancing chronic kidney disease (CKD), yet its role in vascular health and related outcomes remains largely unknown. We aimed to determine whether circulating 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 levels are associated with arterial stiffness and longitudinal cardiovascular (CV) outcomes in advanced CKD (stages 5 and 5D). A prospective observational study. A total of 270 patients with advanced CKD using the Cambridge Coventry Vascular cohort. Baseline 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 measured by liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry. Arterial stiffness was assessed by carotid-femoral pulse wave velocity (PWV) and augmentation index (AIx75). Longitudinal outcomes included a composite of major CV events and all-cause mortality. Baseline 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 was categorized into quartiles. Associations were assessed using multivariable regression adjusted for age, race, and dialysis status. Kaplan-Meier and Cox models assessed longitudinal outcomes. Among 270 participants, quartiles were Q1 < 0.30 ng/mL (n = 64), Q2: 0.30-0.456 ng/mL (n = 71), Q3: 0.457-0.729 ng/mL (n = 68), and Q4 ≥ 0.73 ng/mL (n = 67). Strata were similar in age (44.9 years), sex, and BMI (all P > 0.05). Race differed by quartile ( P < 0.001); 87.4% were White. 24.8% were pre-dialytic, 61.1% treated with hemodialysis, and 14.1% treated with peritoneal dialysis. Arterial stiffness was similar across quartiles (AIx75 ∼20-21%, P = 0.99; PWV: 7.8-8.0 m/s, P = 0.94). 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 showed no association with AIx75 or PWV before or after adjustment using multiple regression modeling. Over 9.3 years, 115 composite events occurred (97 CV events, 18 deaths). Kaplan-Meier analysis did not discriminate risk across 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 quartiles for the composite outcome (log-rank P = 0.23), and adjusted Cox models showed no association. Observational design with possible residual confounding. In advanced CKD, 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 showed no independent association with arterial stiffness or CV events and mortality. Further studies are needed to determine the role of epimeric vitamin D in patients with CKD. Patients with advanced chronic kidney disease (CKD) have a high burden of cardiovascular disease. Alterations in vitamin D metabolism frequently occur in CKD, including reduced levels of 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 , an epimeric form of vitamin D. However, its relationship with vascular health and cardiovascular outcomes is still not well understood. In this study, we evaluated 270 patients with advanced CKD to investigate whether circulating 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 levels were associated with arterial stiffness, cardiovascular events, and mortality. Arterial stiffness was assessed using pulse wave velocity and augmentation index, and participants were followed for more than 9 years. We observed no association between 3-epi-25(OH)D 3 and arterial stiffness, cardiovascular events, or mortality. Further studies are needed to clarify the role of epimeric vitamin D in CKD.

papers.title: Triglyceride- Glucose Index Strongly Predicts Dysglycemia in First-Degree Relatives of People with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus: A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: First-degree relatives (FDRs) of people with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at substantially increased risk of dysglycemia. However, practical approaches for early risk stratification to dysglycemia remain limited. To determine the long-term incidence of dysglycemia and identify baseline metabolic predictors of progression to dysglycemia among normoglycemic FDRs of people with T2DM. A total of 169 normoglycemic first-degree relatives of patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus were included in this retrospective cohort study. All participants were recruited through the Clinical Research Unit of the Endocrine Research Center, Institute of Endocrinology and Metabolism, Tehran, Iran. Baseline evaluation included anthropometric measures, fasting and 2-hour post-load plasma glucose, HbA1c, lipid profile, insulin-related indices, renal parameters, and lifestyle factors. Dysglycemia was defined as progression to prediabetes or diabetes during follow-up. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression, and predictive performance was assessed by receiver operating characteristic analysis. The study included 169 participants with a mean age of 42.94±10.46 years at baseline. During a median follow-up of 7.1 years, 144 (85.2%) participants developed dysglycemia, including 129 (76.3%) who progressed to prediabetes and 15 (8.9%) who developed diabetes. In adjusted analyses, baseline triglyceride-glucose index and 2-hour post-load plasma glucose were independently associated with progression to dysglycemia. One standard deviation (0.25) increase in the triglyceride-glucose index was associated with 84% higher odds of dysglycemia (standardized odds ratio 1.84 (1.10-3.09); P = 0.020), while a comparable increase in 2-hour glucose was associated with 70 % higher odds (standardized odds ratio 1.70 (1.05-2.76); P = 0.031). The triglyceride-glucose index demonstrated modest discriminative ability, with an optimal cut-off value of 4.42. Normoglycemic first-degree relatives of people with type 2 diabetes mellitus experience a high incidence of early glycemic deterioration. Triglyceride-glucose index and 2-hour post-load glucose are the main risk factors, supporting their integration into risk-based screening strategies in order to enable earlier, targeted prevention in high-risk populations.

papers.title: Lactate as a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target in cardiopulmonary bypass-associated acute kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Elevated lactate is a common metabolic perturbation following cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB). This study evaluates the clinical predictive value of lactate and explores its mechanism involving protein lactylation. Machine learning (ML) algorithms applied to multicenter intensive care databases identified preoperative lactate as a dominant predictor of CPB-acute kidney injury (AKI) risk. To validate these predictions biologically, rat CPB and cellular models were utilized. Experimental results demonstrated that CPB induces glycolytic reprogramming, lactate accumulation, and elevated pan-lysine lactylation. Inhibiting the production of lactate was associated with decreased protein lactylation, lower oxidative stress, and reduced local tissue inflammation, thereby mitigating renal injury. Collectively, our interpretable ML predictive models identify lactate as a top clinical predictor of CPB-AKI, while our experimental data establish the lactate-lactylation axis as a potential mechanistic pathway linking metabolic dysfunction to renal damage. This axis represents a candidate therapeutic target requiring further validation.

papers.title: No lysine? No problem: the surprising roles of WNK kinases in physiology and disease.
papers.abstract: WNK (With No lysine K) protein kinases gained early attention because gain-of-function mutations in genes encoding two of them cause hypertension. They differ from other kinases due to the unusual location of the catalytic lysine, hence the name WNK. These kinases control many aspects of ion transport in the kidney and are essential for development and maintenance of the cardiovascular system. In the present review, we describe WNK proteins and selected substrates, in particular, the kinases oxidative stress-responsive kinase 1 and SPS1-related proline/alanine-rich kinase, and their regulation. We spotlight findings that emphasize the broad relevance of WNKs in normal physiology and disease. Our overview focuses on basic aspects of ion transport that occur in many cell types and tissues, functions in the endothelial system, interactions with insulin-dependent and metabolic pathways, the importance in the brain in part through controlling chloride ion balance, and the whirlwind of findings in cancer that reveal how WNK signaling can be repurposed. Other actions that may be of equal importance, e.g., influences on the immune system, are touched on only briefly. We also note a few genome-wide association studies that have uncovered multiple SNPs in genes encoding WNKs and downstream effectors in an array of diseases, in anticipation of more to come in the future.

papers.title: Endocrine and systemic toxicity of pyriproxyfen in adult female zebrafish: disruption of the HPT axis and peripheral organ impairments.
papers.abstract: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) can destabilize the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis, a fundamental regulator of vertebrate development and metabolism. Pyriproxyfen (PPF), a juvenile hormone analog widely utilized in vector control, is recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) for application at concentrations of up to 10 µg/L in drinking water; however, its safety profile for vertebrates remains a matter of concern. In this study, we investigated the endocrine and systemic impacts of PPF in adult female zebrafish exposed for 14 days to 1, 10, or 100 µg/L. Histological, hormonal, and transcriptional analyses across the thyroid, brain, liver, and kidney revealed a non-monotonic response centered on the WHO reference application concentration. The 10 µg/L group exhibited the most significant molecular impairment in the thyroid, characterized by the upregulation of slc5a5 (nis), nkx2.1, pax2a, and tshr, while repressing thyroglobulin (tg) expression. Consistent with these molecular alterations, thyroid epithelial disruption was observed at 1 and 10 µg/L. In contrast, exposure to 100 µg/L increased plasma TSH levels and the expression of pituitary tshb and hepatic dio1, suggesting a compensatory response of the HPT axis. Renal morphometry additionally revealed tubular alterations across all exposure groups. Overall, these findings demonstrate a non-monotonic concentration-response centered on 10 µg/L as a key mechanistic feature of PPF toxicity and support further evaluation of thyroid and renal endpoints in ecotoxicological risk assessment.

papers.title: Hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness in patients with gout: a controlled cross-sectional elastography study.
papers.abstract: Gout shares cardiometabolic risk factors with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We aimed to compare elastography-defined hepatic steatosis and liver stiffness between patients with gout and metabolically stringent controls, and to identify independent determinants of controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) and liver stiffness measurement (LSM). In this single-center cross-sectional study (April 2024-January 2026), 201 adults with gout and 80 controls free of hypertension, diabetes mellitus, chronic kidney disease, and coronary artery disease underwent vibration-controlled transient elastography (FibroScan®). Multivariable linear and logistic regression models identified independent predictors of CAP, LSM, and binary elastographic outcomes. Patients with gout had significantly higher CAP (279 vs. 251.5 dB/m; p < 0.001) and LSM (6.1 vs. 5.1 kPa; p < 0.001). In unadjusted analyses, the odds of hepatic steatosis (CAP ≥ 238 dB/m; OR 2.42, 95% CI 1.40-4.20; p = 0.001) and of increased liver stiffness (LSM ≥ 7.0 kPa; OR 2.46, 95% CI 1.27-4.78; p = 0.007) were higher in the gout group, and LSM ≥ 9.6 kPa was more frequent (12.9% vs. 1.3%; p = 0.001). On multivariable analysis, BMI and ALT were the principal determinants of CAP, whereas BMI and age independently predicted continuous LSM. Gout status was not independently associated with CAP, continuous LSM, hepatic steatosis, or increased liver stiffness (adjusted OR 1.83, 95% CI 0.84-4.01; p = 0.131). Serum uric acid and disease activity measures were not associated with any elastographic outcome. Patients with gout exhibit a substantially higher burden of elastography-defined hepatic steatosis and increased liver stiffness than metabolically stringent controls. This excess was accounted for by adiposity and age rather than by gout status or urate levels, suggesting that non-invasive liver assessment in gout should be guided by cardiometabolic risk profile rather than by the diagnosis of gout itself. Key Points • In unadjusted analyses, patients with gout had more than twofold higher odds of both hepatic steatosis and increased liver stiffness on transient elastography compared with metabolically stringent controls. • BMI and ALT were the strongest independent determinants of CAP; BMI and age were the strongest determinants of continuous LSM. • After adjustment for age, BMI and cardiometabolic covariates, gout status was not independently associated with any elastographic outcome, including increased liver stiffness (LSM ≥ 7.0 kPa). • Serum uric acid, disease activity scores, and urate-lowering or anti-inflammatory therapies were not associated with elastographic liver measures, indicating that hepatic involvement in gout reflects adiposity-driven metabolic burden rather than urate-specific mechanisms.

papers.title: Emerging therapeutic role of cinnamic acid derivatives in hyperuricemia and gout: mechanistic, translational, and pharmacological perspectives.
papers.abstract: Hyperuricemia and gout are increasingly common metabolic and inflammatory disorders characterized by excessive accumulation of uric acid, impaired urate excretion, oxidative stress, and monosodium urate crystal inflammation. Although currently available therapies such as xanthine oxidase inhibitors and uricosuric agents effectively reduce serum levels of uric acid, their long-term clinical use is often associated with adverse reactions, limited tolerability, and incomplete disease management. As a result, there is increasing interest in identifying natural compounds that may serve as a potential preclinical lead for the development of more targeted urate-lowering strategies. Cinnamic acid derivatives, including p-coumaric acid, caffeic acid, ferulic acid, sinapic acid, chlorogenic acid, and synthetic analogs such as 4-nitrocinnamic acid, have shown promising anti-hyperuricemic and anti-gout activities in experimental studies. These compounds have pharmacological effects through several mechanisms, including the inhibition of xanthine oxidase; modulation of urate transporters such as URAT1, GLUT9, and ABCG2; suppression of inflammatory pathways including NF-κB and NLRP3 inflammasome signalling; antioxidant activity; and protection against renal injuries induced by uric acid. This review summarizes the molecular mechanisms, pharmacological evidence, and structure-activity relationships of selected cinnamic acid derivatives related to hyperuricemia and gout management. In addition, it discusses translational challenges associated with bioavailability, pharmacokinetics, toxicity evaluation, and clinical validation. Collectively, cinnamic acid derivatives represent promising pre-clinical leads that warrant further preclinical and clinical investigations to develop safer and more effective therapies against hyperuricemia and gout.

papers.title: Correction to "Multi-Omics Integration Identifies a Five-Gene Metabolic Signature With Experimental Validation in Clear Cell Renal Cell Carcinoma".
Dysregulation of Orexin-A and Implications for Renal Function Assessment in Chronic Kidney Disease.
papers.abstract: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a long-standing kidney condition in which the kidneys are gradually damaged. It usually has multiple symptoms and is often accompanied by complications, such as hormonal imbalances, high blood pressure, anemia, and sleep disorders. Orexin, occasionally mentioned as hypocretin, is a neuropeptide that is mostly generated by orexin-containing neurons in the hypothalamus. Their receptors are found in a variety of tissues, such as the brain and kidney. This study aims to evaluate the impact of renal function on orexin-A levels in CKD. The study included 44 adult patients diagnosed with CKD, and their results were compared with 44 healthy participants of the same age and sex. An enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay kit was used to measure orexin-A, while urea, creatinine, and lipid profile were measured using spectrophotometric methods. Association with orexin-A was performed using Pearson's correlation analysis. The results showed a significant decrease in serum orexin-A (P < 0.001) in patients with CKD. Correlation analysis showed that orexin-A in CKD patients was positively correlated with serum creatinine (r = 0.353, P = 0.018) and high-density lipoprotein (r = 0.354, P = 0.017), while negatively correlated with glomerular filtration rate (GFR) (r = -0.424, P = 0.004). Orexin-A levels decreased in patients with CKD, and this decrease reflects the disruption of the orexin system, which was inversely related to the GFR and directly related to creatinine and high-density lipoprotein levels. Résumé Contexte: La maladie rénale chronique (MRC) est une affection rénale chronique caractérisée par une détérioration progressive de la fonction rénale. Elle est généralement associée à diverses manifestations cliniques et complications, notamment des troubles hormonaux, l’hypertension artérielle, l’anémie et les troubles du sommeil. L’orexine-A, également appelée hypocrétine-A, est un neuropeptide principalement produit par les neurones orexinergiques de l’hypothalamus. Ses récepteurs sont exprimés dans différents tissus, notamment au niveau du cerveau et des reins. Cette étude visait à évaluer l’impact de la fonction rénale sur les concentrations sériques d’orexine-A chez les patients atteints de MRC. Matériels et Méthodes: L’étude a inclus 44 patients adultes atteints de MRC, dont les résultats ont été comparés à ceux de 44 sujets sains appariés selon l’âge et le sexe. Les concentrations sériques d’orexine-A ont été déterminées à l’aide d’un kit immuno-enzymatique (ELISA), tandis que l’urée, la créatinine et le profil lipidique ont été dosés par des méthodes spectrophotométriques. Le coefficient de corrélation de Pearson a été utilisé pour évaluer les associations entre les concentrations d’orexine-A et les paramètres étudiés. Résultats: Les résultats ont montré une diminution significative des concentrations sériques d’orexine-A chez les patients atteints de MRC par rapport aux sujets sains (P < 0.001). Chez les patients atteints de MRC, l’analyse de corrélation a révélé une corrélation positive entre les concentrations d’orexine-A et la créatinine sérique (r = 0.353; P = 0.018), ainsi qu’avec les lipoprotéines de haute densité (HDL) (r = 0.354; P = 0.017). En revanche, une corrélation négative a été observée entre les concentrations d’orexine-A et le débit de filtration glomérulaire (DFG) (r = −0.424; P = 0.004). Conclusions: Les concentrations sériques d’orexine-A sont significativement diminuées chez les patients atteints de MRC. Elles présentent une association inverse avec le DFG et des associations directes avec les concentrations sériques de créatinine et de HDL. Ces résultats suggèrent une implication potentielle du système orexinergique dans les altérations associées à la MRC.

papers.title: Network Analysis of Chronic Disease Diagnosis Co-documentation in Insurance Claims Among Older Arkansans.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity among older adults presents growing clinical and economic challenges, particularly in medically underserved states such as Arkansas. However, it remains unclear whether chronic conditions documented in routine healthcare encounters exhibit structured patterns of diagnosis co-documentation or primarily reflect incidental co-documentation. Understanding these patterns may inform future studies of multimorbidity and healthcare utilization. To characterize statewide, sex-stratified patterns of claim-level diagnosis co-documentation among Arkansas adults aged ≥65 years using administrative claims data. We analyzed 2024 IQVIA administrative claims for Arkansas residents aged ≥65 years (1,408,707 claims from 35,253 unique patients). Analyses were conducted at the claim level; therefore, individuals could contribute multiple claims, and results reflect utilization-weighted diagnosis co-documentation rather than patient-level disease prevalence or multimorbidity. Twenty-five chronic condition categories were defined using ICD-10-CM codes. Pairwise diagnosis co-documentation was quantified using Lewontin's standardized disequilibrium coefficient (D'), which compares observed joint documentation with the expectation under statistical independence. Sex-stratified D' matrices, disease connectedness metrics, and hierarchical clustering were used to characterize patterns of diagnosis co-documentation. Hypertension was the most frequently documented chronic condition among claims for both females (22.2%) and males (23.7%) and exhibited the highest positive connectedness in both sex-stratified analyses. Among females, the strongest diagnosis co-documentation patterns involved hypertension with dyslipidemia, coronary artery disease (CAD), obesity, thyroid disorders, and heart failure (D' = 0.46-0.69). Among males, the strongest diagnosis co-documentation patterns involved hypertension with dyslipidemia (D' = 0.73), obesity (D' = 0.64), CAD (D' = 0.57), and thyroid disorders (D' = 0.56). Females demonstrated relatively greater diagnosis co-documentation among musculoskeletal, endocrine, and mental health conditions, whereas males showed more concentrated diagnosis co-documentation among cardiometabolic and organ dysfunction conditions. Negative D' values identified disease pairs that were infrequently co-documented within the same claims (e.g., autoimmune disease-chronic gastrointestinal disease among males, D' = -1.00), reflecting absent or infrequent claim-level joint documentation. In this claim-level analysis of Arkansas adults aged ≥65 years represented in the IQVIA administrative claims database, diagnosis co-documentation exhibited structured, sex-specific patterns, with hypertension demonstrating the highest positive connectedness among the 25 chronic conditions. These utilization-weighted findings provide a descriptive basis for hypothesis generation and support future longitudinal, patient-level studies to evaluate temporal disease relationships and the potential role of cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CVRM) risk management.

papers.title: Belatacept Conversion in Simultaneous Pancreas-Kidney and Liver-Kidney Transplant Recipients: A Single-Center Feasibility Cohort and Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Calcineurin inhibitor (CNI) nephrotoxicity drives long-term kidney-function decline after simultaneous pancreas-kidney (SPK) and liver-kidney (LK) transplantation, but belatacept conversion, as an alternative strategy, is poorly studied in these recipients, whose non-kidney allograft rejection risk differs. We retrospectively studied six SPK and six LK recipients converted from CNI- to belatacept-based immunosuppression and analyzed the cohorts separately alongside a narrative review of published SPK/LK conversion experiences. Outcomes were estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) trajectories and slopes, donor-specific antibodies (DSA) and rejection, pancreatic, hepatic and metabolic parameters, infections, and survival, reported descriptively with exploratory estimates and 95% confidence intervals (CI). Conversion occurred a median of 64 (SPK) and 89 (LK) months after transplantation, always with a transient low-dose CNI overlap (target trough 3-4 ng/ml). In SPK recipients, median eGFR rose from 45.4 to 55.5 mL/min/1.73m 2 and the median eGFR slope changed from -3.9 to +5.6 mL/min/year (mixed-model slope change +12.6, 95% CI 2.9 to 22.3); in LK recipients, from 38.8 to 46.3 and from -3.1 to +4.1 (estimate +6.3, 95% CI -4.2 to 16.7). No new DSA developed; pre-existing DSA declined or remained stable. Pancreatic and liver function stayed stable. Two infections in LK recipients (Pneumocystis pneumonia, adenovirus) were possibly belatacept-aggravated. Over a median 25 months, 8/12 (67%) remained on belatacept. Late belatacept conversion with a transient low-dose CNI overlap was feasible in selected SPK and LK recipients and was associated with stable-to-improved kidney function without a pancreatic or hepatic safety signal. The uncontrolled design supports feasibility, not efficacy.

papers.title: PBPK Modeling of Varenicline: Relating Variable Pharmacokinetics to Genomics.
papers.abstract: Varenicline is a smoking cessation drug that requires dosing over days to weeks to reach a pharmacologically effective concentration, since higher doses may result in nausea and vomiting. High interindividual variability in varenicline pharmacokinetics may also be related to these adverse effects. This study aimed to identify possible genetic causes of this variability using physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling. A mean PBPK model of varenicline with mechanistic absorption, metabolism, and renal clearance was built using four patient populations. This model was then used to simulate pharmacokinetics in 20 individuals, adjusting SLC22A2 (OCT2) transporter kinetics and physiology to fit the simulations to the observed data. The mean model included parameters for renal clearance through OCT2 (V max 0.017 mg/s/mg-trans) and reduced duodenal and jejunal absorption. This model aligned with observed data from four studies (C max and AUC fold errors 0.88-1.14). In the individual models, AUC differences were mainly accounted for by OCT2 kinetics [V max 0.004 (4.3 × decrease from the mean) to 0.035 (2.1 × increase) mg/s/mg-trans)], but 3/20 subjects (15%) with a high C max also required increased jejunal absorption. Individuals with high varenicline exposure may have reduced renal elimination due to genetic variation in SLC22A2 (OCT2), while those with higher C max may have elevated intestinal pH, giving a higher level of neutral varenicline. The effect on pH may be due to genetic variation in SLCO3A1, a bile acid transporter related to nausea after varenicline dosing.

papers.title: Endothelial dysfunction and long-term survival in cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome stages 0-3: An EASIX-based national cohort study.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTo assess the association of the endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) with all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in adults at cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic (CKM) syndrome stages 0-3.MethodsThis retrospective analysis of a population-based cohort included 10,885 adults aged ≥30 years from NHANES 1999-2018, with mortality follow-up through 2019. EASIX was calculated as lactate dehydrogenase × creatinine/platelet count. Survey-weighted Cox models, restricted cubic splines, subgroup analyses and sensitivity analyses evaluated mortality associations.ResultsDuring a median follow-up of 97 months, 1,122 participants died, including 295 from cardiovascular causes. Each one-unit increase in EASIX was associated with all-cause mortality (adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 1.41, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.24-1.61) and cardiovascular mortality (HR 1.30, 95% CI 1.13-1.49). There was no evidence of non-linearity for all-cause mortality (P = 0.466), while the cardiovascular association was non-linear (P = 0.008). Associations persisted after additional lifestyle adjustment. CKM-stage interactions were not significant in the full cohort.ConclusionsHigher EASIX was associated with greater all-cause and cardiovascular mortality in CKM stages 0-3. Its potential role in clinical risk assessment warrants further validation.

papers.title: Finerenone Use in Coenzyme Q8B-Related Focal Segmental Glomerulosclerosis.
papers.abstract: Genetic focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) caused by mutations affecting coenzyme Q (CoQ) biosynthesis is a rare podocytopathy that is associated with poor response to immunosuppression. Finerenone is a nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid antagonist that reduces oxidative stress, glomerular inflammation, and fibrosis, features seen in CoQ deficiency. We report the first case of its use in COQ8B -related FSGS. A 35-year-old woman was evaluated for persistent postpartum proteinuria and underwent a kidney biopsy that showed features of FSGS. She had a strong family history of early-onset kidney failure. She had no response to corticosteroids, tacrolimus, and empgagliflozin. Genetic testing revealed a homozygous COQ8B mutation. CoQ10 supplementation was not tolerated. Finerenone was initiated in May 2024, with significant improvement in albuminuria from 6,460 mg/g to 1,430 mg/g after 12 months and a slowing of the decline in estimated glomerular filtration rate from -9.55 mL/min/1.73 m 2 /y to -6.77 mL/min/1.73 m 2 /y. There was only mild transient hyperkalaemia. It was stopped after 12 months owing to hypotension, and by 6 months, the proteinuria increased to 4,860 mg/g and creatinine increased from 1.56 mg/dL to 2.22 mg/dL. This case suggests a potential role for finerenone as adjunctive therapy in genetic FSGS.

papers.title: Suspected Bulbar-Predominant Myasthenia Gravis Exacerbation in an Older Adult With Respiratory Deterioration and Silent Aspiration: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterized by fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness. Bulbar-predominant exacerbations may be difficult to recognize in older adults with multiple comorbidities, particularly when respiratory deterioration is initially attributed to cardiopulmonary disease. We report the case of an 83-year-old woman with generalized acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive MG, dementia with behavioral disturbance, moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), chronic kidney disease, and previous deep vein thrombosis who was admitted to a psychiatric unit because of worsening paranoia and suspected delusions. During hospitalization, she developed progressive hypoxemia requiring transfer to the medical ward. Initial evaluation considered pulmonary infection, aspiration-related complications, and COPD exacerbation. Neurological examination subsequently demonstrated new predominantly facial and bulbar weakness with preserved limb strength, accompanied by progressive dysphagia and impaired secretion clearance. Videofluoroscopic swallow study demonstrated significant silent aspiration of thin and mildly thickened liquids; however, the etiology of the dysphagia and aspiration remained potentially multifactorial. Serial arterial blood gases demonstrated persistent hypercapnia; however, stable PaCO₂ values, preserved pH, markedly elevated bicarbonate, and positive base excess suggested a substantial chronic hypercapnic component with concomitant metabolic alkalosis, with underlying COPD representing an important potential contributor. In the context of known generalized MG and newly documented facial and bulbar dysfunction, a suspected bulbar-predominant myasthenic exacerbation was considered a potentially important contributor within a multifactorial respiratory deterioration rather than the sole cause. She was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin and escalation of corticosteroid therapy. Although her respiratory status stabilized, persistent bulbar dysfunction, dysphagia, and frailty remained, and following goals-of-care discussions, the family elected hospice care. This case emphasizes the diagnostic complexity of respiratory deterioration in older patients with MG and the importance of recognizing new bulbar dysfunction while carefully considering competing pulmonary, aspiration-related, cardiogenic, and functional contributors.

papers.title: Serum Uric Acid and Disease Severity in Chronic Liver Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study of Its Association With Child-Pugh Class.
papers.abstract: Chronic liver disease (CLD) is a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with India accounting for the highest absolute number of cirrhosis-related deaths globally. Serum uric acid (SUA), the end product of purine metabolism, is increasingly recognised as a marker of oxidative stress and metabolic derangement and has been reported to be elevated in CLD. The Child-Pugh score remains the most widely used bedside tool for assessing hepatic functional reserve. Data regarding the association of SUA with Child-Pugh class and CLD-related complications in Indian tertiary care settings remain limited. The study aimed to estimate SUA levels in patients with CLD at admission, determine their association with disease severity according to Child-Pugh class, and assess their association with CLD-related complications. This cross-sectional, observational study was conducted over 18 months in the Department of General Medicine at a tertiary care teaching hospital. Ninety-two consecutive patients with CLD aged 18-65 years were enrolled. Fasting SUA, liver function tests, haemogram, and coagulation parameters were recorded, and disease severity was graded using the Child-Pugh classification. Continuous variables were compared using the independent-samples t-test or one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Bonferroni-corrected pairwise comparisons. Categorical associations were assessed using Pearson's chi-square test or Fisher's exact test, as appropriate. A two-tailed p-value <0.05 was considered statistically significant. The mean age was 47.6 years, with a male predominance (76.1%). Alcoholic liver disease was the most common aetiology (65.2%). Sixty-four (69.6%) patients had elevated SUA (>7.2 mg/dL, the cutoff applied uniformly to both sexes), with an overall mean SUA of 7.1 ± 1.9 mg/dL. Mean SUA increased progressively across Child-Pugh classes A (5.2 ± 1.1 mg/dL), B (6.9 ± 1.3 mg/dL), and C (8.4 ± 1.6 mg/dL) (ANOVA F(2,89)=37.38, p<0.001), with all pairwise comparisons significant after Bonferroni correction (all p<0.001). SUA was also significantly associated with Child-Pugh class in categorical analysis (χ²(2)=22.00, p<0.001). Patients with complications had higher mean SUA than those without complications (8.0 ± 1.5 vs. 5.6 ± 1.2 mg/dL; t(90)=8.08, p<0.001), and elevated SUA was significantly associated with any complication (χ²(1)=17.63, p<0.001). Child-Pugh class was similarly associated with complications (χ²(2)=15.68, p<0.001). Among individual complications, elevated SUA was significantly associated with hepatic encephalopathy (χ²(1)=6.15, p=0.013) but not with variceal bleeding, hepatorenal syndrome, spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, or portal hypertension (all p>0.05). Hyperuricaemia was common in this CLD cohort and was significantly associated with Child-Pugh class and the overall presence of complications. These findings support a hypothesis-generating association between SUA and disease severity rather than an established prognostic or independent role. Except for hepatic encephalopathy, SUA was not significantly associated with individual complications. Larger prospective multicentric studies adjusting for renal function and other confounders are needed before SUA can be considered a clinical adjunct marker.

papers.title: Global Landscape of Clinical Studies Open to Enrollment in Carbon Ion Radiotherapy: A PTCOG Review.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy with high linear energy transfer (LET) has shown promise for improving cancer outcomes. Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) combines charged-particle dose conformality with enhanced biological effectiveness. However, clinical development remains constrained by limited center availability, modest trial accrual, and few randomized studies. We reviewed the global landscape of CIRT studies open to enrollment to identify current priorities and gaps. This Particle Therapy Cooperative Group (PTCOG)-sanctioned project, conducted within the CIRT Guidelines Subcommittee, identified studies through registry review and institutional verification. ClinicalTrials.gov and the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials were searched from December 2025 through February 2026. We included interventional CIRT trials and prospective registries open to new enrollment and excluded studies not open to enrollment, retrospective cohorts, proton-only studies, and preclinical studies. Thirty-six studies were identified: 35 interventional trials in 6 countries and 1 North American registry-based comparative-effectiveness study. Japan had the largest share, followed by Germany, China, Italy, Austria, and France. Three centers (SPHIC, QST, and HIT) accounted for 21 of 36 studies. The portfolio included 7 phase I, 23 phase II, 5 phase III, and 1 registry study. Pancreatic cancer and sarcoma-related tumors each accounted for 7 studies; head and neck cancers, 5; prostate and breast cancers, 3 each; glioblastoma, lung cancer, and gynecologic malignancies, 2 each; and mucosal melanoma, mixed solid tumors, kidney cancer, esophageal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma, 1 each. Most studies were conducted at a single institution and emphasized feasibility, toxicity, local control, progression-free survival, or overall survival. This expert-verified inventory shows that CIRT studies open to enrollment remain concentrated by center, disease site, and phase. Future progress may depend more on shared outcome definitions, transparent biological dose reporting, and registry-enabled or multicenter comparative designs than on additional isolated single-institution studies.

papers.title: Resveratrol Pretreatment and Decabromodiphenyl Ethane-Associated Hepatorenal Changes in a High-Dose Female Mouse Model: Redox Changes and Ferroptosis-Associated Markers.
papers.abstract: Decabromodiphenyl ethane (DBDPE) is an emerging brominated flame retardant that has been detected in animal-derived foods. This exploratory experiment used a high-dose toxicological challenge rather than a dietary-exposure scenario. This study evaluated whether resveratrol (Res) pretreatment was associated with differences in selected liver- and kidney-related endpoints in a high-dose DBDPE mouse model. A total of 54 five-week-old specific pathogen-free female Kunming mice were acclimated for 7 days and allocated into six groups ( n  = 9) by weight-ranked allocation. Res (25, 50, or 100 mg/kg body weight/day; 100 mg/kg in the Res-alone group) or vehicle was administered by oral gavage 2 h before DBDPE (500 mg/kg body weight/day) or corn oil, also by gavage, for 28 consecutive days. DBDPE exposure was associated with serum biochemical alterations, descriptive liver and kidney histological changes, redox imbalance, higher iron-assay values, mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities, and changes in ferroptosis-associated markers. The liver index was 5.06% ± 0.20% in the Control group, 5.89% ± 0.60% in the DBDPE group and 5.17% ± 0.41% in the 100 mg/kg Res pretreatment group; the corresponding kidney indices were 1.02% ± 0.10%, 1.16% ± 0.07% and 1.06% ± 0.03%. Res pretreatment was accompanied by lower values for several DBDPE-associated endpoints, by changes in Pik3r1, Nfe2l2 and selected antioxidant-related transcripts, and by tissue-dependent changes in ferroptosis-associated markers. These findings provide in vivo associative evidence under the specified experimental conditions and support further evaluation of Res in DBDPE toxicology models; they do not establish ferroptotic cell death, PI3K/Nrf2 pathway activation, or relevance to typical human dietary exposure.

papers.title: Association of serum creatinine-to-albumin ratio with hyperandrogenemia and low sex hormone-binding globulin in women of reproductive age: a cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2013-2016.
papers.abstract: Hyperandrogenemia (HA) and low sex hormone-binding globulin (SHBG) are core features of polycystic ovary syndrome. The creatinine-to-albumin ratio (CAR), a simple renal-nutritional marker linked to female infertility, has not been studied in relation to HA or low SHBG. To examine the association of CAR with low SHBG and HA, defined by the free androgen index (FAI), in U.S. women of reproductive age. In this cross-sectional analysis of NHANES 2013-2016, we included 683 women aged 18-49 years. CAR (serum creatinine/albumin) was categorized into tertiles; low SHBG was defined as < 30 nmol/L and HA as FAI ≥ 75th percentile. Survey-weighted multivariable logistic regression was used, with multiple imputation (m = 5) as a sensitivity analysis. In Model 1 (age, race/ethnicity, education, income), the highest CAR tertile was associated with low SHBG (OR 2.93, 95% CI 1.49-5.75; P  = 0.003; P for trend = 0.004) and FAI-defined HA (OR 1.87, 95% CI 1.05-3.34; P  = 0.036; P for trend = 0.044). In Model 2 (plus smoking, BMI, low HDL-C), associations attenuated (OR 1.95, 95% CI 1.05-3.64 for low SHBG; 1.24, 95% CI 0.65-2.34 for HA-FAI). HA defined by total testosterone was not associated with CAR. Higher CAR was associated with low SHBG and FAI-defined HA after demographic adjustment, with attenuation after metabolic adjustment, suggesting confounding by shared metabolic factors. As CAR derives from routine laboratory tests, it may be a practical marker of reproductive metabolic risk; the cross-sectional design precludes causal inference.

papers.title: Renal tubule-specific Nrf2 deletion ameliorates diabetic kidney disease by attenuating glomerular hypertension and kidney injury in a mouse model of diabetes.
papers.abstract: We previously reported that expression of nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 (NRF2) is upregulated in the renal tubules of humans with diabetes and in mouse models of diabetes. We hypothesised that Nrf2 deletion would ameliorate renal hyperfiltration and kidney injury in Akita mice (a model of type 1 diabetes). Akita Nrf2 RT knockout (KO) mice were generated by cross-breeding tubule-specific (Pax8)-Cre mice with Akita Nrf2 floxed mice on a C57BL/6 background. Male non-diabetic control mice (Nrf2 fl/fl ), Nrf2 RT KO mice, Akita Nrf2 fl/fl mice and Akita Nrf2 RT KO mice were studied up to the age of 20 weeks (n=8 per group). The glomerular filtration rate (GFR), kidney hypertrophy, tubular injury score, glomerular basement membrane thickness, podocyte loss and foot process effacement and urinary albumin-creatinine ratio were significantly increased in Akita Nrf2 fl/fl mice and were markedly reduced in Akita Nrf2 RT KO mice compared with the corresponding control mice. Attenuation of afferent arteriole vasodilation and efferent arteriole vasoconstriction was observed in Akita Nrf2 RT KO mice compared with Akita Nrf2 fl/fl mice. Furthermore, downregulation of sodium-glucose co-transporter 2 (SGLT2) and angiotensinogen expression in renal proximal tubules was observed in Akita Nrf2 RT KO mice compared with Akita Nrf2 fl/fl mice. Treatment of Akita Nrf2 RT KO mice with a selective A1 adenosine receptor inhibitor increased GFR and fractional excretion of glucose, suggesting that enhanced adenosine signalling may contribute to the altered renal haemodynamics through tubuloglomerular feedback and reduced glomerular injury associated with RT-specific Nrf2 deletion. These findings suggest that tubular NRF2 plays an important role in the progression of diabetic kidney disease in Akita mice through modulation of the GFR and expression of SGLT2 and angiotensinogen in renal proximal tubules and tubuloglomerular feedback.

papers.title: Pharmacokinetic evidence of an abiraterone-rosuvastatin drug interaction resulting in rhabdomyolysis and acute kidney injury.
papers.abstract: Statins are among the most common causes of medication-associated rhabdomyolysis. Abiraterone, an oral androgen biosynthesis inhibitor, has been reported to increase the risk of statin-associated muscle toxicity through inhibition of hepatic transporters involved in statin disposition, potentially increasing systemic statin exposure. Despite this proposed mechanism, direct pharmacokinetic evidence of this interaction in patients experiencing this adverse event has not previously been reported. We report a case of rhabdomyolysis complicated by acute kidney injury (AKI) in a patient on long-term rosuvastatin therapy following initiation of abiraterone for the treatment of prostate cancer. Quantitative plasma analysis using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry demonstrated a rosuvastatin concentration substantially higher than concentrations observed with therapeutic dosing and consistent with previously reported toxic concentrations. This case provides pharmacokinetic support for a clinically significant abiraterone-rosuvastatin drug interaction and underscores the importance of medication review, early recognition of muscle toxicity, and consideration of alternative lipid-lowering strategies to preserve atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) risk reduction in patients being treated with abiraterone. To our knowledge, this is the first reported case demonstrating markedly elevated plasma rosuvastatin concentrations in the setting of abiraterone-associated rhabdomyolysis.

papers.title: Hyperdense Renal Lesion Characterization on Three DECT Technologies: Can Iodine Quantification Differentiate Hyperattenuating Renal Cysts From Papillary Renal Cell Cancers?
papers.abstract: To evaluate the performance of dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) in differentiation of hyperattenuating renal cysts (HCs) from papillary renal cell cancers (pRCCs) on three different DECT technologies (dual-source [dsDECT], rapid kVp-switching [rsDECT], and dual-layer detector-based [dlDECT]). In this institutional review board-approved retrospective study, we included 85 patients with a total of 108 incidental hyperdense renal lesions detected on contrast-enhanced DECT scans (dsDECT, n = 41; rsDECT, n = 42; and dlDECT, n = 25). The study cohort included HCs (n = 73) and pRCCs (n = 35). Final confirmation was obtained with histopathology for pRCCs and with magnetic resonance imaging within 6 months of the DECT for HCs. Quantitative iodine evaluation was performed with iodine concentration (IC) measured within the lesion and the abdominal aorta. Normalized IC (NIC) was generated for each lesion by normalizing the lesion IC to the aortic IC. Both IC and NIC measurements yielded significant differences between HCs and pRCCs for the dsDECT and rsDECT techniques (P < 0.001) but not for the dlDECT (P > 0.05). Cutoff values with 100% sensitivity for pRCC detection were 0.30 and 0.60 mg/mL for dsDECT and rsDECT, respectively. Normalization to the abdominal aorta allowed creation of a uniform cutoff on both technologies, with an NIC value of 0.09 allowing 100% sensitivity for each. Significant intertechnique differences exist for the differentiation of HCs from pRCCs. Normalization of IC to the aorta provides a uniform cutoff for differentiation of these lesions on dsDECT and rsDECT.

papers.title: Paeoniflorin Promotes Mitophagy Against Acute Kidney Injury via PRDX5-Dependent Inhibition of RACK1.
papers.abstract: Impaired mitophagy is a core driver of acute kidney injury (AKI), yet effective pharmacological strategies to restore this mitochondrial quality control mechanism remain limited. Paeoniflorin (Pae), a natural monoterpene glycoside, has shown renoprotective potential, but whether and how it regulates mitophagy remain unclear.. This study investigated the protective effects of Pae in mice subjected to bilateral renal ischaemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and in cisplatin-treated TCMK-1 cells, with renal tubular-specific Prdx5 conditional knockout (Prdx5-CKO) mice used to determine the requirement for PRDX5. Pae treatment dose-dependently ameliorated renal tubular injury, reduced serum creatinine and BUN levels and inflammatory cytokine expression, and restored mitochondrial DNA copy number.Mechanistically, Pae upregulated PRDX5, which interacted with and negatively regulated RACK1. PRDX5 deficiency abolished the protective effects of Pae, aggravated renal injury, and further suppressed PINK1/Parkin expression. Conversely, RACK1 overexpression suppressed PINK1/Parkin and induced cellular injury, while RACK1 knockdown restored mitophagy and alleviated cisplatin-induced damage. Critically, the renoprotective effect of Pae was strictly PRDX5-dependent, as RACK1 knockdown rescued Pae efficacy in PRDX5-deficient cells. These findings demonstrate that Pae alleviates AKI by activating PINK1/Parkin-mediated mitophagy through the PRDX5/RACK1 signalling axis, identifying PRDX5 as an indispensable therapeutic target and revealing a novel mechanism for maintaining mitochondrial homeostasis in AKI.

papers.title: The Mechanism of S-adenosylhomocysteine Hydrolase in Regulating Podocyte Apoptosis and Diabetic Nephropathy via Moap1.
papers.abstract: Elevated levels of S-adenosylhomocysteine (SAH) in patients with diabetes are closely associated with renal dysfunction. Inhibition of SAH hydrolase (SAHH) increases SAH levels, promotes apoptosis, and exacerbates streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic nephropathy. However, the precise mechanism by which SAHH inhibition induces podocyte apoptosis remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate how SAHH inhibition specifically induces podocyte apoptosis and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. We established an STZ-induced podocyte-specific SAHH knockout mouse model and an in vitro model of high-glucose-treated podocytes. Our results showed that podocyte-specific SAHH deletion significantly exacerbated streptozotocin (STZ)-induced diabetic kidney injury. SAHH inhibition significantly upregulated the expression of modulator of apoptosis 1 (Moap1), which in turn promoted podocyte apoptosis through activation of the pro-apoptotic protein BAX. Knockdown of Moap1 partially reversed this apoptotic phenotype. Mechanistically, SAHH inhibition downregulated DNA methyltransferase 3b (DNMT3b) expression, leading to hypomethylation of the Moap1 promoter and subsequent upregulation of Moap1 transcription. ChIP-qPCR and dual-luciferase reporter assays confirmed that DNMT3b directly bound to the region of the Moap1 promoter and regulated its transcriptional activity. Restoration of DNMT3b expression reversed Moap1 upregulation and partially rescued the apoptotic phenotype induced by SAHH inhibition. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that SAHH inhibition promotes podocyte apoptosis by upregulating Moap1 expression through a DNMT3b-dependent hypomethylation mechanism, which in turn activates BAX. This study provides novel potential therapeutic targets for diabetic nephropathy with elevated SAH levels.

papers.title: Nephroprotective Role of Berberine Against Chemotherapy-Induced Renal Toxicity: A Comprehensive Review.
papers.abstract: Chemotherapy-induced nephrotoxicity remains a major dose-limiting complication in cancer treatment. Accumulating evidence indicates that renal injury triggered by agents such as cisplatin, doxorubicin, methotrexate, and cyclophosphamide is primarily mediated by interconnected mechanisms including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammatory signaling, and apoptosis. Despite advances in supportive care, effective nephroprotective strategies remain limited. This review provides a comprehensive mechanistic synthesis of current preclinical evidence regarding the nephroprotective potential of berberine, a bioactive isoquinoline alkaloid. Rather than acting as a single-pathway antioxidant, berberine appears to exert pleiotropic cytoprotective effects through coordinated modulation of multiple signaling networks. These include activation of the Nrf2/Keap1 antioxidant defense system; regulation of autophagy and mitophagy via the AMPK/mTOR and PINK1/Parkin pathways; suppression of inflammatory cascades such as HMGB1/TLR4/RAGE, NF-κB, and MAPK signaling; and inhibition of mitochondrial-dependent apoptotic pathways through modulation of p53 and the Bax/Bcl-2 axis. By integrating these interconnected mechanisms, berberine restores redox homeostasis, preserves mitochondrial integrity, attenuates inflammatory amplification, and prevents tubular cell death. Collectively, the available evidence positions berberine as a promising multi-target adjunct candidate for mitigating chemotherapy-associated renal injury. However, clinical validation and pharmacokinetic optimization remain essential for translational application.

papers.title: Impact of clozapine on the proteome: A systematic review and functional analyses.
papers.abstract: Clozapine is the most effective antipsychotic for treatment-resistant schizophrenia (TRS), yet its use is limited by potentially life-threatening adverse effects including myocarditis, agranulocytosis and pneumonia. Improved mechanistic understanding may facilitate safer prescribing. We conducted the first systematic review integrating proteomic findings associated with clozapine exposure. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed, Embase and Scopus were searched for clozapine-associated proteomic studies in animal, human and cell-based models. Differentially expressed proteins were mapped to Reactome pathways using the Search Tool for the Retrieval of Interacting Genes/Proteins (STRING). Using the same approach, analyses stratified all proteins by model type and replicated proteins by exposure duration and biological system. Replicated proteins were further analysed using QIAGEN Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA). Across studies, 1070 unique proteins changed following clozapine exposure (603 increased, 394 decreased, 73 discordant). Of these, 152 were identified in ≥2 studies, with 79 showing concordant directionality. Nine were replicated in ≥3 studies with consistent direction. Overall STRING analysis identified recurrent immune/inflammatory, cellular-stress and neuronal pathway enrichment, with stratified analyses providing partial support for these and related metabolic processes across model types, exposure duration and biological system. IPA highlighted necrosis-related processes and downstream disease effects involving cardiovascular, hepatic and renal systems. These findings suggest that immune, inflammatory and regulated cell-death pathways may contribute to clozapine-associated adverse effects, although their relationship to treatment response remains unknown. Limited time series data directly compare brain and peripheral blood changes. Prospective longitudinal proteomic studies during clozapine initiation are warranted to identify early biomarkers and intervention windows.

papers.title: Nutritional management strategies post-liver transplantation: a comparative review of pediatric and adult recipients.
papers.abstract: Postoperative malnutrition occurs in 30-60% of liver transplant recipients and impairs perioperative recovery and long-term survival. Distinct malnutrition phenotypes exist across age groups, adult recipients mainly develop sarcopenia driven by sustained hypercatabolism, while pediatric counterparts suffer growth retardation and feeding dysfunction resulting from congenital cholestasis and high anabolic demands. Current studies mostly focus on short-term nutritional support, lacking age-stratified full-cycle intervention covering pre-transplant, early postoperative and long-term maintenance phases, and insufficiently summarize differentiated micronutrient supplementation schemes. This review systematically comparing pathological, metabolic, psychological and nutritional discrepancies between pediatric and adult liver transplant recipients. This review delineates age-specific requirements for macronutrients, fat- and water-soluble vitamins, and trace elements, and summarizes stratified nutritional assessment modalities, enteral and parenteral feeding regimens, and targeted interventions to counteract metabolic adverse effects induced by immunosuppressive agents. Multidisciplinary, staged individualized nutritional regimens are proposed to correct malnutrition, promote catch-up growth in children, preserve muscle mass and reduce metabolic complications in adults, providing evidence-based guidance for clinical precision nutritional management after liver transplantation.

papers.title: Endocrine determinants of MASLD: mechanisms and therapeutic targets.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately 30% of adults worldwide, yet is still framed largely as a hepatological disorder despite being driven substantially by endocrine and metabolic dysfunction. This review proposes a unified endocrine framework organised around seven hormonal axes, presenting each in terms of molecular pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and therapeutic implications. Insulin resistance is the central driver, coupling chronic caloric excess to hepatic de novo lipogenesis through selective hepatic insulin resistance, although genetic variants in PNPLA3 and TM6SF2 can uncouple steatosis from metabolic risk. Adipose tissue dysfunction contributes through adipocyte senescence, adipokine imbalance, and inflammatory adipose-liver signalling. Reduced hepatic thyroid hormone sensitivity, even in euthyroid individuals, predicts steatosis and fibrosis and underpins the first approved liver-directed therapy. Gonadal steroids exert sexually dimorphic effects, with testosterone deficiency, menopausal oestrogen loss, and polycystic ovary syndrome representing distinct risk states. Glucocorticoid dysregulation is stage-dependent, shifting from enhanced hepatic cortisol clearance in steatosis to local amplification in steatohepatitis. The gut-liver-endocrine axis, encompassing incretin, bile acid, and fibroblast growth factor signalling, has proved the most therapeutically tractable. Reduced GH/IGF-1 signalling, whether from pituitary disease or obesity-induced functional suppression, promotes both steatosis and fibrogenesis. Biological sex and life-course influences spanning developmental programming and ageing further modify these determinants. Two agents, resmetirom and semaglutide, now have US FDA accelerated approval for noncirrhotic MASH with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis, supporting the principle that correcting axis-specific endocrine dysfunction can produce measurable hepatic benefit; however, both approvals are accelerated and await confirmatory outcome data, while others remain investigational. An endocrine framework offers both a coherent account of pathogenesis and a rational basis for biomarker-guided, phenotype-targeted therapy.

papers.title: Life's Essential 8, Genetic Susceptibility, and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in Chinese Adults.
papers.abstract: Background: Limited evidence exists regarding the association of cardiovascular health (CVH) with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in Chinese adults, and the influence of genetic risk on this association remains unknown. This study aimed to investigate these associations and discern potential variations based on genetic risk. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 17,077 participants from the third resurvey of the China Kadoorie Biobank. CVH was evaluated by Life's Essential 8 (LE8), with the overall score (0 to 100) calculated as the unweighted average of its 8 component scores and categorized as low (0 to 49), moderate (50 to 79), or high (80 to 100). Polygenic risk score (PRS) for MASLD was generated by meta-analytic approach and large genome-wide association data of liver steatosis and related traits. Genetic risk for MASLD was categorized into low, intermediate, and high based on quintile of metaPRS. The multivariable logistic regression model was used to evaluate the associations of CVH with MASLD and advanced fibrosis in MASLD, subsequently stratified by metaPRS. Results: High CVH was associated with over 90% lower risk of MASLD and advanced fibrosis in MASLD, with odds ratios of 0.07 (0.06 to 0.08) and 0.04 (0.02 to 0.05) compared to low CVH, respectively. Interactions of metaPRS were observed for the impacts of LE8 on both prevalent MASLD and advanced fibrosis in MASLD ( P value for interaction <0.02 and <0.001, respectively), with stronger protective associations among individuals with higher genetic risk. Similar findings were observed when we tentatively expanded LE8 to Life's Crucial 9 (LC9), incorporating the psychological health component. Conclusion: In Chinese adults, adhering to a high CVH was associated with lower odds of prevalent MASLD and advanced fibrosis in MASLD, particularly among individuals at high genetic risk.

papers.title: Multi-omics Profiling Reveals the Effects of Xihuangcao on Hepatic Fibrosis Attenuation through Gut Microbiota and Metabolic Reprogramming.
papers.abstract: In various chronic liver diseases, hepatic fibrosis represents a frequent pathological event. This process involves the activation of hepatic stellate cells, along with the consequent excessive deposition of extracellular matrix. Emerging evidence highlights the contribution of gut microbiota dysbiosis and intestinal barrier dysfunction to its progression, underscoring the potential of targeting the liver-gut axis. Xihuangcao, a traditional Chinese medicinal herb used for acute cholecystitis and jaundice hepatitis, exhibits antifibrotic activity, but its underlying mechanisms remain unclear. In this study, hepatic fibrosis models were established to evaluate the antifibrotic effects of 3 botanical sources of Xihuangcao ( Isodon lophanthoides (Buch.-Ham. ex D.Don) H.Hara, Isodon lophanthoides var. graciliflorus (Benth.) H.Hara, and Isodon serra Kudô) through integrating histopathological, transcriptomics, metabolomics, 16S ribosomal RNA (rRNA) sequencing, and network pharmacology analyses. The results indicated that all 3 botanical sources of Xihuangcao markedly alleviated hepatic fibrosis and reduced collagen deposition. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that Xihuangcao down-regulated profibrotic mediators (Toll-like receptor 5, transforming growth factor-β, and platelet-derived growth factor) and modulated mitogen-activated protein kinase, steroid biosynthesis, bile secretion, and retinol metabolism pathways, highlighting its coordinated suppression of inflammation-driven fibrogenic activation in hepatic fibrosis. Liver metabolomics revealed Xihuangcao's effect on restoration of energy metabolism, amino acid turnover, and redox homeostasis. Xihuangcao also corrected fibrosis-induced gut dysbiosis, characterized by reduced Verrucomicrobia and increased S24-7 abundance, while suppressing pathogenic genera such as Clostridium and Prevotella . Moreover, Xihuangcao decreased profibrotic metabolites (androstan-3α,17β-diol) and suppressed choline-related metabolic pathways associated with fibrogenic signaling. Network pharmacology and experimental validation further identified PI3K/Akt inhibition as a key mechanism suppressing hepatic stellate cell activation. In summary, this study, based on integrative multi-omics analyses (metabolomics, transcriptomics, and 16S rRNA sequencing), found that Xihuangcao alleviates liver fibrosis by modulating inflammatory responses, metabolic disorders, and gut microbiota dysbiosis via the gut-liver axis. Furthermore, network pharmacology combined with in vitro experiments revealed that inhibition of hepatic stellate cell activation through the PI3K/Akt pathway may be the critical mechanism underlying its therapeutic efficacy.

papers.title: Why only 3 months? Immunological constraints on CAR-T therapy in gastrointestinal cancers.
papers.abstract: In June 2026, satri-cel/CT041, a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T-cell product targeting Claudin18.2, received approval from China's National Medical Products Administration for the treatment of Claudin18.2-positive, HER2-negative advanced gastric/gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma after failure of at least two prior lines of therapy. This marks the first CAR-T product approved worldwide for solid tumours. The approval ends the long-standing debate over whether CAR-T cells can be effective against solid malignancies, yet it simultaneously raises a more pointed issue: in its pivotal randomised controlled trial, median progression-free survival was 3.25 months (95% CI 2.86-4.53) with satri-cel against 1.77 months (95% CI 1.61-2.04) with treatment of physician's choice, giving a hazard ratio of 0.37 (95% CI 0.24-0.56). The two medians differ by 1.48 months; that figure marks where each survival distribution is cut in half and is not the benefit any individual patient can expect, and approval does not equate to a cure. Taking this as a starting point, this review systematically dissects the immunological bottlenecks that constrain CAR-T efficacy in gastrointestinal tumours. We first trace the evidence chain from phase I studies through the randomised controlled trial to exploratory adjuvant-therapy settings and then integrate the landscape of targets-Claudin18.2, glypican-3, carcinoembryonic antigen, mesothelin, and CDH17-within a target-tumour matrix encompassing gastric cancer, colorectal cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, and pancreatic cancer. The core section focuses on four intertwined immunological constraints: spatiotemporal heterogeneity and escape at the antigen level; a therapeutic window shaped jointly by epitope masking within tight junctions and immune privilege of the gastric mucosal stem cell niche-this mechanism not only explains why Claudin18.2-directed CAR-T cells exhibit an acceptable safety profile despite target expression on normal tissues but also provides a paradigm for rational selection of next-generation targets; a suppressive microenvironment composed of regulatory T cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, tumour-associated macrophages, transforming growth factor-β, adenosine, and a hypoxic and acidotic metabolic milieu; and CAR-T exhaustion driven by chronic antigen stimulation. We particularly emphasise that metabolic stress and exhaustion are not two parallel obstacles. We put forward a mechanistic model in which persistent antigen stimulation combined with intratumoral hypoxia acts as a "double hit": through mitochondrial dysfunction and reactive oxygen species accumulation, the two inputs raise nuclear factor of activated T-cell (NFAT) activity and so drive the TOX/NR4A-dominated exhaustion program. This model is assembled from chronic-infection and mouse tumour systems and has not been tested in human CAR-T cells or in satri-cel-treated patients. We advance it as a framework for organising the four bottlenecks and for explaining why single-point interventions struggle to lift the efficacy ceiling, not as a demonstrated account. On this basis, we discuss strategies such as armouring, logic gating, transcription factor engineering, gene editing, and chemokine receptor modification, along with combination regimens involving checkpoint inhibition, oncolytic viruses, locoregional administration, and microbiome modulation, and we evaluate alternative platforms including CAR-macrophages, CAR-NK cells, and in vivo CAR-T generation. The watershed has been crossed, but the work of turning 3 months into 30 has only just begun.

papers.title: Targeting hepatic CREBZF protects against atherosclerosis via exosomal miR-210-3p mediated inhibition of endothelial inflammation.
papers.abstract: Cardiovascular diseases (CVDs) continue to be the primary cause of mortality globally. Abnormal liver function has been widely recognized as an independent risk factor for atherosclerotic CVDs. However, how alterations in liver function affect distal vascular function remains largely unknown. CREBZF, a bZIP transcription factor of the CREB/ATF family, has been identified as a driver of hepatic steatosis and fibrosis. Here, we provide the first demonstration that hepatic CREBZF acts as a critical regulator driving atherosclerotic progression. In vivo , hepatic-specific deletion of CREBZF attenuates endothelial inflammation and reduces macrophage infiltration, thereby ameliorating plaque formation in both high-fat diet-fed and spontaneous atherosclerotic mouse models. In vitro , overexpression or knockdown of CREBZF in hepatocytes correspondingly promotes or attenuates endothelial inflammation. Mechanistically, hepatocyte CREBZF regulates endothelial inflammation via exosomes, an effect independent of cholesterol metabolism or of soluble cytokines. Furthermore, CREBZF dynamically modulates the expression of exosomal miR-210-3p and its subsequent levels in recipient endothelial cells. miR-210-3p, in turn, suppresses endothelial inflammation by targeting C-Rel, a component of the NF-κB transcription factor family. Importantly, the pro-inflammatory effect of exosomes derived from CREBZF-overexpressing hepatocytes on endothelial cells is abrogated by a miR-210-3p mimic. Collectively, these findings unveil a novel mechanism by which hepatic CREBZF regulates atherosclerosis through liver-vascular crosstalk mediated by the exosomal miR-210-3p/C-Rel signaling axis, suggesting a potential therapeutic strategy for atherosclerotic CVDs.

papers.title: Silybum marianum peptide-rich fraction alleviates acute liver injury by inhibiting TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB and is associated with changes in gut microbiota composition.
papers.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe and prevalent condition that can progress to irreversible liver damage and failure. This study aimed to investigate the prophylactic hepatoprotective potential of Silybum marianum peptides (SMP) in ALI and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. Using a carbon tetrachloride (CCl 4 )-induced ALI mouse model, we evaluated the dose-dependent effects of SMP. Additionally, we explored the modulatory effects of SMP on the NF-κB pathway, gut microbiota composition, and metabolite profiles. The role of SMP in the TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB signaling axis was further validated in a NIK-overexpressing Hepa1-6 cell model. Our results demonstrated that 14-day SMP administration did not significantly affect body weight, fasting blood glucose levels, or liver and spleen weights, and no significant difference in serum ALT activity was observed. Notably, SMP (200 mg/kg) significantly alleviated CCl 4 -induced liver injury, as evidenced by enhanced hepatic antioxidant capacity, reduced expression of proinflammatory cytokines, and attenuated immune cell infiltration. Furthermore, SMP was associated with changes in gut microbiota composition and community structure in CCl 4 -induced ALI mice. Mechanistically, SMP suppressed the TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB pathway. These findings highlight SMP as a promising candidate for the prevention of CCl 4 -induced ALI, acting through multimodal mechanisms involving anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and gut microbiota-associated pathways.

papers.title: Liver enzyme elevations during statin-ezetimibe therapy in ABCG2 c.421C>A variant carriers: a case series and narrative review.
papers.abstract: Statin-ezetimibe combination therapy is widely used and generally well tolerated; however, liver enzyme elevations may occur during treatment and can be difficult to interpret in patients with polypharmacy and other contributing factors. The potential role of drug-drug-gene interactions (DDGIs) in this context remains insufficiently explored. We present a series of 11 patients from the PGx-CardioDrug study, selected for documented liver enzyme elevations during statin-ezetimibe therapy that led to treatment modification and carriage of the ABCG2 c.421A allele. Clinical characteristics, treatment history, laboratory findings, and outcomes were reviewed alongside available pharmacogenetic results for genes involved in drug transport and metabolism. Available records of five additional ABCG2 c.421CA carriers with documented normal liver enzyme findings during combination therapy were reviewed for descriptive comparison. A narrative review of the literature was conducted to provide a mechanistic interpretation for the observed findings. The series included six women and five men, aged 27-78 years. Muscle symptoms and/or creatine kinase (CK) elevations were observed in six patients, including two with rhabdomyolysis requiring hospitalization. Dose reduction, drug discontinuation, or switching to alternative lipid-lowering therapy resulted in improvement of laboratory parameters in several patients. In two patients, abnormalities persisted or increased during subsequent ezetimibe monotherapy. Follow-up laboratory results were not available for all patients. Eight patients had the ABCG2 c.421CA genotype and three had c.421AA, consistent with the selection criterion. Additional findings included variants in SLCO1B1 , ABCC2 , ABCB1 , and UGT1A1 . In the five potential comparators, normal liver enzyme findings during combination therapy were supported by numerical laboratory values in three patients and clinical documentation in two. These cases illustrate the difficulty of interpreting liver enzyme elevations during statin-ezetimibe therapy in patients with concomitant medications and other contributing factors. The narrative review provides a pharmacokinetic rationale for considering DDGIs, but the case series does not establish their contribution to the observed abnormalities. Genotype-based selection, incomplete clinical data, and the small descriptive comparator group limit interpretation. These observations remain hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Abnormal lipid profiles are associated with markers of impaired fibrinolysis in patients with cirrhosis.
papers.abstract: Patients with liver cirrhosis exhibit abnormalities in lipid metabolism and in circulating proteins of clot breakdown. Recent studies have shown relationships between dyslipidemia and fibrinolytic abnormalities in noncirrhotic populations. We investigated associations between lipid profiles and fibrinolytic markers in patients with cirrhosis. This observational study analyzed samples from 147 patients with stable cirrhosis, decompensated cirrhosis, acute-on-chronic liver failure, and sepsis without pre-existing chronic liver disease, and from 38 healthy controls. We studied fibrinolysis by clot lysis time (CLT), plasminogen, plasminogen activator inhibitor-1 (PAI-1), and tissue-type plasminogen activator (tPA), and lipid profiles by apolipoproteins A1 and B, common lipoproteins, triglycerides, and total cholesterol. CLT was slightly enhanced in stable and decompensated cirrhosis, but prolonged in acute-on-chronic liver failure and sepsis. Plasminogen levels decreased, whereas PAI-1 and tPA increased with cirrhosis severity. All lipid parameters decreased with cirrhosis severity, besides triglyceride levels, which were preserved. In an analysis of all patients with cirrhosis combined, apolipoprotein A1 correlated inversely with CLT, levels of PAI-1 and tPA, and positively with plasminogen. Apolipoprotein B, low-density lipoprotein, and lipoprotein(a) correlated positively with plasminogen. Triglycerides correlated positively with CLT. Cirrhosis is characterized by decreased (apo)lipoprotein levels, preserved triglyceride levels, and a shift from enhanced to impaired fibrinolysis with increasing disease severity. Lower apolipoprotein A1 levels and higher triglyceride levels are associated with impaired fibrinolysis, which may reflect biological interactions between lipid metabolism and fibrinolysis or parallel alterations secondary to hepatic dysfunction.

papers.title: Heart Failure Risk Phenotypes Based on a 2-Dimensional Tree Structure Derived from Clinical Characteristics and Associations with Disease Prevalence and Cardiovascular Mortality in the General Population.
papers.abstract: Using the Discriminative Dimensionality Reduction Tree (DDRTree) algorithm, a 2-dimensional tree model was constructed based on conventional clinical indicators to identify heart failure (HF) risk phenotypes with different pathophysiological characteristics from the general adult population and evaluate their association with HF prevalence and cardiovascular mortality risk. A representative sample of 24 205 general US adults from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey 1999-2018 was analyzed. Eleven routine clinical indicators from multiple physiological dimensions were fed into the DDRTree algorithm to project each of them in a 2-dimensional space. The resulting tree structure revealed distinct HF risk phenotypes whose links to outcome HF prevalence and cardiovascular mortality risk were quantified with weighted logistic regression and Cox proportional-hazard models. Discriminant Dimensionality Reduction Tree identified 3 HF risk phenotypes: normal, metabolic (characterized by upregulated glucose-metabolism markers), and inflammatory (characterized by abnormalities in inflammatory and hepatic-renal markers). After fully adjusting for confounding factors, the metabolic phenotype was significantly associated with the risk of HF compared with the normal phenotype (odds ratio [OR] = 1.96, P < .001, 95% CI: 1.47-2.62), whereas it showed no significant correlation with the risk of cardiovascular death (hazard ratio [HR] = 0.92, P = .539, 95% CI: 0.70-1.20). In contrast, the inflammatory phenotype was significantly correlated with both HF risk (OR = 3.95, P < .001, 95% CI: 2.94-5.33) and cardiovascular mortality risk (HR = 1.47, P = .002, 95% CI: 1.16-1.87). This study elucidates potential risk phenotypes influencing HF and cardiovascular mortality, providing new insights for precise HF risk stratification and targeted preventive interventions in the general population.

papers.title: Excess Liver Fat in Type 2 Diabetes Stratified by Intrapancreatic Fat Deposition: A Meta-Analysis of Dual-Organ MRI Studies.
papers.abstract: Both liver fat content (LFC) and intrapancreatic fat deposition (IPFD) are frequently increased in Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
