We meta-analysed dual-organ MRI studies comparing LFC between individuals with T2DM and non-diabetic controls and explored whether study-level differences in LFC varied according to IPFD burden. Seventeen studies (2142 participants) were included. Individuals with T2DM had significantly higher LFC than non-diabetic controls (standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.89, 95% CI 0.60-1.18). In exploratory subgroup analyses, liver fat excess was larger in studies with mean IPFD ≥ 10% than in those with IPFD < 10% (SMD 1.20 vs. 0.62; p = 0.04), though this finding was not consistently retained in leave-one-out analyses. Alternative IPFD cutoffs yielded directionally similar but non-significant subgroup differences. Study-level differences in IPFD were associated with differences in LFC (β = 0.383, p = 0.006) in univariable meta-regression, but not after BMI adjustment. These findings suggest that higher IPFD is associated with greater liver fat excess in T2DM at the study level. Individual-level analyses are now warranted to clarify this relationship.

papers.title: Metal Accumulation, Liver Histopathology, and Human Health Risk Assessment Across Different Trophic Guilds in a Mining-Affected Neotropical River.
papers.abstract: Metal pollution in aquatic environments represents a recurring global concern; however, traditional paradigms often assume linear bioaccumulation patterns that may fail under catastrophic contamination scenarios. This study evaluated metal concentrations in water, sediment, and tissues of 10 fish species from different trophic guilds in the Paraopeba River after the Brumadinho dam collapse. Multivariate analyses (principal component analysis [PCA], generalized linear model [GLM], and PERMANOVA) were used to explore associations between metal concentrations, ecological traits, and body size integrated with liver histopathology (Histopathological Alteration Index) and Human Health Risk Assessment. Results revealed that metal concentrations in water and fish tissues exceeded regulatory limits, whereas sediment acted as the main reservoir of metals, exhibiting higher concentrations than water. High-severity liver damage was concentrated in benthic piscivores and benthopelagic detritivores, exposing a complex interplay between biomagnification and direct substrate contact. Human Health Risk Assessments indicated unacceptable noncarcinogenic risks driven by aluminum (Al), along with elevated carcinogenic risks for chromium (Cr) and cadmium (Cd) for both adults and children in the region analyzed. These findings demonstrate that ecological traits were associated with differences in metal accumulation, liver damage, and public health threats, reinforcing the need for nonlinear models in postdisaster regulatory frameworks.

papers.title: BRD9 Enhances Activation of Pregnane X Receptor Pathway and the Resistance of Hepatocellular Carcinoma Cells to Molecular Targeted Agents.
papers.abstract: Bromodomain-containing protein 9 (BRD9) is a newly identified oncogenic regulatory factor in multiple human malignancies, yet its precise roles in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) remain largely unknown. This study aimed to investigate the function and mechanism of BRD9 in HCC, particularly its involvement in molecular targeted drug resistance. BRD9 expression was either overexpressed or knocked down in HCC cells. PXR transcription factor activity was assessed using luciferase reporter assays, quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR), and chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP). HCC cells were treated with serial concentrations of molecularly targeted drugs. Antitumor activity was evaluated by MTT assays, colony formation assays, flow cytometry for apoptosis analysis, and subcutaneous tumor models. Drug metabolic rates were quantified using high-performance liquid chromatography (HPLC). Overexpression of BRD9 significantly enhanced the transcriptional activity of PXR and promoted the expression of PXR-dependent multidrug resistance-related genes, including CYP3A4 and ABCB1. Mechanistically, BRD9 overexpression facilitated the recruitment of PXR to the promoter and enhancer regions of CYP3A4, thereby accelerating the metabolic clearance of sorafenib in HCC cells. Functionally, enforced expression of BRD9 rendered HCC cells more resistant to molecularly targeted agents, whereas knockdown of BRD9 sensitized them to these drugs. Furthermore, combination therapy experiments demonstrated that the BRD9 smallmolecule inhibitor I-BRD9 exerted synergistic antitumor activity with sorafenib against HCC cells. These findings reveal that BRD9 mediates molecular targeted drug resistance in HCC through enhancing the transcription factor activation of PXR. This mechanism provides a potential therapeutic target for overcoming drug resistance in HCC, and the synergistic effect of IBRD9 with sorafenib suggests a promising combination strategy. BRD9 promotes resistance to molecular targeted drugs in HCC via PXR-dependent transcriptional activation. Targeting BRD9 may represent a novel approach to sensitize HCC cells to existing therapies.

papers.title: Coumarin-based Scaffolds as Multitarget Modulators of Chronic Inflammation: Insights into Inflammatory Signaling Networks.
papers.abstract: A wide range of chronic illnesses, including metabolic, autoimmune, neurodegenerative, and malignant conditions, are caused by the dysregulation of inflammation, a complex, multi-scale biological defense mechanism. Despite their clinical efficacy, current pharmacotherapies such as NSAIDs, corticosteroids, and biologics are constrained by side effects, insufficient resolution of inflammatory cascades, and poor long-term appropriateness. Interest in natural-product scaffolds with multi-target anti-inflammatory potential has increased due to these therapeutic gaps. Among these, 7-hydroxycoumarin (umbelliferone) has become a leading molecule due to its broad pharmacological spectrum, favorable safety profile, and ability to simultaneously target multiple pathogenic nodes. This review assesses how 7-hydroxycoumarin and its structural derivatives act at these biochemical and molecular intersections and offers an integrated and thorough analysis of inflammation pathways, including COX/LOX-derived eicosanoid biosynthesis, cytokine and chemokine signaling, oxidative and nitrosative stress, ECM degradation, and receptor-mediated immunomodulation. According to preclinical research, 7-hydroxycoumarin inhibits COX-2, iNOS, and MAPK/NF-κB signaling; modulates SOD/CAT/GSH to restore redox homeostasis; reduces cytokine overproduction; and protects tissues in models of oxidative stress, hepatic injury, ulcerative colitis, and inflammation associated with cancer. Its potency, stability, and pharmacokinetics have been improved by advances in synthetic approaches, hybrid design, metal-complex formation, and nanotechnology-based delivery. 7-hydroxycoumarin is positioned as a flexible, multi-target, next-generation scaffold for antiinflammatory drug development, with promising translational relevance for chronic inflammatory illnesses, according to the combined biochemical, pharmacological, and in-silico data.

papers.title: Diagnostic performance of FIB-4 in detecting advanced liver fibrosis in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis and psoriasis using methotrexate.
papers.abstract: Methotrexate is a first-line therapy for rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and psoriasis, but its long-term use has been associated with hepatic fibrosis, highlighting the need for effective screening strategies. In this context, and considering the limitations of liver biopsy as well as the high cost and limited availability of elastography, the FIB-4 score has emerged as the most widely used noninvasive screening tool. This multicenter cross-sectional study evaluated patients followed at specialized Rheumatology and Dermatology centers to assess the accuracy of FIB-4 in predicting advanced hepatic fibrosis in patients with rheumatoid arthritis, psoriatic arthritis, and psoriasis undergoing chronic methotrexate therapy. The specific objectives were to identify optimal cutoff values for FIB-4 in this population and factors associated with advanced fibrosis. Medical records, interviews, and physical examinations were used to collect demographic, clinical, laboratory, lifestyle, and treatment data, calculate age-adjusted FIB-4 scores, and assess disease activity using validated indices. Liver fibrosis and steatosis were evaluated by vibration-controlled transient elastography, and FIB-4 performance for detecting advanced fibrosis was analysed using age-stratified Receiver Operating Characteristic curves and multivariable logistic regression. A total of 172 patients were included, predominantly women, with a mean age of 58 years; rheumatoid arthritis was the most common underlying disease. Advanced fibrosis was identified by elastography in 11%. FIB-4 values increased progressively with fibrosis stage, and Receiver Operating Characteristic curve analysis identified a cutoff of 1.62 - a threshold not previously reported for methotrexate-treated patients. This cutoff demonstrated better performance in individuals younger than 65 years (Area Under the Curve = 0.68 versus 0.64 in those aged 65 years or older) and showed particular utility for ruling out advanced fibrosis. In multivariable analysis, a high-risk FIB-4 category, obesity, diabetes mellitus, and advanced hepatic steatosis were independently associated with advanced fibrosis, whereas inflammatory disease activity and cumulative methotrexate dose were not. FIB-4 is an accessible and potentially useful tool for ruling out advanced hepatic fibrosis in methotrexate-treated patients younger than 65 years, demonstrating reasonable performance in this population. Advanced fibrosis is primarily driven by metabolic factors rather than methotrexate exposure or inflammatory disease activity.

papers.title: Diagnostic value of CT-quantified abdominal fat parameters for metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease.
papers.abstract: To analyze the diagnostic value of CT-derived abdominal fat indices in predicting MAFLD and establish an integrated diagnostic system. A retrospective study on 174 patients with a previous history of abdominal CT examination in our institute between January 2022 and June 2024 was conducted, comprising 120 diagnosed with MAFLD, and 54 controls without it. CT-derived measures including SAT, visceral adipose tissue volume(VAT), total liver volume, and average hepatic. The average value and CT attenuation value of the left and right lobe of liver and the VAT/SAT were compared using Mann-Whitney U test. were compared between both groups. Then, we used Spearman's rank correlation analysis to study whether there existed correlations between CT metrics and metabolic indicators. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic(ROC)curve analysis were utilized to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of individual parameters.Calibration of a composite prediction model was evaluated by using calibration plots. In MAFLD groups, SAT, VAT, liver volume, and the VAT / SAT ratio were higher than those of the control group, while the mean hepatic CT attenuation value, as well as the mean attenuation value of the left lobe and right lobe, were all lower than those of the control group (all P < 0.05). The mean hepatic CT attenuation correlated negatively with BMI (r = -0.607) and TG (r = -0.418), while the sign was positive for VAT. In univariate logistic regression, we found that the mean hepatic CT attenuation is the best diagnostic indicator of MAFLD, with an AUC of 0.923, then were left and right hepatic attenuation (AUC = 0.886), liver volume (AUC = 0.814), and VAT's mean CT attenuation (AUC = 0.796). BMI (r = 0.554) and UA (r = 0.362) were also considered. Combining SAT, VAT, and mean hepatic CT attenuation together in one model resulted in an AUC of 0.928 (sensitivity: 91.7%, specificity: 85.2%). The calibration curves demonstrated an acceptable fit of the model. When multiple variables were combined, the sensitivity improved from 85.8% to 91.7% and specificity changed from 87.0% to 85.2%, yielding an AUC of 0.928 (ΔAUC = 0.005 compared with mean hepatic CT attenuation alone, P = 0.62). CT-measured abdominal fat may represent a reliable and noninvasive approach for the diagnosis of MAFLD.The greatest individual diagnostic utility was exhibited by mean liver CT attenuation alone; however, with multiple variables merged into a combined model, the sensitivity and specificity were also further increased, which could be an effective method to image MAFLD in clinical diagnosis.

papers.title: An incidental heterozygous ATP7B nonsense variant leading to a diagnostic pitfall for Wilson disease: a pediatric case report.
papers.abstract: Wilson disease (WD) is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by pathogenic variants in ATP7B, resulting in impaired copper transport and progressive copper accumulation, most prominently affecting the liver. With the growing use of genetic testing, incidental detection of ATP7B pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in individuals without typical hepatic phenotypes can prompt overdiagnosis and unnecessary investigations. This case highlights the importance of interpreting a single heterozygous ATP7B variant in the context of phenotype and a standardized biochemical diagnostic pathway for WD. A 13-year-old Han Chinese boy presented with recurrent brief paroxysmal attacks for > 1 year, markedly worsened over the preceding month. Episodes were triggered by rising from sitting, characterized by transient postural instability with unilateral head deviation and ipsilateral dystonic/choreiform movements, lasted ~ 10 s, and resolved spontaneously. Consciousness was preserved, with no incontinence, convulsions, or postictal symptoms. Interictal neurological examination was normal. Ambulatory EEG monitoring captured three typical attacks without epileptiform discharges or ictal EEG correlates, and brain MRI was unremarkable. A slit-lamp examination revealed no Kayser-Fleischer ring. A low serum copper level (9.43 µmol/L; reference 10.50-29.90) prompted further evaluation; genetic testing incidentally identified a heterozygous ATP7B variant (NM_000053.4:c.2851 C > T; p.Gln951Ter), reported as likely pathogenic. WD was considered. However, ceruloplasmin was normal (231.6 mg/L; reference 200.0-420.0 mg/L), ceruloplasmin oxidase activity measured by the p-phenylenediamine method was normal (0.372 OD; reference > 0.200 OD), liver biochemistry was normal (ALT 11 U/L, AST 16 U/L, GGT 14 U/L; bilirubin within reference range), and abdominal ultrasound showed a normal liver and biliary tree. Crucially, a follow-up quantitative 24-hour urinary copper test was strictly normal, and parental segregation analysis confirmed that the ATP7B variant represented a paternally inherited heterozygous state without biochemical evidence of Wilson disease, making active Wilson disease highly unlikely. This case illustrates a critical diagnostic pitfall: incidental heterozygous ATP7B variants can trigger severe diagnostic anchoring bias. To prevent overdiagnosis, genetic findings must be subordinated to strict phenotype-driven evaluations, formal Leipzig scoring, and definitive biochemical gold standards.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal metabolic networks in a preclinical model of pancreatic cancer and associated cachexia.
papers.abstract: Cachexia or body wasting is a significant contributing factor to the morbidity and mortality of pancreatic cancer. Despite an unmet need, its metabolic underpinnings remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize a mouse model that recaptures the longitudinal progression of human cachexia during pancreatic cancer development. We profile the metabolomes of pre-, early- and late-stage cancer-associated cachexia in male and female pancreas, its interstitial fluid (IF), plasma, liver, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. We find that each tissue has a unique metabolome and trajectory across stages and reveal a marked lipid enrichment in the tumor IF. Using mathematical modeling, we identify metabolites participating in cross-tissue networks and in vivo validate a lactate-glucose conversion. We find systemic metabolic changes prior to weight loss and use feature selection algorithms to identify early detection markers. Our study provides a resource for system-wide metabolic evolution of pancreatic cancer and associated cachexia, highlighting the potential for timely diagnostics and interventions.

papers.title: Incremental reach of 30-year PREVENT-ASCVD risk assessment in adults with MASLD and low 10-year risk: population implications of the 2026 dyslipidemia guideline.
papers.abstract: Low 10-year ASCVD risk can coexist with substantial long-horizon risk in younger adults. The 2026 dyslipidemia guideline introduced 30-year PREVENT-ASCVD risk ≥10% as a criterion for considering moderate-intensity statin therapy in adults aged 30-59 years with 10-year risk <3%. We aimed to quantify the population scale and incremental classification reach of this criterion among U.S. adults with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). We analyzed NHANES 2017-March 2020 and August 2021-August 2023 as independent complex surveys. Adults aged 30-59 years with VCTE-defined operational MASLD, no clinical ASCVD, no lipid-lowering therapy, LDL-C 70-189 mg/dL, no observable automatic-treatment indication, and 10-year PREVENT-ASCVD risk <3% were included. G1 was defined as 30-year risk ≥10% with LDL-C <160 mg/dL. The complete primary cores included 529 and 303 participants. G1 prevalence was 33.3% and 27.9%, representing 5.85 and 4.50 million U.S. adults. Among participants leaving G0 through either the long-horizon or LDL-C 160-189 mg/dL criterion, 85.7% and 75.1% were identified uniquely by 30-year risk. In the broader operational MASLD pathway, G1 accounted for 15.8% and 13.9% of the weighted distribution and was more concentrated than in confirmed non-MASLD. Findings were stable across alternative specifications and neighboring thresholds. Among adults with operational MASLD who remained at low 10-year ASCVD risk, the 30-year PREVENT criterion identified a substantial population not captured by the parallel LDL-C 160-189 mg/dL pathway and accounted for most downstream classification beyond G0. These findings define the disease-specific population reach of long-horizon risk assessment in MASLD. Not applicable.

papers.title: Cumulative Exposure to High Systemic Inflammation and Incident Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease: A Longitudinal Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to examine the association between cumulative exposure to systemic inflammation and incident metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and related liver fibrosis in mainland China. This study used data from an ongoing longitudinal physical examination cohort. We enrolled 9,725 participants (aged ≥18 years) who completed three consecutive biennial health examinations between 2018 and 2022, with complete follow-up in 2024. Systemic inflammation was quantified using three established biomarkers: neutrophil count (NC), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and systemic immune-inflammation index (SII). Cumulative exposure was calculated from baseline to the third examination by multiplying biomarker values by the time (years) between consecutive examinations. The primary outcome was MASLD development at the fourth examination, and advanced liver fibrosis among incident MASLD cases was further evaluated using the fibrosis-4 index (≥2.67). Multivariable logistic regression models were used to explore the associations between cumulative exposure to inflammation and MASLD incidence and fibrosis severity. At the fourth examination, 939 incident MASLD cases (9.66%) were identified. In fully adjusted models, participants in the highest quartile of cumulative NC exposure had 2.20-fold higher odds of MASLD (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.81 to 2.69; P for trend <0.001) than those in the lowest quartile. Similarly, the highest quartile of cumulative SII exposure had 1.32-fold higher odds (95% CI, 1.09 to 1.59; P for trend=0.003). Conversely, cumulative NLR exposure showed no significant association with MASLD incidence. The addition of cumulative NC or SII to the basic model comprising traditional risk factors improved the ability to predict MASLD. Furthermore, among participants who developed MASLD, the highest quartile of cumulative NC (odds ratio [OR], 4.74; 95% CI, 1.76 to 12.75; P for trend <0.001) and cumulative SII (OR, 3.74; 95% CI, 1.48 to 9.45; P for trend=0.006), but not cumulative NLR, were significantly associated with an elevated risk of advanced liver fibrosis. Greater NC exposure and excessive SII exposure were each independently associated with incident MASLD and related advanced liver fibrosis. Whether reducing inflammation can help prevent MASLD requires further investigation.

papers.title: The new landscape of liver transplantation: Evolving candidates, new technologies, and personalized care.
papers.abstract: Liver transplantation (LT) is entering a new era shaped by changes in disease epidemiology, candidate complexity, donor utilization, and post-transplant management. The decline of viral hepatitis-related cirrhosis, together with the rise of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, alcohol-related liver disease, and hepatocellular carcinoma, has transformed the LT waitlist into an older, frailer, and more cardiometabolically complex population. At the same time, donation after circulatory death and machine perfusion are expanding the donor pool and redefining the boundaries of graft suitability. Candidate selection is also moving beyond traditional diagnosis-based criteria, with increasing acceptance of early LT for carefully selected alcohol-related liver disease, utility-based transplantation for acute-on-chronic liver failure, and biology-driven transplant oncology, in which HCC is established whereas selected iCCA and unresectable CRLM indications remain investigational. In parallel, artificial intelligence and machine learning are being developed as decision-support tools for candidate assessment, waitlist prioritization, donor-recipient matching, and prediction of post-transplant outcomes; prospective validation and evidence of clinical impact remain limited. Immunosuppression is facing a similar transformation, shifting from standardized lifelong exposure toward individualized, monitored minimization and immunologic risk profiling, while complete withdrawal and operational tolerance remain restricted to highly selected recipients within specialized protocols. In this Perspective, we argue that the future of LT will depend on integrating biological reserve, disease behavior, graft quality, and expected survival benefit into transparent, multidisciplinary decision-making. The central challenge will be to translate innovation into durable clinical benefit while preserving equity in access to transplantation.

papers.title: Three Decades of Liver X Receptor Agonist Chemistry: Structural Motifs, Structure-activity Relationship, and Therapeutic Prospects.
papers.abstract: Liver X receptors (LXRs) are nuclear receptors that play an important role in the regulation of gene expression involved in lipid metabolism, cholesterol homeostasis and inflammation. Certain modifications in endogenous LXR activity have been associated with pathological conditions and diseases. The dysregulation of LXR activity can lead to vascular and metabolic diseases, neurological degeneration and formation of malignant tumors. One of the solutions to treat the diseases or at least to slow down the progression is the development of different strategies to modulate LXR signaling for the treatment or prevention of these pathological conditions. Many researchers and pharmaceutical companies are developing selective LXR modulators to precisely control receptor activity and achieve specific pharmacological effects. The activation of LXRs has been linked to the inhibition of cell proliferation and metastasis, the promotion of apoptosis and re-differentiation of tumor cells that drives exosome release to stimulate anti-tumor immunity in certain cancer types. The main challenge is to minimize the adverse effects of LXR induction on lipid metabolism via selective activation of LXRβ isoform. Several lead compounds were identified and tested in clinical trials for few pathologies discussed above. The discovery of a potent and selective LXR ligand involves a combination of multiple steps from lead discovery, optimization, preclinical and clinical testing before getting to marketing authorization. This review offers an overview of synthetic agonists for LXRs developed over the past three decades. Though multiple investigations have been in progress, no FDA-approved LXR-targeting drug is available so far.

papers.title: Paradoxical attenuation of dyslipidemia and atherosclerosis in Apoe -/- Mpst -/- mice.
papers.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H 2 S) is a signaling molecule that affects multiple (patho)physiological pathways. Deficiency of H 2 S due to cystathionine γ-lyase (CSE) deletion has been proven to accelerate atherosclerotic plaque formation. However, the role of 3-mercaptopyruvate sulfurtransferase (MPST), a related H 2 S-producing enzyme that impacts metabolism, has not been studied in atherogenic dyslipidemia. We generated a double Apoe/Mpst knockout mouse (Apoe -/- Mpst -/- ) in the C57BL/6 background. C57Bl/6, Mpst -/- , Apoe -/- and Apoe -/- Mpst -/- mice were fed a western diet for 14 weeks, after which blood and tissues (aorta and liver) were collected; the circulating lipid profile, atherosclerotic plaque formation and expression of enzymes involved in lipid biosynthetic pathways in the liver were evaluated in the four mouse lines. H 2 S production was reduced in the liver of double knockout mice, while the expression of CBS and CSE was not altered. In the serum of Apoe -/- Mpst -/- , we observed decreased levels of total cholesterol, low-density lipoproteins (LDL) and triglycerides (TGs) compared to Apoe -/- ; hepatic apolipoprotein B (ApoB) levels were also downregulated. However, the expression of other key enzymes that participate in cholesterol and fatty acid synthesis remained unchanged. In addition, hepatic lipid deposition was not significantly altered among genotypes. In line with the reduced circulating LDL and TGs levels, atherosclerotic lesions were found to be reduced in the aorta of Apoe -/- Mpst -/- . Our results indicate that MPST deletion in the Apoe -/- dyslipidemia model leads to decreased circulating lipid levels and atherosclerosis, that correlate with a downregulation of hepatic ApoB expression.

papers.title: The Maternal-Placental-Fetal Liver Axis: A Mechanistic Framework for Understanding Benzene Developmental Hematotoxicity.
papers.abstract: Benzene is a ubiquitous environmental pollutant and a human hematotoxicant and carcinogen. Increasing epidemiological and experimental evidence links in utero benzene exposure to adverse pregnancy outcomes, altered fetal development, and increased childhood leukemia risk. Benzene toxicity is initiated through metabolism into reactive intermediates, primarily by cytochrome P450 2E1 (CYP2E1) and myeloperoxidase. These enzymes are expressed not only in the maternal liver but also in the placenta and fetal liver, indicating that multiple compartments may contribute to benzene toxicity during pregnancy. Despite these observations, the mechanisms linking maternal exposure to fetal hematotoxicity remain incompletely understood, as existing studies have largely examined maternal, placental, and fetal effects independently, with the placenta often treated as a passive barrier rather than an active regulator of developmental toxicity. We propose the maternal-placental-fetal liver axis as a mechanistic framework for understanding in utero benzene developmental hematotoxicity, and discuss three biologically plausible bioactivation routes across this axis: maternal hepatic metabolism, placental bioactivation, and direct fetal liver metabolism. We further examine how fetal injury may arise through complementary mechanisms: direct toxicity from transplacental transfer of benzene and its reactive metabolites, and indirect toxicity, whereby benzene-induced placental dysfunction alters the intrauterine environment and may drive secondary fetal injury. We suggest a model where placental dysfunction may amplify, rather than independently drive, fetal benzene toxicity. The maternal-placental-fetal liver axis integrates maternal metabolism, placental biology, and fetal susceptibility, providing a mechanistic framework for understanding the pathways underlying benzene-induced developmental hepatotoxicity and its potential contribution to childhood leukemia.

papers.title: Antioxidant Oxidation Leads to Greater Accumulation of Novel Organophosphate Esters (OPEs) than Traditional OPEs in soil and Groundwater.
papers.abstract: Government agencies have implemented stringent regulations on directly used organophosphate esters (OPEs), such as triphenyl phosphate (TPhP). However, it remains unclear to what extent NOPEs derived from high production volume Organophosphite antioxidants (OPAs) contribute to contamination and environmental risks in industrial-park soil and groundwater. Here, we integrated field investigations of soil and groundwater from a representative industrial park with soil incubation experiments, in vitro rat liver S9 biotransformation assays, and hazard assessment modeling. In industrial soil, the median total concentration of Σ 4 NOPEs reached 4.0 × 10 3 ng g -1 , which was 3.1-fold higher than that of traditional Σ 20 OPEs, with tris(2,4-di-tert-butylphenyl) phosphate (TDtBPP) identified as the predominant compound. In industrial groundwater, the median concentration of Σ 4 NOPEs was 7.5 × 10 3 ng L -1 , approximately 13.2-fold higher than that of traditional Σ 20 OPEs (564 ng L -1 ). The transformation potential of OPAs was strongly dependent on molecular structure, with TDtBPPi undergoing the highest conversion potential. Relative to traditional TPhP, TDtBPP exhibited 72.1-fold greater persistence, 4.10-fold higher resistance to biotransformation, and 94.0-fold greater human exposure risk. This study demonstrates that the transformation of high production volume OPAs represents an overlooked pathway contributing to OPE contamination. OPA-derived NOPEs can accumulate to elevated levels and substantially increase contaminant burdens and associated exposure risks in industrial soil and groundwater.

papers.title: Rethinking Pathogenesis of Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis.
papers.abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a chronic cholestatic liver disease characterized by progressive fibroinflammatory injury of intrahepatic and extrahepatic bile ducts that may lead to cirrhosis, hepatobiliary malignancy, and death, with liver transplantation representing the only effective intervention in end-stage disease. Rather than a single dominant pathomechanism, the data support a model in which four axes - bile acid metabolism, the intestinal microbiome and gut barrier, biliary epithelial dysfunction, and Th17-skewed immune dysregulation - are reciprocally coupled and converge on a shared periductal fibrogenic output dominated by TGF-beta signaling. This review summarizes key mechanistic advances from genetic, epigenomic, single-cell, spatial transcriptomic, and microbiome studies. These investigations implicate antigen presentation pathways, Th17-skewed immune responses, cholangiocyte senescence and profibrotic signaling, and disrupted gut-liver communication as central drivers of chronic biliary injury. Emerging spatial and multi-omics approaches further reveal complex cellular crosstalk among cholangiocytes, immune cells, macrophages, and mesenchymal populations within portal inflammatory niches. We discuss evolving biomarkers and recent clinical trial data targeting bile acid metabolism, fibrosis, the microbiome, and immune pathways. In conclusion, research data suggests viewing PSC as a network disease, which provides a unifying framework for disease pathogenesis and may enable biomarker-guided patient stratification and mechanism-based therapy development targeting distinct pathogenic pathways.

papers.title: A microbiome-bile acid axis mediates protection from chronic liver disease in females.
papers.abstract: Sex-based differences in chronic liver disease (CLD) incidence and progression are well documented, yet the mechanistic basis of this sexual disparity remains elusive. Here, leveraging a large-scale metabolomics database comprising 9,254 individuals, we identify the endogenous bile acid, isoursodeoxycholic acid (isoUDCA), as a candidate mediator of female-associated hepatoprotection. We trace the origin of isoUDCA to a bacterial consortium, which is selectively enriched by estrogen through shaping a specialized intestinal microenvironment. Mechanistically, isoUDCA promotes the nuclear accumulation of SREBP2. This upregulates the intracellular transporter STARD4 and its functionally coupled downstream enzyme CYP7B1, thereby facilitating intracellular cholesterol handling and metabolic conversion. Collectively, our findings support a microbiome-bile acid-liver axis that may contribute to sex differences in CLD susceptibility and support further evaluation of isoUDCA as a potential therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Targeted redox gene-expression profiling reveals shared and distinct expression patterns in HBV- and HCV-associated hepatocellular carcinoma.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress and redox dysregulation are important features of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), but their expression patterns in hepatitis B virus (HBV)- and hepatitis C virus (HCV)-associated HCC remain incompletely characterized. This study investigated redox-related gene expression and its potential functional and prognostic relevance. A predefined 84-gene oxidative stress and redox-related quantitative real-time PCR array was used to profile 11 HCC samples (7 HCV-associated and 4 HBV-associated tumors) and 4 controls. Analyses included hierarchical clustering, gene-list overlap, functional enrichment, protein-protein interaction networks, gene-expression correlations, and exploratory survival analysis. Both HCC groups exhibited altered expression of genes associated with antioxidant defense, glutathione metabolism, mitochondrial redox regulation, and ferroptosis-related processes. In HCV-associated HCC versus controls, TXN, SPINK1, HSP90AA1, and DUSP1 showed increased expression. In HBV-associated HCC versus controls, GCLC, peroxiredoxins, CAT, and SOD1 showed increased expression. Eighteen genes were shared between comparison lists, including GPX4, GPX2, GPX3, PRDX1, PRDX5, TXN, GCLM, SOD2, and FTH1. Enrichment analyses implicated glutathione metabolism, oxidative stress, peroxisome function, and ferroptosis-associated processes. Network analysis identified GPX2, GPX3, GPX4, and SOD2 in a connected module. External exploratory survival analysis associated higher SPINK1 and HSP90AA1 expression with poorer overall survival. These findings identify redox-related expression patterns warranting further investigation. Larger cohorts and functional studies are needed to establish etiological differences, ferroptosis susceptibility, and prognostic significance.

papers.title: Material-specific modulation of microplastic biotoxicity by chlorination: Mechanistic insights into ER stress and associated health risks.
papers.abstract: Chlorination, a widely used disinfection method in drinking water treatment plants, poses underexplored health risks through its interactions with microplastics (MPs). Here, we show that chlorination induces significant physicochemical changes in four common MPs-polyethylene (PE), polyurethane (PU), polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE), and polymethyl methacrylate (PMMA)-focusing on particles smaller than 30 µm. PU and PE MPs exhibit the most pronounced changes including significant surface degradation and oxidation, releasing various organic compounds. In vitro assays show that disinfected PU MPs significantly increased cytotoxicity, while disinfected PE MPs mitigated toxicity by modulating ER stress via the IRE1α/XBP1/BIP pathway. In vivo, 30-day exposure to pristine PE and disinfected PU MPs induce tissue damage, inflammation, and immune responses. Transcriptomic analysis of Liver revealed disrupted lipid, glutathione, and iron metabolism, activating DNA replication and proteasome pathways linked to ER stress. mRNA validation confirmed that disinfected MPs induces toxicity via the PERK/EIF2α/ATF4 pathway, with disinfected PU MPs causing severe damage, with significant CHOP upregulation indicating apoptosis. These findings underscore the biotoxicological impacts of disinfected MPs and provide insights for optimizing disinfection methods and mitigating the health risks of MPs in water treatment, particularly given the widespread use of chlorination worldwide.

papers.title: Selective Systemic Responses During Aeromonas salmonicida Subsp. Salmonicida Infection in Northern Snakehead (Channa argus).
papers.abstract: Northern snakehead (Channa argus) is a bimodal air-breathing fish in which erythrocyte-associated parameters remain relatively stable during physiological challenges such as aerial exposure. However, whether this characteristic is maintained during systemic infection remains unclear. In this study, temporal host responses were characterized following experimental Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida infection by integrating haematological, leukocyte morphological, biochemical, and multi-tissue transcriptional analyses. Most erythrocyte-associated indices, including RBC, HGB, HCT, MCV, MCH, and RDW, showed no significant temporal changes, whereas MON, GRA, and PLT exhibited significant responses. Morphologically abnormal leukocytes increased from approximately 7% in healthy fish to 56% at 6 days post-infection and remained above 50% through 8 days, indicating persistent leukocyte-associated cellular alterations during infection. Biochemical responses were also selective, with changes primarily in protein- and metabolism-associated parameters. Transcriptional responses differed among peripheral blood, head kidney, spleen, and liver, including sustained casp7 suppression in the head kidney and distinct inflammatory and apoptosis-associated responses across tissues. Two-way ANOVA further identified significant tissue × time interactions for casp8, tnfα, and casp3. Collectively, A. salmonicida infection in northern snakehead was characterized by comparatively limited temporal variation in most erythrocyte-associated indices, alongside selective leukocyte, biochemical, and tissue-dependent transcriptional responses. These findings highlight a contrasting blood response characterized by persistent leukocyte alterations despite comparatively limited temporal variation in most erythrocyte-associated indices during bacterial infection in northern snakehead.

papers.title: Integrating Non-Invasive Liver Assessment into Screening Colonoscopy: A Prospective Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Steatotic liver disease is underdiagnosed despite guideline recommendations for risk-based case-finding. Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening colonoscopy engages a prevention-oriented, healthcare-seeking population in whom liver disease may go undetected. We assessed the feasibility, acceptance, and yield of non-invasive liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy visits. This prospective cross-sectional study enrolled adults aged ≥50 years attending screening colonoscopy. Individuals with known chronic liver disease were excluded. Participants underwent hepatic ultrasound and point shear wave elastography. Liver stiffness measurements (LSM) were interpreted using prespecified thresholds of 1.30, 1.50, and 1.70 m/s (∼5, 7, and 9 kPa, respectively). We assessed whether risk-factor-based criteria would have identified participants with elevated stiffness, and evaluated the Fibrosis-4 index (FIB-4) against LSM thresholds. Of 692 adults offered participation, 610 enrolled (88.2% acceptance); one was excluded for decompensated heart failure. Reliable LSM was obtained in 578 of 609 (94.9%). Ultrasound-defined steatosis was identified in 55.5%. LSM exceeded 1.30 m/s in 25.3%; 9.0% and 5.0% met thresholds consistent with significant fibrosis (≥1.50 m/s) and compensated advanced chronic liver disease (≥1.70 m/s), respectively. Among participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s, exposure profiles were metabolic in 63.5%, mixed metabolic-alcohol in 21.2%, and alcohol-related in 15.4%. Risk-factor criteria were met by 76.6% and captured 46/52 participants with LSM ≥1.50 m/s. At this threshold, FIB-4 showed modest discrimination (AUROC 0.682); sensitivity decreased from 0.706 using a single threshold to 0.529 using age-adjusted thresholds. Opportunistic liver assessment integrated into screening colonoscopy was feasible, well accepted, and identified previously undetected steatosis and elevated LSM.

papers.title: Absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion of linzagolix after a single oral dose in rats and monkeys.
papers.abstract: 1. Linzagolix is an orally available gonadotropin-releasing hormone antagonist used to treat female-specific diseases, such as uterine fibroids and endometriosis.2. After a single dose of [ 14 C]linzagolix or linzagolix to female rats and monkeys, linzagolix exhibited the absorption-distribution-metabolism-excretion characteristics of acidic drugs owing to the presence of a carboxylic acid moiety in its structure.3. Linzagolix showed low total clearance, high oral bioavailability, and high plasma exposure associated with high solubility, low metabolic clearance, and entero-hepatic circulation. Linzagolix had a low-volume distribution with limited tissue distribution associated with high plasma protein binding. These absorption-distribution-metabolism-excretion characteristics were comparable between the two species.4. After a single oral dose of [ 14 C]linzagolix to rats, radioactivity was rapidly distributed to almost all tissues; however, the extent of the tissue distribution was limited and decreased in parallel with elimination from the blood.5. In both species, linzagolix was identified as the primary circulating and excretory component. The major biotransformation pathways of linzagolix were two O-demethylations and O-debenzylation. Additionally, sulphate conjugates of O-demethylated metabolites were detected in rats.6. The major excretion route of linzagolix was faecal excretion via the bile in its unchanged form.

papers.title: Macrophage interferon regulatory factor 7 aggravates the progression of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) represents a growing clinical burden with increasing prevalence and lacking approved pharmacological therapies. Interferon regulatory factor 7 (IRF7) is a central mediator of type I interferon-dependent immune responses, yet the precise mechanisms by which macrophage-expressed IRF7 shapes inflammatory and metabolic events during MASH pathogenesis remain incompletely defined. This study aimed to dissect the functional role of IRF7 in MASH development. We assessed IRF7 expression in human and mouse liver specimens, and utilized myeloid-specific Irf7-deficient mice fed with high-fat high-cholesterol diet (HFHCD) or methionine-choline-deficient diet (MCD) to recapitulate MASH pathology. IRF7 was significantly elevated in MASH-affected livers, and myeloid-specific Irf7 deletion markedly mitigated MASH progression. Mechanistically, loss of IRF7 blunted IFN-α and IFN-β production, suppressing macrophage-derived type I interferon-dependent immune cascades. IRF7 directly bound to the promoters of pro-inflammatory Tnfa and Il1b to boost their transcription, and interacted with SMAD3 to activate Tgfb1 transcription. The E3 ubiquitin ligase HUWE1 mediated IRF7 monoubiquitination to enhance its nuclear translocation, driving transcription of pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic genes. This molecular cascade aggravated hepatic steatosis and triggered hepatic stellate cell (HSC) activation, accelerating MASH deterioration. Pharmacological IRF7 inhibition effectively counteracted these pathological alterations. Collectively, myeloid IRF7 fuels MASH progression by amplifying macrophage-mediated liver inflammation, suggesting IRF7 as a promising therapeutic target against MASH.

papers.title: [Treatment of type 2 diabetes mellitus].
papers.abstract: Modern diabetology is undergoing a paradigm shift from glucose-centric management toward risk-adapted precision medicine. Differentiated phenotyping into clusters allows for the early identification of organ-specific risks. Pharmacotherapy now prioritizes cardiorenal protection using sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2) inhibitors, glucagon-like peptide‑1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists, and nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (nsMRAs; finerenone), which reduce vascular events beyond glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) reduction alone. Technological innovations, such as continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), complement traditional markers with dynamic metrics such as time in range. A new, realistic therapeutic goal is metabolic remission, facilitated by potent incretin mimetics and early intervention during the prediabetes stage. The ultimate objective is the sustainable restoration of normoglycemia and the prevention of end-organ damage through a multifactorial, individualized approach. Die moderne Diabetologie vollzieht einen Paradigmenwechsel von der glukozentrischen hin zur risikoadaptierten Präzisionsmedizin. Durch eine differenzierte klinische Subphänotypisierung können organspezifische Risiken frühzeitig adressiert werden. Im Zentrum der Pharmakotherapie steht die kardiorenale Organprotektion mit Natrium-Glukose-Kotransporter-2(SGLT2)-Inhibitoren, Glucagon-like-peptide-1(GLP-1)-Rezeptor-Agonisten und nichtsteroidalen Mineralokortikoidrezeptorantagonisten (nsMRA; Finerenon), die über die reine Hämoglobin-A1c(HbA1c)-Senkung hinaus vaskuläre Ereignisse reduzieren. Technologische Innovationen wie die kontinuierliche Glukosemessung (CGM) ergänzen die HbA1c-Bestimmung durch dynamische Parameter wie die „time in range“. Ein neues, realistisches Therapieziel ist die metabolische Remission, die insbesondere durch potente Inkretinmimetika und frühzeitige Interventionen im Prädiabetesstadium ermöglicht wird. Ziel ist die nachhaltige Wiederherstellung der Normoglykämie und der Schutz vor irreversiblen Endorganschäden.

papers.title: Antidiabetic medications in the pipeline.
papers.abstract: There is an extensive pipeline of therapies for diabetes mellitus. It has been known for the past three decades that obesity is a key pathophysiological player, involving inflammation, insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction leading to type 2 diabetes and to significant cardiovascular, renal and hepatic complications, all central to the metabolic syndrome. On the basis of this knowledge and the disposition of drugs with multiple effects on different disease components, the diabetes therapeutic paradigm has shifted from merely glucocentric to multitargeted against these interconnected pathways.Much more recently, incretin-based multi-agonists have been developed that deliver unprecedented glycemic and weight benefits as well as weekly insulins and oral GLP-1 agonists that are able to reduce the burden of injectable therapies. An antibody-peptide conjugate that acts as a dual GLP-1/GIP receptor modulator has also shown promising results. Today, novel insulin sensitizers are modulating metabolic pathways towards higher energy expenditure with fewer side effects. Adjunctive agents for type 1 diabetes are improving glucose control while reducing hypoglycemia risk. Finally, drugs designed to restrain the inevitable muscle mass loss caused by antiobesity treatments are being tested. The diabetes pipeline is rich and there is hope that in the next few years, the therapeutic landscape will be further transformed with even more efficacious and individualized treatments.

papers.title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum Strains LP5 and BX62 Alleviate Liver Injury of NAFLD in Rats via Regulating Hepatic Cholesterol Metabolism and Antioxidant Signaling Pathways.
papers.abstract: Disorders of lipid metabolism and oxidative stress are pivotal factors in the advancement of non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). This study aims to investigate the liver-protective effects of two Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (L. plantarum) strains, LP5 and BX62, either individually or in combined, on NAFLD in rats induced by high fat and cholesterol diet. Strain L. plantarum LP5 showed potential for modulating cholesterol metabolism, whereas L. plantarum BX62 exhibited enhanced antioxidant properties. All three intervention strategies alleviated liver injury, as evidenced by reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, intestinal permeability, inflammation, and liver injury markers. Notably, L. plantarum LP5 showed greater effects on reducing weight gain and hepatic steatosis, while L. plantarum BX62 provided additional protection against hepatic oxidative damage. Metabolic and molecular analyses suggested that the beneficial effects of L. plantarum LP5 were associated with altered bile acid homeostasis and increased expression of hepatic primary bile acid synthesis-related proteins (CYP7A1 and CYP8B1), whereas L. plantarum BX62 was associated with activation of the Nrf2-HO-1 antioxidant pathway (Nrf2, HO-1, and FTH). Furthermore, all intervention strategies activated AMPK signaling (p-AMPK/AMPK), accompanied by decreased expression of lipogenesis-related proteins (SREBP-1c, FASN, and SCD1) and increased expression of fatty acid oxidation-related proteins (PPARα and CPT1a), contributing to improved hepatic lipid metabolism. Collectively, our findings indicate that L. plantarum LP5 and L. plantarum BX62 alleviate HFHC diet-induced hepatic metabolic disturbances by complementary mechanisms involving cholesterol metabolism and antioxidant responses, highlighting their potential as dietary probiotics for supporting liver health and preventing NAFLD progression.

papers.title: High-temperature stress response in the liver of Trachinotus ovatus: a cascade of oxidative stress, immunity, and bile acid metabolic reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Fish exhibit a high degree of susceptibility to shifts in thermal conditions within the water. The liver is central to metabolic homeostasis and immune defense, and its physiological stability is critical for fish health. The present study evaluated the hepatic physiological responses of Trachinotus ovatus following a 7-day exposure to high-temperature (HT) stress, including alterations in histology, oxidative stress, iron homeostasis, inflammation, immunity, apoptosis, and bile acid (BA) metabolism. HT stress induced alterations in liver histology and disrupted redox homeostasis, accompanied by enhanced Nrf2-mediated antioxidant signaling and changes in antioxidant defense enzyme activities and peroxide levels. Iron homeostasis and lipid peroxide defense exhibited complex alterations, including Fe levels and NCOA4 expression were increased, accompanied by compensatory upregulation of iron-homeostasis genes (FTH1, FPN1, and NFS1) and antioxidant defense genes (GPx4, SLC7A11, and p53). However, reduced lipid peroxidation products (LPO and MDA) suggested that these changes reflected regulatory adaptation rather than the execution of ferroptosis. HT stress induced hepatic inflammatory and immune responses, characterized by activation of pro-inflammatory signaling, dysregulated anti-inflammatory regulation, downregulation of IL-8 expression, and downregulation of the immunoglobulin genes IgM and IgT. Apoptosis-related genes showed divergent expression patterns, with CHOP, Casp-9, and Casp-3 being upregulated, whereas CytC was downregulated. Furthermore, BA metabolism was affected, as shown by reductions in total BA pool size and free BA levels, along with the upregulated expression of BA metabolism-related genes (FXR, SULT1, and UGT8). Three metabolites, cholic acid, chenodeoxycholic acid, and 7-ketolithocholic acid were identified as potential biomarkers. Collectively, these findings suggest that HT stress impaired hepatic physiological homeostasis in T. ovatus, accompanied by tissue architecture disruption, redox imbalance, inflammatory responses, immune suppression, BA metabolic remodeling, and coordinated changes in iron homeostasis and apoptosis-related regulatory pathways.

papers.title: Dietary phytosterol alleviates adverse effects caused by high-carbohydrate diets on growth performance, antioxidant capacity, glucolipid metabolism, and metabolomics in largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) juveniles.
papers.abstract: High-carbohydrate diets (HCD) usually lead to metabolic syndrome in many fish species. However, the role of phytosterol (PS) in alleviating HCD effects on largemouth bass (Micropterus salmoides) is currently unknown. This study investigated the effects of dietary PS on growth performance, antioxidant capacity, histopathology, glucolipid metabolism, and metabolomics in juvenile largemouth bass fed a 5% corn-starch-enriched diet. Fish weighing 11.14 ± 0.48 g were fed a control diet (CON), a 5% corn-starch-enriched diet (HCD), and the same corn-starch-enriched diet supplemented with PS (0.025%, 0.05%, 0.075%, and 0.1%) in quadruplicate for eight weeks. The fish fed dietary PS increased significantly final body weight, weight gain, and specific growth rate (P < 0.05) compared with HCD. Moreover, fish fed dietary PS had significantly lower triglycerides and total cholesterol, while having higher high-density lipoprotein levels, than those fed HCD (P < 0.05). Feeding the fish on dietary PS improved hepatic superoxide dismutase and catalase activities, thereby lowering malondialdehyde content (P < 0.05). The fish fed dietary PS showed reduced hepatic lipid accumulation, increased interleukin-18 gene expression, and decreased interleukin-1β and tumor necrosis factor-alpha gene expression compared with those fed with HCD (P < 0.05). Furthermore, fish fed PS-supplemented diets significantly downregulated palmitic acid, choline, L-proline, and L-threonine metabolites compared with those fed HCD (P < 0.05). Our results demonstrate that dietary PS alleviates HCD-induced impairments by improving growth performance, antioxidant capacity, and glucolipid metabolites, thereby reducing lipid accumulation and inflammation in juvenile largemouth bass.

papers.title: Real-world screening for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease among adults with type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: New treatments for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) require identification of patients at risk of progressing to cirrhosis, yet population-based screening methods are not well established. We conducted a pilot screening study at a large academic primary care practice among patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We calculated FIB-4 scores on existing labs and contacted providers with recommendations for additional testing with vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) and/or specialty referral. Among 2773 patients with T2DM seen at our clinic during the study period meeting inclusion criteria, 2396 had sufficient data to calculate FIB-4. After excluding lab results from the emergency department or inpatient setting, this left a final sample of 1315 patients. Among the 1315 patients included in the study, 78 (5.9%) had FIB-4 scores >2.66, while 732 (55.7%) had FIB-4 scores between 1.3 and 2.66. The diagnostic yield (proportion of patients receiving definitive diagnosis of MASLD with F2 or higher fibrosis as a result of the intervention) among the cohort with FIB-4 > 2.66 was 12/78 (15.4%). The most common reason for fall-out was the patient not wishing to receive further evaluation, with the second being provider concerns about competing risks. The impact of population-level MASLD screening is limited by implementation barriers. Future efforts should focus on direct-to-patient outreach and methods to identify patients without competing risks who are most likely to benefit from MASLD diagnosis and specific treatment.

papers.title: Genetic evaluation in living liver donors: beyond individual risk to system responsibility.
papers.abstract: Living donor liver transplantation (LDLT) increasingly depends on biologically related donors, particularly in Asia and the Middle East, where deceased donation remains limited. This review evaluates genetic risks in living donors and proposes a system-based approach to donor selection. Heterozygous carriers exhibit variable functional capacity determined by enzyme thresholds and epigenetic mechanisms such as X-chromosome lyonization. In ornithine transcarbamylase deficiency (OTCD), maternal donors may have insufficient enzymatic activity, resulting in donor risk and incomplete metabolic correction. Conversely, certain autosomal recessive disorders permit safe use of heterozygous donors within defined functional limits. In regions with high consanguinity, especially in parts of the Middle East, hereditary liver diseases are more prevalent, increasing the likelihood that potential donors share pathogenic variants. Additionally, reports of acute liver failure following gene therapy in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) highlight systemic vulnerability in genetically affected individuals. Donor evaluation must extend beyond anatomical suitability to include disease-specific genetic risk assessment. A system-based, globally informed framework integrating genomics, functional assessment, and multidisciplinary oversight is essential to ensure donor safety and optimize outcomes.

papers.title: Facet-Programmed Oxide Nanointerfaces for Metabolite Activation and AI-Assisted Disease Screening.
papers.abstract: Metal oxides are important nanocatalytic materials for small-molecule activation, owing to their variable valence states and efficient charge-transfer capabilities. This activation is governed by coupled oxide-molecule interfacial processes, for which conventional descriptors such as morphology, composition, and defects remain insufficiently precise. Here, we establish crystal facets as descriptors for oxide surface regulation and use laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) as a high-throughput readout of metabolite activation. Across CeO 2 , Co 3 O 4 , and Cu 2 O, exposed facets strongly regulate metabolite desorption/ionization, with the (110) facet consistently exhibiting superior activity. Mechanistic studies and density functional theory calculations reveal that facet exposure modulates surface valence states, oxygen-vacancy formation, charge transfer, carrier dynamics, and energy dissipation. In particular, (110) CeO 2 integrates favorable defect structures, low work function, efficient charge separation, and localized energy confinement, enabling enhanced metabolite activation with up to three orders of magnitude signal improvement, high reproducibility, and salt/protein tolerance. The optimized (110) CeO 2 matrix enables serum metabolic fingerprinting for AI-assisted discrimination of hepatocellular carcinoma from chronic liver disease and biomarker identification. This work demonstrates facet engineering as a strategy for designing oxide nanointerfaces that translate molecular activation into chemically informative fingerprints for disease screening.

papers.title: Microphysiological organ-on-a-chip system for anti-doping research: long-term CYP activity characterization and S107 metabolism in a HepaRG™-based 3D liver model.
papers.abstract: Identification of metabolic markers of prohibited and emerging performance-enhancing substances remains a key challenge in anti-doping analysis, where limitations of conventional in vitro models in resembling authentic physiological conditions exist. Organ-on-a-chip (OoC) systems combining 3D human liver-cell cultures with microfluidic perfusion offer a predictive alternative for human-like drug metabolism. In this study, a HepaRG™-based liver OoC model incorporating hepatic stellate cells was characterized over a three-week period with a focus on cytochrome P450 (CYP)-mediated metabolism. CYP activity, gene expression, and inducibility were assessed for major hepatic CYP isoforms, complemented by pharmacogenomic profiling. Metabolic performance was further evaluated using S107, a non-approved and prohibited doping agent, with metabolite formation being determined by liquid chromatography and high-resolution mass spectrometry (LC-HRMS/MS) in comparison with published in vitro data. The OoC system maintained stable viability and hepatic functionality throughout the culture period, demonstrating phase-I metabolic competence. Isoform-specific differences in mRNA expression and enzymatic activity highlighted complex regulatory effects within the microphysiological environment, while rifampicin responses confirmed preserved nuclear receptor-mediated inducibility across the system. Functional limitations were observed for CYP2D6 and CYP2B6, which showed absent or restricted activity despite detectable transcriptional signals. For S107, the model generated both phase-I and phase-II metabolites, consistent with literature data from microsomal incubation experiments. Metabolite formation was stable over the three-week period under dynamic perfusion conditions, demonstrating sustained biotransformation capacity. Overall, the HepaRG™ OoC system represents a physiologically relevant in vitro platform for long-term metabolism and demonstrates potential as a predictive tool for anti-doping applications and for elucidating metabolic pathways of emerging performance-enhancing substances.

papers.title: Molecular Insights and Therapeutic Potential of Benzothiazole Derivatives: A Comprehensive Pharmacological Review.
papers.abstract: Benzothiazole (BTA), a fused bicyclic heterocycle of thiazole and benzene units, has become a special scaffold for medicinal chemistry with a vast pharmacological profile. Structural modification at the benzothiazole core provides enormous flexibility toward rationalizing bioactivity in a wide range of therapeutics. Contemporary research is exemplified by benzothiazole derivatives as potent antibacterial agents, efficiently targeting multidrug-resistant pathogens by mechanisms like DNA gyrase inhibition and membrane disruption. They also exhibit multi-target-directed ligand- based anti-Alzheimer's activity by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, butyrylcholinesterase, monoamine oxidases, and β-secretase enzymes. In cancer, benzothiazole hybrids are found to be selectively cytotoxic toward different cancer cell lines, such as breast, lung, and liver cancers, and are generally more active than the traditional drugs. Anti-tubercular activity presents superior inhibition of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including, Multidrug-resistance (MDR) and Extensively Drug- Resistance (XDR), by novel hybrid conjugates and heterocyclic linkages. Additionally, benzothiazole analogues exhibit anti-inflammatory and anti-diabetic activity with cyclooxygenase, Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4), α-glucosidase, and α-amylase enzyme inhibitory activity. Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) analysis consistently indicates that electron-withdrawing or electron-donating functions, linker type, and heteroatom position in modulating pharmacological activity. Recent patents reflect sustained innovation in drug design with the benzothiazole motif, and therapeutic applications exist in antimicrobial, anticancer, neuroprotection, and metabolic disorders. Overall, these findings place emphasis on benzothiazole derivatives as highly effective lead templates with immense therapeutic value, warranting further consideration towards clinical usefulness.

papers.title: Phytodiab® in subjects with metabolic syndrome and early type 2 diabetes: a 12-week observational registry study.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes associated with increased weight is a common metabolic condition that may progress to chronic disease. This pilot observational registry evaluated the effects of Phytodiab ® , a multi-component natural extract formulation, on metabolic and oxidative parameters in subjects with mild-to-moderate type 2 diabetes managed with diet and lifestyle measures. Sixty adults with type 2 diabetes, moderately overweight, without diabetic complications and not receiving pharmacological treatment, were included. Subjects followed standard lifestyle management (SM) alone (N.=30) or Phytodiab ® plus SM once daily before the main meal (N.=30) for 12 weeks. Outcomes included body weight, fat mass, fasting glucose, glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c), and plasma oxidative stress measured in Carr units. Safety, tolerability, compliance, and routine blood parameters were monitored. The two groups were comparable at baseline for age, sex distribution, and clinical profile. There were no dropouts and no tolerability problems. Compliance was high, with 96% of tablets correctly used. At 12 weeks, subjects receiving Phytodiab ® showed significant reductions in weight, fat mass, fasting glucose, HbA1c, and oxidative stress compared with controls (P<0.05). Routine laboratory parameters, including kidney and liver function, blood count, coagulation, and platelet activity, remained normal and unchanged. In this 12-week observational registry, Phytodiab ® plus SM was well tolerated and associated with improvements in metabolic and oxidative parameters in otherwise healthy subjects with mild-to-moderate type 2 diabetes managed with lifestyle measures. These findings are exploratory and support further controlled evaluations in larger populations.

papers.title: Microplastics as Microbiota Modulators: Rewiring the Gut Metabolism Immune Axis.
papers.abstract: Microplastics (MPs) have emerged as pervasive environmental contaminants with increasing relevance to human health. Beyond their role as inert particulate pollutants, accumulating evidence suggests that MPs may act as biologically active modulators of the gastrointestinal ecosystem. The gut represents a major interface for MP exposure, where ingested particles interact with intestinal epithelial cells, mucus layers, immune components, and resident microbial communities. This review summarizes current evidence on MPs' capacity to alter gut microbiota composition, impair intestinal barrier integrity, disrupt microbial metabolite production, and promote inflammatory and metabolic disturbances.Experimental studies indicate that MP exposure may reduce microbial diversity, shift the abundance of key bacterial taxa, impair tight junction proteins, and increase intestinal permeability. These changes may facilitate the translocation of bacterial products such as lipopolysaccharide, thereby activating inflammatory pathways including TLR4/NF-κB signaling. In parallel, MP-associated dysbiosis may alter short-chain fatty acids, bile acid metabolism, and tryptophan-derived metabolites, suggesting plausible biological pathways relevant to insulin resistance, hepatic lipid dysregulation, cardiometabolic risk, and gut-brain axis disruption. However, most available evidence is derived from animal and in vitro models, and causal relationships in humans remain insufficiently established. Major limitations include heterogeneous exposure protocols, non-standardized particle characterization, limited human longitudinal data, and difficulty separating particle-specific effects from those of associated chemical contaminants.Future studies integrating environmentally realistic exposure models, standardized microbiome analyses, multi-omics approaches, and human cohort designs are needed. Overall, the gut microbiota may represent a critical biological interface through which MPs interact with host physiology; however, further evidence is required before definitive conclusions can be drawn regarding their role in human chronic disease susceptibility.

papers.title: Reduction in Rheumatoid Factor and Matrix Metalloproteinase-3 With Successful Glucocorticoid Withdrawal After Initiation of Pemafibrate in a Patient With Rheumatoid Arthritis and Hypertriglyceridemia: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Pemafibrate is a selective peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor α (PPARα) modulator (SPPARMα) used for hypertriglyceridemia. PPARα activation also suppresses nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling, a pathway central to synovial inflammation and joint destruction in rheumatoid arthritis (RA). Whether pemafibrate affects RA-related biomarkers in humans is unknown. A 51-year-old woman (height: 164 cm, body weight: 71 kg, body mass index: 26.4 kg/m²) with RA treated with methotrexate, bucillamine, iguratimod, and low-dose prednisolone (0.7 mg/day) had hypertriglyceridemia with coexisting metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Pemafibrate was started at 0.2 mg/day and increased to 0.4 mg/day after 12 weeks, while the disease-modifying antirheumatic drug (DMARD) regimen was kept unchanged throughout. Over the 20 months following the initiation of pemafibrate, rheumatoid factor (RF) and matrix metalloproteinase-3 (MMP-3) declined, and C-reactive protein (CRP) showed an overall decrease with a transient rise at month 6; prednisolone was tapered and discontinued after 17 months. The 28-joint Disease Activity Score based on C-reactive protein (CRP; DAS28-CRP), already in the remission range at baseline (1.9), remained below the remission threshold throughout. Serum triglycerides fell from 184 mg/dL to 88 mg/dL, and hepatic transaminases (aspartate aminotransferase (AST) and alanine aminotransferase (ALT)) showed a transient early increase followed by a return toward baseline, without meeting criteria for drug-induced liver injury. No adverse events attributable to pemafibrate were observed. In this patient, the introduction of pemafibrate was temporally associated with reductions in RA-related biomarkers and with successful glucocorticoid withdrawal, without any intensification of DMARD therapy. Because the baseline prednisolone dose was already low (0.7 mg/day), this withdrawal should be interpreted cautiously and should not be regarded as strong evidence of a glucocorticoid-sparing effect. Causality cannot be established from a single case; nevertheless, together with earlier clinical reports on fenofibrate, animal studies showing anti-arthritic effects of fenofibrate and bezafibrate, and preclinical evidence of PPARα-mediated NF-κB inhibition, this observation suggests that PPARα agonists merit further investigation as adjunctive agents in RA, particularly in patients with coexisting dyslipidemia or steatotic liver disease.

papers.title: Influence of an oregano-based essential oil on growth performance and carcass traits of beef steers.
papers.abstract: The objective of this study was to determine the influence of an oregano-based essential oil on growth performance, health outcomes, and carcass characteristics of yearling beef steers finished in an all-natural program. Single-sourced yearling steers ( N  = 128; initial body weight [BW] = 335 ± 7.9 kg) were allotted to 16 pens ( n  = 8 pens/treatment with 8 steers/pen). Steers were blocked by pen location in a randomized complete block design ( n  = 8 blocks total). Treatment groups consisted of (1) control group fed no oregano-based essential oil product (CON) and (2) a group fed 4 g/steer daily of By-O-Reg + Beef (Advanced Ag Products, Canton, SD; OEO). Steers were individually weighed on d 0 (arrival), d 38, d 66, d 108, and d 149 for growth performance measures. Steers were transitioned from a 70% concentrate diet to a 90% concentrate diet over the first 14 d and remained on the finishing diet until d 149. The finishing diet provided 1.37 Mcal/kg of NEg. Steers were evaluated daily for indications of disease or visible digestive disorders by a trained technician blinded to the treatments. Steers were harvested at a commercial packing facility when they reached a common compositional endpoint determined by visual assessment. Prior to carcass chilling, hot carcass weight and liver score was recorded for each carcass. Following chilling, ribeye area, 12th rib backfat thickness, marbling score, USDA Quality grade, USDA Yield grade, and instrumental color ( L* , a* , b* ) were recorded. Health outcomes were not influenced by dietary treatment ( P  ≥ 0.18). Inclusion of OEO did not influence ( P  ≥ 0.73) carcass-adjusted final BW, dry matter intake, average daily gain, gain: feed, observed dietary net energy for maintenance (NEm) or net energy for gain (NEg), observed-to-expected dietary NEm or NEg. No differences ( P  ≥ 0.30) were observed between treatment groups for carcass traits or the distribution of USDA Yield and Quality Grades ( P  = 0.94 and P  = 0.79 respectively). Collectively, growth performance, health, and carcass traits of steers finished in an all-natural program in this experiment were not influenced by dietary inclusion of an oregano-based essential oil feed additive.

papers.title: Assessing in vitro long-term liver metabolism models to characterize intrinsic clearance determination in NGRAs.
papers.abstract: In Next Generation Risk Assessments, measurements of hepatic intrinsic clearance (CL int , in vitro ) and metabolite(s) formation can markedly impact in vitro to in vivo extrapolations and subsequent testing of parent and/or metabolites in in vitro bioassays. It is especially important for slowly metabolized chemicals to use the most suitable model and experimental design to ensure that the IVIVE is accurate. We evaluated four long-term hepatic models (sandwich cultures of primary human hepatocytes (PHH), HepatoPac, HµREL and TruVivo), as well as PHH suspensions, using salicylic acid, 1-methyl-2-pyrrolidinone (NMP) and valproic acid. Assay designs differed in terms of positive and negative controls, cell densities and incubation durations. All models generated a measurable CL int , in vitro value for salicylic acid i.e. depletion >20%. Differences may be due to donor differences and the cell number. HepatoPac generally resulted in higher values compared with the other models. NMP was not metabolized by HµREL and TruVivo models and a reliable value was only possible using HepatoPac. NMP was metabolized by sandwich cultures; however, the half-life was much longer than the incubation duration. To derive a more robust value, follow up testing could include longer incubation times. Valproic acid was only metabolized in one of the three models in which it was detected, namely sandwich cultures. In conclusion, PHH sandwich cultures, HepatoPac, HµREL and TruVivo models are superior to PHH suspensions with respect to maintaining XME activities over days and for measuring CL int, in vitro values for slowly metabolized chemicals. To gain regulatory acceptance and better interpret data from different labs, we recommend increasing the number of chemicals tested and harmonization of protocols.

papers.title: Dietary interaction of soybean oil and high starch impairs growth performance via metabolic-inflammatory dysregulation in Siberian sturgeon ( Acipenser baerii ).
papers.abstract: Sturgeons, ancient fish and the source of caviar, are ecologically and economically vital in aquaculture. To enhance feed efficiency, the use of cost-effective non-protein ingredients such as soybean oil and starch has gained growing attention. This study investigated the effects of oil sources and starch levels on growth, lipid metabolism, and inflammation in Siberian sturgeon ( Acipenser baerii ). Four isonitrogenous and isolipidic diets were formulated: fish oil diet with low starch level (FOLS), soybean oil diet with low starch level (SOLS), fish oil diet with high starch level (FOHS), and soybean oil diet with high starch level (SOHS). A total of 240 fish (initial weight: 182.87 ± 0.24 g) were used in a 10-week feeding trial. They were randomly assigned to 12 tanks, with three replicates per diet. Results showed that oil source had no significant effect on growth performance (final body weight [BWf], weight gain rate [WGR], and specific growth rate [SGR], P > 0.05), but high starch significantly reduced final body weight, weight gain rate, and specific growth rate ( P < 0.05). Both soybean oil and high starch independently increased feeding rate and feed conversion ratio ( P < 0.05), with their interaction further reducing these two indexes ( P < 0.05). High starch diets disrupted lipid metabolism. Specifically, they elevated hepatosomatic index, serum triglycerides (TG), total cholesterol (TC), and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol ( P < 0.05), along with increased expression of hepatic genes related to fatty acid β-oxidation ( pparα , P = 0.001). Soybean oil also promoted fatty acid β-oxidation ( pparα and cpt1α , P < 0.05), and in combination with high starch, enhanced lipolysis ( lpl , P = 0.042). Meanwhile, high starch upregulated the expression of pro-inflammatory gene ( il1β , P = 0.020). The mRNA expression results indicated that the soybean oil-high starch combination further aggravated inflammation alongside enhanced fatty acid oxidation, ultimately impairing growth. A principal component analysis (PCA) analysis of the lipidome showed that the serum lipid profile was significantly affected by the oil source ( P = 0.004). Seven metabolites were identified as commonly differentially abundant. Notably, phosphatidylethanolamine [PE (18:0_20:4) and PE (18:0_18:1)] and ceramide phosphate [CerP (d39:2)] were positively correlated with levels of TG, TC, and the expression of β-oxidation and inflammatory genes ( P < 0.05), suggesting their potential key roles in lipid-inflammatory dysregulation. In conclusion, dietary soybean oil and high starch interact to modulate serum lipid molecules, enhance fatty acid β-oxidation and inflammation, reduce feed efficiency, and suppress growth. Therefore, careful regulation of starch levels is essential when substituting fish oil with soybean oil in sturgeon aquafeed formulations.

papers.title: Leptin Insensitivity in NAFLD Is Produced by Oxidative Stress and Cytokine Overexpression.
papers.abstract: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) pathogenesis is caused by an imbalance in the biochemistry and immunology of the liver. The aim of the present study was to evaluate the role of oxidative stress and inflammatory factors in the serum concerning leptin concentration. This study was carried out on 67 females, including 20 healthy and 47 patients diagnosed by liver scan. Anthropometric analysis and routine biochemical tests, including alanine and aspartate transaminase, triglycerides, cholesterol, fasting blood sugar, low-density lipoprotein, high-density lipoprotein, and their ratio, were carried out. Also, the concentration of malondialdehyde and total antioxidant capacity concentration as well as the activity of catalase, superoxide dismutase, and glutathione peroxidase, were estimated. In addition, the concentration of leptin, interleukin-6, and tumor necrosis factor-α was analyzed. Data were analyzed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post-hoc test, with P <0.05 considered statistically significant.
