Patients with NAFLD had significantly higher BMI (33.63±6.37 kg/m² vs. 25.33±2.53 kg/m²), waist circumference (90.6±9.85 cm vs. 81.38±5.44 cm), and hip circumference (93.43±10.06 cm vs. 86.14±5.57 cm) compared with controls ( P <0.05). Their lipid profile showed elevated triglycerides (209.12±73.41 mg/dl vs. 121.19±38.51 mg/dl) and cholesterol (229.73±43.42 mg/dl vs. 171.19±22.91 mg/dl), as well as a higher prevalence of diabetes mellitus (30%). Although total antioxidant capacity did not differ ( P >0.05), MDA levels were significantly increased from controls (1.01±0.22 nmol/L) to Grade 1 (1.24±0.41 nmol/L), Grade 2 (1.33±0.32 nmol/L), and Grade 3 NAFLD (1.43±0.44 nmol/L), while SOD, CAT, and GPx activities were reduced (all P <0.05). IL 6, TNF α, and leptin concentrations were markedly elevated from grade 1 to 3, with the highest at Grade 3 (17.63±10.19 pg/mL, 104.63 ± 14.43 ng/mL, and 2.23±0.92 μg/mL, respectively, for each one; P <0.05). Although leptin controls fat metabolism via satiety, results revealed that the overproduction of leptin might be a consequence of oxidative stress and inflammatory response to fat accumulation in the liver. Therefore, measuring leptin along with IL-6 and TNF-α might help to diagnose liver injury.

papers.title: Glyoxalase 1 (GLO1) Deficiency Is Associated with Myeloid Skewing and Altered Inflammatory Responses.
papers.abstract: Glyoxalase 1 (GLO1) is involved in cellular adaptation to metabolic and oxidative stress, however, its role in regulating immune homeostasis remains poorly understood. Here, we used Glo1 knockout (Glo1-KO) mice to investigate the effects of GLO1 deficiency on bone marrow (BM) hematopoietic composition and the pulmonary inflammation environment. Flow cytometric analysis revealed alterations in BM myeloid-derived suppressor cell population, in Glo1-KO mice. In the lung GLO1 deficiency was accompanied by increased expression of inflammation and tissue-remodeling-associated genes, indicating an altered pulmonary inflammation milieu. Together, these findings demonstrate that GLO1 deficiency is associated with coordinated changes in hematopoietic immune environments and suggest that GLO1 may influence immune regulation across hematopoietic and peripheral tissue compartments.

papers.title: Gut microbiota and serum metabolomics in children with human parainfluenza virus infection.
papers.abstract: Based on gut microbiota and serum untargeted metabolomics analyses, this study investigated changes in gut microbiota structure and serum metabolic profiles in children infected with human parainfluenza virus (HPIV). By integrating multi-omics data, we aimed to explore interactions between gut dysbiosis and serum metabolic disorders, and their potential roles in HPIV pathogenesis, to provide preliminary evidence for microbiota--targeted and metabolic intervention strategies. Clinical data and laboratory results were collected from 230 hospitalized children (<14 years) with HPIV infection. Subsequently, 31 HPIV-infected children and 12 healthy controls were enrolled. Fecal samples were analyzed via 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and serum samples via liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS)-based untargeted metabolomics, followed by integrated multi-omics analysis. Children with severe HPIV infection had longer hospital stays and higher frequencies of wheezing, tachypnea, dyspnea, and vomiting. HPIV infection was associated with gut dysbiosis: opportunistic pathogens ( Anaerococcus , Peptoniphilus , Finegoldia ) were enriched, while beneficial commensals ( Blautia , Bifidobacterium , Faecalibacterium ) were reduced. Metabolomics identified 579 upregulated and 211 downregulated metabolites, primarily enriched in alpha-linolenic acid, butanoate, glycerophospholipid, starch/sucrose, and glycine/serine/threonine metabolism pathways. Correlation analysis showed that enriched opportunistic pathogens positively correlated with pro-inflammatory lipids (e.g., acetoacetic acid, 3-hydroxybutyric acid) and negatively with protective metabolites (e.g., alpha-linolenic acid, sucrose, L-threonine), while Blautia showed opposite patterns. The four key genera and five metabolites demonstrated exploratory discriminatory capacity for HPIV infection (AUC: 0.81 and 0.98, respectively), serving as candidate biomarkers for further validation. HPIV infection may be associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis and serum metabolic disturbances in children, potentially via the gut-lung axis, and these alterations may be involved in modulating pulmonary antiviral immune and inflammatory responses. This multi-omics study provides preliminary evidence for future research on prevention and treatment strategies targeting the gut microbiota or metabolic pathways in children with HPIV infection.

papers.title: Systematic identification of characteristic chemical constituents in Cistanches Herba from saline-alkali land based on hierarchical filtering of mass spectrometry data and spatial metabolomics technology.
papers.abstract: The traditional habitat of the Chinese medicinal plant Cistanches Herba (CH) is the deserts of northwestern China. Recently, CH cultivation has been introduced to saline-alkali land (SAL) in the Yellow River delta region. However, the effects of this SAL environment on the accumulation of secondary metabolites in CH remain unclear. This research aims to systematically characterize the chemical profiles of CH grown in SAL and to identify key chemical markers associated with the SAL environment. CH samples were collected from both SAL and traditional sandy land (SL). Untargeted metabolomics was performed using ultra performance liquid chromatography-quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry (UPLC-QTOF-MS) to characterize the global metabolic profiles of CH from two habitats. Chemical markers associated with SAL environments were screened via weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA), targeted quantification by ultra performance liquid chromatography-triple quadrupole mass spectrometry (UPLC-TQ-MS), and compound loading contributions of principal component analysis (PCA). Subsequently, desorption electrospray ionization mass spectrometry imaging (DESI-MSI) was employed to visualize the in situ spatial distribution of partial screened constituents in mouse organs. Untargeted UPLC-QTOF-MS metabolomics identified 74 chemical constituents from CH samples, including 40 phenylethanoid glycosides, 13 iridoid glycosides, 9 lignans, and other minor constituents. Orthogonal projections to latent structures-discriminant analysis (OPLS-DA) clearly separated the SAL and SL sample groups, with 30 constituents showing prominent contributions to the discrimination. WGCNA revealed 23 metabolites correlated with SAL. By integrating these two screening methods, 12 constituents were preliminarily selected as candidate markers associated with SAL. Subsequently, combining PCA loading coefficients (with the PCA model validated by Kaiser-Meyer-Olkin and Bartlett's sphericity tests) and targeted UPLC-TQ-MS quantification, 4 constituents-verbascoside, echinacoside, isoacteoside, and pinoresinol- were ultimately identified as characteristic chemical markers, all exhibiting significantly higher levels in SAL samples. DESI-MSI results further demonstrated that echinacoside predominantly accumulated in brain tissue, whereas verbascoside or isoacteoside displayed the strongest ion signal in the lung. This study developed an integrated strategy that combines hierarchical filtering of mass spectrometry data to successfully identify 4 characteristic chemical markers of CH associated with SAL. This strategy provides a scientific basis for future quality control and resource development.

papers.title: SLC25A20 promotes tumor growth by reprogramming energy metabolism in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Accumulating evidence has shown that the dysfunction of mitochondria, the multifunctional organelles in various cellular processes, is a pivotal event in the development of various diseases, including human cancers. The molecular alterations in tumors that promote metabolic diversity and distinct targetable dependencies remain poorly defined. The mitochondrial transporter SLC25A20, also known as carnitine-acylcarnitine translocase (CACT), is crucial for fatty acid β-oxidation (FAO) by importing acylcarnitines into the mitochondrial matrix. Here, we demonstrate that SLC25A20 is significantly upregulated in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) tissues and cells, and its expression correlates with poor patient survival. Gain- and loss-of-function experiments reveal that SLC25A20 promotes tumor cell proliferation, survival, migration, and invasion by enhancing FAO-associated mitochondrial bioenergetics and suppressing apoptosis. Mechanistically, SLC25A20-mediated FAO maintains mitochondrial function and supports oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), thereby sustaining tumor bioenergetics and redox homeostasis. Pharmacological inhibition or genetic silencing of SLC25A20 impairs tumor growth in vivo. These findings establish SLC25A20 as a key metabolic driver in LUAD and suggest it may be a therapeutic target.

papers.title: [Mechanisms and Clinical Translation Advances of Physical Targeted Therapy  for Malignant Pleural Effusion].
papers.abstract: Malignant pleural effusion (MPE) is a common severe complication of advanced lung cancer and significantly worsens prognosis. Physical targeted therapies, represented by piezocatalytic therapy, sonodynamic therapy, photodynamic therapy, hyperthermic intrathoracic chemotherapy, radiofrequency ablation and thermosensitive in situ hydrogel drug delivery system, induce reactive oxygen species generation via light, ultrasound, or piezocatalytic energy, or achieve tumor killing through local hyperthermia and temperature-controlled drug release, offering new strategies for MPE. However, existing reviews mostly focus on single modalities, lacking systematic classification and suitability comparison based on the pleural microenvironment and respiratory mechanics. This review summarizes their mechanisms, biological effects, and translational status in the context of pleural anatomy and pathological microenvironment, and highlights multi-field combination, microenvironment remodeling, and precise energy regulation as future directions for MPE therapy. . 【中文题目：物理靶向治疗恶性胸腔积液的机制 与临床转化进展】 【中文摘要：恶性胸腔积液（malignant pleural effusion, MPE）是晚期肺癌常见严重并发症，显著影响患者预后。以压电催化、声动力、光动力、胸腔热灌注、射频消融及温度响应水凝胶为代表的物理靶向治疗，通过光、声、压电等能量诱导活性氧生成，或借助局部高温及温控释药继而实现肿瘤杀伤，为MPE治疗提供了新策略。但现有综述多聚焦单一物理技术，缺乏基于胸膜腔特殊微环境及呼吸力学特征的系统分类与适配性比较。本文结合胸膜腔特殊解剖与病理微环境，系统阐述上述技术的作用机制、生物学效应及转化现状，指出多物理场联合、微环境重塑与精准能量调控是未来方向，以期为MPE治疗提供参考。 】 【中文关键词：恶性胸腔积液；物理靶向治疗；压电催化治疗；声动力治疗；光动力治疗】.

papers.title: [Mechanism of NUF2 in Promoting NSCLC Progression  through the Regulation of Ferroptosis].
papers.abstract: NUF2 component of NDC80 kinetochore complex (NUF2) is a core regulatory protein that ensures proper chromosome segregation, and its aberrant expression is closely associated with cancer initiation and progression. Although the expression level of NUF2 is higher in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) than in normal tissues, its mechanism of action in NSCLC remains unclear. This study aims to investigate the mechanism by which NUF2 promotes the proliferation, migration, and invasion of NSCLC. The expression differences of NUF2 between NSCLC and normal lung tissues as well as the correlation between NUF2 expression and overall survival (OS) of NSCLC patients were analyzed via the Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis (GEPIA) database. Immunohistochemical (IHC) staining was performed to detect the positive expression rate of NUF2 in NSCLC specimens. NUF2 knockdown and overexpression stable cell lines were established in the A549 cell line, and transfection efficiency was verified by Western blot (WB) and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR). The proliferation, migration, and invasion of transfected cells were assessed using the cell counting kit-8 (CCK-8), colony formation assay, wound healing assay, and Transwell assay. The expression levels of ferroptosis-related proteins were determined using WB and RT-qPCR. Commercial assay kits were utilized to measure the contents of malondialdehyde (MDA), reactive oxygen species (ROS), ferrous ion (Fe²+) and glutathione (GSH), while intracellular mitochondrial structural alterations were visualized by transmission electron microscopy (TEM). Xenograft tumor models were established. The expression levels of NUF2, SLC7A11 and ACSL4 were detected by WB, RT‑qPCR and IHC. GEPIA analysis revealed that NUF2 was significantly highly expressed in NSCLC (P<0.05) and was associated with OS (P<0.001). Clinical statistical analyses demonstrated that upregulated NUF2 was significantly associated with advanced clinical stage (P<0.05) and lymph node metastasis (P<0.01). NUF2 knockdown markedly suppressed the proliferation, migration and invasion of NSCLC cells (P<0.001) and reduced xenograft tumor volume in vivo (P<0.05). Mechanistically, NUF2 silencing downregulated the expression of the ferroptosis master regulator SLC7A11 (P<0.01) while upregulating ACSL4 (P<0.01). The levels of MDA (P<0.01), ROS and Fe²+ (P<0.001) were all elevated following NUF2 knockdown, while the content of GSH decreased (P<0.001). TEM observation revealed that NUF2 knockdown led to mitochondrial shrinkage, reduced cristae number and increased membrane density. Conversely, NUF2 overexpression enhanced NSCLC cell proliferation, migration and invasion (P<0.001) and increased xenograft tumor volume (P<0.001). Meanwhile, SLC7A11 expression was elevated (P<0.01) and ACSL4 expression was decreased (P<0.01). The levels of ROS (P<0.001), MDA and Fe²+ were decreased (P<0.01), and the GSH level was increased (P<0.01). NUF2 is highly expressed in NSCLC and is closely associated with poor prognosis and lymph node metastasis. NUF2 inhibits ferroptosis by upregulating SLC7A11 expression and downregulating ACSL4 expression, thereby promoting the proliferation, migration, and invasion of NSCLC. 【中文题目：NUF2通过调控铁死亡促进 NSCLC进展的机制研究】 【中文摘要：背景与目的 NUF2（NUF2 component of NDC80 kinetochore complex）是确保染色体正确分离的核心调控蛋白，其异常表达与癌症的发生、发展密切关联。NUF2在非小细胞肺癌（non-small cell lung cancer, NSCLC）中表达水平高于正常组织，其在NSCLC中的作用机制尚未明确。本研究旨在探究NUF2促进NSCLC增殖、迁移和侵袭的作用机制。方法 GEPIA（Gene Expression Profiling Interactive Analysis）数据库分析NUF2在NSCLC组织与正常组织中的表达差异以及NUF2表达水平与患者总生存期的关系；通过免疫组化染色检测NSCLC组织中NUF2的阳性表达率并分析其与患者临床病理特征之间的关系。在A549细胞系中建立NUF2敲低和过表达稳转株，通过蛋白质免疫印迹（Western blot, WB）和实时荧光定量聚合酶链式反应（quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction, RT-qPCR）验证转染效率；采用细胞增殖与毒性检测试剂盒（cell counting kit-8, CCK-8）、平板克隆实验、划痕实验和Transwell实验分别检测转染后细胞的增殖、迁移和侵袭的情况；通过WB和RT-qPCR检测调控铁死亡相关蛋白SLC7A11和ACSL4的表达水平；相应试剂盒检测丙二醛（malondialdehyde, MDA）、活性氧（reactive oxygen species, ROS）、亚铁离子（ferrous ions, Fe2+）和还原型谷胱甘肽（reduced glutathione, GSH）的含量，透射电镜（transmission electron microscopy, TEM）观察细胞内线粒体数量和结构变化。建立异种移植瘤动物模型，WB、RT-qPCR和免疫组化检测NUF2、SLC7A11和ACSL4的表达情况。结果 GEPIA数据库分析结果显示NUF2在NSCLC中显著高表达（P<0.05），并与患者总生存期呈负向关联（P<0.001）。免疫组化统计结果表明，NUF2高表达与患者的临床分期高（P<0.05）和淋巴结转移（P<0.01）有关。NUF2敲低后NSCLC的增殖、迁移、侵袭能力降低（P<0.001），移植瘤体积减小（P<0.05），NUF2敲低后调节铁死亡的关键分子SLC7A11表达降低（P<0.01）、ACSL4则升高（P<0.01），MDA（P<0.01）、ROS以及细胞Fe2+含量（P<0.001）均升高，而GSH含量降低（P<0.001），TEM观察发现敲低NUF2使线粒体缩小、嵴减少和膜密度增加。过表达NUF2后NSCLC的增殖、迁移、侵袭能力升高（P<0.001），移植瘤体积增大（P<0.001），SLC7A11表达升高（P<0.01）、ACSL4则降低（P<0.01），ROS（P<0.001）、MDA以及细胞Fe2+含量均降低（P<0.01），GSH含量升高（P<0.01）。结论 NUF2在NSCLC中高表达与患者预后差及易发生淋巴结转移密切关联，NUF2可能通过上调SLC7A11和下调ACSL4的表达抑制铁死亡，从而促进NSCLC的增殖、迁移、侵袭。 】 【中文关键词：肺肿瘤；NUF2；SLC7A11；ACSL4；铁死亡】.

papers.title: Tongsai Granules Ameliorate Airway Mucus Hypersecretion in AECOPD by Remodeling LIPA-Driven Ceramide Metabolism.
papers.abstract: Tongsai Granules (TSG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula traditionally used for the treatment of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) with phlegm-heat obstructing lung syndrome, a condition characterized by cough, excessive sputum production, and dyspnea; however, its underlying therapeutic mechanisms remain unclear. To investigate the mechanisms by which TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD through regulation of the LIPA/ceramide axis. A murine AECOPD model and airway epithelial cells were used. Proteomic and lipidomic analyses, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and LIPA overexpression and knockdown assays were performed. TSG improved pulmonary function, attenuated lung injury and inflammation, and suppressed MUC5AC expression in AECOPD mice. Multi-omics analyses showed that TSG regulated lipid metabolism and reduced triglyceride and ceramide accumulation while downregulating lysosomal acid lipase A (LIPA). Several serum-exposed constituents of TSG inhibited MUC5AC expression. Bergenin (BER) was selected as a representative bioactive constituent for subsequent target-identification and mechanistic studies. Molecular docking, SPR, and DARTS assays demonstrated direct interaction between BER and LIPA. LIPA knockdown suppressed MUC5AC expression, whereas LIPA overexpression attenuated the inhibitory effect of BER. Moreover, exogenous ceramide reversed BER-mediated suppression of MUC5AC. TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD by targeting the LIPA/ceramide axis. Bergenin directly targets LIPA to regulate lipid metabolism and suppress MUC5AC overexpression.

papers.title: CAND1 Promotes Lung Cancer Tumorigenesis by Mitochondrial DNA Release mediated Neutrophil Infiltration.
papers.abstract: CAND1, a conserved regulator of cullin-RING ubiquitin ligases, has been well characterized in protein homeostasis, but its functional role in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains largely unknown. Bioinformatic and clinical analyses assessed CAND1 expression and prognostic significance. Multiplex immunofluorescence and flow cytometry evaluated neutrophil infiltration and activation. Transwell assays and flow cytometry assessed neutrophil migration and NETosis. CAND1-modulated LUAD cells were used to examine mitochondrial remodeling, mtDNA release, cGAS-STING/NF-κB signaling, and chemokine expression, and Xenograft models to assess tumor growth and neutrophil involvement in vivo. CAND1 is upregulated across multiple solid tumors, and its elevated expression is associated with poor prognosis in LUAD patients, as validated by public datasets and clinical cohort. CAND1 expression correlates with increased neutrophil infiltration and activation, which is further validated by co-culture experiments with isolated neutrophils and CAND1-overexpressing tumor cells. Mechanistically, CAND1 promotes mitophagy, leading to mtDNA release and sustained activation of the cGAS-STING/NF-κB signaling axis. STING knockdown markedly attenuated CAND1-associated neutrophil migration and reduced the expression of neutrophil-recruiting chemokines, including CCL5, CCL7, CXCL1, CXCL5, and CXCL8. In vivo, CAND1 overexpression accelerates xenograft tumor growth and enhances intratumoral neutrophil infiltration, while neutrophil depletion partially attenuates CAND1-associated tumor growth, supporting a functional contribution of neutrophils to CAND1-associated tumor progression. CAND1 links mitophagy to immune remodeling through cGAS-STING activation and subsequent chemokine-mediated neutrophil recruitment, establishing it as a key regulator of LUAD progression.

papers.title: Targeting oncogenic SOX2 condensates suppresses squamous cell carcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: Squamous cell carcinomas (SCCs) comprise a group of lethal malignancies, yet developing SCC-specific therapies remains challenging, largely due to a lack of druggable targets. We identify SOX2 condensation as a shared cancer hallmark across esophageal, head and neck, and lung SCCs. Within SOX2, the activation domain 1 (AD1) acts as the condensate-promoting region via its aromatic and hydrophobic residues. Site-specific mutagenesis, orthotopic mouse models, and multi-omics sequencing demonstrate that SOX2 condensates upregulate oncogene expression by enhancing SOX2 chromatin occupancy, H3K27ac enrichment, and chromatin interactions at oncogenic loci such as FGFR2, thereby promoting SCC progression. An FDA-approved drug screen reveals that the proteasome inhibitor ixazomib disrupts SOX2 condensates in an HSP70-dependent manner. Upon ixazomib treatment, the substrate-binding domain of HSP70 blocks SOX2 AD1, selectively dissolving SOX2 condensates, downregulating oncogene expression, and suppressing condensate-positive SCC patient-derived xenografts. These findings highlight targeting SOX2 condensates with proteasome inhibitors as an SCC-specific, biomarker-guided therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: The Potential Role of Gut Microbiota in Combating Mycobacterium tuberculosis Infection.
papers.abstract: Tuberculosis (TB) is a chronic infectious disease caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis ( M.TB ) infection. Although there have been significant advances in the treatment of M.TB infection, it still faces significant challenges. The gut microbiota is a highly complex ecosystem that plays an important role in regulating metabolism, immune regulation, and maintaining healthy balance in the human body. More and more studies have found that while gut microbiota regulates the immune regulation process of pulmonary TB through the "gut-lung axis," infection with M.TB can also affect the microbial stability of gut microbiota, thereby affecting host health. This article summarized and discussed the changes of gut flora in TB patients, the possible relationship and impact between gut flora and M.TB infection, and summarized and looked forward to the potential of gut flora in the treatment of TB, in order to provide a reference for the prevention and treatment of gut microorganisms in anti- M.TB infection.

papers.title: Molecular Insights and Therapeutic Potential of Benzothiazole Derivatives: A Comprehensive Pharmacological Review.
papers.abstract: Benzothiazole (BTA), a fused bicyclic heterocycle of thiazole and benzene units, has become a special scaffold for medicinal chemistry with a vast pharmacological profile. Structural modification at the benzothiazole core provides enormous flexibility toward rationalizing bioactivity in a wide range of therapeutics. Contemporary research is exemplified by benzothiazole derivatives as potent antibacterial agents, efficiently targeting multidrug-resistant pathogens by mechanisms like DNA gyrase inhibition and membrane disruption. They also exhibit multi-target-directed ligand- based anti-Alzheimer's activity by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, butyrylcholinesterase, monoamine oxidases, and β-secretase enzymes. In cancer, benzothiazole hybrids are found to be selectively cytotoxic toward different cancer cell lines, such as breast, lung, and liver cancers, and are generally more active than the traditional drugs. Anti-tubercular activity presents superior inhibition of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including, Multidrug-resistance (MDR) and Extensively Drug- Resistance (XDR), by novel hybrid conjugates and heterocyclic linkages. Additionally, benzothiazole analogues exhibit anti-inflammatory and anti-diabetic activity with cyclooxygenase, Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4), α-glucosidase, and α-amylase enzyme inhibitory activity. Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) analysis consistently indicates that electron-withdrawing or electron-donating functions, linker type, and heteroatom position in modulating pharmacological activity. Recent patents reflect sustained innovation in drug design with the benzothiazole motif, and therapeutic applications exist in antimicrobial, anticancer, neuroprotection, and metabolic disorders. Overall, these findings place emphasis on benzothiazole derivatives as highly effective lead templates with immense therapeutic value, warranting further consideration towards clinical usefulness.

papers.title: Comprehensive cardiac, vascular, and pulmonary characterization of a cardiometabolic HFpEF model.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous syndrome in which translational progress is limited by experimental models that insufficiently reflect the cardiometabolic phenotype while affecting endogenous endothelial function. We aimed to characterize a cardiometabolic "two-hit" HFpEF model combining metabolic stress (db/db) with chronic mineralocorticoid excess (d-aldosterone), focusing on integrated cardiac, vascular, and pulmonary phenotyping. Female db/db mice received 4-week d-aldosterone (0.3 µg/h) or vehicle via osmotic minipumps. Metabolic profiling, high-resolution echocardiography including strain and left atrial mechanics, invasive right-heart catheterization, and thoracic aortic wire myography were performed. Aldosterone-treated db/db mice developed cardiac hypertrophy and pulmonary congestion with preserved LVEF but marked diastolic dysfunction, left atrial remodeling with increased stiffness, and impaired global longitudinal LV strain. Pulmonary hypertension with right ventricular dysfunction was evidenced by elevated RVSP/estimated mPAP, reduced PAT/PET, and reduced TAPSE. Thoracic aortae from untreated db/db mice already showed impaired endothelium-dependent relaxation, which was further aggravated by aldosterone, whereas maximal endothelium-independent relaxation remained largely preserved. The db/db+d-aldosterone model recapitulates key features of cardiometabolic HFpEF across the cardiac-vascular-pulmonary axis and provides a translational platform for mechanistic and therapeutic studies targeting endothelial and ventricular-vascular dysfunction in HFpEF. New & Noteworthy: Current HFpEF animal models often limit the investigation of vascular dysfunction, a central component of cardiometabolic HFpEF. We provide a comprehensive functional characterization of a db/db+d-aldosterone two-hit model demonstrating obesity, diabetes, diastolic dysfunction, atrial remodeling, endothelial dysfunction, pulmonary hypertension, and right ventricular impairment. By preserving endogenous endothelial nitric oxide signaling, this model offers a translational platform for studying vascular and cardiopulmonary mechanisms in cardiometabolic HFpEF.

papers.title: Management of Severe Dentoalveolar Trauma Following a Motorcycle Accident With Immediate Ridge Preservation and Delayed Implant Rehabilitation: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Severe dentoalveolar trauma resulting from high-energy motorcycle accidents presents significant clinical challenges because of the combined injuries to the teeth, alveolar bone, and surrounding soft tissues and the potential for associated injuries beyond the oral cavity. This case report describes the staged management of a healthy male patient who presented following a motorcycle accident. Clinical and radiographic examinations revealed multiple non-restorable teeth involving the maxillary and mandibular anterior regions, accompanied by traumatic alveolar fractures and associated bone defects. Initial dental management included extraction of the non-restorable teeth, thorough irrigation with sterile saline, conservative debridement of nonviable fractured alveolar bone while preserving viable residual bone, and immediate ridge preservation using a bovine xenograft covered with a resorbable collagen membrane to preserve the alveolar ridge architecture for future implant rehabilitation. The patient received postoperative antibiotic and anti-inflammatory therapy. Given the high-energy mechanism of injury and the possibility of associated injuries beyond the oral cavity, prompt medical evaluation was recommended. Following uneventful healing and adequate maturation of the preserved ridges, dental implants were placed as part of a staged rehabilitation protocol. After the osseointegration period, the patient progressed to the prosthetic phase. Following second stage surgery and peri-implant soft tissue maturation, definitive implant-supported restorations were delivered, restoring esthetics, function, and occlusal relationships. Clinical and radiographic evaluations supported progression through the successive treatment phases, and the patient reported satisfaction with the final functional and esthetic outcome. This case illustrates a staged approach to severe dentoalveolar trauma involving careful assessment of traumatic injuries, preservation of viable alveolar structures, immediate ridge preservation in appropriately selected sites, and delayed implant-supported rehabilitation. In patients presenting after high-energy trauma, clinicians should also recognize the possibility of concomitant injuries and consider prompt medical evaluation before definitive dental management.

papers.title: IRP2 contributes to COPD-associated hypoxic epithelial injury through regulation of Sestrin2-related stress responses and ferroptosis.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is characterized by persistent oxidative stress and airway epithelial injury. However, the molecular mechanisms linking iron metabolism and cellular stress responses in COPD remain unclear. This study aimed to investigate the role of iron regulatory protein 2 (IRP2) in COPD-associated epithelial injury. 16HBE and A549 cells were exposed to cigarette smoke extract (CSE) under a COPD-associated hypoxic microenvironment. IRP2 was silenced using shRNA, and Sestrin2 restoration experiments were performed. Cellular injury was evaluated by cell viability, ROS production, inflammatory cytokines, intracellular Fe²⁺ accumulation, ferroptosis-related proteins, and NRF2 activation. CSE exposure under a COPD-associated hypoxic microenvironment induced epithelial injury, accompanied by increased oxidative stress, inflammation, iron accumulation, and ferroptosis-related changes. IRP2 silencing alleviated these alterations and enhanced NRF2 nuclear activation with increased expression of antioxidant proteins. Restoration of Sestrin2 partially reversed the protective effects induced by IRP2 depletion. Furthermore, pharmacological inhibition of ferroptosis attenuated epithelial injury. IRP2 contributes to COPD-associated epithelial injury by regulating oxidative stress, iron homeostasis, and ferroptosis-related responses, providing new insights into the molecular mechanisms underlying COPD progression. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10616-026-01066-9.

papers.title: In silico insights into shared molecular mechanisms and drug repurposing for non‑small cell lung cancer and tuberculosis.
papers.abstract: Non‑small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and tuberculosis (TB) represent major global health burdens, with evidence of a molecular interconnection. To understand their shared mechanisms, we integrated three NSCLC and two TB RNA‑seq datasets and identified 33 common differentially expressed genes (cDEGs). Enrichment analyses, protein-protein interaction (PPI) network mapping, cancer‑specific validations, and survival analyses were performed on all cDEGs. The PPI network highlighted KIF18A, ANLN, TLR4, EPAS1 , and DLC1 as central hub genes, with enrichment pointing to immune‑inflammatory signaling, epithelial remodeling, and cell‑cycle regulation as key processes underlying NSCLC-TB comorbidity. Profiling of lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) and lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC), accounting for about 80% of NSCLC, showed KIF18A, ANLN, STIL , and GALNT14 overexpression linked to advanced stage and poor survival, with 4-14% alterations mainly from mRNA upregulation. Leveraging their network centrality and prognostic significance, KIF18A and ANLN were selected as receptor targets for structure‑based drug screening. A library of 213 anti‑NSCLC, anti‑TB, and antimicrobial compounds was screened against these targets using AutoDock and Glide, followed by pharmacokinetic and toxicity assessment. Levofloxacin (targeting ANLN) and Capmatinib (targeting KIF18A) exhibited the most favorable docking scores and ADME/Tox profiles, with stable binding modes, favorable MM-GBSA binding free energies, and refined dynamic cross-correlation and free-energy landscapes over 100 ns molecular dynamics simulations, nominating them as promising in silico predicted drug agents relevant to both NSCLC and TB. Our in silico transcriptomic and structural‑dynamics analysis reveals shared infection-cancer mechanisms and identifies candidate therapeutics for further evaluation. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40203-026-00767-5.

papers.title: Pharmacophore modelling-based screening of natural allosteric EGFR inhibitors using molecular docking, DFT, and molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.abstract: The development of allosteric inhibitors is a promising strategy for targeting epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR) mutations in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), especially in cases where orthosteric inhibitors face resistance. However, despite their selective inhibition of EGFR mutations, fourth-generation allosteric inhibitors show limited antiproliferative efficacy without cetuximab. The present study aims to identify potent natural product-derived allosteric inhibitors for NSCLC using a comprehensive approach, including pharmacophore modelling, Lipinski's Rule of Five (Ro5), ADMET profiling, density functional theory, and molecular docking. Experimentally validated EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) were used to build a pharmacophore model. The validated pharmacophore model was used to screen the Natural Product Activity and Species Source database. Drug-likeness was assessed using Ro5 and ADMET to predict pharmacokinetic and toxicity profiles for further drug development. Molecular docking studies revealed that the identified natural compounds exhibited more favorable docking scores (-8.74 to -7.87 kcal/mol) than the co-crystallized ligand (-7.32 kcal/mol), indicating significant interactions with the receptor residues. Geometry optimization, electrostatic potential, and frontier molecular orbital analyses were performed to assess potential reactive sites and molecular stability. Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations, subsequent post-MD analyses, and binding free energy calculations provided additional support for these findings. The free-energy landscape revealed stable, favorable binding conformations, suggesting that they may act as allosteric inhibitors. These results highlight the potential of natural compounds to combat resistance to EGFR-TKIs in NSCLC. In particular, compounds 1 and 2 emerged as promising candidates targeting mutant EGFR and warrant further experimental validation as potential leads for NSCLC treatment.

papers.title: Suspected Bulbar-Predominant Myasthenia Gravis Exacerbation in an Older Adult With Respiratory Deterioration and Silent Aspiration: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterized by fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness. Bulbar-predominant exacerbations may be difficult to recognize in older adults with multiple comorbidities, particularly when respiratory deterioration is initially attributed to cardiopulmonary disease. We report the case of an 83-year-old woman with generalized acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive MG, dementia with behavioral disturbance, moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), chronic kidney disease, and previous deep vein thrombosis who was admitted to a psychiatric unit because of worsening paranoia and suspected delusions. During hospitalization, she developed progressive hypoxemia requiring transfer to the medical ward. Initial evaluation considered pulmonary infection, aspiration-related complications, and COPD exacerbation. Neurological examination subsequently demonstrated new predominantly facial and bulbar weakness with preserved limb strength, accompanied by progressive dysphagia and impaired secretion clearance. Videofluoroscopic swallow study demonstrated significant silent aspiration of thin and mildly thickened liquids; however, the etiology of the dysphagia and aspiration remained potentially multifactorial. Serial arterial blood gases demonstrated persistent hypercapnia; however, stable PaCO₂ values, preserved pH, markedly elevated bicarbonate, and positive base excess suggested a substantial chronic hypercapnic component with concomitant metabolic alkalosis, with underlying COPD representing an important potential contributor. In the context of known generalized MG and newly documented facial and bulbar dysfunction, a suspected bulbar-predominant myasthenic exacerbation was considered a potentially important contributor within a multifactorial respiratory deterioration rather than the sole cause. She was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin and escalation of corticosteroid therapy. Although her respiratory status stabilized, persistent bulbar dysfunction, dysphagia, and frailty remained, and following goals-of-care discussions, the family elected hospice care. This case emphasizes the diagnostic complexity of respiratory deterioration in older patients with MG and the importance of recognizing new bulbar dysfunction while carefully considering competing pulmonary, aspiration-related, cardiogenic, and functional contributors.

papers.title: Global Landscape of Clinical Studies Open to Enrollment in Carbon Ion Radiotherapy: A PTCOG Review.
papers.abstract: Radiotherapy with high linear energy transfer (LET) has shown promise for improving cancer outcomes. Carbon ion radiotherapy (CIRT) combines charged-particle dose conformality with enhanced biological effectiveness. However, clinical development remains constrained by limited center availability, modest trial accrual, and few randomized studies. We reviewed the global landscape of CIRT studies open to enrollment to identify current priorities and gaps. This Particle Therapy Cooperative Group (PTCOG)-sanctioned project, conducted within the CIRT Guidelines Subcommittee, identified studies through registry review and institutional verification. ClinicalTrials.gov and the Japan Registry of Clinical Trials were searched from December 2025 through February 2026. We included interventional CIRT trials and prospective registries open to new enrollment and excluded studies not open to enrollment, retrospective cohorts, proton-only studies, and preclinical studies. Thirty-six studies were identified: 35 interventional trials in 6 countries and 1 North American registry-based comparative-effectiveness study. Japan had the largest share, followed by Germany, China, Italy, Austria, and France. Three centers (SPHIC, QST, and HIT) accounted for 21 of 36 studies. The portfolio included 7 phase I, 23 phase II, 5 phase III, and 1 registry study. Pancreatic cancer and sarcoma-related tumors each accounted for 7 studies; head and neck cancers, 5; prostate and breast cancers, 3 each; glioblastoma, lung cancer, and gynecologic malignancies, 2 each; and mucosal melanoma, mixed solid tumors, kidney cancer, esophageal cancer, and hepatocellular carcinoma, 1 each. Most studies were conducted at a single institution and emphasized feasibility, toxicity, local control, progression-free survival, or overall survival. This expert-verified inventory shows that CIRT studies open to enrollment remain concentrated by center, disease site, and phase. Future progress may depend more on shared outcome definitions, transparent biological dose reporting, and registry-enabled or multicenter comparative designs than on additional isolated single-institution studies.

papers.title: Akkermansia muciniphila and Its Extracellular Vesicles Alleviate LPS-Induced Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome in Rats: Integrated Microbiome, Metabolomic, and Transcriptomic Analyses.
papers.abstract: Akkermansia muciniphila (AKK) and its extracellular vesicles (EVs) have immunomodulatory and metabolic effects, but their protective effects in acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) remain unclear. This study compared live AKK with AKK-EVs and investigated their effects on LPS-induced ARDS using integrated microbiome, metabolome, and lung transcriptome analyses. An ARDS rat model was established by intratracheal instillation of lipopolysaccharide (LPS). Rats were randomly allocated to the control, ARDS, AKK, and EVs groups. Following model establishment, AKK or AKK-EVs were administered orally once daily for 7 consecutive days. Lung injury was evaluated by body weight, hematoxylin and eosin staining, lung wet/dry weight ratio, and bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) analysis. Fecal 16S rRNA sequencing, untargeted metabolomics, lung transcriptomics, and integrated multi-omics analyses were performed. The pulmonary expression of Il17a, Cxcl1, Tnf, and Il6 was validated by qRT-PCR. Compared with the ARDS group, AKK and AKK-EVs attenuated weight loss and lung histopathological injury and reduced the lung wet/dry weight ratio, BALF total cell count and protein concentration, and BALF IL-17A and TNF-α levels. Both interventions partially remodeled the gut microbial community, including changes in Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136_group, norank_f_Muribaculaceae, Bacteroides, and Escherichia-Shigella. Metabolomic changes mainly involved lipid, amino acid, and bile acid metabolism. Lung transcriptomic analysis identified differential enrichment of the IL-17, TNF, chemokine, and cytokine-cytokine receptor interaction pathways. qRT-PCR further showed increased Il17a, Cxcl1, Tnf, and Il6 expression in the ARDS group and reduced expression following AKK or AKK-EVs intervention. Integrated analyses identified associations among alterations in gut microbiota, metabolites, and pulmonary gene expression. AKK and AKK-EVs alleviated LPS-induced ARDS, accompanied by remodeling of gut microbial and metabolic profiles and attenuation of pulmonary IL-17- and TNF-related inflammatory signaling. AKK-EVs may represent a potential cell-free intervention for ARDS.

papers.title: Phosphorylation of IRS4 at YY111/112 promotes LUSC progression via PI3K/AKT pathway activation.
papers.abstract: Lung squamous cell carcinoma (LUSC) lacks effective targeted therapies despite frequent hyperactivation of the PI3K/AKT pathway, and the contribution of adaptor proteins to this process remains poorly defined. Here, we identify Insulin Receptor Substrate 4 (IRS4) as a common substrate of Src kinase and the phosphatase RPTPα, and uncover a previously unrecognized, conserved phosphorylation site at YY111/112 within the IRS4 PH domain. Src-mediated phosphorylation at this site is essential for IRS4-driven proliferation, anchorage-independent growth, and invasiveness in LUSC cells. Mechanistically, phosphorylation at YY111/112 induces conformational rearrangements in IRS4 that enhance the recruitment of the p85β SH2 domain to the YXXM motif of IRS4, thereby promoting AKT activation without altering IRS4 protein stability or subcellular distribution. An IRS4-derived cell-permeable phosphopeptide containing pYY111/112 disrupts the Src-IRS4 interaction and significantly suppresses tumor growth in vivo in a YY111/112-dependent manner. Consistently, YY111/112 phosphorylation is markedly elevated in human LUSC tissues and correlates with advanced disease stages. Collectively, these findings define a Src-IRS4-PI3K/AKT signaling axis and identify YY111/112 as a critical regulatory site of IRS4 and a potential therapeutic vulnerability in LUSC.

papers.title: Amifostine attenuates pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy and metabolic remodeling via the SIRT1/PPAR-α axis in rats.
papers.abstract: Pathological cardiac hypertrophy induced by chronic pressure overload is accompanied by significant metabolic disturbances, including impaired myocardial lipid metabolism. This study ascertained whether the cytoprotective agent amifostine (WR-2721) exerts cardioprotective effects along pressure overload-induced remodeling and whether these effects are linked to modulation of the SIRT1/PPAR-α axis. Male Wistar rats (n = 24) were assigned to Sham, abdominal aortic constriction (AAC), and AAC + amifostine (200 mg/kg, i.p., weekly for 8 weeks) groups, with amifostine administered concurrently with hypertrophic stress. The cardiac structure and function were appraised using echocardiography and histological analyses, with the expression of SIRT1, PPAR-α, and key regulators of lipid metabolism examined by Western blotting. Amifostine treatment was associated with attenuation of pressure overload-induced cardiac hypertrophy, reflected by lower heart and lung weight ratios, preservation of functional indices, and diminished myocardial fibrosis. At the molecular level, amifostine administration was accompanied by relative normalization of SIRT1 and PPAR-α expression, elevated levels of fatty acid oxidation-related proteins, and suppression of lipogenic markers. These findings suggest that amifostine mitigates pressure overload-induced cardiac remodeling and is associated with improved myocardial metabolic homeostasis, accompanied by favorable changes in the expression of SIRT1, PPAR-α, and lipid metabolism-related proteins. While these observations support the potential involvement of the SIRT1/PPAR-α signaling pathway, further mechanistic studies are required to establish its causal role in mediating the cardioprotective effects of amifostine.

papers.title: Alpha-ketoglutarate ameliorates systemic sclerosis-associated fibrosis by restoring endothelial function.
papers.abstract: Systemic sclerosis (SSc) is a devastating autoimmune disease characterized by multi-organ fibrosis with limited therapeutic options. Using targeted metabolomics, we first observed that levels of alpha-ketoglutarate (α-KG), a key TCA-cycle intermediate, were paradoxically elevated in bleomycin-induced fibrotic lungs and in TGF-β-stimulated fibroblasts, prompting us to test whether exogenous supplementation could augment this compensatory response. Using bleomycin-induced skin and lung fibrosis mouse models, we demonstrated that oral α-KG administration significantly attenuated dermal and pulmonary collagen deposition, reduced inflammatory infiltration, and improved survival. Although fibroblasts are conventionally regarded as the central effectors of fibrosis, integrated single-cell RNA sequencing and bulk transcriptomic deconvolution unexpectedly identified endothelial cells as the predominant cellular target of α-KG in fibrotic lungs. Consistently, α-KG restored endothelial cell proportions in vivo, rescued angiogenic function and preserved barrier integrity in association with upregulation of eNOS, and tight junction proteins in human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) treated with bleomycin. Mechanistically, α-KG suppressed TGF-β/Smad activation and reversed bleomycin-induced metabolic repression, including restoration of fatty acid oxidation signatures and mitochondrial ultrastructure, accompanied by upregulation of the mitochondrial biogenesis regulator NRF1. Collectively, these findings reveal that α-KG exerts broad anti-fibrotic effects in SSc models by protecting endothelial function and inhibiting canonical pro-fibrotic signaling, highlighting its potential as a translatable metabolic therapeutic strategy for SSc.

papers.title: Identification of priority gaseous component in biodiesel exhaust and its potential pulmonary hazards: a data-driven screening and validation strategy.
papers.abstract: Biodiesel is increasingly adopted as a renewable low-carbon fuel, yet the pulmonary toxicity of its exhaust-particularly the gaseous components-remains a critical knowledge gap. To address this, we developed an integrative strategy combining data-driven prioritization with experimental validation. Herein, we employ a multidimensional risk-ranking system that predicts pulmonary fibrosis as the top-ranked adverse outcome (weighted score: 1.00) and ranks formaldehyde as the highest-priority toxicant (weighted score: 0.94). Component-outcome association analysis further predicts aldehydes, particularly formaldehyde, as the top candidate driving pulmonary fibrosis, with an estimated 28% contribution. Both in vivo and in vitro validations demonstrate that biodiesel exhaust (BDE) gas exposure induces substantial pulmonary fibrogenic toxicity, with formaldehyde directly driving epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) in lung epithelial cells. By integrating quantitative proteomics with computational network toxicology, we identify TGF-β1 as a key mediator linking formaldehyde to fibrotic remodeling. This conclusion is further suppported by the upregulation of Tgfb1 expression both in vivo and in vitro. Moreover, analysis of a human Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis (IPF) single-cell dataset highlighted immature neutrophils as a candidate immune subset enriched for the formaldehyde-pulmonary fibrosis-associated gene signature. Overall, this study systematizes the pulmonary toxicity profile of BDE gaseous components and provides an evidence-based foundation for incorporating BDE-derived aldehydes, specifically formaldehyde, into health risk assessments and future emission control policies for biodiesel.

papers.title: Polyphenol-rich Salsola imbericata extract attenuates experimental lung injury via modulating oxidative stress, NLRP3 inflammasome activation and apoptosis singling.
papers.abstract: Salsola imbericata is a halophytic plant with promising yet underexplored pharmacological potential. The present study aimed to characterize the metabolite profile of its ethanolic extract (SI-EtOH) and evaluate its protective effects against experimentally induced lung injury. UPLC-PDA-ESI-TOF-MS/MS-based metabolomics enabled the tentative identification of 62 metabolites belonging to diverse classes, including phenolic acids and their glycosides, flavonoids (notably isorhamnetin derivatives), alkaloids, triterpenoid saponins, fatty acid amides, and organic acids. Pulmonary injury induction resulted in marked oxidative stress, evidenced by a significant increase in malondialdehyde (MDA) levels by 463.3% and a depletion of glutathione (GSH) by 94.2% compared to the control group. Treatment with SI-EtOH (200 and 400 mg/kg) significantly reduced MDA levels by 148.4% and 348.3%, respectively, and restored GSH levels by 26% and 59.8%. Inflammation was also significantly attenuated, with reductions in IL-1B by 148.4% and 348.3%, and IL-18 by 15.8% and 41.5% at the two dose levels, respectively. Furthermore, SI-EtOH suppressed NLRP3 inflammasome activation by 25.0% and 82.1%, and decreased caspase-1 levels by 38.2% and 89.2%, indicating a pronounced anti-inflammatory and anti-apoptotic effect. Histopathological and immunohistochemical findings supported these results, demonstrating improved lung architecture, reduced inflammatory infiltration, and decreased cleaved caspase-3 expression. Overall, S. imbericata exhibits potent protective effects against lung injury, likely mediated through its antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anti-apoptotic activities, supporting its potential as a therapeutic candidate for pulmonary disorders.

papers.title: From Aerosol to Epithelium: An Integrated Clinical, Pathologic, and Mechanistic Review of Nicotine and Cannabis Vaporizer Use and Pulmonary Disease.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of cannabis and nicotine vaporizer use appears to be increasing, but their effects on the respiratory system are incompletely elucidated. This review brings together clinical, pathologic, and molecular knowledge describing airway disease, acute lung injury syndromes, and structural lung injury resulting from nicotine and cannabis vaporizer use. We describe consistent epidemiologic associations of nicotine vaporizer use with obstructive lung disease, bronchitis, emphysema, and constrictive bronchiolitis; cannabis vaporizer use is more frequently associated with acute lung injury and airway disease symptoms. At a molecular level, nicotinic receptor activation drives collagen deposition, epithelial barrier dysfunction, and impaired mucociliary clearance; cannabinoid receptor activation has effects on airway inflammation, epithelial integrity, and immune cell function. Oxidative stress and mitochondrial dysfunction likely mediate effects of nicotine and cannabis vaporizer exposure through receptor-independent mechanisms. Use of nicotine and cannabis vaporizers affects clinical pulmonary disease through a variety of converging molecular and cellular mechanisms in the respiratory epithelium. Significant knowledge gaps remain, particularly with regard to molecular investigations of cannabis vaporizer use and dual nicotine-cannabis vaporizer use. Future investigations integrating molecular mechanisms of disease with clinical and histopathologic outcomes are necessary to better characterize the effects of these increasingly impactful public health risks.

papers.title: Lactobacillus derived small RNAs protect against Klebsiella pneumoniae infection.
papers.abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) is a major multidrug-resistant pathogen with limited treatment options. Plant-derived natural products have broad biological activities, but their protective effects against extraintestinal multidrug-resistant bacterial infections remain poorly understood. Herein, we show that selected plant-derived natural products protect mice against CRKP pulmonary infection by remodeling the gut microbiota. Fecal microbiota transplantation and microbiota-depletion experiments demonstrated that this protection was microbiota dependent, with Lactobacillus emerging as a key genus associated with reduced pulmonary bacterial burden. Among four isolated Lactobacillus species, Lactobacillus murinus ( L. murinus ) conferred the strongest protection against CRKP infection. Mechanistically, L. murinus -derived membrane vesicles (MVs) delivered the small RNA mim-miR-21a-5p to pulmonary macrophages, where it targeted PDCD4 and activated the Nrf2/SOD2 antioxidant pathway. This signaling cascade preserved mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, promoted an M2-like macrophage phenotype, and ultimately restricted CRKP infection. Consistent with these findings, intestinal Lactobacillus , particularly L. murinus , was reduced in patients with CRKP infection compared with healthy controls. Collectively, our findings reveal a mechanism by which plant-derived natural products enhance host resistance to CRKP through microbiota remodeling and identify L. murinus -derived small RNAs and membrane vesicles as key mediator of this gut-lung protective axis.

papers.title: Tumor-associated macrophages in the tumor immune microenvironment of non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.abstract: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains the leading cause of cancer mortality, and resistance to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) is largely driven by the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME), in which tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are major regulators. This review summarizes recent advances in understanding TAM heterogeneity, their contribution to immune resistance in NSCLC, and emerging therapeutic strategies targeting TAMs. A literature search was conducted using PubMed and Google Scholar, focusing on studies published between 2021 and 2025. Key search terms included "non-small cell lung cancer", "tumor immune microenvironment", "macrophage heterogeneity", "M1 macrophages", "M2 macrophages", "SPP1+ macrophages", "TREM2+ macrophages", "immune checkpoint inhibitor resistance", "macrophage metabolic reprogramming", and "TAM-targeted therapies". Relevant studies addressing TAM heterogeneity, immune resistance, metabolic and molecular regulation, and therapeutic targeting in NSCLC were prioritized, while earlier studies were included where necessary to provide mechanistic context. Recent evidence demonstrates that TAMs comprise diverse functional subsets rather than a simple M1/M2 duality. Distinct populations including CXCL9+, SPP1+, C1Q+, and TREM2+ macrophages differentially regulate T-cell exclusion, immune checkpoint resistance, angiogenesis, and metabolic remodeling. Therapeutic approaches targeting CSF1R, CD47-SIRPα, metabolic pathways, nanoparticles, epigenetic regulators, engineered macrophages, and microRNA-based strategies show promise but remain limited by macrophage plasticity and compensatory immune mechanisms. A comprehensive understanding of TAM heterogeneity within the tumor immune microenvironment provides a framework for overcoming immune resistance in NSCLC. Future therapeutic strategies should integrate biomarker-guided patient selection with combination approaches that simultaneously target macrophage plasticity and immune suppression.

papers.title: A latent metabolic dysfunction phenotype integrating insulin resistance and leptin is associated with disease severity in COPD.
papers.abstract: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is increasingly recognised as a systemic condition in which metabolic dysfunction may influence disease severity and exacerbation risk. The combined effects of insulin resistance and leptin dysregulation on COPD outcomes remain incompletely defined. This study evaluated their associations with exacerbation burden, airflow limitation and patient-reported outcomes, and assessed the discriminative performance of HOMA-IR and serum leptin for identifying advanced disease. A cross-sectional observational study was conducted at a tertiary care centre in southern Romania, including 96 patients with COPD and 24 healthy controls. Fasting insulin and serum leptin were measured, and insulin resistance was assessed using HOMA-IR. Spirometry and patient-reported outcomes (CAT, mMRC and SGRQ-C) were assessed in COPD patients. Metabolic markers were analysed individually and as a latent metabolic dysfunction phenotype using generalized structural equation modelling (GSEM). Compared with controls, COPD patients had higher HOMA-IR (+206.9%), insulin (+112.2%) and leptin (+52.8%) levels. Both HOMA-IR and leptin were inversely correlated with spirometric indices, with stronger associations observed for HOMA-IR. Within the COPD cohort, neither individual metabolic markers nor a latent metabolic dysfunction phenotype integrating HOMA-IR, body mass index and leptin was associated with annual exacerbation rate (latent factor IRR = 1.089, 95% CI: 0.841-1.410, p  = 0.517). HOMA-IR demonstrated better discrimination of advanced disease than leptin (AUC = 0.769 vs. 0.590, p  < 0.001). Metabolic dysfunction is substantially more pronounced in COPD than in individuals without airflow obstruction and correlates with the degree of airflow limitation, but does not independently predict exacerbation frequency within the COPD population. HOMA-IR outperformed leptin as a marker of disease severity, a finding that requires further validation.

papers.title: Probiotic modulation of the neonatal gut-lung axis in the regulation of early respiratory function.
papers.abstract: The gut -lung axis represents bidirectional communication between the gastrointestinal and respiratory systems that contributes to immune regulation and inflammatory homeostasis. This study evaluated the effects of probiotic-conditioned media (PCM) and live probiotics on epithelial barrier function, inflammatory responses, oxidative stress, and mitochondrial function using Caco-2 intestinal epithelial and A549 pulmonary epithelial cell models under inflammatory conditions. Cells were treated with 20% PCM or live probiotics at a multiplicity of infection (MOI) of 50:1 and exposed to LPS (1 μg/mL) or TNF-α (10 ng/mL). Barrier integrity was evaluated using transepithelial electrical resistance (TEER) and FITC-dextran permeability assays. Reactive oxygen species (ROS), mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), inflammatory and tight junction gene expression, and SCFA concentrations were assessed using DCFH-DA staining, JC-1 staining, qPCR, and GC-MS, respectively. All experiments comprised three independent biological replicates (n=3), with data presented as mean ± SD and analyzed using one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's post hoc multiple-comparison test. Probiotic treatment increased TEER from 318 ± 21 Ω·cm 2 with LPS to 468 ± 23 Ω·cm 2 with 20% PCM and reduced ROS from 198 ± 12% to 118 ± 8%. Live probiotics produced comparable responses, restoring TEER to 482 ± 20 Ω·cm 2 and reducing ROS to 115 ± 7% in Caco-2 cells. ΔΨm increased from 0.82 ± 0.08 with LPS to 1.52 ± 0.11 with PCM. Acetate and butyrate concentrations increased to 6.8 ± 0.5 and 1.5 ± 0.2 mM, respectively. SCFA analysis showed increased acetate (6.8 ± 0.5 vs. 2.2 ± 0.3 mM) and butyrate (1.5 ± 0.2 vs. 0.5 ± 0.1 mM) in the 20% PCM group compared with the control condition (p<0.01). Compared with the LPS-treated inflammatory condition, probiotic treatment reduced the levels of the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-6 and TNF-α by approximately 50%, while IL-10 expression increased to 1.8 ± 0.2-fold (p<0.05). Collectively, probiotics and PCM supported epithelial protection by improving barrier integrity and attenuating inflammatory and oxidative responses, with increased SCFA production representing a potential contributing mechanism.

papers.title: Clinical relevance of ventriculo-arterial coupling and how to assess it at the bedside.
papers.abstract: This review describes ventriculo-arterial coupling (VAC), its clinical relevance and how to access it at the bedside. VAC refers to the interaction between the contractility of the ejecting ventricles and the load exerted by the arteries. It integrates cardiac performance with the properties of the vascular system to assess cardiovascular efficiency and workload ending in a stroke volume and energy required to create that work. This relationship is quantitatively expressed as the ratio between arterial elastance (Ea) and end-systolic ventricular elastance (Ees). VAC offers valuable insights into hemodynamic status that go beyond traditional parameters like blood pressure, stroke volume or ejection fraction and independently predicts outcome from critical illness. Optimal VAC reflects maximal efficiency of stroke work and preserved cardiovascular reserve, while uncoupling indicates impaired reserve and is associated with worse prognosis. Uncoupling can occur in both acute and chronic settings, can affect either the right ventricle and pulmonary circulation or left ventricle and systemic circulation or both, and is observed across most forms of shock. While VAC has traditionally been analyzed through invasive pressure-volume methods, it can now be approximated at the bedside using echocardiography and simplified elastance calculations. These approaches allow for dynamic assessments of therapeutic interventions, including fluids, vasopressors, inotropes, and mechanical circulatory support. By incorporating VAC into clinical practice, healthcare professionals can enhance hemodynamic phenotyping and support individualized, physiology-guided management of critically ill patients.

papers.title: Integrated identification of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 as potential drivers of smoking-related lung carcinogenesis.
papers.abstract: Smoking is the major environmental risk factor for lung cancer; however, the molecular basis underlying individual susceptibility to smoking-related carcinogenesis remains incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify smoking-specific molecular signatures associated with lung cancer development and to investigate their potential biological mechanisms. Transcriptomic datasets from smokers with and without lung cancer, as well as never-smokers with lung cancer, were analyzed using differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA). Candidate genes were further evaluated using machine learning algorithms, Mendelian randomization (MR), single-cell transcriptomic analysis, molecular docking, and in vitro validation. A total of 16 smoking-specific lung cancer-related genes were identified, which were mainly enriched in cytochrome P450-mediated xenobiotic metabolism, oxidoreductase activity, and chemical carcinogenesis-related pathways. Machine learning analysis established a four-gene signature comprising CYP1A1, CYP1B1, HLA-DRA, and IDO1, among which CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 exhibited substantial contributions to lung cancer classification. MR analysis further demonstrated that genetically predicted expression levels of CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 were positively associated with lung cancer risk. Single-cell transcriptomic analysis revealed that CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 were predominantly expressed in epithelial cells. Molecular docking analysis suggested potential interactions between CYP1A1/CYP1B1 proteins and tobacco-related carcinogens. Furthermore, cigarette smoke extract treatment significantly increased CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 expression at both the mRNA and protein levels in BEAS-2B bronchial epithelial cells. Collectively, these findings indicate that CYP1A1 and CYP1B1 may contribute to smoking-related lung carcinogenesis through regulation of carcinogen metabolism and oxidative stress responses and may serve as potential biomarkers for identifying individuals at increased risk of smoking-associated lung cancer. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13205-026-05099-x.

papers.title: Targeting host ferroptosis in cancer cachexia: Tumor-immune triggers, tissue wasting, and the therapeutic paradox.
papers.abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic wasting syndrome driven by tumor burden, chronic inflammation, disrupted nutrient handling, and neuroendocrine stress. Supportive nutrition, exercise, and symptom management rarely restore lean mass, function, or treatment tolerance once wasting is established. Ferroptosis, iron-dependent cell death caused by phospholipid peroxidation, may connect inflammatory iron redistribution, lipid remodeling, mitochondrial stress, and impaired antioxidant defenses. This review critically evaluates ferroptosis in cachexia from a tumor-host pharmacology perspective, distinguishing causal evidence from associated oxidative signatures. We highlight two experimentally supported mechanisms: neutrophil-derived lipocalin-2 in lung cancer cachexia and tumor exosomal miR-203a-3p in pancreatic cancer-associated muscle wasting. We also examine the paradox that tumor ferroptosis induction may weaken host-tissue resistance and worsen muscle and adipose loss. We propose a "split-ferroptosis" strategy combining tumor sensitization with host-protective iron modulation, lipid peroxide scavenging, endogenous defense reinforcement, and biomarker-guided patient selection to expand the tumor-host therapeutic index.

papers.title: Integration of Network Toxicology and Machine Learning to Prioritize Candidate Molecular Features Associated with NNK-Related Lung Cancer.
papers.abstract: 4-(Methylnitrosamino)-1-(3-pyridyl)-1-butanone (NNK) is a tobacco-specific nitrosamine implicated in tobacco-related lung carcinogenesis. Its biological effects in vivo depend substantially on metabolic conversion to NNAL and cytochrome P450-mediated formation of reactive intermediates. In this study, predicted NNK-associated proteins were integrated with lung cancer transcriptomic data sets, followed by network analysis and machine-learning-based feature prioritization. Five genes, SNAI2, PLAU, DNMT3A, FAP, and CCNB1, were prioritized based on their contributions to the multigene classification framework. Exploratory molecular docking generated computational ligand-placement models with modest docking scores; these results were used only as structural visualizations and do not demonstrate direct biochemical binding. In the metabolically limited A549 cell model, micromolar exposure to parent NNK produced higher CCK-8 signals, altered cell-cycle distributions, increased Transwell migration and invasion counts, and changes in candidate-gene mRNA expression. These parallel observations do not establish that the candidate genes mediate the cellular phenotypes. Moreover, because intact NNK is rapidly metabolized in vivo and is not an established biomarker of systemic exposure in human blood, urine, or saliva, the parent-compound exposure used here does not represent an established human internal-exposure scenario. This study provides a hypothesis-generating framework for prioritizing candidate molecular features for future investigation rather than direct evidence of NNK target engagement or causal gene function.

papers.title: Localized bigeminal activity in the left atrial posterior wall preceding atrial fibrillation initiation.
papers.abstract: Bigeminal activity of the pulmonary veins is considered an indicator of arrhythmogenic triggers of atrial fibrillation (AF). However, few reports have described localized bigeminal activity originating from non-pulmonary vein regions. We observed the phenomenon of local bigeminal activities, which did not develop into premature atrial contraction, in a restricted area of left atrial posterior wall (LAPW), preceding the initiation of the AF. Radiofrequency ablation targeting the site of these bigeminal activities transiently suppressed AF, and subsequent linear ablation connecting the site to the adjacent low-voltage region resulted in durable elimination of AF. The spatial relationship between the localized activity and the low-voltage substrate suggests that conduction abnormalities within diseased atrial myocardium may have contributed to the observed phenomenon. This case highlights the potential role of localized electrical activity arising near a low-voltage substrate of the LAPW in AF initiation and may provide insights into the electrophysiological mechanisms of non-pulmonary vein triggers. Left atrial posterior wall (LAPW) is known to be one of the non-pulmonary vein (PV) origins triggering atrial fibrillation (AF). While bigeminal activity originating from PVs or superior vena cava has been associated with arrhythmogenic triggers, similar activity originating from non-PV origin, such as LAPW, has rarely been described. This case indicates that localized bigeminal activity occurring near a low-voltage substrate of the LAPW may precede AF initiation and provides new insights into non-PV arrhythmogenic substrates as the target of ablation.

papers.title: CFTR I556V Variant Exacerbates Cigarette Smoke-Induced Airway Inflammation in COPD by Promoting NLRP3 Inflammasome Activation.
papers.abstract: Mutations in the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) gene are known to cause cystic fibrosis (CF), a condition that shares several pathophysiological pulmonary features with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD). Despite these similarities, the relationship between CFTR gene mutations and the risk of developing COPD remains unclear and poorly understood. We employed exon sequencing to detect CFTR exon variations in 208 COPD patients and 100 control subjects with normal lung function. Subsequently, we applied the adenine base editor system to generate cells and animal models carrying the CFTR chr7:117227874A>G (I556V) variant. Airway epithelial cell models were used to examine the effect of the I556V variant on reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and mitochondrial membrane potential. Additionally, conventional I556V-CFTR variant ( CFTR V/V ) and wild-type ( CFTR I/I ) mice were exposed to either air or 6 months of cigarette smoke. Immune cell counts were obtained from bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples. Clinically, we identified seven CFTR variants, with I556V showing a significant association with COPD risk (P = 0.045). Individuals carrying the I556V variant had a 2.12-fold increased risk of developing COPD (OR = 2.12, 95% CI = 1.16-3.86), which increased to 96% after adjusting for age, gender, and smoking status (OR = 1.96, 95% CI = 1.01-3.81). Cells harboring the I556V-CFTR variant exhibited a 27.27% increase in ROS levels and an 85.38% increase in the JC-1 monomer ratio (indicating significant loss of mitochondrial membrane potential) compared to CFTR I/I cells. In mice, the I556V-CFTR variant led to significant impairment of lung function and exacerbated airway remodeling after 6 months of cigarette smoke (CS) exposure, characterized by a 23.03% increase in airway wall thickness and a 48.40% increase in collagen deposition compared to CS-exposed CFTR I/I mice. Moreover, there was exacerbated lung inflammation in I556V-CFTR variant mice compared to CFTR I/I . In conclusion, the I556V-CFTR variant is a risk factor for COPD. It likely contributes to disease pathogenesis by downregulating CFTR expression, thereby exacerbating oxidative stress and inflammatory responses.

papers.title: The PIEZO1/CISD1/IP3R Mechanotransduction Axis Drives Macrophage Mitochondrial Dysfunction and Inflammatory Activation in Pulmonary Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is a progressive and fatal interstitial lung disease characterized by excessive extracellular matrix (ECM) deposition and elevated tissue stiffness. While aberrant mechanotransduction is increasingly recognized as a key driver of fibrotic progression, the mechanisms by which mechanical cues orchestrate macrophage dysfunction remain poorly elucidated. Here, we identify the mechanosensitive ion channel PIEZO1 as a key mediator coupling matrix stiffening to macrophage inflammatory activation in pulmonary fibrosis. We demonstrate that PIEZO1 is substantially upregulated in fibrotic lungs, and that its activation drives intracellular calcium overload via the CISD1/IP3R signaling axis. This process elicits aberrant opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (MPTP), causing mitochondrial dysfunction and augmented pro-inflammatory macrophage polarization. Conversely, PIEZO1 inhibition suppresses the CISD1/IP3R signaling cascade, alleviates calcium dysregulation, prevents mitochondrial damage, and attenuates inflammatory activation. In vitro CISD1 inhibition ameliorates PIEZO1-driven mitochondrial abnormalities and pro-inflammatory signaling in macrophages. Furthermore, genetic knockdown of CISD1 mitigates mitochondrial abnormalities and attenuates bleomycin (BLM)-induced lung fibrosis in mice. Collectively, these findings identify a previously unrecognized PIEZO1/CISD1/IP3R mechanotransduction axis coupling tissue stiffening to macrophage-mediated inflammation and fibrosis. This study offers mechanistic insights into fibrosis-associated immune dysregulation, highlighting PIEZO1 and CISD1 as promising therapeutic targets for pulmonary fibrosis.

papers.title: Superoxide Release from Macrophages upon Exposure to Secondary Organic Aerosols, Biomass, and Plastic Burning Particulate Matter.
papers.abstract: Oxidative stress induced by reactive oxygen species (ROS) is a key process for adverse health effects upon respiratory deposition of particulate matter (PM). Alveolar macrophages can release superoxide upon phagocytosis of PM through a process called the respiratory burst. The release of cellular ROS should depend on both PM composition and dose, but the dose-response relationship for various types of PM remains poorly quantified. Here we measure cellular superoxide production by macrophage cells exposed to secondary organic aerosols (SOA) derived from oxidation of limonene, toluene, and naphthalene, as well as PM generated from biomass burning and flaming combustion of five different types of plastics. We quantify cellular superoxide production over the span of 4 h after an initial exposure of macrophages to PM suspensions by applying a chemiluminescence assay combined with electron paramagnetic resonance. We then define the activation threshold as the dose at which cells exhibit a clear increase in superoxide production. Limonene SOA is found to induce the largest amount of superoxide release (∼32 μM) but has the largest activation threshold of 300 μg mL -1 . Naphthalene and toluene SOA show smaller enhancement of superoxide production (∼2.5-7 μM) but have lower activation thresholds from 0.02 to 0.1 μg mL -1 . Biomass burning PM does not show a clear activation threshold. Plastic burning PM shows a varied response depending on the type of plastic, with PM derived from poly-(ethylene terephthalate) (PET) having the highest superoxide production (∼12 μM). The activation thresholds for polystyrene (PS), low-density polyethylene (LDPE), and high-density polyethylene (HDPE) burning PM are very low (∼0.01 μg mL -1 ), while those for poly-(vinyl chloride) (PVC) and PET burning PM are substantially higher (50-100 μg mL -1 ). Our findings highlight the importance of employing dose-response relationships and superoxide activation thresholds, rather than single-dose comparisons, to evaluate and compare the oxidative stress potential of different PMs more accurately.

papers.title: Successful superior vena cava isolation using point-by-point cryothermal ablation after failed radiofrequency ablation.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary vein isolation is the cornerstone of catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation (AF), but non-pulmonary vein (non-PV) triggers such as the superior vena cava (SVC) also play an important role. Electrical isolation of the SVC (SVCI) can be limited by anatomical complexity and the risk of phrenic nerve or sinus node injury, particularly with radiofrequency or cryoballoon techniques. We report a 76-year-old woman with recurrent paroxysmal AF after cryoballoon pulmonary vein isolation. During repeat ablation, AF was initially induced from the left atrial posterior wall and successfully treated with radiofrequency ablation. Subsequent provocation revealed AF triggers from the SVC. Despite careful radiofrequency ablation under phrenic nerve pacing, complete SVCI could not be achieved. Point-by-point cryothermal ablation was then performed under continuous phrenic nerve monitoring, resulting in successful SVCI without complications. This case suggests that focal cryothermal ablation may be a practical and safer alternative when SVCI cannot be achieved with radiofrequency energy. To understand that superior vena cava isolation (SVCI) may be challenging with radiofrequency ablation due to anatomical complexity and safety limitations related to phrenic nerve injury. This case highlights point-by-point cryothermal ablation as a feasible alternative strategy, enabling stable catheter contact, precise lesion delivery, and continuous phrenic nerve monitoring, particularly in regions where point-by-point pulsed-field ablation is not yet available.

papers.title: Thoracoscopic Management of Recurrent Pneumothorax in an Adult Patient with Cri du Chat Syndrome and Severe Scoliosis: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Cri du chat syndrome (CdCS) is a rare genetic disorder that can be associated with scoliosis and marked thoracic deformity. Although scoliosis has been reported to be associated with an increased incidence of pneumothorax, reports of pneumothorax surgery in patients with severe scoliosis associated with CdCS are extremely rare. Herein, we report a case of recurrent pneumothorax in an adult patient with CdCS associated with severe scoliosis who was successfully treated by thoracoscopic surgery. A 41-year-old man with CdCS presented with severe scoliosis, intellectual disability, and dental abnormalities. He was transported to our emergency department with severe left pneumothorax associated with complete left lung collapse and marked hypoxemia. CT after chest drainage revealed a bulla located in the deep thoracic cavity near the mediastinum.
