Because severe thoracic deformity raised concerns regarding both airway management and thoracoscopic manipulation, the patient was initially managed conservatively. However, severe left pneumothorax repeatedly recurred, and surgical intervention was ultimately indicated. Thoracoscopic surgery was performed under 1-lung ventilation using a bronchial blocker. Intrathoracic manipulation was technically challenging because of the marked thoracic deformity associated with severe scoliosis; however, safe operative exposure was achieved using same-axis thoracoscopic manipulation with the thoracoscope and instruments through the same port. A broad-based causative bulla located near the S6-S10 boundary adjacent to the descending thoracic aorta was ligated using ENDOLOOP, followed by intrathoracic administration of 20 mL of 50% glucose solution. The postoperative course was uneventful with no recurrence during 7 years of follow-up. In patients with severe scoliosis associated with CdCS, thoracic deformity may complicate both airway management and thoracoscopic manipulation. However, thoracoscopic surgery may be feasible with appropriate anesthetic planning and adaptation of the operative strategy. In particular, same-axis thoracoscopic manipulation using the thoracoscope and instruments through the same port may be useful for maintaining safe visualization and instrument handling within a narrow thoracic cavity.

papers.title: Cyclic stretch increases glucose uptake and pro-inflammatory response in rat alveolar epithelial type II cells.
papers.abstract: Mechanical ventilation (MV) is used to improve gas exchange but can exacerbate lung inflammation by increasing alveolar cell stretch, leading to ventilator-induced lung injury (VILI). Alveolar epithelial stretching promotes cytokine release, but its effects on glucose uptake remain unclear. In vitro studies suggest that high tidal volume ventilation corresponds to cyclic stretch levels of approximately 18%, whereas larger deformations represent supraphysiological and injurious conditions. Therefore, 30% cyclic stretch was used to reproduce severe alveolar deformation associated with volutrauma. We investigated the modulation of inflammation and glucose uptake in alveolar epithelial type II cells exposed to excessive cyclic stretch. We hypothesized that cells exposed to an overstretch of 30% at 1 and 4 hours would increase glucose uptake and pro-inflammatory responses. Rat alveolar epithelial type II cells (L2 AECs) treated and untreated with lipopolysaccharide (LPS) were exposed to 1 or 4 hours of 30% cyclic stretch. Non-stretched cells, stimulated or not with LPS, served as a control. Glucose oxidase activity was measured using a colorimetric/fluorometric assay, while glucose uptake was assessed by immunofluorescence using the fluorescent glucose analog 2-[N-(7-nitrobenz-2-oxa-1,3-diazol-4-yl)amino]-2-deoxyglucose (2-NBDG). Gene expression and secretion were measured by real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) and enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), respectively. Statistical analyses were performed using one-way ANOVA followed by Šidák's multiple comparisons test, with significance set at p  < 0.05. 30% cyclic stretch significantly increased glucose uptake and glucose oxidase activity in both LPS-treated and untreated cells. Inflammatory gene expression and mediator secretion were predominantly increased in LPS-primed cells, although the effects varied according to the marker and time point. Overall, excessive cyclic stretch increased the glucose-related readouts assessed in AECs L2 cells, whereas inflammatory responses were more strongly influenced by LPS stimulation and varied among mediators and time points.

papers.title: Immunomodulatory potential of Mongolian medicine in sepsis: current evidence, challenges, and translational perspectives.
papers.abstract: Sepsis is a heterogeneous, time-dependent syndrome in which inflammatory injury, immune suppression, endothelial dysfunction, metabolic disturbance, and barrier failure may coexist. This narrative review evaluates whether current pharmacological evidence provides a defensible basis for investigating Traditional Mongolian Medicine as an adjunctive source of immunomodulatory candidates in sepsis. A concise account of sepsis immunopathology is used as an interpretive framework, after which evidence from named Mongolian formulas, extracts, medicinal materials, and isolated constituents is mapped according to ethnomedical specificity, model directness, and study-design limitations. Direct sepsis-specific evidence is scarce. Daruqi particles, HHQG, Hohgardi-9, Nagab-9, Monflu, Batri-7, Qiqirigan-8, and selected extracts have mainly been studied in lipopolysaccharide-induced acute lung injury, organ-injury, enteritis, inflammatory, or metabolic models. These studies suggest effects on NF-κB/MAPK signaling, myeloid-cell infiltration, neutrophil extracellular traps, redox regulation, and lipid metabolism, but generally do not assess polymicrobial infection, pathogen clearance, survival, late immunosuppression, or human immune endotypes. Widely distributed compounds such as quercetin, berberine, geniposide, and gallate are therefore treated only as non-specific constituent-level evidence of pharmacological plausibility. We propose candidate-specific priorities for chemical standardization, rigorous sepsis modeling, pharmacokinetic and safety evaluation, and biomarker-guided translation. The current literature supports an ethnopharmacology-informed research agenda, not therapeutic efficacy in sepsis.

papers.title: Case report: Septic shock associated with Granulicatella adiacens pneumonia in a polytrauma patient following road traffic accident: rare pathogen in critical care.
papers.abstract: Ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) is a common and serious consequence of prolonged mechanical ventilation in critically ill polytrauma patients, especially those with underlying comorbidities such as diabetes mellitus. Although VAP is often caused by gram-negative bacilli and Staphylococcus aureus, infection due to fastidious organisms is uncommon and may delay microbiological diagnosis. Granulicatella adiacens , formerly categorized among the nutritionally variant streptococci (NVS), is a fastidious commensal of the oral and genitourinary tract that is most commonly associated with infective endocarditis and bacteremia, whereas pulmonary infections are exceptionally rare. We present a case report of a 50-year-old diabetic male who sustained severe head, thoracic, and skeletal injuries in a high-impact two-wheeler RTA. He acquired ventilator-associated pneumonia with progression to septic shock on the ICU course. The initial cultures (blood, urine, ET aspirate) were sterile, but the following bronchoalveolar lavage G. adiacens as the predominant organism on enriched media, identifying it as the probable etiological agent. A repeat blood culture, obtained on day 4 because of suspected sepsis, subsequently also grew G. adiacens after the patient's death. The patient, in spite of mechanical ventilation, vasopressors, renal replacement therapy, and broad-spectrum antibiotics, developed multi-organ dysfunction and succumbed on ICU day 5. The case brings to the fore the potential possibility of G. adiacens to cause fatal opportunistic infections in polytrauma victims when invasive ICU therapy and metabolic derangements converge. Early suspicion, prompt interventions like BAL sampling, and enriched media or molecular diagnostics can facilitate the detection of fastidious pathogens in culture-negative sepsis, thus facilitating therapeutic targeting and optimizing outcomes.

papers.title: Integrative multi-omics analysis defines a macrophage-associated phospholipid metabolism signature linked to immune remodeling and prognosis in lung adenocarcinoma.
papers.abstract: Phospholipid metabolism (PLM) has been implicated in macrophage polarization and tumor progression in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD). Metabolic intermediates such as lysophosphatidylcholine modulate macrophage surface receptor signaling, while inhibition of phospholipid synthesis may attenuate tumor-associated macrophage (TAM) infiltration and suppress LUAD progression. However, macrophage-centered PLM-related prognostic signatures in LUAD remain incompletely characterized. We performed an integrative multi-omics analysis combining single-cell RNA sequencing, bulk transcriptomic profiling, and clinical data from TCGA and GEO cohorts. Macrophage-related genes (MacRGs) were identified using single-cell analysis and high-dimensional weighted gene co-expression network analysis (hdWGCNA). Phospholipid metabolism-related module genes were determined through differential expression analysis and WGCNA. Candidate genes were prioritized using machine learning and Cox regression analyses, followed by construction and external validation of a multigene risk model. Functional enrichment, immune microenvironment profiling, mutation landscape analysis, estimated drug sensitivity, and pseudotime trajectory analyses were performed to explore the biological relevance of the signature. Experimental validation was conducted using LUAD tissues and cell models. A four-gene macrophage-PLM-related signature was constructed to calculate a risk score that stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different overall survival. The risk score and T stage were independent prognostic factors, and an integrated nomogram showed acceptable prognostic performance. Functional analyses revealed distinct metabolic and signaling pathway enrichment patterns between risk groups, with 40 shared pathways across the four hub genes. The high-risk group exhibited an altered immune microenvironment characterized by differential infiltration of 20 immune cell subsets, immune checkpoint expression changes, lower ESTIMATE scores, and distinct TIDE profiles. Somatic mutation patterns and tumor mutational burden differed between groups. Drug-sensitivity estimation identified 105 compounds with differential estimated IC50 values between risk groups. DPYSL2 expression was associated with macrophage polarization dynamics, and DPYSL2 overexpression suppressed LUAD cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and clonogenicity in vitro. We identified a macrophage-phospholipid metabolism-associated four-gene prognostic signature that provides prognostic information and reflects immune-metabolic remodeling in LUAD. These findings support further investigation of macrophage-phospholipid metabolism-related genes as candidate biomarkers and may inform future therapeutic stratification studies in LUAD.

papers.title: NeuroMetBench: patient-aware evidence bounds for transcript-derived metabolic representations across cancer proteogenomic contexts.
papers.abstract: Transcript-derived metabolic representations connect gene expression with pathway state, but interpretation depends on sampling unit, endpoint, cohort, and validation evidence. NeuroMetBench is a patient-aware methodology that keeps target quantity, independent unit, endpoint mapping, coverage, uncertainty, transport, numerical diagnostics, and provenance separate rather than collapsing them into a universal score. A frozen three-gene serine score showed RNA-protein rank concordance in 89 lung squamous cell carcinoma (LSCC) patients (Spearman [Formula: see text], 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.8496 to 0.9388) and in a patient-disjoint 90-patient central nervous system/high-grade-glioma (CNS/HGG) cohort ([Formula: see text], 95% CI 0.4697 to 0.7507). Reviewer-driven age/sex sensitivities remained positive in complete cases (LSCC [Formula: see text], partial [Formula: see text]; CNS/HGG [Formula: see text], partial [Formula: see text]), but CNS/HGG complete-case selection was associated with the frozen RNA-score distribution and cannot rule out demographic confounding. A preanalysis-frozen Tel Aviv glioblastoma test was NOT RUN because public RNA/proteomics deposits yielded zero source-documented patient cross-matches (minimum [Formula: see text]). A separately frozen Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC) analysis found 20 exact RNA/protein-matched glioblastomas and positive concordance ([Formula: see text], 95% CI 0.1252 to 0.9101; permutation [Formula: see text]). By contrast, RNA score correspondence with measured L-serine in 75 same-cohort patients was weak and uncertain ([Formula: see text], 95% CI -0.0803 to 0.3737; permutation [Formula: see text]). Evidence strength is therefore axis-specific: cross-modal proxy concordance does not establish metabolic flux, biochemical validation, universal method superiority, framework-wide external validation, or calibration.

papers.title: Targeting FEN1 disrupts EIF4A3-mediated MUC1-C autoregulation: a novel strategy to suppress lung adenocarcinoma progression.
papers.abstract: Flap endonuclease 1 (FEN1), a key enzyme in DNA metabolism, exhibits oncogenic properties in various cancers. However, its functional role and underlying mechanisms in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) progression and tumor immunity remain poorly defined. Here, we demonstrate that FEN1 is significantly upregulated in LUAD tissues and serves as an independent prognostic factor for poor survival. Genetic depletion of FEN1 suppressed LUAD cell proliferation by inducing G0/G1 cell cycle arrest and cellular senescence, while significantly impairing migration and invasion capabilities. Mechanistically, integrated proteomic and molecular analyses revealed that FEN1 knockdown disrupts the carboxyl-terminal subunit of mucin 1 (MUC1-C)/PI3K/AKT autoregulatory loop, a critical driver of oncogenic signaling. Furthermore, FEN1 downregulation inhibited the MUC1-C/p65/ programmed death-ligand 1 (PD-L1) signaling axis, thereby alleviating tumor-mediated immunosuppression. This was evidenced by enhanced antitumor immunity, characterized by the local expansion of CD4 + T cells and restored effector function of CD8 + T cells, both in vitro and in vivo. Mechanistically, independent of its nuclease activity, FEN1 interacts with the N-terminus of eukaryotic translation initiation factor 4A3 (EIF4A3) to facilitate its binding to MUC1-C mRNA. Specifically, FEN1 is required for EIF4A3-mediated maintenance of both the transcript stability and translation efficiency of MUC1-C. Clinically, FEN1, MUC1-C, and PD-L1 are coordinately upregulated in LUAD tissues, and their co-expression predicts poor patient survival irrespective of EGFR mutation status. Our findings establish the FEN1/EIF4A3/MUC1-C axis as a novel mechanism driving LUAD progression by concurrently regulating intrinsic malignancy and extrinsic immune evasion, presenting FEN1 targeting as a promising dual-hit therapeutic strategy.

papers.title: Glutamate attenuates the ILC2 response and allergic airway inflammation via the kainate receptor GluK2.
papers.abstract: Group 2 innate lymphoid cells (ILC2s) play a critical role in initiating the type 2 immune response, particularly in allergic airway diseases. Although the effects of glutamate on the immune system have been reported previously, its role in modulating the function of ILC2s and lung inflammation remains unclear.In this study, we report that the glutamate levels increased in lung tissue following exposure to allergens. Consequently, glutamate was found to restrain ILC2 responses during lung inflammation in mice. Using Rag1 -/- mice, we demonstrated that the inhibitory effect of glutamate on type 2 inflammation was independent of T and B cells. Further ILC2 adoptive transfer experiments in Rag -/- Il2rg -/-  mice confirmed that glutamate likely exerted its effects by directly targeting ILC2s. In vitro experiments revealed that glutamate suppressed ILC2 function through ionic kainate receptor signaling. Genetic deletion of the kainate receptor subunit GluK2 enhanced ILC2 responses and exacerbated type 2 lung inflammation. Mechanistically, transcriptome and metabolic analyses revealed that glutamate reduced oxidative metabolism in ILC2s, thereby limiting their activation. Consistently, in vivo administration of BPAM344-a positive allosteric modulator that potentiates GluK2 signaling-effectively suppressed allergen-induced type 2 inflammation. Notably, ILC2-specific GluK2 deletion markedly attenuated the anti-inflammatory effects of BPAM344, indicating that its protective effects depend on ILC2-intrinsic GluK2 signaling.These findings demonstrate a novel role for glutamate in restraining ILC2 function, as it plays a protective role in alleviating airway inflammation. We propose that GluK2 activation may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for treating ILC2-driven allergic asthma.

papers.title: Associations of body shape, visceral adiposity, and metabolic function indices with risk of major noncommunicable diseases: evidence from a nationwide population cohort.
papers.abstract: Comparative data evaluating the predictive performance of various obesity and metabolic indices for multiple noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) remain limited. We used the data sourced from the Health Evaluation and risk Reduction through nationwide Teamwork cohort (ChinaHEART), a national population-based study that enrolled 4,258,033 Chinese adults and followed them for more than 20 million person-years between November 2014 and December 2023. Fifteen obesity and metabolic indices were categorized into three groups: (1) body shape-related indices, including body mass index (BMI), body roundness index (BRI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), a body shape index (ABSI), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and conicity index (CI); (2) visceral fat-related indices, including lipid accumulation product (LAP) and Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI); and (3) metabolic function-related indices, including triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-BMI, TyG-BRI, TyG-WHtR, TyG-ABSI, TyG-WWI, and TyG-CI. The study outcomes comprised composite events of death or first hospitalization attributable to each of cardiovascular diseases (CVD), diabetes mellitus (DM), cancers, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) individually. Composite obesity and metabolic indices reflecting visceral adiposity accumulation and insulin resistance, respectively exhibited enhanced predictive accuracy for cardiovascular and diabetic risk, whereas their performance for cancer and COPD was comparatively limited. These findings support the paradigm that weight management strategies should be guided by risk assessments rather than relying solely on body weight or body shape. Furthermore, the development of diverse definitions for obesity measurement and management tailored to different population subgroups is warranted.

papers.title: Septal dysfunction and Abnormal Systolic Stretch Are Associated with Right Ventricular Dysfunction in Repaired Tetralogy of Fallot.
papers.abstract: Right ventricular (RV) dysfunction is a major determinant of outcomes after Tetralogy of Fallot repair (rToF). Although right bundle branch block is present in most patients and electro-mechanical dyssynchrony (EMD) has been associated with RV dysfunction, only a subset of patients ultimately develops RV dysfunction. We hypothesized that septal dysfunction is a key feature associated with the development of EMD-induced RV dysfunction in rToF. We retrospectively studied 126 pediatric rToF patients (median age 14.7 years) with contemporaneous ECG, echocardiography, and cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) between 2019-2025. Septal mechanics were quantified by strain-derived systolic rebound stretch (SRS) and further combined with RV free-wall mechanics into a systolic stretch index (SSI). RV mechanical dyssynchrony was visually classified, with septal contraction abrogation and systolic stretch as key features. Multivariable models evaluated associations between systolic stretch parameters and RV dysfunction (CMR-derived RV ejection fraction (EF) ≤ 46%), adjusting for relevant covariates. RV dysfunction was present in 24.6% of patients. Patients with >moderate RV outflow tract obstruction (peak gradient >40 mmHg) were excluded, median pulmonary regurgitant fraction was 35% (IQR, 26-44%). Median SSI was higher in patients with RV dysfunction than in those without (8.9% (IQR 3.2-11.3) vs 2.9% (IQR 1.5-5.5), p<0.001). Premature termination of septal deformation with subsequent stretching, quantified by SRS, was associated with RV dysfunction (p<0.001). Worse septal stretch patterns were associated with RV dysfunction, larger RV end-systolic indexed volume, and longer QRSd (p<0.001). Higher SSI was independently associated with lower RVEF (p<0.001) after adjustment for age, QRSd, RV dilation, and surgical substrate (p<0.001), whereas QRSd lost significance on RVEF after adjusting for SSI. RVEF was lower at SSI values >4%. SSI demonstrated excellent intraobserver and interobserver reproducibility (ICC 0.996 and 0.997, respectively). In pediatric rToF, RV dysfunction was associated with abnormal septal contraction and systolic stretch. RV-SSI, integrating inefficient RV mechanics via septal and RV free-wall systolic stretch, was independently associated with RV dysfunction beyond QRSd, RV volumes and pulmonary regurgitation severity. These findings may help characterize RV electromechanical phenotypes and provide a rationale for future studies evaluating RV resynchronization therapy.

papers.title: Pharmacological Enhancement of O-GlcNAcylation Attenuates Lung Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury.
papers.abstract: Lung ischemia-reperfusion injury (LIRI) contributes substantially to primary graft dysfunction after lung transplantation and also occurs in other clinical settings involving transient interruption and restoration of pulmonary blood flow. O-linked β-N-acetylglucosamine (O-GlcNAc) modification is rapidly altered by cellular stress, yet its role in acute pulmonary ischemia-reperfusion remains incompletely understood. We investigated this question using a murine model of transient left pulmonary hilar occlusion followed by reperfusion and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reoxygenation (OGD/R) model in MLE-12 cells. O-GlcNAcylation was increased pharmacologically with the O-GlcNAcase inhibitor Thiamet G and reduced with the O-GlcNAc transferase inhibitor OSMI-4. Global O-GlcNAc levels, indices of tissue and cellular injury, and Caspase-1/GSDMD-related pyroptotic signaling were then examined. In both models, O-GlcNAcylation increased early after ischemic stress, whereas pyroptosis-related changes became more pronounced as injury progressed. Thiamet G preserved MLE-12 cell viability, reduced LDH release, and lessened histopathological damage, pulmonary edema, and alveolar-capillary protein leakage in vivo. These effects were accompanied by lower Caspase-1 activation, reduced GSDMD cleavage, and fewer Caspase-1/PI double-positive cells. OSMI-4 produced the opposite pattern, with greater tissue and cellular injury and stronger pyroptosis-related signaling. The protective effect of Thiamet G was also weakened when OSMI-4 was given concurrently. These findings indicate that the early rise in O-GlcNAcylation is consistent with an acute stress response to LIRI. Pharmacologically maintaining higher O-GlcNAcylation was associated with less severe injury and weaker Caspase-1/GSDMD-related signaling, supporting further investigation of this modification as a therapeutic target in acute LIRI.

papers.title: PA4933 Mediates Dual Regulation of Oxidative Resistance and Virulence in Pseudomonas aeruginosa Pulmonary Infection.
papers.abstract: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is a critical opportunistic pathogen requiring rigorous prevention and control, which triggers severe infections in immunocompromised populations. Bacterial membrane proteins serve as core regulatory molecules coordinating stress tolerance and virulence homeostasis during host colonization. Nevertheless, the physiological functions of numerous structurally homologous yet unannotated membrane proteins remain largely elusive. In this study, we identified a significantly upregulated hypothetical gene, PA4933, from published transcriptomic datasets of P. aeruginosa PA14 infecting RAW264.7 macrophages. Bioinformatic prediction preliminarily confirmed that PA4933 is a highly conserved seven-transmembrane protein sharing high structural homology with ABC transporters. Mechanistically, PA4933 elevates the transcription of glnA to enrich intracellular glutamine, thereby markedly boosting glutathione (GSH) biosynthesis and enhancing bacterial antioxidant capacity. Meanwhile, PA4933 represses the transcription of virulence-related genes including phzC, rhlA, pel, motA, and motC, which consequently inhibits pyocyanin production, rhamnolipid synthesis, biofilm formation and swarming motility. Such regulatory effects alleviate bacterial damage to multiple infection models, including A549 alveolar epithelial cells, Galleria mellonella larvae and murine acute pneumonia models. Collectively, PA4933 exerts dual regulatory roles: facilitating antioxidant immune evasion while suppressing virulence and mitigating host tissue injury. This protein regulates the infection homeostasis of PAO1, it provides new insights into P. aeruginosa infection.

papers.title: Palmar Cooling as a Thermoregulatory Intervention: Mechanistic Basis and Implications for Exercise and Clinical Applications.
papers.abstract: During exercise, rising metabolic heat production creates competition for blood flow between skeletal muscle and the cutaneous vasculature. The resulting redistribution elevates cardiovascular (CV) strain and accelerates fatigue, particularly during environmental heat stress or in individuals with impaired thermoregulatory capacity. Strategies that enhance heat dissipation without further burdening CV function may therefore improve exercise tolerance. Palmar cooling (PC) is an intervention that targets the glabrous skin of the hands, where dense arteriovenous anastomoses facilitate high-flow, low-resistance blood flow and efficient convective heat exchange, thereby augmenting systemic heat dissipation through the peripheral circulation. Evidence in healthy and athletic populations suggests that PC can decrease thermal strain while improving endurance capacity, resistance training volume, and perceptual responses when applied under meaningful heat stress, although current findings remain heterogeneous. Given age- and disease-related reductions in thermoregulatory and CV reserve, PC may have translational relevance for enhancing exercise tolerance during rehabilitation, reducing heat-related illness risk, and supporting individuals with cardiopulmonary disease. Improved within-session tolerability may, in turn, facilitate greater cumulative training stimulus and adherence, with potential downstream benefits for overall exercise capacity. This narrative review discusses the thermoregulatory, CV, and exercise physiology underlying PC, evaluates the current evidence, and outlines future directions to support clinical translation.

papers.title: Exercise training does not mitigate high-phosphate diet-induced mitochondrial dysfunction in skeletal muscle in male mice.
papers.abstract: Inorganic phosphate consumption in adults is two-to-three-fold higher than the recommended daily allowance due to its widespread use as a preservative and flavor enhancer in processed foods. We previously reported that 12 weeks of high-phosphate diet (HPD) reduced VO 2max and altered metabolic gene expression and mitochondrial dysfunction in mouse skeletal muscle. Here, we investigated whether exercise training reverses the negative consequences of HPD. Male mice were fed normal (NPD) or HPD for 5 weeks, then continued on NPD or HPD with 9 weeks of voluntary exercise training. Serum, urine, and fecal phosphate increased within 1 day of HPD-feeding and remained elevated throughout the study. Trained NPD- and HPD-fed mice performed similarly on forced exercise tests, but mitochondrial respiration was significantly decreased in skeletal muscle from trained HPD-fed mice. RNA sequencing revealed distinct sets of differentially expressed genes when comparing sedentary versus exercise-trained muscle of HPD-fed mice relative to the same comparison in NPD-fed mice. These findings indicate that voluntary exercise training preserves endurance but does not fully restore gene expression or mitochondrial function in muscle from HPD-fed mice. Thus, HPD-induced skeletal muscle dysregulation is not completely reversible with exercise, underscoring the importance of both diet and exercise for metabolic health.

papers.title: Targeting ubiquitin-dependent mitochondrial autophagy and apoptosis in sarcopenia: the therapeutic potential of phytochemicals.
papers.abstract: Sarcopenia is a progressive degenerative disease of skeletal muscle closely associated with aging, disuse, and chronic diseases, affecting approximately 10-16% of the global older adult population. Its core pathological basis lies in the disruption of skeletal muscle cell proteostasis and mitochondrial dysfunction. At the molecular level, excessive degradation of structural proteins mediated by the ubiquitin-proteasome system forms an intertwined vicious cycle with the inability of ubiquitin-dependent mitophagy to clear damaged organelles, ultimately triggering irreversible cell death programmes within an oxidative stress and inflammatory microenvironment. Due to the high complexity and molecular crosstalk within this cell fate-determining network, traditional single-target interventions often yield limited therapeutic efficacy. In recent years, phytochemicals (such as polyphenols, flavonoids, alkaloids, and coumarins) have demonstrated significant therapeutic potential in the field of sarcopenia due to their unique multi-target, multi-pathway synergistic regulatory advantages. This article reviews the dual-faceted regulatory mechanisms of ubiquitination in skeletal muscle mitochondrial quality control, protein hydrolysis, and apoptosis escape and provides an analysis of how phytochemicals achieve autophagy-promoting, anti-apoptotic, and anti-degradative skeletal muscle protection. However, oral bioavailability is often below 1%, microbiota-dependent metabolism, and the absence of phase III clinical trials have hindered the translational application of phytochemicals. This paper explores the use of nano-delivery systems to overcome the bioavailability bottleneck of phytochemicals, as well as translational application strategies based on the gut-muscle axis to reshape the in vivo metabolism of natural products. This review aims to provide a solid theoretical foundation for the development of novel phytochemical-derived drugs targeting ubiquitination and apoptosis networks and to chart a course for reversing skeletal muscle ageing and enhancing human healthspan.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal metabolic networks in a preclinical model of pancreatic cancer and associated cachexia.
papers.abstract: Cachexia or body wasting is a significant contributing factor to the morbidity and mortality of pancreatic cancer. Despite an unmet need, its metabolic underpinnings remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize a mouse model that recaptures the longitudinal progression of human cachexia during pancreatic cancer development. We profile the metabolomes of pre-, early- and late-stage cancer-associated cachexia in male and female pancreas, its interstitial fluid (IF), plasma, liver, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. We find that each tissue has a unique metabolome and trajectory across stages and reveal a marked lipid enrichment in the tumor IF. Using mathematical modeling, we identify metabolites participating in cross-tissue networks and in vivo validate a lactate-glucose conversion. We find systemic metabolic changes prior to weight loss and use feature selection algorithms to identify early detection markers. Our study provides a resource for system-wide metabolic evolution of pancreatic cancer and associated cachexia, highlighting the potential for timely diagnostics and interventions.

papers.title: Miro1 mediates skeletal muscle insulin resistance in type 2 diabetes.
papers.abstract: Imbalanced skeletal muscle mitochondrial dynamics contribute to the onset and progression of type 2 diabetes (T2D) by mechanisms that remain incompletely understood. Here, we examined the role of Mitochondrial Rho GTPase 1 (Miro1), an outer mitochondrial membrane enzyme, in regulating skeletal muscle insulin action and glucose homeostasis in type 2 diabetes (T2D). In a cross-sectional clinical study, we show that Miro1 accumulates in the skeletal muscle of patients with obesity and T2D, which was further replicated in mouse models of T2D. This accumulation is explained by inadequate insulin-mediated interaction between AKT and Miro1 at the outer mitochondrial membrane. In a randomized controlled trial (NCT02977442), we show that exercise training relieves skeletal muscle Miro1 accumulation while improving insulin sensitivity in patients with T2D. Muscle-specific Miro1 deletion improves oxidative capacity and insulin sensitivity in mice and cells. Taken together, these data support a key regulatory role for skeletal muscle Miro1 in the pathophysiology of T2D. ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT02977442.

papers.title: Weight Regain After Incretin Treatment: The Lean Mass Deficit Hypothesis and a Role for Testosterone Combination Therapy in Men.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs), dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1RA and triple (GIP)/GLP-1RA/glucagon agonists achieve placebo-subtracted weight loss of 15% to 22%. Their long-term value depends on how well the weight loss is maintained and on the composition of weight loss, not only amount of weight loss. Part of incretin-induced weight loss is lean tissue. It is unknown whether the proportion of lean mass, and especially, muscle mass loss is greater than with other weight-loss interventions, and whether it may cause clinically meaningful harm. Men with obesity commonly have low or low-normal testosterone, which is associated with reduced muscle mass, increased visceral adiposity, impaired insulin sensitivity, and increased cardiovascular risk. We propose, as an exploratory hypothesis, that in men with obesity and low testosterone, combining incretin therapy with testosterone therapy may preserve muscle mass, increase the proportion of weight lost as fat mass, and reduce fat-predominant weight regain after incretin discontinuation. Resistance exercise and adequate protein intake are first-line measures for preserving muscle mass during weight loss. No lifestyle measure reliably prevents the fat-predominant weight regain that follows diet discontinuation, and long-term adherence to lifestyle interventions is poor. We position testosterone therapy as a pharmacological adjunct for weight loss maintenance in men with obesity and low testosterone, to be evaluated in clinical trials. The only direct human data come from a small, non-randomized pilot study and are hypothesis-generating. The clinical consequences of incretin-associated loss of lean mass, and particularly muscle mass, should be investigated in future studies. The hypothesis requires evaluation in randomized controlled trials that properly assess changes in lean mass and muscle mass, along with safety monitoring, before it can inform clinical practice.

papers.title: Integrated Single-Myofibre Multi-Omics Correlates Inflammatory State to Myosin Energetics in ICU-Acquired Weakness.
papers.abstract: Skeletal muscle atrophy is a pervasive complication of critical illness that worsens survival and recovery, yet remains poorly explained by current clinical or molecular markers. To directly connect disease-associated molecular states to the contractile machinery, this study combined sequential functional, transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of the same single human skeletal myofibres from critically ill patients in the intensive care unit with acquired weakness (ICU-AW) and controls. This integrated approach provides a framework for validating molecular signals directly within the cellular and biomechanical context. Differential expression analyses between control and ICU-AW myofibres show marked donor-level heterogeneity, with no differentially expressed features (FDR < 0.05). Ranked gene set enrichment analyses revealed distinct transcriptional and proteomic signatures between conditions, as well as a subtle yet conserved myofibre state enriched in ICU-AW, characterised by inflammatory and chemotactic gene programmes, intracellular structural remodelling and bioenergetic adaptation. Nineteen features were significantly (FDR < 0.05) altered at both RNA and protein levels from the same myofibre. Overall, these 19 overlapping features link an inflammatory transcriptional landscape to a proteomic shift toward mitochondrial and translational machinery, revealing a coordinated stress-adaptation programme with selective post-translational control in fibres from patients with ICU-AW. Further integration with the functional dataset revealed fibres in this state displayed selectively disrupted myosin dynamics, evidenced by prolonged ATP turnover time of myosin heads in their super-relaxed conformation, suggesting altered myosin energetics as a contributor to muscle dysfunction. These findings define a discrete, disease-associated myofibre state and validate a proof-of-concept integrative single-fibre framework for connecting multi-omic heterogeneity to molecular motor function in complex human disease. The identification of coordinated transcriptomic and proteomic programmes, validated through functional measurement, suggests that targeting this fibre state may offer new therapeutic opportunities in ICU-acquired dysfunction and related muscle disorders.

papers.title: Exercise training and mitochondrial remodeling in aging skeletal muscle: A translational systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Aging skeletal muscle shows impaired mitochondrial function, altered redox regulation, disrupted fusion-fission balance, and reduced mitochondrial turnover. This translational systematic synthesis and meta-analysis evaluated whether exercise training remodels mitochondrial and functional outcomes in aging muscle. PubMed, EMBASE, and Web of Science were searched to June 26, 2026 following PRISMA 2020. Twenty-eight studies involving aged exercise groups compared to sedentary groups were included. Outcomes covered oxidative stress, mitochondrial dynamics, mitophagy, mitochondrial biogenesis/function, skeletal muscle morphology, and physiological performance. Random-effects meta-analysis showed a significant improvement in VO₂max/VO₂peak after exercise training (SMD = 0.46, p < 0.001; I² = 0%), whereas pooled changes in citrate synthase (SMD = 0.18, p = 0.450) and BMI (SMD = -0.09, p = 0.557) were not significant. The directional synthesis showed that mitochondrial biogenesis and function were consistently responsive across species, particularly for OXPHOS proteins, mitochondrial volume density, ATPmax, and SIRT1/SIRT3 signaling. Human and rodent studies assessed different, only partly overlapping mitophagy and mitochondrial dynamics markers. Therefore, differences in pathway responsiveness across species cannot be separated from differences in which markers were measured. Exercise training and lifelong physical activity were associated with changes in mitochondrial biogenesis, dynamics, mitophagy-related signaling, and muscle function in aging skeletal muscle. The observed patterns varied by training protocol and study design, but indirect comparisons and heterogeneous outcome measures preclude conclusions about the superiority of any modality. Human and rodent findings should therefore be interpreted as complementary evidence rather than equivalent estimates of biological response.

papers.title: Alternative splicing of a species- and skeletal muscle-specific microexon diversifies the menu of clathrin heavy chains in mice and rats.
papers.abstract: Little is known about alternative splicing of microexons in most tissues other than the brain. Humans have two homologous clathrin heavy chains. Ubiquitously expressed, CLTC drives clathrin-mediated endocytosis. Highly expressed in skeletal muscles, CLTCL1 instead regulates glucose metabolism. Previously, we reported that a conserved microexon (exon 31) in the CLTC gene is alternatively spliced during striated muscle development. Here, we identified a novel Cltc microexon (exon 33, hereafter microexon 33), which is only included in mouse and rat adult skeletal muscles. Microexon 33 inclusion shortens the CLTC C-terminus and adds 10 distinct terminal residues. This divergence occurs at the same position at which the human CLTCL1 constitutively includes its penultimate exon (another microexon). CLTCL1 is a pseudogene in mice and rats. Humans diversified the menu of clathrin heavy chains by gene duplication and tissue-specific gene expression, whereas mice and rats might have achieved similar diversification by tissue-specific regulation of Cltc alternative splicing.

papers.title: Whole-Food Protein Sources Differentially Modulate Postprandial Plasma Dileucine Profiles in the Post-Exercise State.
papers.abstract: Dileucine, a leucine-containing dipeptide, may enhance anabolic signaling more than leucine alone. This study examined postprandial plasma dileucine and leucine concentrations after ingesting animal- and plant- whole foods and their association with muscle protein synthesis rates (MPS). Secondary analysis was performed on plasma samples collected from two randomized controlled trials totaling 26 healthy adults (25 ± 4.3 y). Participants consumed low-fat pork (LFP), high-fat ground pork (HFP), complementary rice and beans (COMP), an iso-nitrogenous mixed nutrient beverage (ISO), or a carbohydrate control (CHO). Plasma concentrations and MPS was measured. Plasma dileucine increased significantly only after LFP ingestion (p < 0.05), with a greater 300-min iAUC compared to CHO (p = 0.038). Plasma leucine increased in all conditions except COMP and CHO with LFP demonstrating the highest concentrations (p < 0.05). A modest correlation was observed between dileucine Cmax and the change in MPS (ΔMPS; r = 0.436, p = 0.037), whereas leucine Cmax showed no significant association (r = 0.265, p = 0.102). Whole-food protein sources generally do not elevate plasma dileucine, except for LFP. While dileucine C max correlated with ΔMPS, the strength of this relationship suggests dileucine is likely one of several postprandial factors influencing MPS beyond free leucine.

papers.title: Timing the effort: Chronobiological drivers of skeletal muscle adaptation and metabolic health.
papers.abstract: Exercise acts as a non-photic zeitgeber, resetting skeletal muscle circadian clocks that regulate metabolism, mitochondrial function, and insulin sensitivity. This review synthesizes current evidence on how exercise timing modulates skeletal muscle clock function and metabolic adaptation, with emphasis on divergent molecular pathways, sex-specific regulation, chrono-nutrition, and emerging evidence on immune-circadian interactions, myokine-mediated muscle-organ communication, and cellular stress responses. Exercise performed at different circadian phases activates distinct signaling networks despite identical mechanical workloads. Early active phase exercise, typically performed following an overnight fast, preferentially activates the AMPK-SIRT1-HIF1α axis, promoting lipid oxidation, metabolic stress sensing, and circadian phase advancement through PER/CRY modulation. Conversely, late phase exercise favors p38 MAPK-ATF2/CREB-PGC-1α signaling, enhancing mitochondrial biogenesis, oxidative phosphorylation, and Akt-AS160-GLUT4-mediated glucose disposal. Emerging evidence further suggests that circadian regulation of macrophage polarization, cGAS-STING signaling, contraction-induced myokine secretion, and proteostasis may contribute to time-dependent systemic adaptations, although direct human evidence remains limited. In addition, pronounced sexual dimorphism indicates that estrogen-mediated regulation of BMAL1/CLOCK signaling influences mitochondrial function and substrate selection. In conclusion, exercise timing represents an important regulator of metabolic health. Integrating circadian biology, nutritional timing, chronotype, sex, metabolic phenotype, and immune-metabolic context may facilitate the development of precision chrono-exercise strategies for metabolic and cardiometabolic disorders.

papers.title: Diabetic Polyneuropathy Patients Exhibit an Altered Skeletal Muscle Proteome Phenotype.
papers.abstract: Diabetic polyneuropathy (DPN) is a debilitating complication of diabetes that affects motor nerves and may impair skeletal muscle health. This study investigated skeletal muscle proteomic alterations associated with DPN compared with type 2 diabetes without DPN (T2D) and healthy controls (CON). An exploratory proteomic profiling was performed in 15 participants divided into three groups based on clinical and neurophysiological diagnosis (DPN, n = 5; T2D, n = 5; CON, n = 5). Biopsies from the gastrocnemius lateralis muscle were analyzed using LC-MS/MS-based proteomics and pathway enrichment analyses. A total of 265 and 444 proteins were differentially expressed in DPN compared with T2D and CON, respectively (q < 0.05). Enrichment analyses revealed marked alterations in mitochondrial-related pathways, including cellular respiration, distinguishing DPN from both comparison groups. Differences between T2D and CON were present but less pronounced. DPN was characterized by downregulation of glycogen-regulating proteins (phosphorylase kinase G1 and A1) and upregulation of ferritin light chain (FTL), alpha actin 2, and myosin-binding protein H. DPN is associated with a distinct and progressive skeletal muscle proteomic phenotype, supporting mitochondrial dysfunction as a key feature and providing a basis for future mechanistic and therapeutic studies.

papers.title: Skeletal muscle transcriptomic profile of older adults with high-impact musculoskeletal pain in the study of muscle, mobility and aging (SOMMA).
papers.abstract: High-impact musculoskeletal pain (i.e., pain that limits daily activities and function) affects a substantial proportion of older adults and is associated with accelerated mobility decline. While skeletal muscle is central to movement and functional capacity, its molecular contribution to pain-related disability in aging remains poorly understood. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from 742 community-dwelling adults aged 70 years or older from the Study of Muscle, Mobility and Aging (SOMMA). Bulk RNA sequencing was performed on vastus lateralis muscle biopsies. Pain impact was classified using self-reported pain and limitations in activities of daily living. Differential gene expression was examined comparing high-impact pain, low-impact pain, and no pain, with sex-stratified analyses. Pathway enrichment analyses were conducted to identify biological processes associated with high-impact pain. High-impact musculoskeletal pain was associated with a distinct skeletal muscle transcriptomic profile, whereas minimal differences were observed between low-impact pain and no pain. Sex-stratified analyses revealed substantial differences in pain-related gene expression for men and women. In men, high-impact pain was characterized by enrichment of musculoskeletal structural and extracellular matrix pathways. In women, high-impact pain was associated with broader transcriptional alterations involving immune, inflammatory, metabolic, and cytoskeletal processes. High-impact musculoskeletal pain in older adults was associated with sex-dependent skeletal muscle transcriptomic signatures distinct from those observed in low-impact pain. These findings implicate muscle-specific molecular pathways in pain-related functional limitations and highlight the importance of sex-informed approaches to understanding and treating chronic pain in aging.

papers.title: Suspected Bulbar-Predominant Myasthenia Gravis Exacerbation in an Older Adult With Respiratory Deterioration and Silent Aspiration: A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is an autoimmune disorder of the neuromuscular junction characterized by fluctuating skeletal muscle weakness. Bulbar-predominant exacerbations may be difficult to recognize in older adults with multiple comorbidities, particularly when respiratory deterioration is initially attributed to cardiopulmonary disease. We report the case of an 83-year-old woman with generalized acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive MG, dementia with behavioral disturbance, moderate chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), chronic kidney disease, and previous deep vein thrombosis who was admitted to a psychiatric unit because of worsening paranoia and suspected delusions. During hospitalization, she developed progressive hypoxemia requiring transfer to the medical ward. Initial evaluation considered pulmonary infection, aspiration-related complications, and COPD exacerbation. Neurological examination subsequently demonstrated new predominantly facial and bulbar weakness with preserved limb strength, accompanied by progressive dysphagia and impaired secretion clearance. Videofluoroscopic swallow study demonstrated significant silent aspiration of thin and mildly thickened liquids; however, the etiology of the dysphagia and aspiration remained potentially multifactorial. Serial arterial blood gases demonstrated persistent hypercapnia; however, stable PaCO₂ values, preserved pH, markedly elevated bicarbonate, and positive base excess suggested a substantial chronic hypercapnic component with concomitant metabolic alkalosis, with underlying COPD representing an important potential contributor. In the context of known generalized MG and newly documented facial and bulbar dysfunction, a suspected bulbar-predominant myasthenic exacerbation was considered a potentially important contributor within a multifactorial respiratory deterioration rather than the sole cause. She was treated with intravenous immunoglobulin and escalation of corticosteroid therapy. Although her respiratory status stabilized, persistent bulbar dysfunction, dysphagia, and frailty remained, and following goals-of-care discussions, the family elected hospice care. This case emphasizes the diagnostic complexity of respiratory deterioration in older patients with MG and the importance of recognizing new bulbar dysfunction while carefully considering competing pulmonary, aspiration-related, cardiogenic, and functional contributors.

papers.title: Targeting Muscle-Specific E3 Ligases in Cancer Cachexia Through Structure-Based Virtual Screening of Small-Molecule Inhibitors.
papers.abstract: Cachexia is a multifactorial metabolic syndrome characterized by severe skeletal muscle loss that cannot be reversed by nutritional support. Common in cancer and other chronic diseases, it significantly increases morbidity and mortality. Muscle wasting is primarily driven by activation of the ubiquitin-proteasome pathway through the E3 ubiquitin ligases MuRF1 and Atrogin-1, which promote protein degradation and muscle atrophy. This study used computational modeling and docking to identify small-molecule inhibitors targeting these ligases, including repurposed drugs with anti-cachectic potential. Thalidomide and EM12-So2F were prioritized based on integrated docking, binding affinity, and drug-likeness/ADME analyses for validation in C2C12 myotube-based cachexia models.

papers.title: Trait-like proteomic signatures of stress resilience: correlates of freeze-like response resistance.
papers.abstract: The freeze-like response is a fundamental defensive mechanism that remains poorly understood despite its potential to impair functioning under acute threat. We examined its biological correlates using untargeted serum proteomics in participants exposed to ecologically valid simulated armed attacks, comparing untrained individuals ( n  = 20) with experienced police rapid response personnel ( n  = 20). Freeze-like responses, characterized by unresponsiveness to attack, were assessed via expert video analysis of participant performance during the scenarios. Serum samples collected before and after threat exposure were analyzed via LC‒MS/MS, identifying 1,238 protein groups. Experienced personnel demonstrated markedly greater resistance to freeze-like responses. No significant proteomic changes were observed from pre- to post-exposure in either group, suggesting that freeze-resistance may be associated with stable, trait-like signatures rather than acute stress-responsive processes. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis identified a module strongly correlated with freeze-resistance ( r  = 0.75, p  = 4 × 10 -9 ) and training status ( r  = 0.71, p  = 6 × 10 -8 ), which also correlated with skeletal muscle mass ( r  = 0.57, p  = 8 × 10 -5 ). This module was enriched for processes including extracellular matrix organization, muscle development, carbohydrate metabolism, and antioxidant activity. These molecular patterns may reflect the downstream effects of comprehensive training that integrates physical conditioning, operational experience, and psychological preparation. This study provides the first proteomic characterization of freeze-like response resistance under realistic threat conditions, supporting the view that resilience involves stable physiological adaptations rather than solely reactive stress mechanisms.

papers.title: Glucose-Lowering Therapies in Type 2 Diabetes-Associated Sarcopenia: Mechanisms, Clinical Evidence and a Muscle-Centred Framework.
papers.abstract: Sarcopenia is increasingly recognised as a clinically important comorbidity in diabetes mellitus, particularly in older adults and individuals with long-standing type 2 diabetes. Because skeletal muscle is the principal site of insulin-stimulated glucose disposal, declines in muscle mass, quality, strength and physical performance may exacerbate insulin resistance and glycaemic instability and increase the risks of frailty, disability, falls, fractures, cardiovascular events and mortality. Contemporary glucose-lowering therapies have transformed diabetes care through established cardiorenal benefits and weight reduction, yet skeletal muscle outcomes are rarely prespecified or systematically assessed in pivotal trials. This evidence gap is especially relevant for weight-reducing agents such as glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, which are often associated with reductions in dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived or bioelectrical impedance analysis-derived lean-mass estimates. However, these changes should be interpreted cautiously, as they often occur in the context of overall weight loss and may be influenced by alterations in body water. In addition, dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry- or dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry-derived lean-mass estimates do not directly quantify contractile skeletal muscle. Accordingly, reductions in lean-mass estimates alone are insufficient to infer clinically meaningful muscle loss without concurrent assessment of muscle strength or physical performance. This narrative review summarises the bidirectional mechanisms linking diabetes and sarcopenia and appraises major glucose-lowering drug classes from a muscle-centred perspective. It integrates mechanistic insights with human evidence on muscle-relevant outcomes, including body composition, strength and physical performance, and addresses practical safety and monitoring considerations in sarcopenia-prone phenotypes, including sarcopenic obesity. We also propose a pragmatic, hypothesis-generating Cardiorenal-Muscle Quadrant Framework that considers glycaemic efficacy and cardiorenal benefit alongside muscle reserve, functional status and treatment-related risks, with emphasis on functional monitoring, resistance exercise, nutritional optimisation and individualised glycaemic targets in older or frail adults.

papers.title: Are both hemolysis and impaired myocyte integrity associated with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency?
papers.abstract: Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) is a potent antioxidant enzyme. G6PD deficiency, predominant among males, is a neonatal "neurotoxic" risk, characterized by episodic hemolysis that is sometimes infection triggered. Clinical risk among heterozygous G6PD-deficient females is often under-recognized. Recent reports of rhabdomyolysis among G6PD-deficient individuals are reviewed here. In one case, a male athlete with G6PD deficiency (<10% activity) experienced multiple, acute episodes of rhabdomyolysis, painful muscle symptomatology, injury and hemolysis after strenuous exertion. Both his mother with G6PD-deficiency (<45% activity) and maternal grandmother have chronic histories of episodic or triggered fatigue-related disruptive symptoms. Other case reports of G6PD-deficient individuals with muscle injury and exertional symptoms (with or without hemolysis) showed unique laboratory findings of elevated creatine kinase, myoglobin, lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, and aminotransferases levels and myoglobinuria. Disrupted myocyte energetics and loss of cellular integrity can be attributed to impaired downstream pentose phosphate pathway (PPP)-related oxidant stress protection, which is a key enzymatic consequence of G6PD-deficiency. These triggered stresses may explain the muscle fatigue and propensity to exertional injury. Correlation between stress-sensitive-impaired muscle injury among all G6PD-deficient individuals, including neonates, requires further clinical validation to ascertain oxidant-stress impact of impaired PPP-dependent cellular energetics of red blood, white blood, neural, and muscle cells.

papers.title: The prevalence of nutritional disorders in inflammatory bowel disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: The epidemiology of nutritional disorders in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) remains poorly characterized. Existing evidence is fragmented across specific conditions or confined to single regions, and no study has simultaneously assessed the principal nutritional disorders-malnutrition, overweight or obesity, and sarcopenia-in a unified framework. To address this gap, we systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and China Biology Medicine from inception to July 31, 2024 and updated on July 30, 2026. Observational studies reporting prevalence based on standard diagnostic criteria were included. Pooled estimates with 95% confidence interval (CI) and prediction interval (PI) were derived using a random-effects model. Pre-specified subgroup analyses were conducted by sex, age, disease subtype and activity, diagnostic criteria, study setting and gepgraphic variation. Study quality and publication bias were also assessed. After literature screening, 201 studies across 32 countries were included. Underweight affected 11.5% (95% CI: 9.0-14.6%, 95% PI : 1.0-61.7), whereas consensus-based malnutrition [GLIM (Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition), ESPEN (European Society for Clinical Nutrition and Metabolism), MNA (Mini Nutritional Assessment), SGA/PG-SGA (Subjective Global Assessment or its variant Patient-Generated SGA) affected 27.6% (95% CI: 20.5-36.1%, 95% PI : 3.6-79.7). Notably, this malnutrition estimate was derived almost exclusively from hospital-based settings (over 80%) and predominantly from a single region. Overweight and obesity affected 23.1% (95% CI : 20.6-25.9, 95%PI : 8.1-50.8) and 13.5% (95%CI : 11.7-15.6, 95%PI : 2.9-44.6), respectively. For muscle depletion, low muscle mass defined by skeletal muscle index was identified in 48.3% (95% CI: 41.8-55.0%, 95% PI : 19.7-78.1), whereas consensus-based sarcopenia [EWGSOP (European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People) or AWGS (Asian Working Group on Sarcopenia)] affected 12.6% (95% CI: 6.1-24.2%, 95% PI : 0.9-70.6). Of note, the majority of included studies for malnutrition and sarcopenia were hospital-based. Active disease was associated with significantly higher prevalence of malnutrition. No significant differences were observed between disease subtypes. In conclusion, our findings provide a broad overview of the prevalence of major nutritional disorders in patients with IBD, highlighting that nutritional care in IBD should extend beyond simple weight monitoring. However, given the wide prediction intervals, these pooled estimates should be viewed as averages across highly heterogeneous settings rather than a precise global figure. Future research, particularly population-based studies with standardized diagnostic criteria across diverse regions, is needed to validate our observation.

papers.title: Relative muscle mass and grip strength as complementary correlates of metabolic syndrome: a nationwide DXA-based study of Korean adults.
papers.abstract: Both muscle mass and strength relate to metabolic health, but their separate contributions to metabolic syndrome (MetS) are unclear. Using the 2024 Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (KNHANES) with concurrent dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA)-based appendicular skeletal muscle mass (ASM) and handgrip strength (HGS), we examined the independent associations of relative muscle mass and HGS with MetS in Korean adults aged ≥40 years. We analyzed 3033 adults from KNHANES. ASM/body weight (ASM/BW) and HGS/body weight (relative HGS) served as primary indicators. Participants were classified into four groups by sex-specific medians of both indicators, and complex-sample logistic regression estimated odds ratios (ORs) for MetS with both indicators entered simultaneously. In the fully adjusted joint model, ASM/BW was inversely associated with MetS in men (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.73-0.86) and women (OR 0.86, 0.80-0.92), as was relative HGS (men OR 0.98, 0.96-0.99; women OR 0.97, 0.95-0.98). The odds of MetS were highest with concurrently low muscle mass and strength (men OR 3.04; women OR 2.42). The ASM/BW association persisted when MetS was defined without the waist criterion, whereas the relative HGS association was attenuated; ASM/BMI showed similar inverse associations, whereas ASM/Ht² showed a different pattern. ASM/BW showed more consistent associations with MetS across the sensitivity analyses performed than relative HGS, although associations differed by normalization method, the optimal choice of which remains uncertain. Because the design is cross-sectional, these findings indicate association only and require prospective validation before clinical application.

papers.title: Emerging roles of OSM and EDA2R-NIK signalling in cancer-associated muscle wasting.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated cachexia (CAC) is a multifactorial metabolic syndrome characterized by progressive skeletal muscle wasting that reduces physical function, compromises treatment tolerance, and contributes to cancer-related mortality. Although systemic inflammation is a major driver of CAC, the mechanisms through which circulating inflammatory signals are translated into muscle-specific catabolic programmes remain incompletely understood. Recent studies have identified oncostatin M (OSM), a member of the IL-6 cytokine family, as an important mediator of cancer-induced muscle wasting through OSM/JAK/STAT3 signalling. OSM also induces the expression of ectodysplasin A2 receptor (EDA2R) in skeletal muscle, which engages NF-κB-inducing kinase (NIK)-dependent non-canonical NF-κB signalling to promote atrophy-related gene expression, proteolysis, and metabolic dysfunction. Beyond CAC, the emerging association of EDA2R with aging, muscle-wasting disorders, and circulating disease signatures highlights its broader biological and translational relevance. In this review, we discuss recent advances in the understanding of mechanisms underlying skeletal muscle wasting linked to CAC. Specifically, we focus on OSM/JAK/STAT3 and EDA2R-NIK signalling and explore their potential implications for targeted therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Emerging evidence suggests that circadian disruption and muscle wasting form a self-reinforcing loop.
papers.abstract: Circadian disruption and skeletal muscle wasting frequently co-occur in critical illness, shift work, and aging. We propose a bidirectional self-reinforcing loop in which each process amplifies the other. Environmental disruption of the skeletal muscle clock impairs protein turnover and mitochondrial function, triggering atrophy. The resulting loss of muscle mass weakens peripheral clock output and disrupts systemic circadian rhythms. The forward arm is supported by genetic evidence, particularly from global Bmal1 knockout models and human sleep-deprivation studies. The reverse arm is supported by correlative evidence from clinical observations and disease models. Chronotherapeutic interventions targeting this loop have shown preclinical efficacy and warrant clinical translation.

papers.title: Stage-specific transcriptional atlas of goose satellite cells uncovers sex-biased molecular dynamics associated with embryonic skeletal muscle development.
papers.abstract: Sexual dimorphism in avian skeletal muscle is established during embryogenesis, but the stage-resolved transcriptional programs governing this process in geese remain largely unexplored. To construct a stage-specific transcriptional atlas of muscle satellite cells (SMSCs), we performed histological examination and RNA sequencing of PAX7 + SMSCs isolated from male and female Zhedong White goose embryos across four developmental stages (E13, E15, E18, and E23). Quantitative PCR was used to validate selected differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Although myofiber morphology exhibited no overt sexual divergence, immunofluorescence revealed distinct sex- and stage-dependent dynamics, with male embryos displaying a higher PAX7 + cell abundance at E18 and females at E23. Transcriptomic profiling identified 357, 261, 312, and 672 DEGs at E13, E15, E18, and E23, respectively, uncovering a progressively intensifying sexual bias. At E13, female-biased DEGs were enriched for positional identity genes (HOXC9/C11, HOXD12/13) and pro-proliferative factors (GDF7, FGF16), whereas male-biased DEGs included adhesion molecules (IGSF10/11). At E15, females upregulated genes linked to myofiber maturation (ACTA1, MYH7B) and lipid metabolism (PLIN1, ADIPOQ), while males showed enrichment in extracellular matrix remodeling (MMP7, COL17A1) and immune-related pathways. At E18, females enhanced neuroendocrine signaling (ADCYAP1, AGTR2), whereas males upregulated contractile apparatus components (RYR1, CASQ1) and testis-associated transcripts (BRDT, DHH). By E23, females exhibited signatures of metabolic and neuromuscular optimization, whereas males showed enrichment in extracellular matrix genes (COL11A2, COL9A1/2) and masculinization-associated factors (YBX2, GGN). Temporal pathway analysis demonstrated a progression from immune/chemokine processes at E13, through cytoskeletal organization at E15 and supramolecular fiber components at E18, to DNA metabolism coupled with chemokine signaling at E23. Protein-protein interaction network analysis pinpointed stage-specific hub genes: EGFR (E13), ACTA1/ADIPOQ (E15), RAC2 (E18), and GNG10 (E23). Quantitative PCR validated eight selected DEGs. Collectively, this transcriptional atlas delineates sex-biased molecular dynamics that operate within the Zhedong White goose SMSC pool in the absence of conspicuous histological differences, and provides a foundational gene resource for prioritizing mechanistic investigations into sexually dimorphic muscle development, focusing specifically on the embryonic leg muscles.

papers.title: Targeting host ferroptosis in cancer cachexia: Tumor-immune triggers, tissue wasting, and the therapeutic paradox.
papers.abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic wasting syndrome driven by tumor burden, chronic inflammation, disrupted nutrient handling, and neuroendocrine stress. Supportive nutrition, exercise, and symptom management rarely restore lean mass, function, or treatment tolerance once wasting is established. Ferroptosis, iron-dependent cell death caused by phospholipid peroxidation, may connect inflammatory iron redistribution, lipid remodeling, mitochondrial stress, and impaired antioxidant defenses. This review critically evaluates ferroptosis in cachexia from a tumor-host pharmacology perspective, distinguishing causal evidence from associated oxidative signatures. We highlight two experimentally supported mechanisms: neutrophil-derived lipocalin-2 in lung cancer cachexia and tumor exosomal miR-203a-3p in pancreatic cancer-associated muscle wasting. We also examine the paradox that tumor ferroptosis induction may weaken host-tissue resistance and worsen muscle and adipose loss. We propose a "split-ferroptosis" strategy combining tumor sensitization with host-protective iron modulation, lipid peroxide scavenging, endogenous defense reinforcement, and biomarker-guided patient selection to expand the tumor-host therapeutic index.

papers.title: The lipotoxicity-ferroptosis axis in the transition from insulin resistance to type 2 diabetes: mechanistic integration and therapeutic opportunities.
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance is an early feature of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), but progression to persistent hyperglycemia requires failure of pancreatic β-cell compensation. Lipotoxicity develops when adipose storage and oxidative capacity are exceeded, increasing fatty-acid flux and accumulation of ceramides, diacylglycerols, and oxidizable phospholipids in liver, skeletal muscle, and pancreatic islets. Ferroptosis is an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by uncontrolled phospholipid peroxidation. Lipotoxicity can increase ferroptosis susceptibility by enriching polyunsaturated fatty acid-containing membrane phospholipids, increasing organelle-derived reactive oxygen species, and weakening system Xc--glutathione-glutathione peroxidase 4 defense; however, expansion of a redox-active iron pool is a distinct, cell- and context-dependent requirement. We organize these processes into a four-state working model spanning metabolic compensation, systemic lipid overflow and insulin resistance, ferroptosis sensitization, and β-cell decompensation. This is a non-obligate conceptual trajectory rather than a universally recognized clinical sequence. Evidence is strongest in pancreatic β-cell and liver models; direct skeletal-muscle causality is limited, and a causal role in human T2DM has not been established. Ferroptosis also has cell-specific effects: protecting β cells may be beneficial, whereas ferroptotic removal of selected inflammatory or lipid-storing cell populations can improve metabolic outcomes in some models. Upstream lipid unloading through weight loss and established metabolic treatments has the greatest clinical maturity. ACSL4/LPCAT3-dependent membrane remodeling, GPX4-centered defense, ferritinophagy, labile iron, parallel suppressor systems, and targeted delivery remain predominantly preclinical or candidate approaches. Multidimensional biomarker panels may support future mechanistic studies, but no individual marker or composite panel is currently validated to diagnose ferroptosis or a ferroptosis-susceptible phenotype in T2DM. The lipotoxicity-ferroptosis axis should therefore be viewed as a testable, tissue-specific amplifier rather than a universal or solitary cause of T2DM.

papers.title: Sarcopenia and muscle dysfunction in young adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus: associations with bone mineral density.
papers.abstract: To evaluate bone mineral density (BMD), body composition, muscle strength, physical performance, and the prevalence of sarcopenia in young adults with type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), and to explore clinical, metabolic, and skeletal correlates associated with sarcopenia. A cross-sectional study that evaluated BMD, body composition, muscle strength, and physical performance in 42 young adults with T1DM compared with 42 age- and sex-matched non-diabetic controls. DXA was used to assess areal and volumetric BMD, as well as whole-body composition, while muscle strength and function were evaluated using handgrip strength, gait speed, sit-to-stand, and timed up-and-go tests. Sarcopenia was defined following EWGSOP2 criteria. Areal and volumetric BMD values did not differ between groups at the lumbar spine, femoral neck, or total hip, suggesting preserved BMD in this young population. Body composition, including appendicular skeletal muscle mass index, was also similar between groups. In contrast, the T1DM group displayed significantly reduced muscle strength and impaired physical performance across multiple functional tests. Sarcopenia was diagnosed in 23.8% of T1DM participants, whereas no cases were identified in controls (OR 23.3). Within the T1DM group, participants with sarcopenia exhibited lower femoral BMD and cortical surface BMD than those without sarcopenia. Young adults with T1DM exhibit a high prevalence of sarcopenia and impaired muscle function despite preserved BMD and muscle mass. Among individuals with T1DM, sarcopenia was associated with lower femoral BMD and cortical surface BMD, supporting the importance of early musculoskeletal assessment in diabetes care.

papers.title: Exploring the potential targets and possible mechanisms of Shenqi Fuzheng Injection in the treatment of cancer-associated muscle wasting based on network pharmacology.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated muscle wasting (CAMW) is a debilitating condition observed in cancer patients, characterized by progressive skeletal muscle loss driven by tumor-secreted inflammatory cytokines, metabolic reprogramming, and enhanced apoptotic signaling, severely affecting the quality of life of patients. Shenqi Fuzheng Injection (SFI) is a traditional Chinese medicine preparation made from Codonopsis pilosula (Dangshen) and Astragalus membranaceus (Huangqi) in specific proportions, which has the effects of replenishing qi, strengthening the body, alleviating the side effects of radiotherapy and chemotherapy, relieving fatigue, and enhancing immune function. This study aims to explore the potential mechanisms of SFI in cancer-associated muscle wasting-a clinically significant form of sarcopenia frequently observed in cancer patients-through network pharmacology and molecular docking techniques. The key components in Shenqi Fuzheng Injection were found to have strong binding affinity with Caspase-3, Caspase-8, TNF, and TP53. Cell experiments further verified the effects of Shenqi Fuzheng Injection in alleviating mitochondrial damage in myoblasts and reducing apoptosis. Comprehensive analysis indicates that Shenqi Fuzheng Injection may target Caspase-3 and Caspase-8 to reduce apoptosis, thereby achieving therapeutic effects on cancer-associated muscle wasting. This study is exploratory and hypothesis-generating in nature; further in vivo validation is required to confirm these computational predictions.

papers.title: Serum metabolic signatures associated with running performance in healthy men living in a cold environment: insights into amino acid and energy metabolism.
papers.abstract: Chronic exposure to cold environments may impose distinct metabolic demands that are relevant to physical performance; however, the metabolic characteristics associated with physical performance in individuals living in cold environments remain incompletely understood. We aimed to characterize serum metabolomic profiles associated with differences in physical performance among healthy adults residing in a cold region. Among 178 healthy males residing in a cold-region environment, 141 participants with available serum metabolomics data were included and stratified according to 3,000-meter running performance into Good (≤14 minutes 13 seconds, n = 76) and Poor (>14 minutes 13 seconds, n = 65) groups. Fasting serum samples underwent untargeted ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry profiling. Differentially abundant metabolites were identified using covariate-adjusted linear models implemented in the limma framework, with appendicular skeletal muscle mass index included as a continuous covariate. Differentially abundant metabolites were defined using a Benjamini-Hochberg FDR-adjusted P  < 0.05 and |log 2 FC| > 0.25. Global metabolic profiles were explored using PCA and PLS-DA, followed by KEGG pathway enrichment analysis. A total of 141 males aged 28-40 years were included. After adjustment for ASMI, 10 differentially abundant metabolites were identified between the Good and Poor groups. Six metabolites showed higher adjusted abundances in the Good group, including cortisol (FDR = 0.031, log 2 FC = 0.321, 95% CI: 0.155 to 0.488), whereas four metabolites showed higher adjusted abundances in the Poor group, including glutamic acid (FDR = 0.013, log 2 FC = -0.262, 95% CI: -0.380 to -0.145). Nominally significant enrichment was observed for nitrogen metabolism ( P value = 0.011), arginine biosynthesis ( P value = 0.026), butanoate metabolism ( P value = 0.028), and histidine metabolism ( P value = 0.030); however, no pathway remained significant after FDR correction. Differences in running performance were associated with distinct serum metabolic patterns involving amino-acid and nitrogen metabolism, phospholipid metabolism, and stress- and redox-associated metabolic processes. These findings may provide metabolic hypotheses on inter-individual differences in running performance and identify candidate metabolic pathways for further investigation.

papers.title: Chronic Limb-Threatening Ischemia Shows No Adaptability of Mitochondrial Function After Revascularisation.
papers.abstract: Peripheral arterial disease (PAD) impairs limb perfusion, leading to myopathy characterised by altered mitochondrial content and respiration. Because ischemic muscle appears to adapt differently across PAD stages, we examined stage-specific skeletal-muscle mitochondrial function before and after successful revascularisation. Muscle biopsies of gastrocnemius and vastus lateralis muscle were obtained from 32 patients-21 with intermittent claudication (IC) and 11 with chronic limb-threatening ischemia (CLTI)-before and 6 weeks after successful revascularisation. Mitochondrial respiration was assessed by high resolution respirometry (HRR). HRR results were normalised to citrate synthase activity (CSA) as a marker of mitochondrial content. Inter-individual variation was expressed as the gastrocnemius-to-vastus respiration ratio ('GV ratio'). In the IC group, CSA-normalised mitochondrial respiration of gastrocnemius muscle was significantly reduced after revascularisation, paralleled by a significant decline in the GV ratio. In contrast, CLTI patients showed no significant pre- to postoperative change in CSA-normalised respiration or GV ratio, but mitochondrial content significantly improved by revascularisation. Mitochondrial respiration 6 weeks after successful revascularisation adapts only modestly in milder PAD stages such as IC, while more advanced stages (CLTI) display no functional adaptations. These findings suggest that mitochondrial adaptive capacity is stage-dependent and may require targeted therapeutic strategies beyond revascularisation alone, especially in CLTI.
