However, these studies used high-fat purified diets, containing reduced amounts of fiber compared to non-purified diets, known to alter gut physiology and microbiome composition. Therefore, we evaluated the effect of purified HFD-induced obesity on enteric neuron density and gastrointestinal transit compared to its proper control diet, that is, a purified control diet. Wild type mice were fed a standard chow diet, purified low fat diet (LFD) or HFD. Colonic transit was measured via glass bead expulsion following 12, 18, and 24 weeks of diet. Colonic muscularis externa was collected for immunofluorescent stainings of enteric neurons. Starting from 18 weeks of HFD, a decline in enteric neuron number was observed compared to LFD. In addition, delayed colonic transit was observed in HFD-fed mice when compared to LFD-fed animals after 18 weeks of exposure. Our study demonstrates that prolonged exposure to a HFD results in a reduced enteric neuron density and delayed colonic transit, and underscores the need to use a proper control diet when evaluating the impact of a HFD on gut physiology.

papers.title: Dietary Soybean and Kappaphycus sp. Differentially Modulate Gut Microbiota Diversity and Predicted Functional Profile in Nile Tilapia (Oreochromis niloticus).
papers.abstract: Diet composition shapes gut microbiota, influencing nutrient utilization, health, and growth. The shift toward sustainable ingredients such as soybean meal (SB) and seaweed (SW) requires an understanding of their effects on the gut microbiota. This study investigated how SB and SW diets modulate gut microbiota and predicted functional profile in Nile tilapia. Fish were assigned to four dietary treatments for 62 days: fishmeal (FM), SB, SW, and a natural meal (NM, non-formulated diet). Gut microbiota were characterized using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, and functional potential was inferred using PICRUSt2. Diet significantly influenced microbial beta diversity (PERMANOVA, R 2  = 0.60, F = 4.05, p = 0.001). Alpha diversity was highest in the SW and lowest in the NM, with a significant difference detected only between these groups. Fusobacteriota and Pseudomonadota predominated across treatments, while Cetobacterium was consistently identified as a core genus. SB and SW diets were associated with distinct taxonomic and predicted functional profiles. SB diet showed higher representation of pathways related to nucleotide turnover, central carbon metabolism, and stress response, and was associated with growth performance. SW showed higher predicted abundances of amino acid biosynthesis and carbohydrate metabolism pathways, and achieved the highest protein digestibility. In contrast, NM showed lower predicted functional potential and lower growth indices. Overall, SB and SW were associated with changes in microbial composition and predicted metabolic functions while maintaining relatively stable core microbiota. These findings support the relevance of gut microbiota as a biological indicator when evaluating sustainable feed ingredients for Nile tilapia aquaculture.

papers.title: Silybum marianum peptide-rich fraction alleviates acute liver injury by inhibiting TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB and is associated with changes in gut microbiota composition.
papers.abstract: Acute liver injury (ALI) is a severe and prevalent condition that can progress to irreversible liver damage and failure. This study aimed to investigate the prophylactic hepatoprotective potential of Silybum marianum peptides (SMP) in ALI and elucidate its underlying mechanisms. Using a carbon tetrachloride (CCl 4 )-induced ALI mouse model, we evaluated the dose-dependent effects of SMP. Additionally, we explored the modulatory effects of SMP on the NF-κB pathway, gut microbiota composition, and metabolite profiles. The role of SMP in the TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB signaling axis was further validated in a NIK-overexpressing Hepa1-6 cell model. Our results demonstrated that 14-day SMP administration did not significantly affect body weight, fasting blood glucose levels, or liver and spleen weights, and no significant difference in serum ALT activity was observed. Notably, SMP (200 mg/kg) significantly alleviated CCl 4 -induced liver injury, as evidenced by enhanced hepatic antioxidant capacity, reduced expression of proinflammatory cytokines, and attenuated immune cell infiltration. Furthermore, SMP was associated with changes in gut microbiota composition and community structure in CCl 4 -induced ALI mice. Mechanistically, SMP suppressed the TRAF3/NIK/NF-κB pathway. These findings highlight SMP as a promising candidate for the prevention of CCl 4 -induced ALI, acting through multimodal mechanisms involving anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and gut microbiota-associated pathways.

papers.title: A novel acyl-CoA binding protein (EnACBP): Molecular characterization, localization, and immunoprotective efficacy against Eimeria necatrix.
papers.abstract: Acyl-CoA binding proteins (ACBPs) are conserved intracellular lipid-binding proteins found across eukaryotes that play essential roles in fatty acid metabolism, membrane biogenesis, and cellular energy homeostasis. In this study, the gene ENH_00086110, which encodes a novel ACBP-family protein designated EnACBP, was cloned and characterized from Eimeria necatrix. The deduced mature protein contains 511 aa with a calculated molecular mass of 56.18 kDa. Bioinformatic analysis indicated that EnACBP contains a conserved acyl-CoA binding (ACB) domain in its C-terminal region (residues 424-506) and lacks any recognizable conserved motifs in its extensive N-terminal region. Recombinant protein (rEnACBP) was expressed predominantly as inclusion bodies in Escherichia coli, with a molecular weight of approximately 60 kDa, and was recognized by a mouse anti-His tag monoclonal antibody. qRT-PCR analysis revealed that the transcription level of EnACBP was significantly higher in gametocytes (GAM) and unsporulated oocysts (UO) than in second- and third-generation merozoites (MZ-2 and MZ-3) (P < 0.05). The native EnACBP was detected in both MZ-2 and GAM extracts, with a prominent band of ~72 kDa in GAM. Immunofluorescence assay localized EnACBP to wall-forming body type 1 (WFB1) and the outer oocyst wall. Following the E. necatrix challenge, the anticoccidial index (ACI) of immunized groups was 184.50 and 195.40 at an immunization dose of 100 µg per chicken per immunization. Compared to the controls, the immunized groups induced higher proportions of splenic CD4 + /CD3 + and CD8 + /CD3 + T lymphocyte and higher level of IgY antibody. These findings not only lay a foundation for understanding the role of EnACBP protein in gametogenesis and oocyst wall formation, but also present a potential protective antigen for the development of a subunit vaccine against avian coccidiosis.

papers.title: Selective Systemic Responses During Aeromonas salmonicida Subsp. Salmonicida Infection in Northern Snakehead (Channa argus).
papers.abstract: Northern snakehead (Channa argus) is a bimodal air-breathing fish in which erythrocyte-associated parameters remain relatively stable during physiological challenges such as aerial exposure. However, whether this characteristic is maintained during systemic infection remains unclear. In this study, temporal host responses were characterized following experimental Aeromonas salmonicida subsp. salmonicida infection by integrating haematological, leukocyte morphological, biochemical, and multi-tissue transcriptional analyses. Most erythrocyte-associated indices, including RBC, HGB, HCT, MCV, MCH, and RDW, showed no significant temporal changes, whereas MON, GRA, and PLT exhibited significant responses. Morphologically abnormal leukocytes increased from approximately 7% in healthy fish to 56% at 6 days post-infection and remained above 50% through 8 days, indicating persistent leukocyte-associated cellular alterations during infection. Biochemical responses were also selective, with changes primarily in protein- and metabolism-associated parameters. Transcriptional responses differed among peripheral blood, head kidney, spleen, and liver, including sustained casp7 suppression in the head kidney and distinct inflammatory and apoptosis-associated responses across tissues. Two-way ANOVA further identified significant tissue × time interactions for casp8, tnfα, and casp3. Collectively, A. salmonicida infection in northern snakehead was characterized by comparatively limited temporal variation in most erythrocyte-associated indices, alongside selective leukocyte, biochemical, and tissue-dependent transcriptional responses. These findings highlight a contrasting blood response characterized by persistent leukocyte alterations despite comparatively limited temporal variation in most erythrocyte-associated indices during bacterial infection in northern snakehead.

papers.title: SIRT6 Activation Improves Intervertebral Disc Health in the Aging Spine.
papers.abstract: Aging is a critical risk factor for intervertebral disc degeneration, a major contributor to chronic low back pain. Loss-of-function studies showed that SIRT6, a nuclear NAD + -dependent deacetylase, maintains disc health. We therefore investigated whether long-term SIRT6 activation via systemic delivery of the small-molecular agonist MDL-800 improves disc health in 24-month-old mice. Studies revealed healthy disc morphology, enhanced cell viability, and lower degeneration scores following MDL-800 treatment. SIRT6 activation decreased H3K9ac levels, improved extracellular matrix quality, and reduced senescence, as evidenced by lower levels of p21, IL-6, TGF-β, and CCL2. Tissue RNA-Seq, measurements of histone 3 modification, and multi-omics ATAC-seq/RNA-seq revealed altered epigenetic (decreased H3K9ac, H3K36me3, and H3K79me2) and transcriptomic landscapes. MDL-800 increased autophagy without affecting disc cellular bioenergetics. Plasma metabolomics, scRNA-sequencing of lymphoid tissues (bone marrow and spleen), and cytokine profiling showed good systemic tolerance of the treatment. While we noted a small decrease in vertebral structural parameters and mild hyperalgesia in treated cohorts, there were no vertebral fractures, and the broader motor function and behavior remained unaffected, raising no safety concerns. Our studies underscore the feasibility of SIRT6 activation as a pharmacological strategy to maintain the health of the aging spine.

papers.title: 2-Hydroxyisobutyrylation of SRSF9 regulates CD44 alternative splicing to promote colorectal cancer liver metastasis.
papers.abstract: Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) remains a major cause of cancer mortality, yet the metabolic mechanisms that remodel metastatic RNA-splicing programs are poorly defined. Here, integrated quantitative proteomics and lysine 2-hydroxyisobutyrylation (Khib) proteomics of patient-matched normal mucosa, primary CRCs, and liver metastases revealed a progressive increase in global Khib, with enrichment on RNA-splicing proteins. Serine/arginine-rich splicing factor 9 (SRSF9) emerged as a Khib-modified splicing factor whose expression and K155 Khib levels increased from normal tissue to primary tumors and liver metastases. Gain and loss of function studies in CRC cell lines, patient-derived organoids, subcutaneous xenografts, and splenic injection liver metastasis models showed that SRSF9 promotes proliferation, invasion, tumor growth, and liver colonization. Mechanistically, K155 Khib stabilized SRSF9 protein; the K155R mutation accelerated degradation and abolished SRSF9-driven malignant phenotypes. KAT7 and SIRT6 act as regulators of Khib modification, which positively and negatively modulate the K155 Khib modification of SRSF9, respectively. SRSF9 bound CD44 pre-mRNA through its RRM1 domain and promoted alternative splicing toward the oncogenic CD44V8-10 isoform, which was elevated in patient tumors and metastases and rescued the impaired proliferation and metastatic capacity caused by SRSF9 loss. Finally, a CD44V8-10-targeting antisense oligonucleotide suppressed CRC growth and liver metastasis in preclinical models. These findings define a KAT7/SIRT6-regulated Khib-SRSF9-CD44V8-10 axis that couples metabolic acylation to metastatic splicing and nominate CD44V8-10 as a therapeutic vulnerability in CRC liver metastasis.

papers.title: The gad B pathway confers oxidative stress tolerance in Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SAL and acts synergistically with L-glutamate to restore intestinal barrier integrity.
papers.abstract: The therapeutic efficacy of probiotics is often limited by poor survival under gastrointestinal oxidative stress; however, stress adaptation mechanisms in Lactiplantibacillus remain poorly understood. This study evaluated the probiotic properties of a host-derived strain, Lactiplantibacillus plantarum SAL, elucidated the molecular basis of its oxidative stress tolerance, and assessed whether L-glutamate (L-Glu) supplementation synergistically enhances its protective effects on intestinal barrier integrity. Probiotic traits (gastrointestinal tolerance, antibacterial activity) and antitumor efficacy (CT26 colon cancer xenograft model in nude mice) of L. plantarum SAL were assessed. Transcriptome profiling of H 2 O 2 -challenged SAL identified key stress-responsive genes. The effects of L-Glu supplementation on oxidative stress resistance and antibacterial activity were evaluated in vitro . A D-galactose (D-gal)-induced oxidative injury mouse model was used to investigate the restorative effects of the L. plantarum SAL + L-Glu synbiotic on intestinal barrier function. Compared with the reference strain L. plantarum WCFS1, SAL possessed superior probiotic traits, with significantly higher viability at 6% NaCl ( p  < 0.01) and in simulated gastric fluid at pH 1.5 after 2 h ( p  < 0.001). SAL administration markedly suppressed tumor growth and attenuated splenomegaly in the colon cancer model, with inhibition rates of 21.26% by tumor weight and 32.51% by tumor volume. Transcriptomic profiling identified 313 differentially expressed genes (149 upregulated, 164 downregulated), revealing glutamate decarboxylase ( gad B) as a key oxidative stress tolerance gene. Heterologous expression of recombinant Gad B confirmed its enzymatic activity (14.06 U/mg), mediating resistance via γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) biosynthesis. Supplementation with 1.5% L-Glu significantly increased the antioxidative capacity of L. plantarum SAL, maintaining viable counts at ~10 8  CFU/mL under 8 mM H 2 O 2 versus ~10 7  CFU/mL without supplementation. In the D-gal-induced oxidative damage model, the L. plantarum SAL + L-Glu synbiotic restored colon barrier integrity, increased goblet cell numbers, reduced inflammatory infiltration, and decreased plasma levels of malondialdehyde (MDA) and oxidized glutathione (GSSG) to levels comparable to those of normal controls ( p  > 0.05). Mechanistically, GadB -mediated GABA biosynthesis conferred cross-protection against oxidative stress, a function distinct from its canonical acid resistance role and previously unrecognized in Lactiplantibacillus . Augmentation of the gad B pathway by exogenous L-Glu enhances the probiotic efficacy of L. plantarum SAL by synergistically boosting oxidative stress tolerance and reinforcing intestinal barrier repair. These findings establish gad B-mediated GABA biosynthesis as a previously unrecognized cross-protective mechanism against oxidative stress, thereby extending the classical acid-resistance paradigm of the GAD system. This targeted metabolic modulation thus offers a promising synbiotic strategy for counteracting oxidative stress-linked gut disorders. Although Nrf2 activation is a plausible mediator, direct confirmation in intestinal tissues and dose optimization are still required.

papers.title: Palmitoyltransferase DHHC13 controls lysosomal cholesterol egress through palmitoylating Niemann-Pick C1.
papers.abstract: Protein S-palmitoylation provides a key regulatory mechanism for diverse cellular activities. Although palmitoylated proteins are frequently observed in cholesterol-enriched membrane microdomains, how protein palmitoylation reciprocally regulates cholesterol metabolism remains elusive. Here, we identify DHHC13 as a critical regulator linking protein palmitoylation to lysosomal cholesterol egress. Through an shRNA screen, we found that lack of DHHC13 led to pronounced lysosomal cholesterol accumulation. Mechanistically, DHHC13 directly palmitoylated Niemann-Pick C1 (NPC1). Loss of palmitoylation disrupted NPC1 association with lysosomes and caused its degradation, thereby impairing lysosomal cholesterol egress. Dhhc13 -/- mice phenocopied Npc1 -/- mice, displaying cholesterol deposition in the brain, liver, spleen, and kidney, along with significant Purkinje cell loss. Furthermore, two clinically relevant DHHC13 mutants (Q173H and R451Q) associated with neurodegenerative disorders showed diminished catalytic activity and failed to restore NPC1 palmitoylation or lysosomal cholesterol egress. Collectively, our findings uncover DHHC13 as a critical regulator of lysosomal cholesterol metabolism via NPC1 palmitoylation, providing mechanistic insights into cholesterol-related neurological disorders.

papers.title: 4-Hydroxycoumarin inhibits biofilm formation and enhances antibiotic efficacy against Escherichia coli O157:H7.
papers.abstract: Conventional bactericidal antibiotics often fail to eradicate Escherichia coli O157:H7 ( E. coli O157) infections due to biofilm-mediated antimicrobial tolerance, and monotherapy can inadvertently drive resistance selection. This study aimed to identify compounds capable of modulating LuxS/AI-2-related phenotypes and to evaluate their potential to disrupt biofilms and enhance antibiotic efficacy against E. coli O157. The effects of 4-HC on biofilm formation, extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) biosynthesis, and flagella-mediated motility were assessed in vitro. Antibiotic potentiation was evaluated through combination assays across multiple antibiotic classes. In vivo efficacy was tested in a murine systemic infection model, with qualitative histological observation used to evaluate splenic, hepatic, and ileal tissue damage. 4-HC disrupted biofilm formation by suppressing EPS biosynthesis and flagella-mediated motility, thereby destabilizing biofilm architecture and impairing bacterial dissemination. 4-HC acted as a broad-range potentiator for most antibiotics tested, with the most pronounced effect observed in combination with fosfomycin sodium. This combination reduced systemic bacterial burden and restored intestinal barrier function in vivo . In the murine model, the 4-HC-fosfomycin regimen improved survival and markedly attenuated splenic necrosis and ileal tissue damage, with efficacy superior to monotherapy. 4-HC disrupts biofilm formation and enhances antibiotic efficacy against E. coli O157 infection, supporting the strategy of combining biofilm-modulating adjuvants with conventional antibiotics to combat antimicrobial resistance. However, rigorous safety evaluation is required before clinical translation.

papers.title: Total Ginsenosides from Panax ginseng Improve Exercise Tolerance in Rats with Spleen Qi Deficiency-like Features: Integrated Metabolomics of Serum and Hepatic Mitochondria-enriched Fractions.
papers.abstract: Panax ginseng C.A.Mey. has traditionally been used to replenish Qi and strengthen the spleen, including for poor appetite and weakness associated with spleen deficiency. Ginsenosides are major constituents, but their metabolic effects under spleen Qi deficiency-like conditions remain to be clarified. To evaluate whether total ginsenosides (TGS) improve spleen Qi deficiency-like features in rats and characterize systemic and hepatic metabolic changes. A rat model was established using 50% food restriction combined with repeated weight-loaded swimming, and TGS (75, 150, or 300 mg·kg -1 ) was administered for 21 days. Body weight, grip strength, swimming endurance, biochemical indices, and mitochondrial ultrastructure were evaluated. Untargeted metabolomic analyses of serum and hepatic mitochondria-enriched fractions were performed in the control (CON), model (MOD), and high-dose TGS (TGS-H) groups, and hepatic SIRT1 and PGC-1α protein expression was measured. Lipid accumulation, mitochondrial membrane potential, and SIRT1 and PGC-1α expression were also examined in oleic acid-treated HepG2 cells. TGS, particularly at 300 mg·kg -1 , attenuated the suppression of body-weight gain and improved grip strength and swimming endurance. These functional improvements were accompanied by increased ATP content and ATPase activities and attenuation of mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities. After TGS-H treatment, serum levels of several amino acids increased, and lipid profiles shifted toward the control pattern. In hepatic mitochondria-enriched fractions, accumulation of selected fatty acids decreased, and levels of selected organic acids increased. TGS increased hepatic PGC-1α protein expression at all three doses, whereas SIRT1 expression increased significantly only at the high dose. In oleic acid-treated HepG2 cells, increased expression of both proteins was accompanied by reduced lipid accumulation and partial recovery of mitochondrial membrane potential. In rats with spleen Qi deficiency-like features induced by limited nutritional supply and repeated physical exertion, TGS attenuated the suppression of body-weight gain and improved exercise tolerance, accompanied by changes in energy-related indices. These findings provide experimental support for the traditional use of ginseng to replenish Qi and strengthen the spleen in relation to symptoms of weakness.

papers.title: Effects of pyridaben on the spleen and T lymphocytes and intervention strategy in grass carp (Ctenopharyngodon idella).
papers.abstract: The widespread use of pyridaben (PDB) poses serious threat to aquatic organism health. 6-Gingerol, a bioactive component of ginger, has been demonstrated to possess both antioxidant and immunomodulatory properties. However, the effects of spleen injury of PDB in aquatic species and the potential mitigating effects of 6-Gingerol remain insufficiently characterized. The present study aimed to characterize the toxic effects of PDB on the spleen of grass carp and to evaluate whether 6-Gingerol could effectively counteract PDB-induced toxicity. The results showed that PDB exposure could induce splenic erythrocyte extravasation, vacuolization, interstitial arrangement loose and apoptosis. Flow cytometry further revealed that PDB exposure decreased the proportion of splenic CD4 T-lymphocytes by 9.47% while increasing CD8 T-lymphocytes by 5.91%. In contrast, 6-Gingerol treatment reversed above pathological spleen injury and recover splenic CD4/CD8 T lymphocytes disturbance. Meanwhile, PDB exposure could disrupt mitochondrial morphology in grass carp spleen, accompanied by the suppression of glycometabolism-related genes and reduction in ATP levels. In contrast, treatment with 6-Gingerol effectively mitigated these PDB-induced mitochondrial dysfunctions. Further analyses confirm that 6-Gingerol inhibits PDB-induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) overload and 8-hydroxy-2'-deoxyguanosine (8-OHdG) overproduction, accompanied restoration of Nrf2 nuclear accumulation. Importantly, 6-Gingerol positively regulates AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) to counteract PDB-induced decline of peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor-gamma coactivator 1 α (PGC1α) in spleen. In conclusion, our results suggest that 6-Gingerol alleviates PDB-induced immunotoxicity and protects mitochondrial function in grass carp, an effect associated with the regulation of the AMPK signaling pathway. These findings provide theoretical basis for understanding the aquatic toxicity induced by PDB and offer new insights into the protective strategy of 6-Gingerol against toxic substances.

papers.title: Subverting colonization resistance: Salmonella pathogenesis at the interface of microbiota, metabolism and inflammasome.
papers.abstract: The intestinal tract is a key immune organ and microecological system, where colonization resistance (CR) mediated by gut microbiota prevents pathogen invasion. Salmonella disrupts CR via type VI and type III secretion systems (T6SS/T3SS), inducing dysbiosis, inflammasome-driven inflammation, and intestinal barrier damage. This creates a self-reinforcing cycle:dysbiosis alters microbial metabolites, sustains inflammation, and enhances pathogen fitness, favoring chronic infection. This review integrates molecular mechanisms of microbiota disruption, inflammasome activation, and metabolic imbalance to explain how Salmonella overcomes CR. We also highlight microbiota-based countermeasures, including probiotics, natural antimicrobials, and phage therapy, as promising strategies to restore gut homeostasis.

papers.title: Supplementation of Bacillus cereus Enhances Anti-Colitis Effects of Triple Probiotics in Mice: Correlative Evidence for a Gut Microbiota-Spermidine-Related Axis in Quadruple-Probiotic Protection.
papers.abstract: Background: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory bowel disease associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis. The triple-probiotic mixture BLE ( Bifidobacterium infantis , Lactobacillus acidophilus , Enterococcus faecalis ) contains highly oxygen-sensitive strains prone to viability loss during gastrointestinal transit. Adding facultative-aerobic Bacillus cereus generates a four-strain probiotic formulation BLEB. This study aimed to determine whether adding B. cereus improves the anti-colitis capacity of BLE and explore the underlying microbiota-spermidine-related regulatory mechanism. Methods: Acute dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis mouse models were applied to compare the therapeutic effects of BLE and BLEB. We evaluated disease phenotype, intestinal epithelial barrier integrity, and splenic Treg/Th17 immune homeostasis. Dynamic 16S rRNA sequencing and untargeted intestinal metabolomics characterized gut microbial and metabolic alterations, with Spearman correlation for microbiota-metabolite association analysis. Transcriptomic profiling was performed on DSS-injured Caco-2 cells to examine molecular responses to spermidine. Results: BLEB exerted superior dose-dependent anti-colitis effects compared with BLE. BLEB enriched beneficial Lactobacillaceae and restored luminal polyamine metabolites including spermidine. Spearman correlation revealed significant positive correlations between Lactobacillaceae -affiliated genera and polyamine levels. In vitro, spermidine reversed DSS-provoked transcriptional perturbations and upregulated the transcription of glutathione-centered antioxidant-related genes in Caco-2 cells. Conclusions: Ecological synergy introduced by B. cereus may reshape gut microbiota and increase microbiota-related spermidine, partially contributing to the enhanced mucosal protection conferred by BLEB. This work provides pre-clinical evidence supporting the development of aerobic-anaerobic combined probiotic cocktails for auxiliary UC therapy.

papers.title: Canonical and Non-Canonical Regulators of Lipid Metabolism in the Liver and the "Liver-Other Organs" Axes.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease and is closely associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and the recently conceptualized cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome. For decades, the pathogenesis of steatosis has been viewed primarily through the lens of insulin and the canonical transcriptional programs it regulates-sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1c, carbohydrate response element-binding protein, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors, and AMP-activated protein kinase. At the same time, recent data point to the existence of a complex network of non-canonical regulators that, independently of insulin, significantly modulate hepatic lipid metabolism. This review systematizes information on the fibroblast growth factors FGF21 and FGF19, adipokines (adiponectin, leptin), apolipoprotein C-III, as well as the monoamine neurotransmitters serotonin and dopamine. These molecules act within the interorgan axes "liver-adipose tissue," "gut-liver," "brain-liver," and "liver-spleen," coordinating lipolysis, gluconeogenesis, very-low-density lipoprotein secretion, inflammation, and fibrogenesis. Disruption of the dynamic balance between canonical and non-canonical regulators is central to the progression from simple steatosis to steatohepatitis and fibrosis. The clinical translation of this concept has already begun: the thyroid hormone receptor β agonist resmetirom and the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist semaglutide have received regulatory approval for specific categories of patients with noncirrhotic metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and fibrosis, while FGF21 and FGF19 analogs, the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide, and agents targeting apolipoprotein C-III are at various stages of clinical development or are being used for related metabolic indications. Expanding the insulin-centric paradigm to include non-canonical axes opens up new diagnostic and therapeutic possibilities for MASLD.

papers.title: Early-Life Oat Supplementation Is Associated with Altered Cecal Microbiota and Microbial Metabolic Profiles and Reduced Campylobacter jejuni Colonization in Broiler Chickens.
papers.abstract: Campylobacter jejuni is a leading foodborne pathogen that commonly colonizes the intestinal tract of broiler chickens and represents a significant food safety concern. Dietary intervention may provide a practical approach to modulate the gut microbiota and reduce pathogen colonization. This study investigated the effects of oat supplementation on C. jejuni colonization and dissemination, cecal microbiota and predicted functions, and cecal short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) and ileal amino acid profiles during early-life infection in broiler chickens. One-day-old Ross 308 broiler chickens were fed a basal diet or diets containing 10% oat (MDF) or 20% oat (HDF) and orally infected with C. jejuni at 2 days of age. C. jejuni loads in the cecum, jejunum, liver, and spleen were quantified by culture. Cecal microbiota composition and predicted functional profiles were characterized by shotgun metagenomic sequencing, while cecal SCFAs and ileal amino acids were quantified at 21 and 35 dpi using gas chromatography and an automatic amino acid analyzer, respectively. Oat supplementation reduced intestinal C. jejuni loads and limited dissemination to the liver and spleen, with the MDF diet reducing cecal loads by up to 3.3 log 10 CFU/g at 35 dpi ( p < 0.05). Infection altered cecal microbial diversity and community structure, while oat supplementation modified these infection-associated microbial patterns, with MDF showing the most consistent effects. Differential abundance analysis identified changes in taxa, including Bacteroides , Parabacteroides , and Phocaeicola , together with changes in predicted functions related to motility and chemotaxis, iron acquisition, and dormancy/sporulation. These microbial changes coincided with alterations in cecal isobutyrate and ileal amino acids, particularly glutamate, serine, proline, and aspartate, in MDF-fed infected chickens. Overall, MDF supplementation was most consistently associated with reduced C. jejuni colonization and dissemination and concurrent changes in the developing cecal microbial and metabolic profiles.

papers.title: Phenolic-Rich Extract from Pyracantha fortuneana Fruit Alleviates DSS-Induced Colitis in Mice: Insights from Gut Microbiota, Metabolomic, and Transcriptomic Analyses.
papers.abstract: Pyracantha fortuneana (Maxim.) H.L.Li fruit is a bioactive dietary resource, yet its effects on intestinal inflammation and the associated microbial, metabolic, and host responses remain poorly understood. This study characterized P. fortuneana fruit extract (PFE) and evaluated its protective effects in a dextran sodium sulfate (DSS)-induced colitis model using microbiota, metabolomic, and transcriptomic analyses. Chemical profiling confirmed the presence of representative phenolic acids, flavonoids, and condensed tannins in PFE. Administered before and during 2.5% DSS exposure, PFE reduced disease activity, attenuated colon shortening and the elevated spleen index, and improved colonic histopathological appearance. PFE also reduced IL-6 and increased IL-10 and serum GSH-Px levels, while high-dose PFE decreased TNF-α. It restored ZO-1 expression, increased colonic diamine oxidase levels, and tended to increase Occludin expression. PFE increased microbial diversity and evenness, reduced Turicibacter and Ruminococcus , and increased Prevotella and Jeotgalicoccus . Non-targeted metabolomics identified changes in selected cecal bile acid- and lipid-related metabolites, whereas transcriptomic and protein analyses implicated bile secretion- and PPAR-related responses, accompanied by increased ASBT, PPARγ, and NLRP6 expression. Collectively, these findings demonstrate the protective effects of PFE against DSS-induced colitis and support its further investigation as a potential food-derived bioactive ingredient for intestinal health.

papers.title: A Novel Cross-Kingdom Regulatory Mode of Thermostable miR166 from Taraxacum mongolicum Inhibits HepG2 Cell Proliferation in Association with Downregulation of the Candidate Target STAP2 .
papers.abstract: Taraxacum mongolicum contains various bioactive components. This study investigated the potential of thermostable microRNAs (miRNAs) derived from this plant as cross-kingdom regulators and evaluated their anti-proliferative effects on HepG2 cells. High-throughput sequencing was used to screen thermostable miRNAs and predict their target genes. Enrichment and target gene expression in gavaged mice were analyzed to assess cross-kingdom regulatory potential. Cellular assays evaluated anti-proliferative activity. miR166 was identified as a thermostable miRNA in T. mongolicum , and bioinformatics indicated its possible involvement in cancer-associated mucin-type O-glycan biosynthesis. RT-qPCR revealed that miR166 was negatively correlated with signal transducing adaptor family member 2 ( STAP2 ) mRNA expression. In mice, administration of total RNA extracted from fresh T. mongolicum or its water decoction led to significant changes in miR166 levels in stomach, blood, liver, spleen, and intestine, accompanied by reduced STAP2 mRNA, suggesting cross-kingdom regulation. Overexpression of miR166 induced a delay in G1/S transition in HepG2 cells in a concentration-dependent manner, accompanied by reduced STAP2 expression and decreased cell viability. These findings provide preliminary experimental evidence that thermostable miR166 from T. mongolicum is associated with inhibition of HepG2 proliferation. They also suggest STAP2 as a candidate regulatory target, offer a potential new molecule for further investigation in liver cancer intervention, and provide a preliminary molecular basis for the medicinal and edible value of T. mongolicum .

papers.title: Theabrownin from Pu-erh Tea Restores Intestinal Immunity via Gut Microbiota-Metabolite Network in Immunosuppressed Mice.
papers.abstract: Theabrownin (TB), a polymeric pigment derived from ripened Pu-erh tea, demonstrates beneficial effects on lipid reduction, weight management, and mitigation of metabolic syndrome. However, the role of TB in restoring immune function in vivo has not been studied. This study evaluated the therapeutic effects and underlying mechanisms of TB in cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced immunosuppressed mice. TB was administered at doses of 1.215, 0.608, and 0.304 mg/kg body weight, with levamisole hydrochloride (40 mg/kg) serving as a positive drug control. Each experimental group comprised eight mice. Evaluations primarily consisted of histopathological examination, enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay, Western blotting, flow cytometry, 16S rRNA sequencing, and ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS)-based untargeted metabolomics. The results demonstrate that high- and medium-dose TB treatment significantly alleviated immunosuppression, as evidenced by restored body and organ weights, colon length, splenic and colonic histoarchitecture, blood cell counts, and immunoglobulin levels. These improvements correlated with upregulated colonic cytokines, claudin-1, occludin, toll-like receptor 2/4, and reduced regulatory T cell populations. High- and medium-dose TB treatment also enriched beneficial gut microbiota, including Lactobacillus and Candidatus saccharimonas , accompanied by strong microbiota-metabolite correlations (M 2 = 0.725, p = 0.003). Metabolic KEGG pathway enrichment analysis revealed that moderate-dose TB significantly activated caffeine metabolism and histidine metabolism, accompanied by the enrichment of multiple immune signaling pathways driven by diacylglycerol series lipid metabolites, whereas high-dose TB induced a greater number of immune signaling pathways. Overall, TB may reverse CTX-induced immunosuppression by integrating gut microbiota-metabolite reprogramming, highlighting TB's potential as an immunomodulatory functional component of medicine-food homologous products.

papers.title: T2SS Components GspJ, GspL, and GspM Regulate Virulence in Vibrio alginolyticus .
papers.abstract: Vibrio alginolyticus is a major aquaculture pathogen whose virulence is largely mediated by the type II secretion system (T2SS). However, the functions of key T2SS components, including gspJ , gspL , and gspM , remain unclear. Earlier research indicated that a Scutellaria baicalensis extract at 8 mg/mL markedly suppressed the growth, motility, and biofilm-forming capacity of V. alginolyticus ND-01 (OD 600 = 0.5) following 12 h of treatment, with the resulting stress substantially altering the expression of multiple genes, including gspJ , gspL , and gspM . The gspJ -RNAi, gspL -RNAi, and gspM -RNAi strains were constructed using RNAi. Biological functional assays demonstrated that stable silencing of gspJ , gspL , and gspM markedly decreased biofilm formation ability (84.01%, 24.99%, and 78.26%, respectively) and host cell adhesion (73.57%, 75.65%, and 79.61%, respectively); gspJ and gspM silencing reduced motility (54.82% and 57.42%, respectively), whereas gspL silencing enhanced motility by 38.49%, indicating their essential roles in virulence-associated phenotypes. Notably, in vivo infection of Epinephelus coioides revealed that gspL -RNAi significantly attenuated pathogenicity, as evidenced by reduced host mortality (50%) and decreased bacterial colonization in liver and spleen tissues, compared with the wild-type group. Consistently, Label-Free Proteomic Analysis of the gspL -RNAi strain identified 189 differentially expressed proteins in the gspL -silenced strain, with enrichment in two-component signaling, ABC transport systems, and amino acid metabolism. Network analysis further positioned gspL as a central regulatory hub linking T2SS activity to signal transduction, transport, and metabolic pathways. In addition, the expression of gspJ -RNAi, gspL -RNAi, and gspM -RNAi exhibited distinct responses to environmental stresses, including pH and temperature variation. Collectively, our findings highlight that gspJ , gspL , and gspM are critical regulators of virulence in V. alginolyticus , with gspL playing a central role in coordinating T2SS function with global regulatory networks. This study advances our understanding of the pathogenic mechanisms of V. alginolyticus and provides potential targets for the development of anti-virulence aquaculture strategies.

papers.title: Dietary Cadmium Exposure in Black Goats: Impacts on Growth Performance, Serum Biochemical and Immune Parameters, Meat Quality, and Tissue Accumulation.
papers.abstract: Cadmium (Cd) present in soil can accumulate in plants and subsequently affect the safety and quality of animal-derived food products. This study investigated the effects of dietary Cd exposure derived from rice straw on the growth performance, serum biochemical and immune parameters, meat quality, and tissue accumulation of black goats. A 90-day feeding trial was carried out with 42 healthy male black goats at 4 months. Prior to the feeding trial, six goats were slaughtered to establish baseline group, and the remaining 36 goats were randomly assigned to two groups fed with a diet containing Cd-contaminated rice straw (CAD, n = 18) or not (CON, n = 18). At 30, 60, and 90 d, six goats per group ( n = 6) were randomly selected and slaughtered for sample collection. The results showed that dietary Cd exposure had no significant effects on growth performance and the indices of heart, liver, spleen, lung, and kidney ( p > 0.05). Meanwhile, it induced tissue-specific and time-dependent Cd accumulation, with lymph nodes identified as the primary Cd target tissue in goats, followed by kidney and liver ( p < 0.05). The CAD group exhibited higher concentrations of serum urea nitrogen and interleukin-10, and lower concentrations of serum glucose and creatinine. Fecal cadmium deposition efficiency (CdE) ranged from 95.68% to 97.01% in the CON group and from 68.48% to 88.74% in the CAD group, whereas the CdE in muscle and internal organs remained below 2% in both groups. These findings indicate that fecal excretion constitutes the predominant elimination pathway for ingested Cd, with only a negligible proportion retained in edible tissues and internal organs. However, based on the present findings, we cannot recommend the use of Cd-contaminated rice straw as a feed source for goats, nor can we confirm the safety of meat from exposed animals for human consumption. Further long-term studies, including human health risk assessments, are needed before any recommendations can be made.

papers.title: GoAstV Induced Mitophagy and Ferroptosis in the Spleen of Goslings.
papers.abstract: A novel goose astrovirus (GoAstV) has emerged in various provinces of China, leading to a mortality rate of up to 50% among GoAstV goslings. The spleen is an important immune organ in geese. Studies have shown that goslings infected with GoAstV exhibit higher viral loads in their spleens, and the spleens sustain damage. However, the mechanism underlying its induction of spleen injury remains to be elucidated. Therefore, a gosling infection model with GoAstV was established in this experiment. The Con group was subcutaneously injected with 0.2 mL of saline, while the GoAstV group was subcutaneously injected with GoAstV JX01 (2 × 10 6 TCID50/0.2 mL). Spleen tissues were collected on days 1, 3, 6, 9 post-infection (dpi). The results showed that the body weight of the GoAstV group decreased significantly, while the spleen weight and spleen index increased significantly. Post-mortem examination revealed that the spleen of the GoAstV group was significantly enlarged. The viral load in the spleen reached its peak at 6 dpi. Histopathological and electron microscopy revealed lymphocyte necrosis, autophagic lysosomes, and mitochondria autophagosomes. The spleen of the GoAstV group exhibited increased iron content, elevated malondialdehyde (MDA) production, decreased glutathione (GSH) content, and reduced glutathione peroxidase (GSH-Px) activity. RT-qPCR and Western blot analyses revealed that GoAstV upregulated mRNA expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines and inhibited anti-inflammatory cytokines. GoAstV also upregulated genes and proteins linked to ferroptosis and mitophagy, while downregulating those associated with anti-ferroptosis and SQSTM1. In conclusion, our findings suggest that GoAstV infection may induce mitophagy and ferroptosis in the gosling spleen, thereby contributing to splenic injury.

papers.title: Intrapancreatic Fat Deposition and Prostate Cancer Risk: A Primary Case-Control Study.
papers.abstract: IntroductionVisceral fat is associated with cancer risk. Intrapancreatic fat deposition (IPFD) has been associated with pancreatic diseases, but its role in extra-pancreatic malignancies remains unclear. This case-control study aimed to investigate the association between IPFD and prostate cancer risk.MethodsA total of 143 patients with newly diagnosed, treatment-naïve prostate cancer and 286 age-matched controls without malignancy were enrolled in this retrospective study. IPFD was assessed using unenhanced computed tomography (CT) by two markers: pancreatic CT attenuation (PanCT) and pancreatic-to-spleen attenuation ratio (P/S). Multivariable logistic regression was performed to evaluate the association between IPFD and prostate cancer risk, with sequential adjustment for demographic, metabolic, and hepatic parameters.ResultsThe risk of prostate cancer decreases as PanCT (p < 0.01) and P/S increases (p = 0.05). Participants with prostate cancer had lower pancreatic CT attenuation compared to controls. In fully adjusted models, higher PanCT quartiles were associated with progressively lower odds of prostate cancer (Q2: OR 0.32, 95% CI 0.15-0.69; Q3: OR 0.21, 95% CI 0.08-0.52; Q4: OR 0.11, 95% CI 0.04-0.29; all p < 0.01). Similar inverse associations were observed for P/S ratio quartiles (Q3: OR 0.30, 95% CI 0.13-0.68; Q4: OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.13-0.75).ConclusionIntrapancreatic fat deposition is independently associated with an increased risk of prostate cancer, regardless of hepatic fat and body mass index.

papers.title: Age-associated radiomic phenotyping in mice using multi-energy photon-counting and preclinical CT: an exploratory study.
papers.abstract: To investigate whether CT-derived radiomic features capture imaging patterns associated with chronological age groups in mice and to assess the influence of imaging platform and photon-counting CT reconstruction strategy on classification performance. Female C57BL/6NRj mice from three chronological age groups (28, 88, and 99 weeks; n = 11) underwent clinical photon-counting CT (PCCT) and preclinical Albira II CT. Heart, liver, and spleen were segmented and radiomic features were extracted. The individual mouse was defined as the independent biological unit. Model development and evaluation used nested leave-one-mouse-out cross-validation with all preprocessing, feature selection, model selection, and, where applicable, reconstruction-energy selection restricted to the respective training folds. Organ-level class probabilities were averaged to generate one mouse-level prediction. Monoenergetic PCCT reconstructions from 40 to 180 keV were evaluated, including a fully nested energy-and-pipeline selection analysis. A grouped mouse-level permutation analysis with 200 permutations was performed for the primary monoenergetic workflow. Albira II correctly classified 5/11 mice (45.5%; 95% CI, 21.3-72.0%), whereas PCCT-SPP correctly classified 10/11 mice (90.9%; 95% CI, 62.3-98.4%). The fully nested monoenergetic PCCT workflow correctly classified 9/11 mice (81.8%; 95% CI, 52.3-94.9%; balanced accuracy, 83.3%; macro-F1, 83.3%). Energy-specific performance varied considerably: 110 keV showed the highest accuracy (81.8%) and was selected in 7/11 outer folds, whereas the highest macro one-vs-rest AUC occurred at 130 keV (0.867). None of the 200 permuted analyses reached the observed fully nested monoenergetic accuracy (plus-one corrected Monte-Carlo p = 0.005). CT-derived radiomic features showed chronological age-group-associated patterns in this exploratory murine cohort, with classification performance varying substantially across imaging platforms and reconstruction strategies. PCCT-SPP showed the numerically highest performance, while monoenergetic PCCT demonstrated pronounced energy dependence without evidence for a universally optimal reconstruction energy. These findings require validation in larger independent cohorts and correlation with independent biological-aging reference measures.

papers.title: Macrophages Contribute to Pulmonary Hypertension Associated With Sickle Cell Disease.
papers.abstract: Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a fatal sequela in sickle cell disease (SCD) patients and occurs with greater prevalence compared to the general population. Macrophages (Mϕ) are one of the first immune cells to be recruited to the lungs in mouse models of PH, including SCD-PH, and a key cell type that contribute toward disease progression. Here, we first determined if phenotypic difference exist between control (C57BL/6) and Berkeley-SS (Berk-SS, SCD) mouse pulmonary Mϕs and, if so, how chronic moderate hypoxic exposure (~8,000 ft, Pb ~568 mmHg for 10 weeks) altered molecular and metabolic pathways. Next, we aimed to determine if the microenvironment of the Berk-SS lung is primed for Mϕs recruitment compared to the C57BL/6 lung. Using precision cut lung slice (PCLS), we determined PCLS from Berk-SS mice have significant increases in adhesion molecules associate with Mϕ recruitment and recruit splenic Mϕs at a greater rate compared to control mice. We confirmed these results in an acute hypoxic exposure (18,000 ft for 3 days) experiment and our results suggest that Berk-SS mice recruit more interstitial Mϕ with a pro-inflammatory phenotype when compared to C57BL/6 mice. Lastly, the depletion of Mϕ in our Berk-SS PH model improved right ventricular function, decreased pulmonary vascular muscularization, and improved exercise tolerance. Together, these data emphasize a critical role of Mϕ pulmonary recruitment in SCD-PH pathophysiology that is driven by inflammation.

papers.title: Red blood cell metabolome maps disease burden, mutation class, and splenectomy status in hereditary spherocytosis.
papers.abstract: Hereditary spherocytosis (HS) is caused by inherited defects in red blood cell (RBC) membrane and membrane-skeletal proteins, but the metabolic features associated with genotype, splenic selection, RBC injury, and clinical burden remain incompletely resolved. We performed RBC metabolomics in the VASCUSPHERO cohort, including 16 controls and 22 HS samples, and integrated omics data with splenectomy status, RBC deformability, microparticles, phosphatidylserine exposure, reactive oxygen species, calcium, CD47, complete blood count traits, and leukocyte subsets. The HS cohort included 12 spectrin beta, erythrocytic (SPTB)-only cases, 5 solute carrier family 4 member 1 (SLC4A1)/band 3 cases, 4 ankyrin 1 (ANK1)-only cases, and 1 combined ANK1/SPTB case. HS and control samples differed in global metabolomic space, with changes involving acylcarnitines, polyamines, pantothenate metabolism, gamma-glutamyl metabolites, sulfur metabolism, bile acids, and glutathione-related pathways. Metabolite and pathway scores correlated with reticulocytosis, deformability, RBC injury markers, and hematologic traits. Mutation-stratified analyses identified genotype-associated structure, whereas a cross-sectional analysis within SPTB-mutant HS identified splenectomy-associated metabolic and phenotypic differences. An exploratory, phenotype-derived burden score prioritized pantothenate, N1-acetylspermidine, N1-acetylspermine, gamma-glutamylputrescine, and selected acylcarnitines as candidate metabolic reporters. These findings position the RBC metabolome as an integrated, but not yet clinically validated, readout of membrane genetics, hemolytic stress, and splenectomy-associated remodeling. The Vascusphero project is a registered trail in ClinicalTrials.gov with identifier: NCT04451785 (https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT04451785).

papers.title: Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Deficiency Reprograms Macrophage Metabolism in Hyperlipidemia.
papers.abstract: Macrophages regulate inflammatory responses in hyperlipidemia and dysmetabolic states while performing a critical homeostatic function by clearing damaged or senescent red blood cells (RBCs) through erythrophagocytosis. This process delivers heme and iron that must be detoxified and recycled through NADPH-dependent pathways. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency (G6PDd), affecting ~6% of the global population, limits NADPH generation and predisposes RBCs to oxidative damage and hemolysis. Whether G6PD deficiency alters macrophage metabolic responses to RBC clearance in hyperlipidemic environments remains unknown. Humanized mouse models expressing canonical (hG6PD ND ), African (hG6PD A- ), or Mediterranean (hG6PD Med- ) G6PD variants were exposed to Western diet-induced hyperlipidemia. RBCs, plasma, and splenic macrophages were analyzed using metabolomics, lipidomics/oxylipin profiling, and quantitative proteomics. Hyperlipidemia increased circulating lipid species and altered RBC metabolism, while G6PD deficiency selectively reduced pentose phosphate pathway intermediates. Plasma metabolomics revealed signatures consistent with increased hemolysis in hyperlipidemic G6PD-deficient mice. Splenic macrophages from G6PDd animals showed biochemical evidence of erythrophagocytosis, glutathione depletion, and remodeling of central carbon metabolism. Variant-specific alterations included increased glycolytic flux, disrupted TCA cycle activity, and elevated succinate/fumarate ratios consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction. Proteomics revealed extensive mitochondrial and proteasomal remodeling. G6PD deficiency and hyperlipidemia converge to reprogram macrophage metabolism through NADPH limitation, redox imbalance, and impaired handling of RBC-derived metabolites. These findings identify an NADPH-dependent metabolic vulnerability linking RBC fragility, erythrophagocytosis, and inflammatory macrophage reprogramming.

papers.title: Gestational exposure to haloxyfop-R-methyl drives maternal and embryonic residue burden and hepatic biochemical injury in Wistar rats.
papers.abstract: Haloxyfop-R-methyl is a grass-selective aryloxyphenoxypropionate herbicide whose gestational exposure is toxicologically important because maternal xenobiotic burden can coincide with fetal organogenesis, placental transfer, and hepatic metabolic stress. The present investigation evaluated organ-specific accumulation of haloxyfop-R-methyl in pregnant Wistar rats and their fetuses following exposure on GD3, GD13, or GD17. It also assessed the corrective efficacy of narcissin and sophoroflavonoside (SFL) against pesticide-induced alterations in maternal hepatic biomarkers. Pregnant rats received haloxyfop-R-methyl orally at a sublethal dose equivalent to 1/10 LD₅₀ on gestational day (GD) 3, 13, or 17. Maternal and fetal liver, lung, spleen, and brain were collected on GD20-GD21 for LC-MS-based residue quantification. A parallel experiment measured maternal plasma alanine aminotransferase (ALT), aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and total bilirubin. These biomarkers were assessed after haloxyfop-R-methyl exposure alone or combined with narcissin or SFL. LC-MS calibration showed strong linearity, with slopes of 93,384.20 and 97,181.37 and uncentered R 2 values of 0.99993 and 0.99978. Haloxyfop-R-methyl was absent from controls but was detected in all examined maternal and fetal tissues. Residue concentrations differed among exposure-timing groups at terminal sampling. Maternal liver and lung showed the highest concentrations in the GD17-dosed group, reaching 0.619 ± 0.050 and 0.529 ± 0.041 µg g⁻ 1 , respectively. Fetal liver and lung also showed the highest concentrations in the GD17-dosed group, reaching 0.419 ± 0.035 and 0.405 ± 0.020 µg g⁻ 1 . Fetal-to-maternal residue ratios were highest in several organs in the GD17-dosed group, particularly lung, liver, and brain. Haloxyfop-R-methyl increased maternal ALT, AST, and total bilirubin across all exposure windows. The highest values occurred in the GD17-dosed group at terminal sampling. However, all groups were sampled on GD20-GD21, resulting in different intervals between dosing and sampling. Therefore, the observed differences cannot distinguish gestational stage effects from effects of time elapsed since exposure. Narcissin and SFL reduced pesticide-induced biochemical alterations. SFL showed greater protective efficacy across most endpoints, particularly bilirubin on GD3 and AST on GD13. Standardized effect-size analysis confirmed large haloxyfop-R-methyl-associated effects and measurable biochemical correction following flavonoid treatment. The integrated residue-biomarker framework characterizes exposure window-associated maternal-fetal residue distribution and flavonoid-mediated biochemical correction during pregnancy.

papers.title: Stepwise derivatization GC-MS/MS of 39 FFAs in spleen-deficiency rat liver.
papers.abstract: Free fatty acids (FFAs) are important targets in metabolic diseases. However, accurate quantification of a wide range of C2-C24 FFAs in the liver is challenging due to their structural diversity and large variations in abundance. To address this, a stepwise derivatization pretreatment was employed in this study: after liver homogenization, short-chain fatty acids were first extracted with diethyl ether-water (1:1, V/V). The ether layer was dehydrated with anhydrous Na 2 SO 4 and then derivatized with BSTFA. The remaining pellet was extracted with chloroform-methanol (1:2, V/V), and after nitrogen evaporation, the extract was subjected to methyl esterification. A quantitative method for 39 FFAs was established on a Trace1600-TSQ9610 platform (TG-SQC column, MRM mode). Methodological validation showed that for all FFAs, the linear correlation coefficients R 2 were ≥ 0.991, intra- and inter-day accuracies ranged from 85.94% to 115.28%, precision RSD ≤ 13.16%, stability RSD ≤ 14.91%, and the LLOQ ranged from 0.03 to 10 μg/mL. When applied to the livers of spleen-deficiency SD rats, the method revealed significant decreases in C14:0, C15:0, and C18:0, and significant increases in C9:0, C18:1n9c, and C20:4n6 (VIP > 1, |Log 2 FC| > 1, P < 0.05). This method provides a reliable tool for hepatic FFA profiling and the discovery of preliminary candidate biomarkers. Limitations of this study include a small sample size (n = 3 per group), which may affect the robustness of the supervised OPLS-DA model and the interpretation of the differential findings, and the extraction recovery was not independently evaluated.

papers.title: High Normal dietary casein attenuates bisphenol A-induced multiorgan toxicity in rats: Preservation of renal integrity, glucose homeostasis, and immune surveillance via modulation of oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis.
papers.abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) causes multiorgan toxicity via oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis, and the effect of nutritionally relevant elevation of casein intake is unknown. To evaluate whether a nutritionally relevant elevation of dietary casein (18% vs. 14%) attenuates BPA-induced multiorgan toxicity in rats, male Wistar rats were divided into four groups (n = 8/group) and treated for 35 days: control (14% casein), casein 18% alone, BPA (50 mg/kg/day +14% casein), and BPA + 18% casein. We measured oxidative and inflammatory markers, renal function, metabolic parameters, hematological parameters, histopathology and immunohistochemistry in kidney, spleen, and pancreas. BPA significantly increased malondialdehyde, interleukin-6, tumor necrosis factor-alpha, creatinine, kidney injury molecule-1, insulin resistance, white blood cells, neutrophils, and monocytes, and decreased reduced glutathione, glutathione S-transferase, superoxide dismutase, catalase, interleukin-4, serum soluble CD4 and CD8 protein levels, hemoglobin, red blood cells, platelets, and lymphocytes. BPA also caused renal tubular necrosis, splenic degeneration, pancreatic fibrosis, and upregulated caspase-3 and inducible nitric oxide synthase. Co-administration of 18% casein partially attenuated these effects, reducing malondialdehyde by 35-40%, creatinine by 40%, and insulin resistance by 53%, and restoring antioxidant enzymes and glucose tolerance. However, several parameters remained significantly different from controls. Nutritionally relevant elevation of casein (18%) provides significant partial protection against BPA-induced toxicity, supporting dietary protein modulation as a supportive strategy.

papers.title: Comparison of Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Between Individuals With Werner Syndrome and Those With Insulin-Resistant Type 2 Diabetes: Hepatic Steatosis and Fibrosis Indices.
papers.abstract: This study compared metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) in individuals with Werner syndrome (WS) and individuals with insulin-resistant type 2 diabetes (T2D). It also examined the association with imaging findings of MASLD in individuals with WS, clarified the characteristics of MASLD that accompany WS, and identified useful indices for its diagnosis in addition to imaging. Three hepatic steatosis and two hepatic fibrosis indices in 48 individuals enrolled in the Japanese Werner Syndrome Registry were compared with those in 101 Japanese individuals with insulin-resistant T2D from another clinical study. In individuals with WS, the liver/spleen ratio (L/S ratio) was calculated from computed tomography (CT) images, and its associations with each index were examined. Statistical analyses were performed using the Welch test and pairwise comparisons. Individuals with WS had lower hepatic steatosis and fibrosis index values than those with insulin-resistant T2D. The mean L/S ratio calculated from CT images was 1.05 ± 0.24 in individuals with WS. The L/S ratio, which is one of the indicators for diagnosing MASLD, was < 0.9 in 5 of 20 cases (25%). Among the various indices in individuals with WS, only the hepatic steatosis index (HSI) was correlated with the L/S ratio (r = -0.863, p = 0.0003). The prevalence of MASLD is lower in individuals with WS than in those with insulin-resistant T2D. The HSI was associated with the L/S ratio in individuals with WS, suggesting that HSI may reflect hepatic steatosis-related changes in this population. Further studies in larger cohorts are needed to validate these findings. The study was registered at the UMIN Clinical Trial Registry (https://upload.umin.ac.jp/cgi-open-bin/ctr_e/ctr_view.cgi?recptno=R000034058) on November 3, 2017 (ID: UMIN000029812).

papers.title: From marrow memory to adverse ventricular remodeling: trained immunity after myocardial infarction.
papers.abstract: Myocardial infarction [MI] triggers a sterile inflammatory response that is essential for necrotic-tissue clearance and scar formation and should normally subside as repair progresses. In a subset of patients, however, persistent myeloid activation accompanies progressive fibrosis, ventricular dilatation, and adverse remodeling long after the acute insult. Trained immunity may help explain this temporal mismatch by allowing myocardial injury to leave a durable functional bias in innate immune cells or their hematopoietic progenitors. Damage-associated molecular patterns, inflammatory cytokines, and sympathetic signals released after MI may reprogram bone-marrow hematopoiesis through metabolic and epigenetic mechanisms. Bone-marrow-derived cells can enter the circulation and injured myocardium directly; the spleen may provide an additional reservoir, hematopoietic niche, and amplification or deployment compartment rather than an obligatory intermediate. Resident and recruited cardiac macrophages then interpret this systemic input within the heart, where macrophage-fibroblast-extracellular matrix interactions influence scar composition, remote-zone fibrosis, ventricular geometry, and progression toward heart failure. This review follows a heart-hematopoietic-heart network and distinguishes direct MI-trained-immunity evidence from MI-specific bridging evidence, adjacent trained-immunity models, and downstream remodeling evidence. Individual components are supported to different degrees, but causal continuity from MI-induced hematopoietic memory to adverse ventricular remodeling has not yet been demonstrated. Defining where durable memory is established, how myeloid output reaches the heart, and when it becomes maladaptive may support phase-specific interventions that preserve early repair while limiting later inflammation and fibrosis.

papers.title: Case report: Fatal hematogenous gastrosplenic mucormycosis in an immunocompetent adult following sigmoid perforation, septic shock, and short-term stress glucocorticoids.
papers.abstract: Mucormycosis is an aggressive angioinvasive fungal infection that predominantly affects chronically immunosuppressed individuals. Hematogenous dissemination of Mucorales causing synchronous gastric full-thickness perforation and total splenic infarction is exceptionally rare, particularly in immunocompetent hosts without chronic comorbidities. To our knowledge, this presentation has not been reported in a patient with only three days of stress-dose glucocorticoid therapy following sigmoid perforation and septic shock. We report a fatal case of synchronous gastric perforation and total splenic infarction secondary to hematogenous Mucorales dissemination in a previously healthy adult who developed septic shock from spontaneous sigmoid perforation. The patient received only three days of guideline-recommended stress-dose hydrocortisone and had no pre-existing diabetes, malignancy, or organ transplantation. Routine serum 1,3-β-D-glucan testing and peritoneal fungal cultures were both negative. Empirical micafungin, an echinocandin, was administered for eight days before liposomal amphotericin B was initiated, during which time progressive fungal angioinvasion led to irreversible multi-organ failure and death. Histopathology confirmed broad, aseptate, right-angle branching hyphae invading gastric and splenic vessels, whereas no fungal elements were detected at the primary sigmoid lesion, supporting a predominantly hematogenous dissemination pathway without primary intestinal fungal colonization - an unprecedented finding that fundamentally distinguishes this case from classic primary gastrointestinal mucormycosis. These histopathological findings are biologically consistent with the CotH3 (CotH family protein 3) - GRP78 (glucose- regulated protein 78 kDa) host-fungal virulence axis, which represents a plausible mechanistic explanation for multi-organ angioinvasion observed in this patient. This case delivers three critical clinical takeaways. First, even brief stress-dose glucocorticoids may induce sufficient transient immune paralysis to permit life-threatening hematogenous mucormycosis in patients without chronic underlying immunosuppression, acting as one potential contributing factor alongside sepsis-related critical-illness immune dysfunction. Second, empirical carbapenem plus echinocandin regimens, commonly used in ICUs, lack activity against Mucorales ; prolonged reliance on this combination can result in irreversible fatal visceral injury. Third, negative peritoneal fungal cultures and serum 1,3-β-D-glucan do not exclude intra-abdominal mucormycosis; early re-laparotomy for histopathological biopsy is essential in refractory cases.

papers.title: Protective effects of sanguinarine-baicalin salt in broilers challenged with avian pathogenic Escherichia coli O78.
papers.abstract: Avian pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) O78 causes acute colibacillosis in broilers and contributes to mortality, impaired growth, and multi-organ injury. This study evaluated the in vitro antibacterial activity and in vivo protective effects of sanguinarine-baicalin salt (SBS) in broilers subjected to an acute systemic APEC O78 challenge. Minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), bacterial growth, and biofilm formation were assessed in vitro. In vivo, broilers were intraperitoneally challenged with APEC O78 on days 11-13 and treated with dietary SBS at 5-320 mg/kg diet from day 14. Survival, growth performance, organ injury, serum biochemical and inflammatory indices, intestinal morphology, jejunal gene expression, cecal microbiota, and exploratory hepatic proteomic responses were evaluated. The MIC of SBS was 256 μg/mL, compared with 32 μg/mL for amoxicillin. SBS delayed bacterial growth but did not significantly inhibit biofilm formation under the tested conditions. In vivo, SBS improved survival, with the 20 mg/kg diet group showing the lowest treatment-period mortality. The 20-40 mg/kg diet range generally produced the most favorable overall responses, including improvements in growth performance, liver and spleen indices, and serum ALT, CREA, UA, and inflammatory cytokines. SBS treatment was also associated with improved intestinal morphology, increased transcription of barrier-related genes, reduced transcription of TLR4/NF-κB-related inflammatory genes, and changes in cecal microbial composition. Exploratory hepatic proteomics revealed APEC-associated alterations and treatment-associated shifts involving proteins related to cellular stress, redox homeostasis, tissue structure, and hepatic lipid and energy metabolism. Overall, dietary SBS showed protective effects against acute systemic APEC O78 challenge, accompanied by systemic, hepatic, and intestinal host responses.

papers.title: A Metabolomics and Network Pharmacology Approach Using LC-MS to Investigate the Mechanisms of Fufang Ejiao Jiang in Treating Chemotherapy-Induced Myelosuppression.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the mechanism and pharmacologically active compounds of Fufang Ejiao Jiang (FFEJJ) in the prevention and treatment of myelosuppression after chemotherapy (MAC) through a combination of serum metabolomics and network pharmacology. Sprague Dawley rats were randomly assigned to three groups: the blank group, the model group, and the FFEJJ group (10.8 g/kg). A MAC rat model was induced using cyclophosphamide. Simultaneously with model establishment, rats were intragastrically administered once daily for 15 consecutive days. The routine blood parameters of the rats were measured, and pathological changes in the spleen and bone marrow were observed. Nontargeted serum metabolomics was employed to identify differential metabolites associated with MAC and their related pathways. Liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) was used to analyze the chemical composition of FFEJJ, and its mechanism and pharmacologically active compounds in the treatment of MAC were further predicted using network pharmacology. FFEJJ significantly improved the hematopoietic function of bone marrow in the MAC model rats. Compared to the blank group, the model group exhibited obvious spleen injury and bone marrow disorder, with noticeable fatty infiltration in the bone marrow cavity. Following FFEJJ treatment, the condition of spleen tissue and bone marrow in MAC rats was significantly improved. Serum metabolomics analysis of endogenous metabolites identified 14 differential metabolites associated with the MAC mechanism in both positive and negative ion modes, primarily involving pathways such as aminoacyl-tRNA biosynthesis, primary bile acid biosynthesis, and unsaturated fatty acid biosynthesis. Using LC-MS, 31 components were identified in FFEJJ. Network pharmacology predictions suggest that the potential pharmacologically active compounds of FFEJJ in the treatment of MAC include apigenin, oleanolic acid, maslinic acid, and azelaic acid. The underlying mechanism may be partly associated with the phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase/serine-threonine kinase (PI3K-Akt) signaling pathway. FFEJJ promotes hematopoietic recovery in MAC rats, likely by regulating endogenous metabolic disorders. Apigenin, oleanolic acid, maslinic acid, and azelaic acid are predicted to be multitarget active compounds, with PI3K-Akt signaling as a candidate pathway.

papers.title: Ligustilide enhances TNT-mediated mitochondrial transfer to accelerate the reactivation of TECs in sleep deprivation induced postpartum mouse.
papers.abstract: Angelica sinensis (Oliv.) Diels (Danggui) has been widely used by puerperae in China for postpartum recovery for more than a thousand years. Its key active ingredient, ligustilide (LIG), has been documented to exert thymus-repairing effects; however, its role and underlying mechanisms in postpartum thymic regeneration impairment remain unclear. During the puerperium, the acutely atrophied maternal thymus gradually returns to its non-pregnant state. However, frequent sleep deprivation (SD) resulting from neonatal breastfeeding often slows down the thymus recovery process. This study investigated the efficacy and underlying mechanism of LIG, an active ingredient of A. sinensis, against SD-induced thymic regeneration disorder (SDTRD) in postpartum mice. Postpartum SD was induced by automated disturbance; a progesterone-estrogen withdrawal (PE) model followed by a 7-day high-dose steroid treatment. LIG (1 mg/kg) was administered during regeneration. Thymic architecture (H&E), thymic epithelial cells (TECs) localization (immunofluorescence), and thymocyte subsets (flow cytometry) were quantified. Spleen sjTREC, thymic cytokines, and transcripts for mitochondrial biogenesis/function were measured by qPCR. TEM assessed mitochondrial ultrastructure. Dual-color mitochondrial tracing combined with a thymocytes-iTECs co-culture system and a bone-marrow-cell thymic homing assay mapped intercellular mitochondrial transfer. Tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) were disrupted with cytochalasin D; Rho-GTPase activation (including Cdc42) was evaluated. Postpartum mice with SD showed damaged mitochondrial ultrastructure and reduced mitochondrial biogenesis in TECs, leading to TECs dysfunction and interruption of postpartum thymic regeneration. LIG significantly restored the abnormal spatial localization of TECs, improved the reticular framework of cortical TECs (cTECs), promoted thymocyte development, and increased output of CD4 + T-cells. Mechanistically, LIG may facilitate the formation of F-actin-dependent TNTs between thymocytes and TECs, mediating mitochondrial transfer from thymocytes to dysfunctional TECs. This process may rely on Rho GTPase signaling pathways (Cdc42 activation) to regulate F-actin polymerization. LIG may promote F-actin-dependent TNT-mediated mitochondrial transfer from thymocytes to TECs, thereby reactivating TECs, restoring the thymic microenvironment, rescuing thymocyte development and export, and ultimately ameliorating SD-induced postpartum thymic regeneration. These findings provide new experimental evidence for developing LIG as a preventive and therapeutic intervention for defective postpartum thymic repair.

papers.title: Partial Splenectomy as a Definitive or Interim Solution for Young Children with Transfusion-dependent Hemolytic Anemia: Long-term Results from a 15-Year Cohort.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of partial splenectomy (PS) as a definitive or interim spleen-preserving strategy in young children with transfusion-dependent congenital hemolytic anemia (HA). Patients with congenital HA who required frequent blood transfusions and underwent PS at the present center between 2010 and 2025 were included. The hemoglobin (Hb) level, reticulocyte count, and the need for transfusions (if any) during the follow-up period were noted. Ultrasonography of the splenic remnant was obtained at baseline, 1 mo, and 18 mo following the PS. Fourteen children (median age: 23 mo; range: 7-40) underwent PS by laparotomy (n = 12) or laparoscopy (n = 2). Median follow-up after PS was 9 y (IQR: 4.8-10.5). Following PS, 8/14 (57%) patients became transfusion-free, with a median Hb of 10.3 g/dL at last follow-up. Five (36%) patients continued to require occasional transfusions and subsequently underwent total splenectomy after a median of 3 y; All of them became transfusion-free thereafter. No episode of mortality, sepsis, or thrombosis occurred. PS may serve as a definitive procedure in selected young children with congenital hemolytic anemia and as a bridge to later total splenectomy in others. This approach may be particularly relevant in resource-limited settings, where blood availability, transfusion safety, and the risk of transfusion-transmitted infections are concerning.

papers.title: Mass Spectrometry Imaging Reveals Biodistribution and Biotransformation of Black Phosphorus.
papers.abstract: Black phosphorus (BP) holds significant potential in biomedicine, biosensing, and phototherapy; however, its instability and the poor understanding of its in vivo fate have limited its applications. Here, we developed an integrated label-free mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) platform to investigate BP's in vivo distribution, transformation, clearance, and metabolism in tumor-bearing mice. We detected BPs and related nitrogen/oxygen-containing phosphorus (P) clusters in six organs and tumor tissues, revealing distinctive tissue distributions. BP and its degradation products primarily accumulated in the liver and spleen, with the liver showing a radial distribution pattern around hepatic lobules. Notably, BP and related clusters can cross the blood-brain barrier into brain parenchyma. We further establish the in vivo transformation and metabolic pathways of BPs. Cellular experiments confirmed that nitric oxide synthase (NOS)-mediated nitric oxide (NO) generation drives BP nitridation during its transformation and metabolism under physiological conditions. This work not only provides vital information for biomedical applications of BP, but also establishes a platform for understanding in vivo translocation and transformation of nanomaterials, aiding their biosafety and health impact assessments.

papers.title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals the immune response mechanisms of Acrossocheilus fasciatus against Citrobacter freundii infection.
papers.abstract: Acrossocheilus fasciatus is an economically important freshwater fish species in China. In recent years, Citrobacter freundii infection has caused significant harm to the aquaculture industry. In this study, we performed histological observation and RNA-seq analysis of the intestines and spleens of control (CK) and C. freundii infected A. fasciatus (EG). The results showed that infected fish exhibited abdominal haemorrhage, intestinal villous shedding, hydropic degeneration of hepatocytes and splenic sinus dilation with congestion. RNA-seq analysis identified 3054 DEGs in the intestine and 7706 DEGs in the spleen, with 1247 overlapping DEGs identified by combined analysis. A substantial portion of these genes clustered within biological activities linked to immunity and metabolic regulation, particularly engaging immune-related routes such as endoplasmic reticulum-based protein maturation, alongside the complement system and coagulation signalling cascades. This study systematically reveals the synergy and division of labor between the intestine and spleen during C. freundii infection, providing fundamental data for understanding the immune response mechanisms of A. fasciatus and a theoretical basis for optimising disease prevention and control strategies.

papers.title: Shugan-Liangxue Prescription Inhibits Immune Escape Against Breast Cancer by Regulating Tryptophan Metabolism.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveTryptophan metabolism plays a pivotal role in promoting tumor progression by modulating immune escape in breast cancer (BC). Shugan-Liangxue prescription (SLP), a traditional Chinese medicine, has shown beneficial effects in enhancing antitumor immunity for BC treatment.
