This study aims to investigate the effect of SLP on tryptophan metabolism in BC and to explore the underlying mechanisms.MethodsThe immunopharmacological BC model in rats was established by chemical carcinogen induction and complete freund's adjuvant perturbations and treated with SLP. Tamoxifen and other metabolism-associated drugs were used as controls. The therapeutic efficacy of SLP was evaluated by tumor volume, weight, and oncocyte proliferation. Serum cytokines and subsets of immune cells in the spleen were measured to evaluate the anti-tumor immunity. Metabolite levels and expressions of signal molecules of tryptophan metabolic pathway were measured to explore the mechanisms.ResultsOur findings demonstrated that SLP treatment significantly inhibited tumor growth and tumor cell proliferation, and enhanced antitumor immunity by promoting Th1 polarization, increasing cytotoxic immune cells (CD8+ T cells, NKG2D+ NK cells), and reducing inhibitory immune cells (Foxp3+ Tregs, NKG2A+ NK cells, M2 macrophages) in the spleen. Additionally, SLP regulated glucose and lipid metabolism, as evidenced by reduced serum glucose and non-esterified fatty acid levels. SLP suppressed tryptophan catabolism by down-regulating expression of IDO1 and AhR and reducing kynurenine levels.ConclusionsIn summary, correlative analyses suggest SLP may mitigate breast cancer immune escape partially via the Trp metabolic pathway to boost anti-tumor immune surveillance, and its immunomodulatory activity is potentially linked to glucose and lipid reprogramming. While our findings support the involvement of the Trp-Kyn-AhR axis, causal verification via pathway rescue and inhibition assays is still needed.

papers.title: A novel porcine interleukin-2-interferon-α-thymosin α1 tripartite fusion protein confers antiviral activity against pseudorabies virus.
papers.abstract: Pseudorabies virus (PRV), the causative agent of Aujeszky's disease in pigs, threatens swine production and can infect other mammals, with rare zoonotic cases reported. Effective antiviral agents against PRV remain lacking. Here, we constructed and purified a recombinant fusion protein combining porcine Interleukin-2 (IL-2), interferon α (IFN-α), and Thymosin α1 (Tα1). The fusion protein showed no cytotoxicity or induction of apoptosis in PK-15 cells. In vitro, it significantly enhanced peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) metabolic activity and upregulated expression of key interferon-stimulated genes (ISGs) involved in antiviral defense, including IFIT1, ISG15, MX1, and OAS, which are critical for antiviral activity. Analysis of the viral life cycle indicated that Interleukin-2-Interferon-α-Thymosin α1 (IL-2-IFN-α-Tα1) inhibited PRV replication without affecting viral attachment, entry, assembly, or egress. Treatment with the fusion protein conferred marked therapeutic efficacy against PRV infection, including improved survival, reduced viral loads in the brain and spleen, and alleviated inflammatory pathology. These results demonstrate that IL-2-IFN-α-Tα1 fusion protein has potential as a novel immunomodulatory agent for controlling PRV infection in swine, offering a promising strategy for antiviral intervention in veterinary medicine.

papers.title: COMMD family members exhibit immune-associated expression patterns following dietary selenomethionine supplementation and subsequent Bacillus cereus challenge in Pelodiscus sinensis.
papers.abstract: The copper metabolism MURR1 domain-containing (COMMD) protein family participates in diverse cellular and immune-related processes, yet little is known about this family in reptiles. In this study, we performed a genome-wide characterization of the COMMD gene family in the Chinese soft-shelled turtle (Pelodiscus sinensis) and examined its tissue expression and transcriptional patterns following dietary selenomethionine (Se-Met) supplementation and subsequent Bacillus cereus challenge. Ten COMMD family members (COMMD1-COMMD10) were identified, all of which contained a conserved COMM domain and showed conserved evolutionary relationships with vertebrate orthologs. Most COMMD genes were highly expressed in the liver and spleen, although distinct tissue-specific patterns were observed among individual family members. After 45 days of dietary Se-Met supplementation, turtles were challenged with B. cereus, and COMMD genes exhibited heterogeneous, gene-, tissue-, and time-dependent transcriptional responses without a uniform concentration-dependent pattern. Pearson correlation analysis further revealed significant co-expression associations between several COMMD family members and representative immune-related genes, including TLR2, MyD88, TRAF6, NF-κB, TNF, and IL18. These transcriptional associations suggest potential links between COMMD family members and immune-related responses but do not establish direct regulatory relationships. This study provides a genomic and expression-level resource for future functional investigation of COMMD family members in reptilian immunity.

papers.title: Mitochondria-Nanozyme Hybrid Therapeutic for Modulation of the Inflammatory Cascade in Psoriasis.
papers.abstract: The chronic recurrence of psoriasis is driven by a self-amplifying inflammatory cascade in which oxidative stress and mitochondrial metabolic dysfunction reinforce each other, and single-target conventional therapies often fail to break this cycle. Here, we present a micro-nano hybrid system, Mito-Ce, constructed by covalently immobilizing ceria nanozymes (CeNPs) onto the surface of isolated functional mitochondria through thiol-maleimide chemistry. This design endows the hybrid with dual functionalities, including mitochondrial bioactivity and durable ROS-scavenging capabilities of CeNPs. In H2O2-stimulated macrophages, upon internalization. Mito-Ce markedly reduced intracellular ROS and consequently suppressed the secretion of pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β). Topical application of Mito-Ce to an imiquimod-induced mouse model of psoriasis visibly resolved psoriatic plaques, reduced the PASI score, and reversed epidermal hyperplasia. Beyond local repair, Mito-Ce rebalanced systemic immunity, evidenced by a decline in splenic pathogenic Th17 cells and polarization toward anti-inflammatory M2 macrophages. Transcriptomic profiling further revealed that Mito-Ce broadly reversed the pathological gene expression program, downregulating stress-responsive and phagocytosis-related genes while upregulating genes associated with metabolism, epidermal proliferation, and tissue homeostatic remodeling. These coordinated networks ultimately re-established immune-barrier homeostasis at the molecular level. Collectively, by integrating nanozyme-mediated ROS scavenging with mitochondrial bioactivity, the Mito-Ce hybrid could treat psoriasis through coordinated disruption of the inflammatory cascade, potentially offering a highly effective platform for various chronic inflammatory disorders.

papers.title: Low-level of mitochondrial DNA alterations during direct-acting antiviral treatment in leukocytes of people who inject drugs living with HCV.
papers.abstract: Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) have revolutionized hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, offering high cure rates and favorable safety profiles. However, concerns remain regarding their long-term mitochondrial safety, particularly among vulnerable populations such as people who inject drugs (PWID), who are frequently exposed to multiple mitotoxic agents. This longitudinal study investigated mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) instability, including deletions and single-nucleotide variants, among PWID living with HCV during DAA treatment, using whole mitochondrial genome sequencing. We analyzed samples of 33 PWID living with HCV before treatment (baseline), at the end of treatment (week 12), and after long-term follow-up (week 48), in comparison with 30 HCV-seronegative PWID. Associations with clinical events were assessed during a 3-year follow-up after study completion. mtDNA deletions were detected in 9.1% of PWID living with HCV at baseline and increased to 19.2% post-treatment, whereas no mtDNA deletions were observed in HCV-seronegative PWID. Heteroplasmy levels (i.e., proportion of mutated to wild-type mtDNA) remained below 1%. Variants were widespread in both HCV-positive and HCV-seronegative PWID, predominantly in the non-coding D-loop region. A small number of low-heteroplasmy treatment-emergent variants were detected during follow-up, but none persisted at long-term follow-up. No significant associations were found between mtDNA instability and hepatic or splenic complications assessed at 3 years. These findings suggest that DAA exposure is associated with low-level mtDNA instability in blood leukocytes. Nonetheless, long-term mitochondrial surveillance is warranted, especially in post-mitotic tissues, to fully assess the implications of cumulative mitotoxic exposures in this high-risk population. Direct-acting antivirals (DAAs) have revolutionized hepatitis C virus (HCV) treatment, but their safety is still under debate. Given the nature of these regimens, mitochondrial genotoxicity could represent a potential off-target effect. We searched for mitochondrial DNA alterations in people who inject drugs living with HCV. The prevalence of HCV infection is high in this population, and any potential toxicity would be exacerbated as they are exposed to other mitotoxic drugs. We detected low-level mitochondrial DNA alterations in blood leukocytes, including a modest increase in mitochondrial DNA deletions, but these alterations remained at very low levels (below 1%) and were not associated with any clinical complications during 3 years of follow-up. These findings provide reassuring evidence regarding the short-term mitochondrial safety of DAA treatment in blood leukocytes while supporting the need for longer-term studies in post-mitotic tissues. This study is registered with Clinical Trial Registry as NCT03526939 and NCT03537196.

papers.title: Jianpi Biyan formula ameliorates spleen-deficiency-type allergic rhinitis and modulates the gut-nose axis: Integrated evidence from gut microbiota, SCFA metabolism, and TLR4/NF-κB signaling.
papers.abstract: The Jianpi Biyan formula (JPBY) is a modern Chinese herbal compound derived from the classic Qing Dynasty formula "Jiegeng Yuanshen Decoction." It is primarily used to treat allergic rhinitis (AR) with spleen deficiency as the core pathogenesis and has demonstrated good clinical efficacy; however, its modern biological mechanisms remain unclear. This study investigated the effects of JPBY on spleen-deficiency-type AR, with particular emphasis on the gut microbiota, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA) metabolism, mucosal barrier integrity, and TLR4/NF-κB-associated inflammatory responses. A rat model of spleen-deficiency-type AR was established to evaluate the effects of JPBY on nasal symptoms, spleen deficiency-related manifestations, gastrointestinal function, and intestinal and nasal mucosal integrity. Gut microbiota profiling, SCFA metabolomics, and transcriptomic analyses were integrated to characterize JPBY-associated changes in gut and nasal inflammatory and metabolic profiles. Serum-absorbed components of JPBY were identified using UHPLC-MS/MS, and network pharmacology, molecular docking, immunofluorescence, Western blotting, and ELISA were subsequently employed to investigate potential molecular targets and signaling pathways. JPBY significantly alleviated nasal symptoms and spleen deficiency-related manifestations, improved gastrointestinal digestive function, and enhanced intestinal and nasal mucosal barrier integrity in spleen-deficiency-type AR rats. JPBY also markedly altered the composition of the gut microbiota and SCFA metabolism. Integrated multi-omics analyses identified associations among gut microbial alterations, SCFA metabolism, mucosal barrier function, and inflammatory signaling. In particular, TLR4/NF-κB signaling was identified as a potential molecular pathway associated with inflammatory changes in both intestinal and nasal tissues. Consistent with these findings, JPBY suppressed TLR4/NF-κB-associated signaling in both colonic and nasal tissues and modulated the levels of Th1/Th2/Treg/Th17-related cytokines. Collectively, these findings indicate that JPBY ameliorates spleen-deficiency-type AR while simultaneously remodeling the gut microbiota and SCFA metabolism, improving intestinal and nasal mucosal barrier function, and attenuating TLR4/NF-κB-associated inflammation. The coordinated alterations observed across the gut and nasal compartments suggest that gut-nose axis-related mechanisms may be involved in the effects of JPBY, although a direct causal relationship remains to be established.

papers.title: Tirzepatide alleviates hepatic steatosis and inflammation in MASLD partly through suppression of macrophage Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB signaling.
papers.abstract: Metabolic stress, hepatic lipid accumulation, and macrophage-associated sterile inflammation are closely involved in the development of metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Tirzepatide improves metabolic outcomes, but its effects on macrophage inflammatory signaling in MASLD remain unclear. This study investigated the protective effects of tirzepatide against high-fat, high-fructose diet (HFHFD)-induced MASLD and examined the potential involvement of macrophage Dectin-1/spleen tyrosine kinase (Syk)/nuclear factor-κB (NF-κB) signaling. After 7 weeks of HFHFD feeding to establish the MASLD model, male C57BL/6J mice received tirzepatide (10 nmol/kg, subcutaneously, every 3 days) for an additional 7 weeks. Biochemical assays, histology, hepatic RNA sequencing (RNA-seq), RT-qPCR, Western blotting, and immunofluorescence were performed. Palmitic acid (PA)-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, siRNA-mediated Dectin-1 knockdown, and a RAW264.7 cell-derived conditioned medium-based macrophage-hepatocyte indirect interaction model were used for mechanistic validation. Tirzepatide treatment improved HFHFD-induced metabolic dysfunction, liver injury, hepatic steatosis, and inflammatory responses in mice. RNA-seq revealed enrichment of C-type lectin receptor and NF-κB signaling pathways, while HFHFD-induced Clec7a upregulation was reversed by tirzepatide. Tirzepatide reduced hepatic macrophage accumulation, Dectin-1 expression, and Syk/p65 phosphorylation. In PA-stimulated RAW264.7 cells, tirzepatide suppressed pro-inflammatory cytokine expression and secretion and inhibited Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB activation. Conditioned medium from tirzepatide-treated RAW264.7 cells attenuated lipid accumulation and abnormalities in lipid metabolism- and inflammation-related gene expression in HepG2 cells. Dectin-1 knockdown itself attenuated PA-induced inflammatory responses and was associated with a reduced additional response to tirzepatide. These findings suggest that tirzepatide alleviates HFHFD-induced MASLD, with suppression of macrophage Dectin-1/Syk/NF-κB signaling potentially contributing to these effects.

papers.title: Antitumor efficacy and safety profile of gallic acid in the murine sarcoma 180 model.
papers.abstract: Gallic acid (GA) is a plant-derived polyphenol with recognized anticancer activity, but in vivo evidence, especially in mesenchymal solid tumors, remains limited. This study investigated the antitumor effects and mechanistic pathways of GA in the murine Sarcoma 180 (S-180) model. Fifty male Swiss mice bearing S-180 tumors received oral GA (10, 25, or 50 mg/kg/day), 5-fluorouracil (5-FU; 25 mg/kg, intraperitoneal), or vehicle for seven days. Tumor weight and growth inhibition were assessed, along with histopathology and immunohistochemistry for proliferation (Ki-67, a proliferation marker), apoptosis (cleaved caspase-3 and caspase-8, Bcl-2-associated X protein [Bax], and B-cell lymphoma 2 [Bcl-2]), nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), and systemic toxicity markers (hematological, hepatic, and renal). GA at 50 mg/kg significantly reduced tumor weight and proliferation, decreased Ki-67 and NF-κB expression, increased Bax, reduced Bcl-2, and enhanced cleaved caspase-3, indicating predominant activation of the intrinsic (mitochondrial) apoptotic pathway. Caspase-8 levels remained unchanged. Although 5-FU produced greater tumor inhibition, it induced leukopenia and splenic atrophy, whereas GA preserved hematological, hepatic, and renal parameters. These findings support GA as a promising candidate for adjuvant cancer therapy.

papers.title: Hepatic B-Cell Lymphoma in a Common Mynah ( Acridotheres tristis ): A Case Report.
papers.abstract: Hepatic lymphoma is rarely characterized in mynah birds, and severe hepatomegaly in this group is often interpreted in relation to iron storage disease or other metabolic hepatopathies. This report describes hepatic B-cell lymphoma in a 14-year-old common mynah ( Acridotheres tristis ) presented with lethargy, altered vocalization, poor body condition, ascites, dyspnea, chronic ataxia, and left-leg lameness. Radiography revealed a large soft-tissue opacity in the middle coelomic cavity, with caudodorsal displacement of the intestinal loops and compression of the thoracoabdominal air sacs. Ultrasonography identified a very large hepatic mass with granular and mixed echogenicity occupying most of the coelomic cavity. The bird was euthanized at the owner's request because of the severity of the lesion and poor clinical condition. At necropsy, the liver was markedly enlarged, dark red to reddish-brown, mottled and occupied most of the coelomic cavity. Histologically, the hepatic parenchyma was extensively replaced by densely packed mononuclear neoplastic cells, with effacement of hepatic cords and hepatocellular necrosis. No neoplastic infiltration was identified in the examined tissues, including spleen, kidney, intestine, lung, and heart; therefore, the liver was the only confirmed site of lymphoma among the examined tissues in this case. An immunohistochemical and histochemical panel including CD3, CD79 α /MB-1, CD20, lysozyme, CD68, alpha-1-antitrypsin, toluidine blue, and Giemsa staining was applied to characterize the tumor lineage and exclude other round-cell neoplasms. Neoplastic cells showed diffuse cytoplasmic immunoreactivity for CD79 α /MB-1 and lacked evidence of T-cell, monocyte/macrophage, or mast cell differentiation, supporting a diagnosis of hepatic B-cell lymphoma. This case highlights the need for tissue-based diagnosis in mynah birds with marked hepatomegaly and demonstrates the value of integrating diagnostic imaging, histopathology, immunohistochemistry, and molecular testing in avian hepatic round-cell tumors.

papers.title: Inhibiting trained immunity in Duchenne muscular dystrophy enhances muscle regeneration and reduces fat deposition.
papers.abstract: Background Trained immunity (TI) refers to a hyperresponsive functional state of innate immune cells, such as inflammatory monocytes, induced in response to a variety of stimuli including signals released from damaged tissue, and characterised by increased cytokine production. Inflammatory monocytes play a critical role in Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) by driving chronic muscle inflammation and disease progression. In this study we examined the role of trained immunity in dystrophic muscle pathology by specifically targeting this process in monocytes. Methods We used the mdx mouse model of DMD to investigate TI induction in splenic and bone marrow monocytes isolated during the peak of muscle injury and inflammation. Transcriptional changes in monocytes were examined by performing RNA-Seq, while cytokine production following stimulation with LPS was examined by multiplex ELISA. Mice were treated for two weeks with twice weekly i.v. injections of apolipoprotein A1-based, rapamycin-loaded nanobiologics (mTORi-NB) to specifically target TI in monocytes within the bone marrow and the spleen through the inhibition of the mTOR pathway which plays a central role in TI induction. Inhibition of TI in monocytes was assessed in vitro by measuring cytokine production following stimulation with LPS. Satellite cells and FAPs were sorted from limb muscles and cultured in vitro to assess the effect of the treatment on their proliferation and differentiation properties. Results Dystrophic muscle injury was associated with transcriptional changes in mdx monocytes linked to chromatin and metabolic remodelling as well as with hyperproduction of proinflammatory cytokines, consistent with TI induction. Treatment of mdx mice with mTORi-NB resulted in improved skeletal muscle regeneration and reduced fat deposition. In vitro experiments confirmed the enhanced myogenic properties in satellite cells and reduced adipogenesis in FAPs mediated by the inhibition of TI in monocytes. Conclusions Dystrophic muscle injury induces TI in both bone marrow and splenic monocytes characterised by hyperproduction of proinflammatory cytokines. Targeting TI specifically in monocytes through mTOR inhibition enhances muscle regeneration and reduces intramuscular fat deposition. Overall, our findings suggest that inhibition of TI represents a promising therapeutic strategy to slow DMD progression.

papers.title: Cytokinesis Arrest-induced Binucleation of Macrophages Produces Highly Efficient Efferocytes.
papers.abstract: Efferocytosis, the phagocytic clearance of dying cells and debris, supports tissue homeostasis, immune tolerance, and inflammation resolution, whereas its failure contributes to autoimmunity, atherosclerosis, aging, and impaired tissue repair. Although many molecular regulators of efferocytosis have been defined, less is known about whether macrophages can be reprogrammed into a distinct cellular state with intrinsically enhanced efferocytosis capacity. Guided by a CRISPR screen, we found that Pdcd6ip loss induces cytokinesis arrest and binucleation, creating macrophages with superior efferocytic function. Binucleated Pdcd6ip -/- bone marrow-derived macrophages demonstrate a coordinately enhanced multi-corpse capture and processing, and resolution response, and acquired a distinct transcriptomic signature. In vivo , Pdcd6ip deletion enhanced splenic macrophage efferocytosis, reduced autoimmune responses after repeated apoptotic cell challenge, and promoted plaque stability without metabolic or hematologic changes. PDCD6IP perturbation similarly increased binucleation and engulfment in human macrophage-like cells. Thus, incomplete cytokinesis represents an unrecognized route to macrophage specialization with enhanced efferocytosis capacity.

papers.title: The chromatin reader protein MLLT1 is critical to maintain normal B lymphopoiesis.
papers.abstract: MLLT1 (also named ENL) is a chromatin reader protein whose encoding gene was originally identified as a chromosomal translocation partner with MLL ( KMT2A ) in acute leukemia. However, its role in normal hematopoiesis has not been investigated. This study uncovers a critical role of Mllt1 in normal B cell lymphopoiesis. We found Mllt1 to be essential for early B lymphocyte development using a conditional Mllt1 knockout mouse model that we developed. A significant decrease of bone marrow B-lineage progenitors, splenic transitional B cells and peripheral blood B cells were observed in Mllt1 del mice compared to control Mllt1 fl/fl mice. Similarly, Mllt1 deletion in in vitro cultured B-enriched progenitor cells from Mllt1 fl/fl ; Rosa26CreER T2/ + mice resulted in reduced B cells, demonstrating the cell-intrinsic role of Mllt1 in this process. Direct MLLT1 target genes including Il7r and critical B-lineage transcription factors, Ebf1 and Pax5 , were decreased following Mllt1 deletion. Gene set enrichment, gene ontology, and functional analyses of Mllt1 -deficient cells showed significant alterations related to B cell development, critical relevant signaling pathways, DNA replication, and mitochondrial function. In vitro complementation with MLLT1 rescued the B cell phenotype observed with endogenous Mllt1 deletion; however, specific MLLT1 YEATS domain mutants lacking chromatin reader and RNA-binding functions were unable to rescue the phenotype. Taken together, our research demonstrates a previously unappreciated role for MLLT1 as critical for maintenance of B cell lymphopoiesis.

papers.title: Endocrine determinants of MASLD: mechanisms and therapeutic targets.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately 30% of adults worldwide, yet is still framed largely as a hepatological disorder despite being driven substantially by endocrine and metabolic dysfunction. This review proposes a unified endocrine framework organised around seven hormonal axes, presenting each in terms of molecular pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and therapeutic implications. Insulin resistance is the central driver, coupling chronic caloric excess to hepatic de novo lipogenesis through selective hepatic insulin resistance, although genetic variants in PNPLA3 and TM6SF2 can uncouple steatosis from metabolic risk. Adipose tissue dysfunction contributes through adipocyte senescence, adipokine imbalance, and inflammatory adipose-liver signalling. Reduced hepatic thyroid hormone sensitivity, even in euthyroid individuals, predicts steatosis and fibrosis and underpins the first approved liver-directed therapy. Gonadal steroids exert sexually dimorphic effects, with testosterone deficiency, menopausal oestrogen loss, and polycystic ovary syndrome representing distinct risk states. Glucocorticoid dysregulation is stage-dependent, shifting from enhanced hepatic cortisol clearance in steatosis to local amplification in steatohepatitis. The gut-liver-endocrine axis, encompassing incretin, bile acid, and fibroblast growth factor signalling, has proved the most therapeutically tractable. Reduced GH/IGF-1 signalling, whether from pituitary disease or obesity-induced functional suppression, promotes both steatosis and fibrogenesis. Biological sex and life-course influences spanning developmental programming and ageing further modify these determinants. Two agents, resmetirom and semaglutide, now have US FDA accelerated approval for noncirrhotic MASH with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis, supporting the principle that correcting axis-specific endocrine dysfunction can produce measurable hepatic benefit; however, both approvals are accelerated and await confirmatory outcome data, while others remain investigational. An endocrine framework offers both a coherent account of pathogenesis and a rational basis for biomarker-guided, phenotype-targeted therapy.

papers.title: Integrated pituitary adaptations to the low estrogen state.
papers.abstract: Estrogen's broad trophic effects on anterior pituitary function are not fully understood. The compound 4-vinyl cyclohexene diepoxide (VCD) induces early ovarian failure and reduced E2 production, which may differentially affect anterior pituitary cells. We recently identified transcriptomic changes in pituitary gonadotropes at the single-cell level in females treated with VCD for 20 days, which were acyclic, with low serum estradiol (E2) levels and 8-12-fold increases in gonadotropins 138 days later. We tested vehicle-control and VCD-treated female mice in metabolic cages and assayed serum hormone levels by EIA, and pituitary cell transcripts by qRT-PCR and single-cell RNA-seq. VCD-treated mice showed normal metabolic health. Compared with controls, VCD-treated females exhibited a 5-fold elevation in serum pituitary thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) levels and near-normal thyroid hormone levels. Pituitary Tshb mRNA levels were reduced, and pituitary Gh, Prl , and Pomc mRNA levels were unchanged. Serum growth hormone (GH) levels were higher in VCD-treated mice than in controls 62 days after the start of treatment (perimenopause) and then reduced to control levels after 118-138 days. Ingenuity Pathway Analyses (IPA) of upregulated differentially expressed gene (DEG) transcripts predicted activation of G protein-mediated signaling pathways in one scRNA-seq somatotrope subcluster and in the thyrotrope and lactotrope clusters. In contrast, downregulated DEGs in corticotropes and the remaining two somatotrope clusters predicted downregulation of critical signaling pathways. The unchanged pituitary Gh, Prl , and Pomc mRNA levels correlated with unchanged serum levels. The interim rise in serum GH 62 days after treatment agrees with reports of perimenopausal responses due to estrogen spikes. Reduced pituitary Tshb correlates with the recently reported reduced expression in gonadotropes. IPA analysis of upregulated DEGs in thyrotrope clusters predicted the activation of canonical signaling pathways that support elevated serum TSH levels. The near-normal thyroid hormone levels suggest subclinical hypothyroidism in menopausal women. Downregulated DEGs in corticotropes and in two somatotrope subclusters predicted compromised stress and metabolic responses. Finally, reduced multihormone gene expression suggested compromised plasticity in a low-estrogen environment. These different responses to a sustained low-estrogen state, such as that seen in menopause, reflect the diversity of estrogen's trophic actions.

papers.title: Association between triglyceride glucose-waist height ratio index and incident thyroid nodules: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Insulin resistance is associated with thyroid nodule formation. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index is a widely recognized surrogate for insulin resistance, and its clinical value increases when integrated with adiposity indices. We tested whether an elevated triglyceride glucose-waist height ratio (TyG-WHtR) is independently associated with incident thyroid nodules. This prospective cohort study recruited 65,347 participants between January and December 2021, with follow-up surveys conducted between January and December 2025. We examined associations of baseline and cumulative TyG-WHtR quartiles with thyroid nodule occurrence using multivariable binary logistic regression. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) models tested nonlinear trends in the association between thyroid nodules and TyG-WHtR. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were generated to compare the area under the curve (AUC) across four metabolic metrics: baseline TyG, WHtR, TyG-WHtR, as well as cumulative TyG-WHtR, with thyroid nodule status as the outcome. We also conducted subgroup and sensitivity analyses, which collectively confirmed the robustness of our observed associations. During a mean follow-up of 4.08 ± 0.27 years, 4,029 participants (15.8%) were diagnosed with thyroid nodules by 2025. In fully adjusted models, the highest versus lowest quartile of baseline TyG-WHtR showed an OR of 1.57 (95% CI: 1.22-2.02), and cumulative TyG-WHtR yielded an OR of 1.57 (95% CI: 1.25-1.96). Each 1-SD increment in baseline and cumulative TyG-WHtR corresponded to ORs of 1.15 (1.05-1.26) and 1.17 (1.07-1.27), respectively. RCS analyses confirmed linear dose-response relationships for both (P for nonlinearity > 0.05). ROC curve analysis demonstrated that cumulative TyG-WHtR had the highest AUC (0.539) for thyroid nodules. TyG-WHtR is independently associated with thyroid nodule risk, with cumulative TyG-WHtR showing a stronger association than baseline TyG-WHtR. Maintaining favorable TyG and waist circumference levels over time may reduce thyroid nodule risk in this Chinese population. Higher triglyceride glucose-waist height ratio is independently associated with an increased risk of thyroid nodules.

papers.title: Endocrine and systemic toxicity of pyriproxyfen in adult female zebrafish: disruption of the HPT axis and peripheral organ impairments.
papers.abstract: Endocrine-disrupting chemicals (EDCs) can destabilize the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) axis, a fundamental regulator of vertebrate development and metabolism. Pyriproxyfen (PPF), a juvenile hormone analog widely utilized in vector control, is recommended by the World Health Organization (WHO) for application at concentrations of up to 10 µg/L in drinking water; however, its safety profile for vertebrates remains a matter of concern. In this study, we investigated the endocrine and systemic impacts of PPF in adult female zebrafish exposed for 14 days to 1, 10, or 100 µg/L. Histological, hormonal, and transcriptional analyses across the thyroid, brain, liver, and kidney revealed a non-monotonic response centered on the WHO reference application concentration. The 10 µg/L group exhibited the most significant molecular impairment in the thyroid, characterized by the upregulation of slc5a5 (nis), nkx2.1, pax2a, and tshr, while repressing thyroglobulin (tg) expression. Consistent with these molecular alterations, thyroid epithelial disruption was observed at 1 and 10 µg/L. In contrast, exposure to 100 µg/L increased plasma TSH levels and the expression of pituitary tshb and hepatic dio1, suggesting a compensatory response of the HPT axis. Renal morphometry additionally revealed tubular alterations across all exposure groups. Overall, these findings demonstrate a non-monotonic concentration-response centered on 10 µg/L as a key mechanistic feature of PPF toxicity and support further evaluation of thyroid and renal endpoints in ecotoxicological risk assessment.

papers.title: Network Analysis of Chronic Disease Diagnosis Co-documentation in Insurance Claims Among Older Arkansans.
papers.abstract: Multimorbidity among older adults presents growing clinical and economic challenges, particularly in medically underserved states such as Arkansas. However, it remains unclear whether chronic conditions documented in routine healthcare encounters exhibit structured patterns of diagnosis co-documentation or primarily reflect incidental co-documentation. Understanding these patterns may inform future studies of multimorbidity and healthcare utilization. To characterize statewide, sex-stratified patterns of claim-level diagnosis co-documentation among Arkansas adults aged ≥65 years using administrative claims data. We analyzed 2024 IQVIA administrative claims for Arkansas residents aged ≥65 years (1,408,707 claims from 35,253 unique patients). Analyses were conducted at the claim level; therefore, individuals could contribute multiple claims, and results reflect utilization-weighted diagnosis co-documentation rather than patient-level disease prevalence or multimorbidity. Twenty-five chronic condition categories were defined using ICD-10-CM codes. Pairwise diagnosis co-documentation was quantified using Lewontin's standardized disequilibrium coefficient (D'), which compares observed joint documentation with the expectation under statistical independence. Sex-stratified D' matrices, disease connectedness metrics, and hierarchical clustering were used to characterize patterns of diagnosis co-documentation. Hypertension was the most frequently documented chronic condition among claims for both females (22.2%) and males (23.7%) and exhibited the highest positive connectedness in both sex-stratified analyses. Among females, the strongest diagnosis co-documentation patterns involved hypertension with dyslipidemia, coronary artery disease (CAD), obesity, thyroid disorders, and heart failure (D' = 0.46-0.69). Among males, the strongest diagnosis co-documentation patterns involved hypertension with dyslipidemia (D' = 0.73), obesity (D' = 0.64), CAD (D' = 0.57), and thyroid disorders (D' = 0.56). Females demonstrated relatively greater diagnosis co-documentation among musculoskeletal, endocrine, and mental health conditions, whereas males showed more concentrated diagnosis co-documentation among cardiometabolic and organ dysfunction conditions. Negative D' values identified disease pairs that were infrequently co-documented within the same claims (e.g., autoimmune disease-chronic gastrointestinal disease among males, D' = -1.00), reflecting absent or infrequent claim-level joint documentation. In this claim-level analysis of Arkansas adults aged ≥65 years represented in the IQVIA administrative claims database, diagnosis co-documentation exhibited structured, sex-specific patterns, with hypertension demonstrating the highest positive connectedness among the 25 chronic conditions. These utilization-weighted findings provide a descriptive basis for hypothesis generation and support future longitudinal, patient-level studies to evaluate temporal disease relationships and the potential role of cardiovascular-renal-metabolic (CVRM) risk management.

papers.title: Metabolism-mediated herb-drug interaction between milk thistle and resmetirom in MCD diet-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis rat model.
papers.abstract: Resmetirom is a liver-directed thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist for metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis, whereas milk thistle is widely used as a hepatoprotective supplement. This study evaluated whether milk thistle supplement coadministration alters resmetirom metabolism, systemic exposure, and pharmacological response. A validated LC-MS/MS method was used to quantify resmetirom in rat plasma and microsomal samples. Male Sprague-Dawley rats with a methionine and choline-deficient diet-induced metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) received vehicle, resmetirom (8 mg/kg), milk thistle supplement (100 mg/kg total silybin A + B equivalent), or their combination for 8 days. Milk thistle increased resmetirom C max by 17 %, AUC 0-t by 37 %, and AUC 0-∞ by 32 %, while reducing apparent oral clearance by 25 %. In rat liver microsomes, milk thistle supplement extract (50 µM total silybin A + B equivalent) decreased the resmetirom elimination-rate constant from 0.0021 to 0.0002 min -1 , prolonged microsomal half-life from 330.84 to 3914.31 min, and reduced intrinsic clearance from 3.88 to 0.39 µL/min/mg protein. The combination was associated with greater improvements in liver enzymes, bilirubin, lipid parameters, relative liver weight, body-weight recovery, and hepatic histology than either monotherapy. These findings provide preclinical evidence of a metabolism-mediated milk thistle-resmetirom interaction that increases resmetirom exposure and is accompanied by an enhanced pharmacodynamic response in rats.

papers.title: Evaluation of Alterations in Serum Uric Acid Levels in Newly Diagnosed Overt Thyroid Dysfunction: A Prospective Observational Study From a Tertiary Care Center.
papers.abstract: Thyroid dysfunction is widely recognized to affect metabolic regulation and renal handling of uric acid and creatinine, but historical clinical findings have remained inconsistent. This study evaluates biochemical profiles and diagnostic markers across control, hyperthyroid, and hypothyroid cohorts to establish clear correlations and diagnostic thresholds. To comprehensively analyze baseline demographic characteristics, thyroid profiles (T3, T4, TSH (thyroid stimulating hormone)), and renal parameters (uric acid, creatinine) across patient cohorts; to explore Pearson correlations among these metrics; and to conduct receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis to determine the diagnostic utility and optimal cutoffs for serum uric acid and creatinine as biomarkers for thyroid dysfunction. A comprehensive cross-sectional analysis was performed on a study population of N = 300 participants, split into a control group (n = 150) and a thyroid dysfunction group (n = 150, comprising 50 hyperthyroid and 100 hypothyroid patients) at a tertiary care center over 12 months. Detailed biochemical profiling, Pearson correlation coefficients, and ROC curve analyses with sensitivity/specificity calculations were performed to assess marker efficacy. The overall mean age was 33.10 ± 13.65 years, with a balanced distribution across cohorts (p = 0.137). Significant discrepancies in T3 (p = 0.004) and TSH (p < 0.001) were confirmed. Serum uric acid was significantly elevated in thyroid dysfunction compared with controls (5.62 ± 2.28 vs. 4.46 ± 1.13 mg/dL, p < 0.001), showing a strong positive correlation with TSH (r = 0.197, p = 0.001). Conversely, serum creatinine was modestly but significantly lower in the thyroid dysfunction group (0.86 ± 0.16 vs. 0.92 ± 0.22 mg/dL, p = 0.010), showing a significant negative correlation with TSH (r = -0.176, p = 0.002). ROC analysis revealed significant diagnostic accuracy for uric acid (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.642, p < 0.001), with an optimal screening cutoff of 4.05 mg/dL (71.3% sensitivity), whereas creatinine demonstrated poor discriminatory performance (AUC = 0.441, p = 0.076). Serum uric acid demonstrates highly significant alterations and predictable diagnostic value in thyroid dysfunction, closely correlating with TSH levels. Creatinine shows a reverse metabolic association and poor diagnostic accuracy. Routine screening of serum uric acid, but not necessarily creatinine, is clinically indicated in newly diagnosed thyroid dysfunction cases to guide metabolic risk stratification.

papers.title: Conductive Cu-MOF synergizing with enzyme-free catalytic cascade amplification for ultrasensitive electrochemical detection of miRNA-21.
papers.abstract: MicroRNA-21 (miRNA-21) is an oncogenic biomarker overexpressed in various early-stage tumors, making its accurate detection vital for diagnosis. However, its concentration in clinical samples is extremely low, posing a significant analytical challenge. Conventional electrochemical sensors often rely on exogenous enzymes for amplification, which suffer from high cost, instability, and complex immobilization procedures. Moreover, the poor conductivity of common electrode materials limits signal transduction efficiency. Therefore, developing an enzyme-free sensing platform with a highly conductive interface that enables robust signal amplification remains an urgent unmet need for trace miR-21 quantification. In this work, a laser-induced graphene (LIG) electrode modified with conductive Cu-MOF is developed to mediate an enzyme-free cascade toehold-mediated strand displacement reaction (CTSDR). When miRNA-21 is recognized, the CTSDR is successfully initiated to form numerous G-quadruplexes (G4), which subsequently bind hemin to create a peroxidase-like G4/hemin complex. This complex efficiently catalyzes the hydroquinone (HQ)/H 2 O 2 redox system, generating a significantly amplified current. The sensor delivers a wide linear range from 10 1 to 10 7  fM, with a detection limit reaching down to 1.94 fM. It also demonstrates outstanding selectivity, readily discriminating single-base mismatched sequences, and good reproducibility. Importantly, this strategy successfully detects miRNA-21 in thyroid cancer cell lines and clinical patient serum samples, proving its excellent practical viability. This work is novel in synergistically integrating a conductive LIG electrode enhanced with Cu-MOF and an enzyme-free catalytic cascade amplification for the first time, and in revealing that CTSDR-generated fuel strands undergo a previously unreported transition to G4 structures induced by K + , enabling ultrasensitive miRNA-21 detection without external enzymes or intricate labeling. Given its facile Cu-MOF synthesis, straightforward electrode modification, and excellent clinical concordance, this strategy provides a highly accessible, affordable, and reliable tool for early tumor diagnostics and routine point-of-care biomarker screening.

papers.title: Athyreosis and Thyroid Hormone Signaling: A System-Based Framework for Long-Term Endocrine Health.
papers.abstract: Thyroidectomy and radioactive iodine therapy are definitive treatments for Graves' disease, toxic nodular disease, and differentiated thyroid cancer. With improving survival rates and expanding indications for definitive therapy, a growing population is living for decades in a state of athyreosis requiring lifelong thyroid hormone replacement. Current management strategies largely emphasize serum thyroid-stimulating hormone targets and oncological surveillance, yet the long-term metabolic and physiological implications of chronic athyreosis remain incompletely explored. The potential longevity implications of long-term athyreosis are examined through a system-based framework integrating hormonal balance, mitochondrial regulation, metabolic adaptation, skeletal and cardiovascular health, and inflammatory signaling. This narrative review synthesizes evidence from endocrinology, metabolism, oncology, and aging research to evaluate physiological differences between endogenous thyroid hormone secretion and pharmacological replacement in athyreotic patients. Particular attention is given to tissue-level triiodothyronine availability, deiodinase activity, and downstream bioenergetic effects. Athyreotic patients lack intrinsic thyroidal triiodothyronine secretion and depend entirely on the peripheral conversion of levothyroxine to generate circulating and intracellular triiodothyronine. Emerging evidence suggests that levothyroxine monotherapy may not fully replicate physiological thyroid hormone dynamics in all individuals, potentially influencing mitochondrial biogenesis, resting energy expenditure, body composition, bone turnover, and cardiovascular remodeling. In thyroid cancer survivors, chronic thyroid-stimulating hormone suppression introduces additional considerations for skeletal and cardiac outcomes. Patients treated for autoimmune thyroid disease may also exhibit persistent immune dysregulation despite gland ablation. Athyreosis represents a distinct and permanent endocrine state with implications extending beyond biochemical euthyroidism. A system-based perspective that considers mitochondrial resilience, cardiometabolic integrity, skeletal preservation, and inflammatory tone may enhance long-term management strategies for this expanding survivorship population. Prospective studies are needed to clarify the impact of various thyroid hormone replacement paradigms on functional aging and longevity outcomes.

papers.title: Thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist simedeutirom (HSK31679) for Chinese patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis: a 52-week, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial.
papers.abstract: Simedeutirom is a selective thyroid hormone receptor-β agonist that has previously been shown to reduce hepatic fat content in metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. We assessed the efficacy and safety of simedeutirom in patients of Asian descent with biopsy-confirmed metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) and F2 or F3 fibrosis. This multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 2b trial was conducted at 42 clinical sites in China. Adults (aged 18-74 years) with biopsy-confirmed MASH, a non-alcoholic fatty liver disease activity score (NAS) of at least 4, F2 or F3 fibrosis, and MRI-proton density fat fraction liver fat content of at least 8% were randomly assigned (1:1:1) by block randomisation (block size of six; no stratification) via a centralised web-based system to receive once-daily simedeutirom 80 mg, simedeutirom 160 mg, or placebo for 52 weeks. Participants and study personnel were masked to treatment assignment. The primary endpoint was MASH improvement (ie, two-point or more reduction in NAS, one-point or more improvement in hepatocellular ballooning, and no increase in steatosis score) without worsening of fibrosis (ie, no increase in fibrosis stage) at week 52. Efficacy was analysed in the full analysis set, which included all randomly assigned participants who received at least one dose and had at least one efficacy assessment after baseline; participants without liver biopsy data after treatment or who used prohibited medications affecting efficacy were considered non-responders. The trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT06168383) and is complete. Between Jan 5, 2024, and Jan 16, 2026, 186 participants were randomly assigned (62 per group). In the full analysis set (n=179), the median age was 42·0 years (IQR 35·0-54·0), 116 (65%) participants were men, and 63 (35%) were women. 22 (37%) of 59 participants in the 80 mg group, 18 (30%) of 60 in the 160 mg group, and six (10%) of 60 in the placebo group had MASH improvement without worsening of fibrosis at week 52. ORs versus placebo were 4·87 (95% CI 1·76-13·48; p=0·0023) in the 80 mg group and 5·24 (1·74-15·72; p=0·0032) in the 160 mg group, with absolute differences of 27·3 percentage points (95% CI 12·2-41·1) and 20·0 percentage points (5·7-33·6), respectively. Grade 3 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred in three (5%) of 61 participants in the simedeutirom 80 mg group, five (8%) of 62 in the simedeutirom 160 mg group, and three (5%) of 62 in the placebo group; no individual grade 3 event affected more than one participant, and no grade 4-5 treatment-emergent adverse events occurred. Serious adverse events occurred in three (5%) participants in the simedeutirom 80 mg group, four (6%) in the simedeutirom 160 mg group, and three (5%) in the placebo group; none were treatment related. No deaths or adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation occurred. Simedeutirom led to higher rates of MASH improvement without worsening of fibrosis than placebo after 52 weeks, warranting further investigation in phase 3 trials. Haisco Pharmaceutical Group.

papers.title: A muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein regulates postnatal heart growth through mitonuclear ubiquinone-PPAR signaling.
papers.abstract: Increased mitochondrial biogenesis and aerobic respiration in postnatal mammalian organs are essential for adaptation to extrauterine life, yet the functions of many tissue-enriched, developmentally regulated mitochondrial proteins remain poorly defined. By integrating mitochondrial proteome annotations with mouse and human transcriptomic datasets, we identified Coenzyme Q10a (Coq10a), a striated muscle-enriched mitochondrial protein, as a regulator of postnatal cardiac growth. Coq10a, the mammalian homolog of the yeast ubiquinone-binding protein Coq10p, is highly induced in the heart after birth through thyroid hormone-, Nkx2.5-, and Tbx5-dependent regulation. To define its physiological function, we generated three independent Coq10a -deficient mouse models. Both global and cardiomyocyte-specific loss of Coq10a promoted postnatal cardiac hypertrophy without impairing basal cardiac function or mitochondrial respiration. Instead, Coq10a deficiency altered intracellular ubiquinone partitioning, resulting in increased ubiquinone accumulation in a microsomal membrane fraction. Transcriptomic analyses revealed enrichment of PPAR-associated metabolic gene sets and induction of established PPAR-responsive genes in Coq10a -deficient hearts. Pharmacological inhibition of PPARα and PPARγ, but not PPARδ, attenuated the hypertrophic phenotype. Molecular dynamics simulations, docking analyses, and mutagenesis identified PPARα residues that contribute to differential responsiveness to ubiquinone. Although Coq10a -deficient hearts maintained near-normal function under basal conditions, they exhibited increased susceptibility to pressure-overload stress. Together, these findings establish Coq10a as a regulator of intracellular ubiquinone partitioning and support a model linking altered mitochondrial lipid distribution and PPAR-associated signaling to postnatal cardiac growth. More broadly, they demonstrate how tissue-enriched mitochondrial proteins can mediate organ-specific physiological functions beyond energy production.

papers.title: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: A call for global awareness and research.
papers.abstract: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea (FHA) is a common yet under-recognized cause of secondary amenorrhea resulting from reversible suppression of the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis. Triggered by chronic stress, low energy availability, disordered eating, and/or excessive exercise, FHA leads not only to anovulation and hypoestrogenism but also to broader neuroendocrine disruption involving the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal and thyroid axes. Although historically associated with extreme trauma and the "female athlete triad," FHA occurs worldwide and remains significantly underdiagnosed across diverse cultural and socioeconomic settings. Beyond reproductive consequences, FHA has been associated with reduced bone density, endothelial dysfunction, adverse cardiometabolic profiles, sexual dysfunction, mood disorders, and cognitive symptoms, while potential effects on brain and gut physiology remain less established. Despite these multisystem concerns, evidence-based treatment strategies are limited, and diagnosis is often delayed due to stigma, normalization of menstrual irregularities, and lack of clinical awareness. There is a critical need for global education, standardized diagnostic and management guidelines, mechanistic research to define long-term risks, and development of targeted interventions that restore both ovarian function and underlying neuroendocrine health. In this clinical perspective, we highlight key gaps and priorities to improve recognition, management, and long-term outcomes. FHA should be recognized as an important marker of overall well-being and a call to advance scientific understanding and care for affected individuals worldwide.

papers.title: [Changes in the mineral composition of orbital bones in thyroid disease].
Integrated Transcriptomic and Network Analysis Identifies Candidate Kinase-Mediated Thyroid-Associated Targets of Withaferin A.
papers.abstract: Withaferin A (WA), a bioactive steroidal lactone derived from Withania somnifera , has been reported to exhibit diverse pharmacological activities, including anti-inflammatory and metabolic regulatory effects. Although previous studies suggest a potential link between WA and thyroid-related molecular pathways, the molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain incompletely understood. Here, we employed a comprehensive computational approach to explore WA-responsive molecular changes potentially relevant to thyroid-associated processes. RNA-sequencing data from WA-treated MCF-10A human mammary epithelial cells (GSE158085) were analysed to identify differentially expressed genes (DEGs). Because thyroid-specific WA transcriptomic datasets are not currently available, the DEGs were intersected with curated hypothyroidism-associated genes to generate a cross-tissue, exploratory set of candidate genes. The genes that overlapped were used to construct protein-protein interaction networks, prioritize high-centrality candidate genes, and conduct enrichment analyses for transcription factors and kinases. Further analysis of selected upstream kinases was performed using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations with WA. A total of 1458 differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were identified, 10 of which overlapped with hypothyroidism-associated genes. Network analysis identified candidate interactions among the overlapping genes, while higher-confidence analysis retained four connected genes (PTPN22, STAT4, DUOX2, and DUOXA2). Transcription factor enrichment identified ERG, SUZ12, NANOG, TCF3, RUNX1, and TP63 as potential upstream regulators, while kinase enrichment identified candidate upstream kinases associated with the predicted regulatory network. Based on enrichment evidence, structural availability, and literature-supported biological relevance, MAPK14 (p38α), AKT1, and MAPK8 (JNK1) were selected for molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations. Structural analyses suggested potential interactions between WA and the selected kinases, with target-specific dynamic behaviour across the simulated systems. Collectively, the findings highlight WA-responsive genes and predicted gene-TF-kinase relationships that may be relevant to thyroid-associated molecular processes. However, these associations are hypothesis-generating and provide a basis for further investigation in thyroid-derived experimental models.

papers.title: Canonical and Non-Canonical Regulators of Lipid Metabolism in the Liver and the "Liver-Other Organs" Axes.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most common chronic liver disease and is closely associated with obesity, insulin resistance, and the recently conceptualized cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome. For decades, the pathogenesis of steatosis has been viewed primarily through the lens of insulin and the canonical transcriptional programs it regulates-sterol regulatory element-binding protein 1c, carbohydrate response element-binding protein, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptors, and AMP-activated protein kinase. At the same time, recent data point to the existence of a complex network of non-canonical regulators that, independently of insulin, significantly modulate hepatic lipid metabolism. This review systematizes information on the fibroblast growth factors FGF21 and FGF19, adipokines (adiponectin, leptin), apolipoprotein C-III, as well as the monoamine neurotransmitters serotonin and dopamine. These molecules act within the interorgan axes "liver-adipose tissue," "gut-liver," "brain-liver," and "liver-spleen," coordinating lipolysis, gluconeogenesis, very-low-density lipoprotein secretion, inflammation, and fibrogenesis. Disruption of the dynamic balance between canonical and non-canonical regulators is central to the progression from simple steatosis to steatohepatitis and fibrosis. The clinical translation of this concept has already begun: the thyroid hormone receptor β agonist resmetirom and the glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonist semaglutide have received regulatory approval for specific categories of patients with noncirrhotic metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis and fibrosis, while FGF21 and FGF19 analogs, the dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/GLP-1 agonist tirzepatide, and agents targeting apolipoprotein C-III are at various stages of clinical development or are being used for related metabolic indications. Expanding the insulin-centric paradigm to include non-canonical axes opens up new diagnostic and therapeutic possibilities for MASLD.

papers.title: TSH Stimulation Reveals Additional Bone Metastases on [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT in Metastatic Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma.
papers.abstract: A 62-year-old woman with metastatic follicular thyroid carcinoma underwent 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-D-glucose ([ 18 F]FDG) PET/CT before a second course of radioactive iodine therapy because of a markedly elevated serum thyroglobulin level (498.0 ng/mL). The initial PET/CT was performed under thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) suppression (0.01 μIU/mL) and demonstrated FDG uptake in known osseous metastases involving the T10 and L5 vertebrae, while additional skeletal metastases were not conspicuous. Repeat PET/CT performed 6 days later after recombinant human TSH (rhTSH) stimulation (TSH, 70.96 μIU/mL) showed substantially increased FDG uptake in the known T10 and L5 lesions, with SUVmax increasing from 3.33 to 6.31 and from 3.98 to 11.61, respectively. In addition, metastases in the T9 vertebra and sternum became conspicuous only after TSH stimulation and remained evident on subsequent follow-up imaging, supporting their metastatic nature. This paired within-patient comparison directly demonstrates that, in this patient, osseous lesions inconspicuous under TSH suppression became clearly visualized after rhTSH stimulation and persisted on follow-up imaging, illustrating the potential influence of TSH status on the apparent skeletal metastatic burden on [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT.

papers.title: Effects of SGLT-2 inhibitors on thyroid-stimulating hormone and systemic immune-inflammation index in type 2 diabetes: a retrospective study.
papers.abstract: This retrospective study examined whether long-term SGLT-2i use is associated with differences in thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and the systemic immune-inflammation index (SII) in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) without known thyroid disease. The neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), renal function (eGFR), diabetes duration, and metformin use were also evaluated as potential covariates. This was a single-center, retrospective observational study. Adults with T2DM who had used empagliflozin or dapagliflozin for at least six months were compared with an age- and sex-matched control group of patients with T2DM not using SGLT-2i, drawn from the same outpatient clinics. Key exclusion criteria included known thyroid disease, known positivity for thyroid autoantibodies, active inflammatory or autoimmune processes, advanced organ failure, and immunomodulatory treatment. TSH, SII, and NLR were measured. Statistical analyses included intergroup comparisons, correlation, multivariate linear regression, post-hoc power calculation, and multicollinearity diagnostics (variance inflation factor, VIF). The study included 330 patients across the empagliflozin (n = 139), dapagliflozin (n = 85), and control (n = 106) groups. Median TSH (1.6, 1.8, and 1.9 µIU/mL; p = 0.338) and SII (481, 531, and 468.5; p = 0.509) did not differ significantly between groups. SII and NLR were significantly correlated (r = 0.467, p < 0.001). In multivariate regression, female sex (B = 0.161, p = 0.015) and eGFR (B=-0.0043, p = 0.037) were independent predictors of log-transformed TSH; SGLT-2i use, SII, NLR, age, metformin use, and diabetes duration were not. The study had 80% power to detect a Cohen's f of 0.17 or greater; observed effect sizes were substantially below this threshold (f = 0.02 for TSH, f ≈ 0.00 for SII). Long-term SGLT-2i use was not associated with significant changes in TSH or SII in patients with T2DM without known thyroid disease, and the achieved effect sizes suggest that any true effect, if present, is likely small. Renal function emerged as an independent correlate of TSH, suggesting that the relationship between the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis and renal physiology merits further attention in this population, independent of SGLT-2i exposure. Prospective, multicenter studies incorporating free thyroxine and triiodothyronine measurements are warranted to further clarify these relationships. This study is retrospective and does not involve a clinical trial registration.

papers.title: Identification of biomarkers related to lymph node metastasis and prognosis in thyroid cancer based on integrated bioinformatics exploration.
papers.abstract: Thyroid Carcinoma (THCA) is a common endocrine malignancy, and Lymph Node Metastasis (LNM) is a critical determinant of poor prognosis. This study aimed to identify LNM-related biomarkers and establish a prognostic model for THCA patients using integrated bioinformatics approaches. Clinical data from SEER were analyzed to identify prognostic factors in THCA. Transcriptomic data from TCGA were used to identify differentially expressed genes between LNM and non-LNM samples. Survival analysis, machine learning (Boruta and LASSO), and functional enrichment were applied to screen candidate biomarkers. Immune infiltration and a ceRNA network were also explored. Six independent prognostic factors were identified from SEER (n = 38,955): age, gender, marital status, race, pathologic T-stage, and pathologic M-stage. A nomogram incorporating these factors showed good predictive performance (AUC = 0.744). Transcriptomic analysis revealed 332 LNM-related genes. Through integrative machine learning, six biomarkers ‒ CLDN10, OTOS, NEXMIF, ACOT6, ASXL3, and SLC4A4 ‒ were selected. These genes were predominantly enriched in immune response and metabolic pathways. M0 macrophages and resting dendritic cells showed significant abundance differences between LNM and NLNM samples, with CLDN10 positively correlated with resting dendritic cells (R = 0.47, adjusted p < 0.01). A ceRNA network involving 14 miRNAs and 4 lncRNAs was constructed, with hsa-miR-15a-5p predicted to regulate SLC4A4, ASXL3, and NEXMIF. We identified six candidate LNM-related biomarkers and clinical factors associated with THCA prognosis. These findings provide a basis for further investigation into LNM mechanisms and may offer new perspectives for prognostic assessment, though independent validation is required.

papers.title: Architecture and regulation of the PGC-1α promoter: Implications for metabolic adaptation and disease.
papers.abstract: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1-alpha (PGC-1α), encoded by the PPARGC1A gene, operators as a master transcriptional coactivator in energy metabolism, and is governed by an exceptionally complex promoter network. This review summarizes the multi-promoter architecture, isoform diversity, and conserved cis-regulatory elements of PPARGC1A, including critical binding sites for MEF2, ERR, CREB, FoxO, NRF and HNF-4α. This review delineates the molecular mechanisms through which nutritional signals (fasting, exercise), systemic hormones (thyroid hormone, glucocorticoids, estrogen), and cellular stress signals (NO, TNF-α, Ang II) dictate PGC-1α expression via targeted promoter modulation. The impact of epigenetic regulatory mechanisms such as DNA methylation and histone modifications are discussed. The highly tissue-specific functional profiles of PGC-1α across skeletal muscle, liver, adipose tissue, and the myocardium is summarized, highlighting its indispensable role in mediating metabolic adaptation, muscle fiber-type determination, glucose and lipid homeostasis, adaptive thermogenesis, and the preservation of mitochondrial integrity. Finally, this review outlines contemporary methodologies for promoter analysis and proposes future research trajectories. Notably, leveraging the unique metabolic and environmental adaptability of porcine models, the use of comparative genomics and targeted epigenetic strategies is advocated to decode the PPARGC1A promoter, aiming to establish a theoretical foundation for the advanced utilization of superior agricultural germplasm.

papers.title: Network pharmacology and machine learning reveal kit as a target of roburic acid in anaplastic thyroid carcinoma: Preliminary in vitro validation.
papers.abstract: This study aims to systematically explore the potential molecular mechanism of Roburic Acid (RBA) in the treatment of Anaplastic Thyroid Carcinoma (ATC) through the approaches of network pharmacology, machine learning and in vitro experiments. Public databases were used to retrieve the potential targets of RBA and disease-related targets of ATC. Intersection analysis was performed to identify the common targets, followed by the construction of a Protein-Protein Interaction (PPI) network for these common targets. Enrichment analyses, including GO functional and KEGG pathway analyses, were carried out for the targets. Core targets were further prioritized using SVM, LASSO and random forest machine learning algorithms. Validation of the binding affinity and stability of RBA with the core target was performed using molecular docking and dynamics simulations. Finally, in vitro experiments-including cell viability, scratch assay, apoptosis detection, and Western blot-were conducted using the ATC cell line KHM-5M to validate the therapeutic effect and underlying mechanism of RBA. A total of 401 RBA-associated targets and 2151 ATC-related targets were identified; their intersection yielded 173 shared targets. GO enrichment analysis indicated that these targets were mainly involved in responses to peptide hormones and nuclear receptor activity, among other biological functions. KEGG pathway analysis showed significant enrichment in cancer-related pathways, including the PI3K-Akt and MAPK signaling pathways. Using SVM, LASSO regression, and random forest models, KIT was consistently identified as the single core target. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations demonstrated strong binding between RBA and c-KIT, characterized by low binding energy and the formation of a stable protein-ligand complex. In vitro, RBA significantly reduced KHM-5M cell viability and migration; the inhibitory effect on migration became pronounced at 24 h and was comparable to that of the positive control DOX. Furthermore, RBA promoted apoptosis and dose-dependently suppressed c-KIT phosphorylation. This study integrated network pharmacology, machine learning, and molecular simulations to identify KIT as a high-confidence core target of RBA in ATC. Preliminary in vitro validation demonstrated that RBA suppresses ATC cell viability and migration, induces apoptosis, and inhibits c-KIT phosphorylation in a dose-dependent manner.

papers.title: Predicting the efficacy of iodine-125 seed implantation therapy for metastatic lesions of radioiodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer using pre-operative PET/CT parameters: A clinical study.
papers.abstract: To analyze the clinical response of iodine-125 seed implantation ( 125 I-SI) in patients with radioactive iodine-refractory differentiated thyroid cancer (RAIR-DTC), and to explore the association between metabolic parameters derived from pre-operative 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (18F-FDG PET/CT) and treatment efficacy. This retrospective study included 48 RAIR-DTC patients, who underwent 125 I-SI for metastatic lesions at Jiangxi Cancer Hospital from November 2019 to June 2025. Correlations between parameters, such as gender, age, metabolic tumor volume (MTV), standardized uptake value maximum (SUV max ), peak standard uptake value (SUV peak ), maximum standardized uptake value normalized by lean body mass (SUL max ), peak standardized uptake value normalized by lean body mass (SUL peak ), total lesion glycolysis (TLG), tumor-to-liver ratio (TLR), number of iodine-125 ( 125 I) seeds, activity of 125 I seeds, and 90% of dose received by gross tumor volume (D 90 ), with efficacy of 125 I-SI were analyzed. Statistical analyses included two independent-sample t -tests, Mann-Whitney U test, Fisher's exact test, and logistic and Cox regression analysis. Performance was assessed using area under the curve (AUC), calibration, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Patients were regularly followed up after treatment. At 6 months, 18 patients achieved complete metabolic response (CMR), 18 partial metabolic response (PMR), and 12 stable metabolic disease (SMD). D 90 was an independent predictor of 6-month efficacy ( p = 0.031, OR = 0.798, 95% CI: 0.428-0.925), with an AUC of 0.742. DCA and calibration curves confirmed the model's robust predictive capability. Cox regression identified TLG as a significant predictor of local progression-free survival (LPFS) (HR = 4.106, 95% CI: 2.850-5.620, p = 0.036). 125 I seed implantation is an effective treatment for locally metastatic RAIR-DTC lesions. D 90 is a reliable predictor of 6-month efficacy, and TLG is significantly associated with LPFS following 125 I-SI.

papers.title: Prediction of radiation-induced hypothyroidism after proton-based supraclavicular nodal irradiation in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: The thyroid gland lies adjacent to the supraclavicular target and is highly radiosensitive, placing patients at risk for radiation-induced hypothyroidism (RIHT). While RIHT incidence and predictive models have been well described after photon-based irradiation, evidence in the proton therapy setting remains limited. To evaluate the incidence of RIHT in breast cancer patients undergoing proton-based supraclavicular nodal irradiation and to develop proton-specific normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models incorporating dose-volume, dose-averaged linear energy transfer (LETd)-volume, and dose-LETd-volume histogram (DLVH) metrics. A total of 113 breast cancer patients treated with proton supraclavicular irradiation were retrospectively analyzed. Dose-volume, LETd-volume, and DLVH metrics were extracted for the thyroid gland and individual thyroid lobes. After exclusion of non-informative variables, univariable logistic regression models were developed for all retained candidate predictors. Internal validation and model selection were performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples, and the final bootstrap-selected predictor was defined as the variable with the highest selection frequency. Model performance was assessed using apparent and optimism-corrected area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Biological dose metrics were additionally generated using six published LET-dependent relative biological effectiveness (RBE) models and compared with the fixed-RBE model using paired DeLong tests. Seventeen patients (15.0%) developed RIHT after a median follow-up of 25 months (range, 9-80 months). Under the fixed-RBE framework, the final bootstrap-selected predictors were complementary DLVH metrics: CD10L2 (cc), denoting the absolute volume not simultaneously receiving dose ≥ 10 Gy(RBE) and LETd ≥ 2 keV/µm, CD35L3 (cc), and CD5L4 (cc) for the thyroid gland, ipsilateral lobe, and contralateral lobe, respectively. The corresponding apparent AUCs were 0.794, 0.763, and 0.817, with optimism-corrected AUCs of 0.738, 0.708, and 0.766, respectively. Among the LET-dependent RBE models, the Wedenberg model based on contralateral lobe CD10L4 (cc) yielded the numerically highest optimism-corrected AUC of 0.772. Although LET-dependent RBE models showed slightly higher apparent AUCs than the fixed-RBE model in some analyses, paired DeLong tests did not demonstrate statistically significant differences. RIHT is a clinically relevant toxicity after proton-based supraclavicular irradiation. Under the fixed-RBE framework, the optimal cutoff values for the final bootstrap-selected complementary DLVH predictors were 5.6 cc for thyroid gland CD10L2 (cc), 2.9 cc for ipsilateral lobe CD35L3(cc), and 4.3 cc for contralateral lobe CD5L4 (cc). Complementary DLVH metrics may be informative for RIHT risk prediction and support thyroid-aware optimization strategies in proton treatment planning, pending further validation.

papers.title: Editorial Expression of Concern: Thyroid hormone inhibits lung fibrosis in mice by improving epithelial mitochondrial function.
Vitamin C attenuates PM 2.5 -induced thyroid dysfunction and mitophagy dysregulation by rebalancing ER-mitochondrial Ca²⁺ dynamics.
papers.abstract: As a prevalent air pollutant, PM 2.5 has been associated with a wide array of adverse health effects; however, the mechanisms by which it damages the thyroid remain only partially understood. In this study, we investigated whether calcium dyshomeostasis driven by endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress and changes related to mitophagy may contribute to PM 2.5 -induced thyroid injury in female Sprague-Dawley rats and FRTL5 thyrocytes, as well as whether vitamin C (Vc) could provide protective effects. Our results demonstrated that PM 2.5 compromised thyroid function and histoarchitecture, triggered ER stress, altered the expression and spatial distribution of IP3R1, GRP75, and VDAC1 at mitochondria-associated ER membranes (MAMs), and induced mitochondrial Ca²⁺ overload, accumulation of reactive oxygen species (ROS), loss of membrane potential, and changes in PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy markers, accompanied by GPX4 suppression and Fe²⁺ accumulation. Inhibition of ER stress (using 4-PBA), blockade of IP3R-mediated Ca²⁺ release (using 2-APB), or disruption of mitochondrial division (using Mdivi-1) each mitigated cellular damage, providing pharmacological evidence for the proposed ER-mitochondria injury axis. Additionally, Vc similarly attenuated these alterations to varying extents. In conclusion, our findings offer valuable insights into the potential mechanisms through which Vc may alleviate PM 2.5 -associated thyroid toxicity by restoring the ER-mitochondrial Ca²⁺ balance, which has significant implications for pollutant risk assessment and protective strategies.

papers.title: Potential governing mechanisms of iodine radioisotopes behavior in marine and freshwater fish: Transfer, accumulation, biotransformation, and uncertainties under climate change.
papers.abstract: The anthropogenic, long-lived radioisotope 129 I is a growing long-term concern for aquatic ecosystems due to its predominantly chronic release from nuclear industry facilities, high environmental mobility, and strong biological affinity. Unlike well-studied radionuclides, the mechanisms governing the transfer, accumulation, and biotransformation of iodine radioisotopes in marine and freshwater biota remain insufficiently understood, particularly in fish, which represent a critical link in human exposure pathways. This knowledge gap limits the accuracy of radiological risk assessments and the development of effective mitigation strategies for a contaminant that persists on geological time scales. These uncertainties are further amplified under climate change, as rising temperatures, acidification, and increased co-occurring pollutant loads alter fish physiology and affect iodine metabolism. In aquatic systems, 129 I occurs mainly as iodide and iodate, both biologically relevant and involved in enzymatically mediated pathways leading to the synthesis of iodine-containing compounds, including thyroid hormones. Despite the ecological and physiological importance of these processes, existing reviews largely address iodine in fish in a general or thyroid-centered context. This review synthesizes and critically evaluates current knowledge on the mechanisms of iodine radioisotope transfer, accumulation, and biotransformation in marine and freshwater fish, with particular emphasis on membrane transport systems, tissue-specific metabolism, and climate change effects.

papers.title: Thyroid function and frailty in hospitalized older adults: the role of FT3 and FT3/FT4 ratio.
papers.abstract: Frailty is a crucial factor in managing older adults, given its strong predictive power for adverse health outcomes. Recent attention has focused on the relationship between frailty and thyroid function, particularly the so-called low T3 syndrome. However, the relationship between frailty and peripheral thyroid hormone metabolism remains under-investigated. This cross-sectional study included 112 patients hospitalized in a single-centre geriatric unit. Data on thyroid function, cognitive performance (MMSE), handgrip strength, and comorbidities were collected. Frailty was assessed using the Rockwood Frailty Index (FI), with FI > 0.25 indicating frailty. The study population (58 men, 54 women; median age 81 years) showed mild cognitive impairment (MMSE median 22.0; IQR 18.0-26.3) and reduced handgrip strength (13 kg; 10-20 kg). Median FI was 0.304 (0.196-0.383), and 62.5% of patients were frail. Frail patients were older and had significantly lower MMSE scores, weaker handgrip strength, and poorer renal function. FT3 levels and the FT3/FT4 ratio were significantly lower in frail than non-frail patients (P = 0.001 and P = 0.005, respectively). Increasing FT3/FT4 quartiles were associated with progressively lower FI values and frailty prevalence (P = 0.032 and P for trend = 0.042, respectively). In multivariable analysis, age (P = 0.017), MMSE (P < 0.001), and the FT3/FT4 ratio (P = 0.016) were independently associated with FI. Lower FT3 levels and FT3/FT4 ratios were associated with greater frailty in hospitalized older adults. Prospective studies are warranted to validate their clinical utility as biomarkers of frailty.

papers.title: The hepato-thyroid axis in male obesity: unraveling inter-organ crosstalk through non-invasive biomarkers.
