papers.abstract: To investigate the relationship between liver function and thyroid function tests in men with overweight and obesity. Body-mass-index (BMI), relative-fat-mass (RFM), Fibrosis-4-index (FIB-4), hepatic-steatosis-index (HSI), fatty-liver-index (FLI), albumin-bilirubin-grade (ALBI), and triglyceride-glucose-index (TyG-index) were used to perform a correlation study on liver and thyroid functions in the male participants with overweight/obesity. We utilized data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2011-2012. We performed correlation analysis to examine these relationships. This study enrolled 811 male participants, including 263 lean and 548 individuals with overweight/obesity based on BMI. Analysis showed that 133 subjects had RFM of < 22.8%, while 678 were overweight/obese. Significant positive correlations were found between liver function markers (ALT, AST, GGT) and thyroid hormones (fT3, tT3), as well as between non-invasive liver indices (HSI and FLI for steatosis, ALBI for function and prognosis, and FIB-4 for fibrosis risk) and thyroid function parameters. ALBI was positively correlated with globulin, BMI, and tT4, and it had significant negative correlation with tT3, fT3, fT4, total protein, ALT, and AST. FIB-4 was positively correlated with TSH, and tT4 ( p  = 0.0026, and 0.0147, respectively). It had significant negative correlation with tT3, fT3, and BMI ( p  = 0.0122, < 0.0001, and 0.0008, respectively). FIB-4 had significant weak correlation with TSH in euthyroid subjects ( r  = 0.077 and p  = 0.034). In this study, several non-invasive liver indices were significantly associated with thyroid function parameters in men with obesity. Indices may assist in identifying individuals at higher risk of liver-thyroid dysfunction, though prospective studies are needed to confirm their utility. The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s40200-026-02107-y.

papers.title: Pharmacotherapy for MASLD/MASH: approved therapies, drug repurposing, and emerging mechanism-based candidates.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASLD/MASH) pharmacotherapy is changing rapidly after the approval of resmetirom and semaglutide for selected adults with noncirrhotic MASH and F2-F3 fibrosis; management must also address obesity, type 2 diabetes, dyslipidemia, cardiovascular risk, and kidney disease. This structured narrative review evaluates approved, comorbidity-directed, repurposed, and emerging therapies according to mechanism, regulatory status, endpoint strength, safety, interactions, and implementation. PubMed and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched without a lower date limit through September 2026 and supplemented by U.S. and European regulatory documents, society guidance, randomized trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and selected mechanistic studies. Therapies include thyroid hormone receptor-beta agonism, incretin and glucagon-containing agonists, peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor pathways, sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibition, de novo lipogenesis/fatty acid synthase inhibition, fibroblast growth factor 21 analogues, lipid/remnant pharmacology, farnesoid X receptor signaling, antioxidants, and lower-evidence repurposing candidates. Resmetirom and semaglutide anchor approved MASH-directed treatment in eligible F2-F3 disease, while comorbidity-directed therapy should be individualized by liver stage and cardiometabolic priorities. Tirzepatide, FGF21 analogues, denifanstat, and rational combinations may broaden treatment, but cross-trial comparisons and surrogate endpoints require cautious interpretation.

papers.title: Levothyroxine dose requirements, oral bioavailability and gut microbiome enterotype dynamics during the early post-bariatric period: a single-centre, prospective, cohort study.
papers.abstract: Bariatric surgery induces profound metabolic changes; however, its impact on levothyroxine (LT4) requirements, hormone pharmacokinetics, and gut microbiome composition remains incompletely understood. The current study is aimed to evaluate longitudinal changes in metabolic parameters, LT4 dose requirements, free thyroxin (FT4) absorption (AUC₀-₆h), and gut microbiome features following Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) and sleeve gastrectomy (SG). In this prospective cohort study, 79 patients with hypothyroidism undergoing bariatric surgery (RYGB n = 40; SG n = 39) were followed at baseline, 3 month, and 6 months postoperatively. Metabolic parameters, thyroid function, LT4 dose, FT4 AUC₀-₆h, and gut microbiome diversity were assessed using linear mixed-effects models. Both groups showed significant metabolic improvement at 6 months, including reductions in body mass index (RYGB: 44.5 → 32.1 kg/m²; SG: 42.9 → 33.0 kg/m², p < 0.001) and fasting blood sugar (RYGB: 114.8 → 92.4 mg/dL; SG: 109.9 → 96.1 mg/dL, p < 0.001). LT4 requirements increased significantly, particularly in RYGB (137.5 → 158.2 µg/day; p = 0.018) and SG (133.3 → 144.8 µg/day; p = 0.067), with a stronger effect in weight-adjusted dose (both p < 0.05). FT4 AUC₀-₆h increased significantly after surgery (RYGB: +330 ± 210, p = 0.003; SG: +185 ± 190, p = 0.041), indicating altered LT4 pharmacokinetics. Gut microbiome analysis revealed increased Shannon diversity (RYGB p-trend = 0.048) and significant enrichment of Akkermansia muciniphila (1.20% → 2.40%, p < 0.001), particularly in RYGB. After false discovery rate (FDR) adjustment, the major longitudinal changes remained significant, particularly for metabolic parameters, LT4 dose (µg/kg/day), and Akkermansia muciniphila in the RYGB group. Patient-level analyses showed a modest positive association between changes in A. muciniphila abundance and FT4 AUC₀-₆h after multivariable adjustment, whereas other microbiome-LT4 associations were not significant. Bariatric surgery was associated with substantial metabolic improvement, increased LT4 requirements, increased systemic FT4 exposure, and changes in gut microbiome composition. The observed microbiome-LT4 association was modest and should be considered exploratory and hypothesis-generating rather than causal. These findings highlight the need for individualized thyroid function monitoring and LT4 dose adjustment during the postoperative period. Not applicable.

papers.title: Thyroid Disease in the Era of Obesity and Glucagon-Like-Peptide-1 Agonists.
papers.abstract: The thyroid gland plays a critical role in regulating metabolism. Dysfunctions in the thyroid gland are closely associated with alterations in body mass index. The relationship between thyroid disease and obesity is complex and bidirectional with hypothyroidism and hyperthyroidism influencing body weight. In the last decade, there has been an increase in the incidence of thyroid cancer as well as the prevalence of obesity. Emerging weight loss therapies and their potential association with thyroid malignancy remains an active area of investigation. Additionally, important perioperative and surgical considerations must be addressed in patients undergoing thyroidectomy.

papers.title: OPTN-TRIP6-mediated F-actin mechanical support regulates phagophore closure to govern craniofacial skeletal development.
papers.abstract: The development of craniofacial bones is highly dependent on the intramembranous ossification process driven by orofacial mesenchymal stem cells (OMSCs). Optineurin (OPTN), a traditional mitophagy receptor, promotes OMSC matrix mineralization by mediating the extracellular release of amorphous calcium phosphate (ACP) through the initiation of mitophagy via liquid-liquid phase separation. However, the dynamic mechanisms by which OPTN regulates mitochondrial engulfment remain elusive. In this work, we show that in both zebrafish and mouse models, Optn absence causes systemic bone loss and craniofacial abnormalities. Mechanistically, OPTN recruits thyroid receptor-interacting protein 6 (TRIP6) to the surface of damaged mitochondria, inducing local F-actin polymerization and remodeling, which relies on cytoskeletal mechanical forces to support the bending and closure of the phagophore. The depletion of OPTN or TRIP6 significantly impairs mitophagy flux, triggering a massive accumulation of dysfunctional mitochondria. Overall, this study elucidates that the OPTN-TRIP6-F-actin axis ensures autophagosome closure through cytoskeletal remodeling, revealing a novel paradigm in which cytoskeletal mechanical regulation maintains mitochondrial homeostasis to orchestrate craniofacial osteogenesis.

papers.title: Neudesin alterations in hypothyroidism with and without metabolic syndrome and type 2 diabetes: association with metabolic disturbances and potential biomarker value.
papers.abstract: Hypothyroidism is one of the common endocrine disorders that often coexists with metabolic syndrome (MS) and type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM), affecting glucose metabolism, lipids balance and insulin resistance. Neudesin, neuron-derived neurotrophic factor (NENF), is a protein responsible for neurotrophic and metabolic effects; however, the role of neudesin in the development of metabolic disorders associated with thyroid disorders is still unknown. The aim of the study was to investigate the association between the blood neudesin level and metabolic changes in hypothyroid patients with or without MS. The case-control study was performed by comparing three groups of patients: hypothyroidism + metabolic syndrome; hypothyroidism only, and control group. Clinical and biochemical parameters were evaluated: glycemic indices, insulin resistance (HOMA-IR), lipid profile, and thyroid hormone test (TSH, total triiodothyronine [TT3] and total thyroxine [TT4]). Serum neudesin was detected and the level was compared between three groups. The greatest metabolic changes in patients with hypothyroidism and MS include increased fasting glucose, triglyceride, HOMA-IR, TSH, and decreased HDLC, TT4. Although all patients receive levothyroxine 100 μg daily, TSH remained elevated in both patient groups (12.94 ± 4.26 and 11.83 ± 3.79 μIU/mL vs. 1.47 ± 0.74 μIU/mL in controls). Patients with MS had the least favorable profile, with greater adiposity, blood pressure, glycemia, triglycerides, and HOMA-IR and lower HDLC. Serum neudesin was approximately 4.5-fold higher in both hypothyroid groups (6.47 ± 2.21 and 6.11 ± 1.27 ng/mL) than in controls (1.39 ± 0.50 ng/mL; p < 0.001) but did not differ between patients with and without MS (p = 0.720) and did not discriminate between them (AUC 0.509, 95% CI 0.356-0.663). Serum neudesin is therefore raised in treated, incompletely controlled hypothyroidism irrespective of MS status. Because both patient groups were also dysglycemic, the rise cannot be attributed to thyroid status alone, and the separation from controls requires independent validation. Increased level of serum neudesin is associated with hypothyroidism in presence of MS and reflects the association between thyroid disorders and metabolic disorders. Therefore, neudesin could be considered as a biomarker of metabolic risks in hypothyroid patients.

papers.title: Disruption of the thyroid hormone system and patterns of altered thyroid hormone serum concentrations after chemical exposures in adult rodents - a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Identification of thyroid hormone system-disrupting chemicals (THSDC) requires a solid understanding of the mechanisms by which exposure leads to adverse outcomes in the thyroid hormone system (THS). In this systematic review, we present the results from our extensive evidence mapping of thyroid hormone (TH) and thyroid stimulating hormone (TSH) patterns in serum or plasma, after exposure to various THSDCs in adult rodents. Following PRISMA guidelines, we systematically searched PubMed, Web of Sciences and Scopus for relevant studies. Eligible studies were selected according to predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria. Our review of 234 peer-reviewed studies revealed that only a small group of compounds induced changes in T4 and TSH consistent with the canonical view of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid (HPT) negative feedback loop, whilst the most frequent pattern was a decrease in T4 without TSH changes. The lack of a TSH response may have been due to T4 decreases not being sufficient to change HPT feedback. However, risk of bias analysis also identified deficits in TH/TSH analytical methodology, including the timepoints of TH measurements, possibly explaining discrepancies between studies. We further compared T4/TSH patterns to mechanism-of-action information and other THS-related outcomes and found that THSDCs frequently affected TH synthesis, induced hepatic enzymes involved in TH metabolism, and exhibited other differences in pharmacokinetic properties. Given the diverse chemical nature of the various THSDCs and variety of molecular targets in the THS, there is likely no single explanation for the different patterns observed. Our compilation of T4/TSH patterns observed after different chemical exposures demonstrated that it is important to not solely rely on the canonical serum hormonal patterns to determine adversity of chemical exposures. Chemicals with different responses should be carefully considered, as current regulatory criteria may fail to identify them as being harmful to human health. https://zenodo.org/records/5528557, identifier doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.5528557.

papers.title: Cohort-specific dosimetric and delivery tradeoffs for proton dynamic arc vs. IMPT for breast and chest wall irradiation.
papers.abstract: To compare proton dynamic arc therapy (DynamicArc) with conventional intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) for breast/chest wall irradiation across diverse clinical anatomies. Forty patients were analyzed (10/cohort): tissue expanders, permanent implants, no reconstruction, and bilateral disease. DynamicArc plans used coplanar partial arcs (150-160°) with arc retracing; paired IMPT plans used 2-4 static fields. RayStation 2023BDTK-generated plans shared contours and prescriptions (50.4 Gy[RBE]/28; subset bilateral 42.56 Gy[RBE]/16) and were robustly optimized/evaluated (±5 mm setup,±3.5% range) with Monte Carlo dose calculation (0.5%uncertainty,40000ions/spot) and a 7.5cm range shifter. Target coverage and OAR endpoints were compared using Wilcoxon signed-rank tests with FDR correction. Additionally, robustness pass rates, LET d metrics, and estimated treatment times were compared. DynamicArc achieved target coverage comparable to IMPT and improved robustness pass rates for selected targets. In the expander cohort, DynamicArc improved coverage posterior to the expander port and increased coverage of the chest wall evaluation volume and nodal targets. Improved D95% was accompanied by increased target V105% in several targets. DynamicArc increased thyroid mean dose and skin V95% in multiple cohorts, although skin D2cc and skin V100% remained low. Focal hotspot metrics for the esophagus, heart, and LAD were largely unchanged, with LAD D0.03cc numerically lower though not statistically significant in the expander cohort. Ipsilateral lung V20 was generally similar, with a reduction in implant cases. Several unadjusted significant findings did not remain significant after FDR correction. High-dose CTV LET d was broadly comparable between techniques with changes in the tails of the distribution. DynamicArc increased spots, energy layers, and beam-on time, but estimated total treatment time was comparable after accounting for IMPT room entry and imaging. DynamicArc achieved comparable target coverage with improved robustness in challenging anatomies, at the cost of increased V105%, thyroid mean dose, and skin V95% while maintaining comparable treatment times.

papers.title: UBE2C-TRIM21-driven NOS2 degradation stabilizes Tregs and suppresses pyroptotic signaling in thyrocytes in Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
papers.abstract: Hashimoto's thyroiditis (HT) features persistent immune intolerance and progressive thyrocyte injury, yet the mechanistic linkage between regulatory T cell (Treg) instability and inflammasome-driven inflammatory damage in thyroid follicular cells remains unclear. We hypothesized that a Treg-intrinsic proteostasis module restrains inflammatory effectors to preserve immune tolerance and limit thyrocyte pyroptotic signaling. We integrated peripheral-blood Treg transcriptomics from HT patients and healthy controls with functional perturbation, proteomic interaction screening, ubiquitination reconstitution, immunometabolic profiling, and in vivo validation. Candidate regulators were prioritized using differential expression and network analyses, then interrogated in Tregs using gain/loss-of-function approaches and Transwell co-culture with primary thyroid cells. Protein-protein interactions were identified by Flag immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry and validated by co-immunoprecipitation and BiFC. NOS2 ubiquitination and degradation were assessed by CHX chase, ubiquitination assays, linkage profiling, and in vitro reconstitution. Mitochondrial and metabolic consequences were evaluated by JC-1 staining and Seahorse OCR/ECAR assays. Translational relevance was tested in an experimental autoimmune thyroiditis (EAT) model with adoptive transfer of engineered Tregs and assessment of thyroid pathology, cytokines, autoantibodies, and pyroptosis-associated markers. Ubiquitin-conjugating enzyme E2C (UBE2C) emerged as a consistently downregulated hub gene in HT-associated Tregs and was linked to ubiquitin-proteasome and inflammatory programs. UBE2C preserved the Treg suppressive program (FOXP3/CD25, IL-10/TGF-β), improved protection of thyroid cells, and reduced thyrocyte inflammasome/pyroptosis-associated signaling (NLRP3/ASC induction, caspase-1 processing, and GSDMD-N generation). TRIM21 was identified as a UBE2C-interacting E3 ligase partner that cooperated with UBE2C to drive predominantly K48-linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of NOS2 (with K516 as a key acceptor site). NOS2 accumulation impaired Treg mitochondrial membrane potential and shifted bioenergetics toward glycolysis, undermining Treg stability and restoring thyrocyte inflammasome activation. In EAT, adoptive transfer of UBE2C-enhanced Tregs mitigated thyroid inflammation, reduced TgAb/TPOAb, increased IL-10/TGF-β, and suppressed tissue pyroptosis-associated markers, whereas NOS2 reconstitution counteracted these benefits. The UBE2C-TRIM21-NOS2 axis defines a proteostasis checkpoint that stabilizes Tregs and disrupts a Treg-thyrocyte inflammasome-GSDMD injury loop, highlighting potentially actionable nodes for future tolerance-restoring strategies in HT.

papers.title: Long-Term Determinants of Lean Mass in Ageing Adults: A 17-Year Longitudinal Cohort Study With Repeated Measures.
papers.abstract: Age-related loss of lean mass is a hallmark of sarcopenia and a contributor to functional decline and morbidity in ageing populations. This study aimed to identify long-term determinants of lean mass during ageing. Data from 3033 participants (ages 20-96 years; 49% women) in the Geelong Osteoporosis Study were analysed using linear mixed effect models with random intercepts. Appendicular lean mass (ALM) was derived from arm and leg lean mass measured using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry. Time-varying covariates were included; missing data were imputed using predictive mean matching. Over 16.7 years (IQR 9.7-23.2), women and older participants had lower ALM (β = -8.36; 95% CI -8.58, -8.15; β = -0.07; 95% CI -0.08, -0.06). Higher ALM was associated with socio-economic status (0.33; 0.14, 0.51), dietary calcium intake (0.46; 0.20, 0.67), femoral neck BMD (0.38; 0.29, 0.47) and thyroid hormone therapy (0.52; 0.04, 0.99). Physical inactivity (-0.48; -0.65, -0.31), smoking (-0.24; -0.46, -0.06) and stroke history (-0.51; -0.96, -0.07) were associated with lower ALM. Non-linear associations were observed for follow-up duration (fu: β = -0.16; fu 2 : β = 0.01; -p < 0.001), body mass index (BMI: β = 0.55; BMI 2 : β = -0.00; p < 0.001), systolic blood pressure (SBP: β = 0.06; SBP 2 : β = -0.00; p < 0.001), serum C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (CTx: β = 0.14, p < 0.001; CTx 2 : β = -0.01, p = 0.03) and high-sensitivity Creactive protein (hsCRP: β = -10.38; hsCRP 2 : β = 11.70; -p < 0.001). In fat-mass-adjusted models, low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (0.14; 0.04, 0.24) and triglycerides (0.22; 0.11, 0.33) were positively associated with ALM, whereas high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (-0.53; -0.81, -0.25) was inversely associated with ALM. Sociodemographic, lifestyle, anthropometric, clinical, biochemical and treatment-related factors show independent associations with longitudinal changes in ALM.

papers.title: Non-alcoholic Wernicke encephalopathy following pancreaticoduodenectomy (Whipple procedure): a case report and review of the literature.
papers.abstract: Wernicke encephalopathy (WE) is an acute neurological emergency caused by thiamine deficiency. It is uncommon after pancreaticoduodenectomy and may be overlooked when postoperative metabolic disturbances coexist. A 66-year-old woman underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy for a duodenal neoplasm. Her postoperative course was complicated by pancreatic fistula, extended-spectrum beta-lactamase-producing Escherichia coli infection, impaired oral intake, and prolonged nutritional support. During the third to fourth postoperative weeks, she developed fluctuating encephalopathy, bradylalia, and horizontal nystagmus. Serum thiamine was 1.2 µg/dL (reference range: 2.8-8.5 µg/dL), and magnetic resonance imaging showed periaqueductal T2/fluid-attenuated inversion recovery hyperintensity. Hypoosmolar hyponatremia with clinical euvolemia and preserved thyroid and adrenal function was considered compatible with probable postoperative syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone secretion, although urinary biochemical confirmation was unavailable. Intravenous thiamine 500 mg every 8 hours for 3 days, followed by 250 mg daily for 5 days, produced partial improvement within 24-72 hours. At 3-month follow-up, the neurological manifestations had resolved. Pancreaticoduodenectomy and its complications can accelerate thiamine depletion within a broader spectrum of postoperative nutritional and metabolic disturbances. The oculomotor findings, low serum thiamine, characteristic imaging findings, and treatment response supported a diagnosis of WE. Hyponatremia probably contributed to the altered mental status but did not explain the ocular signs or periaqueductal lesions. WE should be considered in postoperative patients with nutritional compromise and new neurological or oculomotor findings. Parenteral thiamine should not be delayed while awaiting confirmation, and coexisting electrolyte disorders should be corrected cautiously.

papers.title: Correlation between the thyrotropin-thyroxine resistance index and insulin resistance in polycystic ovary syndrome patients with phlegm-dampness syndrome.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) patients classified as the phlegm-dampness syndrome typically suffer from metabolic dysfunction mainly driven by insulin resistance (IR). Indices evaluating thyroid hormone responsiveness have emerged as promising biomarkers for metabolic disease research. However, limited research has investigated the thyrotropin-thyroxine resistance index (TT4RI), a marker quantifying central pituitary thyroid sensitivity, in this distinct PCOS subgroup. This study aimed to explore the association between TT4RI and IR in PCOS patients with phlegm-dampness syndrome. We enrolled 486 PCOS patients with complete baseline data in the present study. Among them, 264 patients were diagnosed with PCOS accompanied by phlegm-dampness syndrome. The 264 patients were further subdivided into two subgroups: with IR (n=208) and without IR (n=56), and clinical indicators were compared between the two subgroups. We evenly stratified the 264 phlegm-dampness syndrome PCOS patients into three groups to perform intergroup comparisons. Spearman's correlation and multivariate linear regression analyses were used to investigate the association. ROC curves were also employed to compare the discriminatory performance of TT4RI, thyroid-stimulating hormone index(TSHI), and FT3/FT4 in identifying insulin resistance in these patients(n=264). The sole primary outcome of this study was HOMA-IR. Relative to the subgroup without IR (n=56), the subgroup with IR (n=208) patients displayed significantly higher blood pressure, obesity-related anthropometric values, triglycerides (TG), fasting plasma glucose (FPG), fasting insulin (FINS), homeostasis model assessment of insulin resistance (HOMA-IR),free triiodothyronine (FT3), thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and TT4RI (P<0.05).Patients in the high TT4RI tertile group exhibited a relatively more prominent phenotype of IR. TT4RI exhibited positive correlations with weight, body mass index (BMI), FPG, FINS, HOMA-IR, free thyroxine (FT4), and TSH (P<0.05).In the multiple linear regression model, after adjusting for age, BMI, systolic blood pressure(SBP) and SHBG, only a marginally significant association was observed between HTT4RI group and IR. ROC analysis indicates that TT4RI exhibits limited discriminatory performance for identifying IR among PCOS patients with phlegm-dampness syndrome. Among phlegm-dampness syndrome PCOS women, diminished central pituitary thyroid hormone sensitivity is associated with increased insulin resistance. Further prospective research is needed to confirm these findings and explore clinical relevance.

papers.title: Overt and subclinical hypothyroidism during pregnancy: effects on neonatal amino acids, acylcarnitines, and TSH levels.
papers.abstract: Maternal hypothyroidism during pregnancy, including overt and subclinical hypothyroidism, is a common endocrine disorder complicating pregnancy and is associated with increased risks of adverse maternal and fetal outcomes. However, its effects on neonatal metabolism remain inadequately understood. This study aimed to assess the association between hypothyroidism in pregnancy and neonatal amino acid and acylcarnitine levels. This retrospective case-control study included 1,987 pregnant women with overt hypothyroidism in pregnancy, 2,023 with subclinical hypothyroidism in pregnancy, and 2,043 euthyroid pregnant women from Fujian Provincial Maternity and Children's Hospital between 2016 and 2024. Their newborns all underwent newborn screening for 11 amino acids and 31 acylcarnitines using tandem mass spectrometry. After adjusting for potential confounding factors including gestational age at delivery, birth weight, and neonatal sex, newborns born to mothers with hypothyroidism in pregnancy (overt and subclinical) showed significant differences in the levels of 9 amino acids compared with those born to mothers with normal thyroid function. These amino acids are involved in the arginine-proline metabolism, glycine metabolism, and the urea cycle pathway. Amino acid levels also differed between the two subtypes. In addition, the levels of short-chain, medium-chain, and long-chain acylcarnitines in newborns from the hypothyroidism groups were significantly higher than those in the control group, with several acylcarnitine indicators (C16, C16:1, C16OH, C18:1OH, and C6DC) exhibiting characteristic differences between the two subtypes. The levels of thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) in newborns from both hypothyroidism groups were significantly higher than those in the control group, whereas no statistically significant difference in TSH levels was observed between the overt and subclinical hypothyroidism groups. Our findings revealed a significant association between hypothyroidism in pregnancy (overt and subclinical) and neonatal amino acid and acylcarnitine levels, which were mainly involved in branched-chain amino acid, arginine, proline, and glycine metabolism, as well as the urea cycle and fatty acid oxidation pathways. These results underscore the importance of identifying maternal conditions that correlate with neonatal metabolites, providing a reference for exploring strategies to optimize neonatal nutrition and improving long-term health outcomes.

papers.title: Metabolic reprogramming in differentiated thyroid cancer progression: A tumor metabolomics analysis.
papers.abstract: Differentiated thyroid cancers exhibit biologic and clinical heterogeneity not fully explained by conventional staging. Metabolic reprogramming is a hallmark of cancer, and its contribution to differentiated thyroid cancer progression is an ongoing area of study. Metabolomics-the comprehensive analysis of metabolites within biologic systems-may identify stage-specific metabolic signatures. Fifty-five differentiated thyroid cancer specimens underwent untargeted metabolomic profiling using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Stage was assigned per American Joint Committee on Cancer, Eighth Edition criteria. Pathway enrichment analysis was performed, and specific metabolites were evaluated to define metabolic phenotypes of early-stage (I/II; n = 49) versus advanced-stage (III/IV; n = 6) tumors. Over 10% of 17,270 metabolic features were significantly (P < .05; |fold change| >1.5) altered in advanced-stage differentiated thyroid cancers. Pathway analysis demonstrated remodeling of fatty acid, linoleate, pyrimidine, and alanine/aspartate metabolism with tumor progression. Advanced-stage tumors accumulated metabolites associated with nucleotide and epigenetic flux (guanosine monophosphate, adenosine monophosphate, S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine, and 1-methylnicotinamide), invasive membrane remodeling (γ-linolenate, oleate), and immune evasion (kynurenine, serotonin) while attenuating markers of oxidative metabolism (α-ketoisocaproate, acetyl phosphate) and adrenergic signaling (adrenaline). Correlation analysis demonstrated internal synchrony among these markers and a counter-regulatory relationship between differentiated function and biosynthetic expansion. Locally advanced differentiated thyroid cancers appear to exhibit a metabolic phenotype characterized by adrenergic suppression, immune evasion, invasive membrane remodeling, nucleotide and methylation flux, bioenergetic collapse, and resource shunting, all at the expense of differentiated and homeostatic functions. These hypothesis-generating findings suggest that metabolomic profiling could complement existing risk-stratification frameworks. Prospective validation of metabolic phenotypes as predictors of recurrence and progression is warranted.

papers.title: Masked Fanconi syndrome: a rare presentation of cystinosis with early-onset hypothyroidism and metabolic alkalosis.
Açaí seed extract attenuates metabolic dysfunction and adipocyte hypertrophy by improving oxidative and inflammatory status in ovariectomized rats.
papers.abstract: Menopause is a physiological transition characterized by the cessation of ovarian function and a decline in estrogen production, contributing to metabolic dysfunction, adipose tissue remodeling, oxidative stress, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Due to contraindications of hormone therapy for some women, natural compounds have been investigated. We hypothesized that açaí seed extract (ASE) would improve metabolic parameters and reduce white and brown adipose tissue (BAT) remodeling through antioxidant and anti-inflammatory mechanisms. Sprague-Dawley rats (90 days old) underwent bilateral ovariectomy (OVX), with Sham rats as controls. ASE supplementation (200 mg/kg/day) started 4 weeks after surgery and lasted 8 weeks. Food intake and body weight were assessed. Body composition was evaluated by nuclear magnetic resonance. After treatment, animals were euthanized by decapitation. Plasma lipid profile, 17 β-estradiol, leptin, and thyroid hormones were assessed. Retroperitoneal white adipose tissue (rWAT) and BAT were isolated for morphometric analysis and assessment of oxidative damage, antioxidant activity, and proinflammatory cytokines. UCP-1 immunostaining was evaluated in BAT. 17 β-estradiol concentrations and uterine weight were reduced by OVX and were not modified by ASE. ASE attenuated OVX-induced alterations in body fat mass, dyslipidemia, leptin, and total T3; prevented adipocyte hypertrophy in rWAT; reduced interleukin 6 and oxidative damage; and improved antioxidant activity in rWAT and BAT. The extract reduced body weight gain, body fluid, and tumor necrosis factor alpha concentrations and increased UCP-1 immunostaining, independent of ovarian status. The results suggest that ASE has potential to mitigate metabolic alterations associated with OVX, with some effects occurring independently of ovarian status.

papers.title: The metabolic matrix hypothesis of recurrent BPPV: Otoconia-otolithic membrane-endolymph fragility.
papers.abstract: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo (BPPV) is treated as a purely mechanical disorder of displaced otoconia, yet this model alone does not readily account for spontaneous otoconia detachment, bilateral or multicanal disease, high recurrence rates, or the clustering of BPPV with systemic metabolic conditions in a subset of patients. This article proposes and structures a unifying mechanistic model-the Metabolic Matrix Hypothesis-linking systemic metabolic states to otoconial fragility, and derives testable predictions from it. It is a hypothesis-generating narrative and theoretical synthesis-not a systematic review or meta-analysis-of otoconial matrix biology, otolithic membrane anchoring, endolymph chemistry, and the dispersed clinical literature on metabolic risk factors for BPPV. Evidence supporting each proposed pathway is graded narratively as established clinical association, experimental or animal evidence, mechanistic inference, or speculative extension. In a biologically distinct subset of patients, recurrent idiopathic BPPV may represent the mechanical expression of a systemic metabolic fragility of the otoconia-otolithic membrane-endolymph unit. Vitamin D deficiency, estrogen withdrawal, osteoporosis, insulin resistance, oxidative stress, thyroid autoimmunity, and microvascular insufficiency may act as convergent entry points into impaired matrix resilience rather than independent risks. The model generates testable predictions and a clinically accessible metabolic evaluation for recurrent, bilateral, or multicanal disease, complementing repositioning maneuvers.

papers.title: MIB2-mediated ubiquitination of HK2 inhibits glycolysis in PTC.
papers.abstract: Papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC), the most common endocrine malignancy, frequently exhibits invasive behaviors including tumor invasion and cervical lymph node metastasis, which serve as major determinants of prognosis. However, reliable predictive biomarkers for these aggressive features remain elusive. This study systematically elucidates the tumor-suppressive role of MIB E3 ubiquitin protein ligase 2 (MIB2) in PTC and delineates its underlying molecular mechanism. Integrated bioinformatics analysis and validation in clinical specimens demonstrated significant downregulation of MIB2 in PTC tissues relative to normal thyroid counterparts, with reduced MIB2 expression strongly inversely correlated with aggressive clinicopathological parameters, including lymph node metastasis and extrathyroidal extension. Functional assays revealed that ectopic MIB2 expression markedly attenuated PTC cell proliferation, migration, and invasion in vitro and tumorigenicity in vivo, whereas MIB2 knockdown exacerbated these malignant phenotypes. Mechanistically, MIB2 directly interacted with hexokinase 2 (HK2) via its RING domain, thereby promoting K48-linked polyubiquitination and subsequent proteasomal degradation of HK2. This led to substantial suppression of HK2 protein levels, impairment of glycolytic flux, and consequent restriction of PTC cell aggressiveness. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration that MIB2 functions as a key negative regulator of PTC invasiveness by targeting HK2 for K48-linked ubiquitination-dependent degradation, thereby modulating glycolytic metabolism. These findings establish MIB2 as a critical suppressor in PTC progression and highlight its potential as a diagnostic biomarker and therapeutic target for aggressive PTC, providing a foundation for the development of precision intervention strategies.

papers.title: Cancer-Associated Fibroblasts Drive Papillary Thyroid Cancer Progression through ROS/NF-κB/IL-6 Signaling in Hypoxic Microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are key components of the tumour microenvironment (TME) in papillary thyroid carcinoma (PTC) and play a critical role in disease progression. We previously reported that interleukin-6 (IL-6) promotes PTC progression through activation of MAPK signalling. However, whether CAFs serve as a major source of IL-6 and the underlying regulatory mechanisms remain incompletely understood. By integrating single-cell RNA-seq data from PTC patients, we identified fibroblasts as the predominant cellular source of IL-6, with IL-6 expression positively correlated with the CAF marker ACTA2. Primary CAFs isolated from PTC tissues exhibited enhanced proliferation, migration, glycolysis and IL-6 secretion compared with normal fibroblasts (NFs), and these phenotypes were further potentiated by hypoxia. Mechanistically, hypoxia induced reactive oxygen species (ROS) accumulation in CAFs, which activated NF-κB signalling to drive IL-6 production. Blocking NF-κB with JSH-23 or scavenging ROS with NAC or MitoQ abrogated hypoxia-induced IL-6 expression. In non-contact co-cultures, CAF-derived IL-6 promoted PTC cell proliferation and MAPK pathway activation under hypoxia, whereas IL-6 knockdown reversed these effects. In vivo, co-injection of CAFs with PTC cells enhanced tumour growth, which was significantly suppressed by the IL-6 receptor blocker tocilizumab. Collectively, these findings reveal that hypoxia activates a ROS/NF-κB/IL-6 axis in CAFs, which in turn drives PTC progression through paracrine IL-6 signalling. Targeting this pathway may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for aggressive PTC.

papers.title: Respiration-Deficient Cells Require Pyruvate Carboxylase to Suppress Asparagine Auxotrophy.
papers.abstract: Mutations in mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) compromise ETC activity and impair oxidative phosphorylation. Since eukaryotic cells contain multiple copies of mtDNA, the resulting phenotype depends on the proportion of mutant mitochondrial genomes (the heteroplasmy level). Using isogenic cell lines carrying similar mtDNA deletions, a linear decline in cellular respiration was observed as mitochondrial DNA heteroplasmy increased. Despite this, cellular redox imbalance did not change until heteroplasmy exceeded 50%. As heteroplasmy increased past 70%, cells also exhibited an integrated stress response (ISR) and impaired translation was observed. These defects were reversed by either addition of asparagine or overexpression of pyruvate carboxylase (PC). The dependence on exogenous asparagine in other respiration-deficient cells was found to correlate inversely with the PC expression level. For example, patient-derived thyroid tumor cells, harboring high heteroplasmy for a Complex I mtDNA mutation and low levels of PC, exhibited asparagine auxotrophy, and L-asparaginase treatment suppressed tumor growth. Together, these findings demonstrate a role for mitochondrial pyruvate carboxylase in cellular asparagine synthesis under conditions of compromised respiratory activity.

papers.title: Thyroid Dysfunction and Its Association with Glycemic Control in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus (T2DM): A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: Diabetes mellitus (DM) is characterized by metabolic anomalies, such as hyperglycemia, resulting from pancreatic β-cell dysfunction. In this context, thyroid dysfunction is the second most prevalent endocrine disorder after DM, and the interaction with glycemic control in type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) remains a topic of debate. Therefore, this meta-analysis aimed to evaluate the impact of thyroid dysfunction on glycemic control in T2DM patients. A systematic literature search was conducted using ScienceDirect, the Cochrane Library, and PubMed up to December 8, 2024, under PRISMA guidelines. Research evaluating the effect of thyroid dysfunction on glycemic control in T2DM was included, with Glycated hemoglobin (HbA1c) levels as the primary outcome measure. Furthermore, research lacking relevant outcome data, full-text availability, or appropriate design was excluded. Data extraction and quality assessment were performed collaboratively, using the STROBE checklist. Meta-analysis was conducted using Review Manager 5.4, with mean difference (MD) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) as the effect size. Random-effects models were used to account for anticipated clinical heterogeneity, assessed by Higgins' I-squared (I²) statistic. The initial search identified 1,397 research studies, with only 3 papers meeting the inclusion criteria. A pooled analysis reported a significant increase in HbA1c levels in T2DM patients with thyroid dysfunction (MD: 1.94, 95% CI: 0.73 - 3.14; p < 0.000001) with high heterogeneity (I² = 98%). Thyroid dysfunction was prevalent in T2DM patients and was associated with poorer glycemic control. Routine thyroid function assessment could also be integrated into T2DM management to optimize metabolic outcomes.

papers.title: Intranodular Lactate for Thyroid Nodule Assessment: Universal Performance and Maximum Impact in Indeterminate Cytology.
papers.abstract: Thyroid nodules with indeterminate cytology often undergo diagnostic surgery despite a relatively low risk of malignancy, and molecular testing is limited by cost and availability. Because the Warburg effect is independent of cytological category, we evaluated intranodular lactate across all Bethesda categories, with emphasis on indeterminate cytology. Prospective, cross-sectional study of 338 surgically treated thyroid nodules at a single tertiary referral center, with histopathology as the reference standard. Nodules were classified according to the Bethesda System and TI-RADS. Lactate was measured with a portable analyzer from the solid component of each nodule and from extranodular thyroid parenchyma, with capillary lactate as a systemic control. Performance was assessed by ROC analysis, sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and Bayesian post-test probabilities. Lactate increased progressively from extranodular parenchyma (1.85 ± 0.49 mmol/L) to benign (2.30 ± 0.96) and malignant nodules (4.69 ± 1.92 mmol/L; p < 0.0001). The optimal cutoff was 3.0 mmol/L (AUC 0.90 overall; 0.83 in Bethesda III-IV), with 91% sensitivity and 83% specificity. Negative predictive value was 92% for Bethesda I/III/IV/V and 95.6% for Bethesda III/IV. Lactate did not differ between classic and follicular papillary carcinoma subtypes (p = 0.34), and no extranodular sample affected by lymphocytic thyroiditis exceeded the cutoff. Estimated relative reduction in diagnostic surgery was 61.7% (Bethesda III-IV) and 48.5% (Bethesda III-V). Intranodular lactate is a feasible, low-cost metabolic biomarker that performs consistently across cytological categories, with greatest clinical value in Bethesda I, III, and IV nodules, where it may substantially reduce unnecessary diagnostic surgery.

papers.title: Seasonal heat stress effects on the physiological, hematological, hormonal and biochemical responses of Tunisian sheep breeds.
papers.abstract: Heat stress represents a major environmental constraint affecting sheep production and welfare in Mediterranean and arid regions. This study assessed thermoregulatory, hematological, endocrine and metabolic responses to increasing thermal load in three indigenous Tunisian breeds reared under natural environmental conditions in northern Tunisia. Thirty multiparous ewes belonging to Barbarine (BTR), Queue Fine de l'Ouest (QFO) and Noire de Thibar (NTB) breeds (10 animals/breed) were monitored during three thermal phases corresponding to thermoneutral, mild heat stress and moderate heat stress conditions, defined according to temperature-humidity index (THI) classes. Physiological variables were recorded throughout all thermal phases, whereas hematological, hormonal and biochemical parameters were assessed during thermoneutral and moderate heat stress conditions. Data were analyzed using a repeated-measures mixed linear model including breed, THI class and their interaction as fixed effects and ewe as a random effect, with significance set at P < 0.05. Heat stress significantly increased rectal temperature, respiratory rate, heart rate and skin temperature in all breeds (P < 0.05). NTB ewes exhibited the highest rectal temperature under moderate heat stress, suggesting lower thermotolerance. Moderate heat stress triggered elevations in red blood cell counts, hemoglobin, total protein and cholesterol, whereas glucose, mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration and alkaline phosphatase decreased (P < 0.05). Plasma thyroxine and cortisol declined in all breeds (P < 0.05). Interestingly, thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) was significantly reduced only in NTB ewes (P < 0.05), possibly reflecting a lower threshold or more pronounced down-regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis under severe metabolic adjustments compared to lighter-fleeced local breeds. These findings demonstrate breed-specific adaptive variations essential for optimizing sheep selection and management under Mediterranean climatic shifts.

papers.title: Disrupted thyroid hormone-mitochondrial coupling in diabetic cardiomyopathy: a candidate upstream amplifier of metabolic and redox maladaptation.
papers.abstract: Diabetic cardiomyopathy (DCM) is characterized by mitochondrial metabolic inflexibility, redox imbalance and defective organelle quality control, yet the endocrine program coordinating these abnormalities remains incompletely defined. Thyroid hormone (TH) is a major regulator of cardiac energy metabolism and mitochondrial adaptation. In experimental diabetes, myocardial triiodothyronine (T3) can decline despite preserved circulating thyroid hormone concentrations, accompanied by type 3 iodothyronine deiodinase (DIO3) induction and altered TH transport. We propose that this local defect disrupts thyroid hormone-mitochondrial coupling and may thereby constrain adaptation of substrate oxidation, oxidative phosphorylation, redox defense and organelle turnover. Preclinical diabetic-heart studies demonstrate local TH dysregulation and show that appropriately dosed T3 treatment can reverse selected structural and functional abnormalities. Complementary cardiac studies identify mitochondrial biogenesis, reactive oxygen species control, mitophagy and calcium handling as plausible downstream effectors. Together, these findings support impaired local TH signaling as an underrecognized candidate upstream mechanism linking the diabetic endocrine environment to mitochondrial maladaptation. A tissue-specific therapeutic-window model may reconcile the adverse consequences of both deficient and excessive TH signaling while providing a framework for biomarker development, mechanistic testing and precision intervention in DCM.

papers.title: Endocrine determinants of MASLD: mechanisms and therapeutic targets.
papers.abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) affects approximately 30% of adults worldwide, yet is still framed largely as a hepatological disorder despite being driven substantially by endocrine and metabolic dysfunction. This review proposes a unified endocrine framework organised around seven hormonal axes, presenting each in terms of molecular pathogenesis, clinical presentation, and therapeutic implications. Insulin resistance is the central driver, coupling chronic caloric excess to hepatic de novo lipogenesis through selective hepatic insulin resistance, although genetic variants in PNPLA3 and TM6SF2 can uncouple steatosis from metabolic risk. Adipose tissue dysfunction contributes through adipocyte senescence, adipokine imbalance, and inflammatory adipose-liver signalling. Reduced hepatic thyroid hormone sensitivity, even in euthyroid individuals, predicts steatosis and fibrosis and underpins the first approved liver-directed therapy. Gonadal steroids exert sexually dimorphic effects, with testosterone deficiency, menopausal oestrogen loss, and polycystic ovary syndrome representing distinct risk states. Glucocorticoid dysregulation is stage-dependent, shifting from enhanced hepatic cortisol clearance in steatosis to local amplification in steatohepatitis. The gut-liver-endocrine axis, encompassing incretin, bile acid, and fibroblast growth factor signalling, has proved the most therapeutically tractable. Reduced GH/IGF-1 signalling, whether from pituitary disease or obesity-induced functional suppression, promotes both steatosis and fibrogenesis. Biological sex and life-course influences spanning developmental programming and ageing further modify these determinants. Two agents, resmetirom and semaglutide, now have US FDA accelerated approval for noncirrhotic MASH with moderate-to-advanced fibrosis, supporting the principle that correcting axis-specific endocrine dysfunction can produce measurable hepatic benefit; however, both approvals are accelerated and await confirmatory outcome data, while others remain investigational. An endocrine framework offers both a coherent account of pathogenesis and a rational basis for biomarker-guided, phenotype-targeted therapy.

papers.title: Global Warming and Type 2 Diabetes: Sex and Gender as Drivers in a Multidimensional Feedback Loop.
papers.abstract: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a determinant of metabolic health. Emerging evidence indicates that rising temperatures impair glucose homeostasis-specifically through reduced brown adipose tissue activity and increased insulin resistance-thereby exacerbating type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) risk. Concurrently, food systems drive substantial greenhouse gas emissions (GHGE), with gender-differentiated dietary patterns uniquely influencing both environmental impact and health outcomes. In this perspective, we move beyond well-established separate links to propose an original integrated and systemic conceptual framework. This framework connects gender-related drivers in dietary behaviors, GHGE, global warming, brown adipose tissue dysfunction, and T2DM risk into an integrated multidimensional feedback model, providing a novel basis to generate hypotheses for future mechanistic, epidemiological, and intervention studies, supporting gender-sensitive prevention strategies.

papers.title: Multi-omics profiling reveals molecular features of visceral adiposity in autonomous cortisol secretion.
papers.abstract: Autonomous cortisol secretion (ACS) from adrenal adenomas increases cardiometabolic risk. Visceral adiposity is a hallmark of ACS. We characterized ACS-associated visceral adiposity using multi-omics profiling of periadrenal adipose tissue and plasma. ACS exhibited higher visceral-to-subcutaneous fat ratio (VSR), adipocyte hypertrophy, and inflammation-related pathway enrichment than non-functioning adrenal tumors. RNA-seq deconvolution and immunohistochemistry indicated increased macrophage infiltration. Plasma steroid metabolomics identified 11-deoxycorticosterone (11-DOC), a mineralocorticoid metabolite, as positively associated with VSR in premenopausal ACS women independent of cortisol. The 11-DOC-associated gene module correlated with inflammation-related pathways, notably macrophage activation. Lipidomics identified ceramides as ACS discriminators, with Cer(d18:1/16:0) most strongly associated with inflammation- and lipid metabolism-related pathways. Mendelian randomization showed genetically predicted plasma Cer(d18:1/16:0) was positively associated with trunk fat mass. These findings identify circulating 11-DOC and adipose ceramide accumulation as molecular features associated with adipose inflammation and visceral adiposity in ACS, providing hypothesis-generating insights that require functional validation.

papers.title: Excess Liver Fat in Type 2 Diabetes Stratified by Intrapancreatic Fat Deposition: A Meta-Analysis of Dual-Organ MRI Studies.
papers.abstract: Both liver fat content (LFC) and intrapancreatic fat deposition (IPFD) are frequently increased in Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM). We meta-analysed dual-organ MRI studies comparing LFC between individuals with T2DM and non-diabetic controls and explored whether study-level differences in LFC varied according to IPFD burden. Seventeen studies (2142 participants) were included. Individuals with T2DM had significantly higher LFC than non-diabetic controls (standardised mean difference [SMD] 0.89, 95% CI 0.60-1.18). In exploratory subgroup analyses, liver fat excess was larger in studies with mean IPFD ≥ 10% than in those with IPFD < 10% (SMD 1.20 vs. 0.62; p = 0.04), though this finding was not consistently retained in leave-one-out analyses. Alternative IPFD cutoffs yielded directionally similar but non-significant subgroup differences. Study-level differences in IPFD were associated with differences in LFC (β = 0.383, p = 0.006) in univariable meta-regression, but not after BMI adjustment. These findings suggest that higher IPFD is associated with greater liver fat excess in T2DM at the study level. Individual-level analyses are now warranted to clarify this relationship.

papers.title: Diagnostic value of CT-quantified abdominal fat parameters for metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease.
papers.abstract: To analyze the diagnostic value of CT-derived abdominal fat indices in predicting MAFLD and establish an integrated diagnostic system. A retrospective study on 174 patients with a previous history of abdominal CT examination in our institute between January 2022 and June 2024 was conducted, comprising 120 diagnosed with MAFLD, and 54 controls without it. CT-derived measures including SAT, visceral adipose tissue volume(VAT), total liver volume, and average hepatic. The average value and CT attenuation value of the left and right lobe of liver and the VAT/SAT were compared using Mann-Whitney U test. were compared between both groups. Then, we used Spearman's rank correlation analysis to study whether there existed correlations between CT metrics and metabolic indicators. Logistic regression and receiver operating characteristic(ROC)curve analysis were utilized to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of individual parameters.Calibration of a composite prediction model was evaluated by using calibration plots. In MAFLD groups, SAT, VAT, liver volume, and the VAT / SAT ratio were higher than those of the control group, while the mean hepatic CT attenuation value, as well as the mean attenuation value of the left lobe and right lobe, were all lower than those of the control group (all P < 0.05). The mean hepatic CT attenuation correlated negatively with BMI (r = -0.607) and TG (r = -0.418), while the sign was positive for VAT. In univariate logistic regression, we found that the mean hepatic CT attenuation is the best diagnostic indicator of MAFLD, with an AUC of 0.923, then were left and right hepatic attenuation (AUC = 0.886), liver volume (AUC = 0.814), and VAT's mean CT attenuation (AUC = 0.796). BMI (r = 0.554) and UA (r = 0.362) were also considered. Combining SAT, VAT, and mean hepatic CT attenuation together in one model resulted in an AUC of 0.928 (sensitivity: 91.7%, specificity: 85.2%). The calibration curves demonstrated an acceptable fit of the model. When multiple variables were combined, the sensitivity improved from 85.8% to 91.7% and specificity changed from 87.0% to 85.2%, yielding an AUC of 0.928 (ΔAUC = 0.005 compared with mean hepatic CT attenuation alone, P = 0.62). CT-measured abdominal fat may represent a reliable and noninvasive approach for the diagnosis of MAFLD.The greatest individual diagnostic utility was exhibited by mean liver CT attenuation alone; however, with multiple variables merged into a combined model, the sensitivity and specificity were also further increased, which could be an effective method to image MAFLD in clinical diagnosis.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal metabolic networks in a preclinical model of pancreatic cancer and associated cachexia.
papers.abstract: Cachexia or body wasting is a significant contributing factor to the morbidity and mortality of pancreatic cancer. Despite an unmet need, its metabolic underpinnings remain poorly understood. Here, we characterize a mouse model that recaptures the longitudinal progression of human cachexia during pancreatic cancer development. We profile the metabolomes of pre-, early- and late-stage cancer-associated cachexia in male and female pancreas, its interstitial fluid (IF), plasma, liver, adipose tissue and skeletal muscle. We find that each tissue has a unique metabolome and trajectory across stages and reveal a marked lipid enrichment in the tumor IF. Using mathematical modeling, we identify metabolites participating in cross-tissue networks and in vivo validate a lactate-glucose conversion. We find systemic metabolic changes prior to weight loss and use feature selection algorithms to identify early detection markers. Our study provides a resource for system-wide metabolic evolution of pancreatic cancer and associated cachexia, highlighting the potential for timely diagnostics and interventions.

papers.title: Variation in Intrinsic Aerobic Capacity Reveals Distinct Differences in the Maintenance of Rat Knee Joint Integrity.
papers.abstract: The objective was to test how intrinsic aerobic capacity affects the articular cartilage, infrapatellar fat pad (IFP), subchondral bone, and synovial membrane of the rat knee joint. Thirty-five 24-week-old male N:NIH rats selectively bred for high aerobic capacity (high-capacity-runner [HCR]; n = 17) and low aerobic capacity (low-capacity-runner [LCR]; n = 18) were fed either a high-fat/high-sucrose (HFHS) diet or a chow diet for 12 weeks. Alterations in articular cartilage, subchondral bone microarchitecture, IFP hypertrophy, and synovial membrane cytokine levels were quantified. Body composition, serum cytokines, and glucose tolerance were assessed at Week 12. Compared to HCR rats, LCR rats had higher modified Mankin scores, bone volume, total volume, bone mineral density, bone volumetric fraction, and trabecular thickness, and lower specific bone surface, bone surface density, and connectivity density. LCR rats also had higher RANTES (Regulated on Activation, Normal T Cell Expressed and Secreted) and lower EGF (epidermal growth factor) levels in synovium analytes. Furthermore, in response to the HFHS diet, there were no differences in adipocyte hypertrophy within the IFP for either the HCR or LCR rats. LCR rats demonstrated hyperglycemia, elevated pro-inflammatory marker levels, and decreased anti-inflammatory marker levels compared to HCR rats. It was concluded that intrinsic high aerobic capacity maintains superior knee joint integrity both with and without an obesogenic dietary challenge, likely due to superior metabolic resistance. Whether intrinsic high aerobic capacity might protect joint degeneration in obesity and metabolic syndrome in other species including humans, warrants investigation.

papers.title: Analysis of myocardial work in different obesity phenotypes and its association with epicardial adipose tissue.
papers.abstract: To evaluate subclinical cardiac dysfunction across distinct obesity phenotypes using myocardial work (MW) indices, and to investigate the moderating role of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) on MW impairment. One hundred ninety-two participants were categorized by BMI and metabolic status into four groups: metabolically healthy normal weight (MHNW), metabolically healthy obesity (MHO), metabolically unhealthy normal weight (MUNW), and metabolically unhealthy obesity (MUO). MW indices were measured using speckle-tracking echocardiography. EAT volume was quantified from ECG-gated CT scans. Associations were analyzed using ANCOVA and regression models. Despite no significant differences in left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) among the groups, MUNW and MUO individuals exhibited significantly impaired MW, characterized by lower global work index (GWI), global constructive work (GCW), and global work efficiency (GWE), alongside higher global waste work (GWW), compared with MHNW controls. MHO patients showed significantly better MW profiles than MUNW and MUO groups. EAT volume was increased in all obesity phenotype groups. Although no direct association was found between EAT volume and MW indices, EAT volume significantly moderated the relationship between Metabolically Unhealthy (MUH) and both GWE and GWW. MW detects subclinical dysfunction earlier than LVEF across obesity phenotypes, with impairment progressively worsening from MHO to MUNW to MUO. In metabolically unhealthy individuals with increased EAT volume, more pronounced reductions in GWE and elevations in GWW were observed. This study has been registered in the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry under the registration number ChiCTR2500100754 (registration date: April 15, 2025).

papers.title: Constitutive UCP1 expression is associated with a glucose-dependent phenotype in murine mesenchymal stem cells.
papers.abstract: Mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs) possess significant metabolic plasticity, enabling them to adapt dynamically to environmental stressors during tissue repair. Although UCP1 is associated with nonshivering thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue (BAT) through the uncoupling of oxidative phosphorylation, its impact on MSCs metabolism remains unexplored. Herein, we evaluated the ectopic expression of UCP1 in MSCs and its effects on classical surface markers, the redox state and glucose metabolism. MSCs were genetically modified to constitutively overexpress UCP1 using a lentiviral construct. Transduction efficiency was evaluated by direct UCP1 expression and the co-expressed EGFP fluorescent tag. Surface marker phenotype and proliferation were evaluated by expression of multipotency markers and metabolic activity, respectively. Metabolic phenotypes were assessed by measuring mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), quantifying cytoplasmic and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS), and evaluating glucose uptake via the 2-NBDG assay, while key glycolytic markers were evaluated by qPCR and immunoblot. UCP1-overexpressing MSCs showed a marked reduction in ΔΨm; however, normalized intracellular ATP levels remained stable across varying cell densities. Crucially, persistent UCP1 expression did not affect surface markers or cell metabolic activity, retaining their classical surface marker profile; furthermore, the engineered cells showed reduced baseline ROS levels compared with the parental line. Most notably, MSC-UCP1 cells showed increased glucose uptake and increased sensitivity to glucose deprivation, displaying increased expression of glycolytic markers. Our data indicate that constitutive UCP1 expression is associated with a shift in MSC metabolism towards a glucose-dependent state. This distinct metabolic profile highlights the plasticity of MSCs energetics and suggests a potential therapeutic application for genetically engineered MSCs in treating energy imbalance disorders such as obesity and type 2 diabetes.

papers.title: Association Between Lipid Accumulation Product and Visceral Adiposity Index, as Markers of Visceral Adiposity and Metabolic Dysfunction, and Stroke: NHANES 1999-2018.
papers.abstract: Lipid accumulation product (LAP) and visceral adiposity index (VAI) are surrogate markers of visceral adiposity-related endocrine and metabolic dysfunction, including insulin resistance, rather than simple obesity indices. This study aimed to evaluate their associations with stroke prevalence using nationally representative data. This cross-sectional study analyzed data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 1999-2018. Stroke status was determined through standardized questionnaires. LAP and VAI were calculated using established gender-specific formulas. Analyses used the fasting subsample weights with strata and primary sampling units, and missing covariates were multiply imputed. Weighted logistic regression, restricted cubic spline (RCS), subgroup and incremental discrimination analyses were performed. Among 21,146 participants, 721 reported a prior stroke (weighted prevalence 2.64%). Both indices were higher in stroke cases (median LAP 54 vs 42; VAI 1.72 vs 1.46, both p < 0.001). In the primary model (Model 3), each 1-SD increment was associated with higher stroke odds for LAP (OR = 1.115, 95% CI 1.061-1.171, p < 0.001) and VAI (OR = 1.073, 95% CI 1.020-1.129, p = 0.007), and the highest quartile exceeded the lowest (LAP: OR = 1.557, 95% CI 1.117-2.170; VAI: OR = 1.381, 95% CI 1.026-1.858). Both were attenuated after additional adjustment for metabolic mediators (HbA1c, systolic blood pressure, eGFR and medication use), consistent with partial mediation. RCS analyses showed significant overall associations (LAP p < 0.001; VAI p = 0.041) without significant nonlinearity ( p = 0.177 and 0.143). Only race/ethnicity modified the LAP-stroke association ( p for interaction = 0.009; non-Hispanic Black OR = 1.427, 95% CI 1.231-1.654). Adding either index did not materially improve discrimination. Higher LAP and VAI values are associated with a greater prevalence of stroke after adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic, and lifestyle factors, and their attenuation after adjustment for metabolic variables is consistent with partial mediation through insulin resistance and its hemodynamic consequences. Both indices are inexpensive endocrine-metabolic markers of visceral adipose tissue dysfunction and insulin resistance that warrant prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Long-term voluntary exercise partially reverses obesity-associated transcriptomic remodeling in brown adipose tissue.
papers.abstract: Although exercise may counteract some changes caused by obesity-induced functional and molecular remodeling of brown adipose tissue (BAT), the extent to which long-term voluntary exercise reverses obesity-associated BAT transcriptional changes remains unclear. Male C57BL/6J mice were assigned to the control, high-fat diet (HFD), or HFD plus voluntary exercise (HFD + VE) groups for four months (n = 4 per group). Interscapular BAT transcriptomic profiles were analyzed using the Clariom S Mouse Array. Differential expression was explored using eBayes ANOVA, and transcript clusters with an absolute fold change >2, a nominal P value < 0.05, and a mean log2 signal intensity ≥8 in the group with higher expression were selected for exploratory analyses. FDR-adjusted P values were additionally examined to account for multiple testing. Gene Ontology enrichment analysis was performed using DAVID. Using the prespecified exploratory criteria (absolute fold change >2, nominal P < 0.05, and mean log2 signal intensity ≥8 in the group with higher expression), 579 transcript clusters differed between the control and HFD groups. In the HFD versus HFD + VE comparison, 89 transcript clusters met these exploratory criteria; 74 showed lower expression and 15 showed higher expression with VE. None of the 89 transcript clusters remained significant at FDR <0.05 after genome-wide multiple-testing correction. GO enrichment analysis nevertheless identified coordinated immune/inflammatory and muscle contraction-related biological processes, several of which remained significant after FDR correction for GO-term testing. Long-term voluntary exercise was associated with transcriptomic changes that opposed a subset of HFD-associated alterations, particularly immune and inflammatory signatures. A restricted contractile/Ca2+-related transcriptional signature was also identified, although the transcriptomic data alone do not establish altered Ca2+ signaling. These exploratory findings highlight the need for further investigation of the cellular and signaling mechanisms underlying exercise-associated BAT remodeling.

papers.title: Epicardial adipose tissue radiomics complement calcium scoring in black adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus.
papers.abstract: Conventional markers of risk such as coronary artery calcium (CAC) scores are lower and less predictive in Black adults, despite a high prevalence of Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and Metabolic Syndrome We evaluated whether incorporation of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) features capture prognostic signal beyond CAC and social deprivation index, in predicting major adverse cardiovascular events. Adults with T2DM undergoing non-contrast CT calcium scoring from the CLARIFY registry (NCT04075162), including 1024 non-Hispanic Black participants and 3072 propensity-matched non-Hispanic White participants were included. EAT was automatically segmented and radiomic features were extracted and selected using survival-based machine learning. Cox proportional hazards models were constructed using CAC, Social Deprivation Index (SDI), and EAT features alone and in combination. The primary endpoint was 3-point major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE-3P), defined as cardiovascular death, non-fatal myocardial infarction, or non-fatal stroke. Model discrimination, reclassification, and calibration were assessed. During a median follow-up of approximately 5 years, 206 (20%) Black participants and 422 (14%) matched White participants experienced MACE-3P In Black participants, the SDI+CAC+EAT model demonstrated the highest discrimination (C-index 0.62) and significantly improved reclassification compared with CAC alone (NRI) of 0.29 (95% CI 0.15-0.56; p < 0.0007). In contrast, the SDI+CAC+EAT model showed no improvement in discrimination when compared to CAC alone (C-index 0.67 v. 0.67) in the White cohort. In adults with T2DM, EAT may serve as a complimentary imaging marker when combined with CAC scores to provide incremental prognostic information or refine risk characterization.

papers.title: Energy-Based Devices for GLP-1 Receptor Agonist-Associated Facial Aging: A Tissue-Specific Safety Framework.
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonist (GLP-1RA)-associated rapid weight loss may be accompanied by facial changes resembling accelerated aging, colloquially termed "Ozempic face". In this review, this proposed phenotype is termed GLP-1RA-associated facial accelerated aging (GLP-1RA-FAA) and is characterized primarily by facial volume loss and skin laxity, with possible but incompletely characterized alterations in dermal-adipose support, adipose-derived stem-cell biology, fibroblast-extracellular-matrix homeostasis, and facial muscle. Demand for energy-based device (EBD) treatment in this population is increasing; however, whether conventional EBD parameters are effective or safe in medication-associated facial volume depletion is unknown. A narrative review was informed by structured searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library from January 2000 through August 31, 2026. Evidence was selected for clinical directness and relevance to radiofrequency, high-intensity focused ultrasound, broadband light, microwave, extracorporeal shock wave therapy, diode laser, and synchronized radiofrequency with high-intensity facial electrical stimulation. Available modalities differ in their intended tissue depth and in the potential relevance of three conceptual targets: preservation of adipose tissue, dermal fibroblast-extracellular-matrix remodeling, and facial muscle-SMAS support. Preclinical body-contouring studies suggest that sustained subcutaneous heating in the approximate 43-45°C range can be associated with adipocyte injury or apoptosis; however, no facial thermal dose threshold has been established, particularly in GLP-1RA-treated patients. No individual EBD modality has demonstrated simultaneous restoration of adipose, dermal, and muscle-related targets in prospective GLP-1RA-specific studies. Conservative control of treatment depth, careful avoidance of unnecessary deep energy deposition in volume-depleted regions, investigation of low-intensity dermal remodeling strategies, and evaluation of muscle-targeting approaches are proposed as research considerations. These concepts are hypothesis generating and do not constitute clinical recommendations or standards of care. Prospective controlled studies in well-characterized GLP-1RA-treated populations are required before device-specific protocols can be adopted. Medications used for weight management, including semaglutide (Ozempic ® and Wegovy ® ) and tirzepatide (Mounjaro ® and Zepbound ® ), can be associated with noticeable facial changes, particularly after substantial or rapid weight loss. These changes are often referred to informally in relation to specific medication brands, although they are not specific to one medication and may occur with medication-driven weight loss more broadly. Facial volume loss, looser skin, hollowing of the cheeks or temples, and a more tired or gaunt appearance may result mainly from loss of facial fat and other soft-tissue support. Whether these medications also affect the cells that maintain skin structure or facial muscles is still being studied. Energy-based devices are treatments that use controlled heat, light, ultrasound, or electrical stimulation. They are increasingly considered for skin tightening and facial rejuvenation. Different devices act at different tissue depths: some mainly affect the skin, whereas others may also reach deeper connective tissue, fat, or muscle. In people with medication-associated facial volume loss, deep or overly aggressive treatment may, in theory, affect already reduced fat layers or cause unwanted tissue injury. However, this possibility has not been adequately tested in people using GLP-1 receptor agonists or other weight-loss medications. This review examines the potential tissue targets, mechanisms, and available evidence for major energy-based technologies. It outlines cautious, research-oriented considerations, including careful control of treatment depth, conservative settings in thin or volume-depleted areas, and individualized assessment of whether muscle-targeting treatments may be appropriate. Direct clinical evidence in people with GLP-1RA-associated facial changes remains very limited. The approaches discussed in this review are early research considerations, not established treatment guidelines or standards of care.

papers.title: Adult-Onset Vitamin-A Deficiency Reshapes the Gut Microbiome and is associated with Sex-Specific and shared Systemic Effects in Adult Wistar Rats.
papers.abstract: Vitamin A deficiency (VAD) remains a major global health concern. Vitamin A promotes immunity, neurogenesis, energy balance, and gut integrity. However, most studies have focused on early developmental stages and adult-onset VAD remain poorly understood. To determine whether physiological, behavioural, and gut microbial responses to adult-onset VAD differ between male and female rats. Adult male and female Wistar rats (9-10 weeks) were fed a vitamin A-sufficient (VAS, n = 6) or VAD (n = 6) diet for 20 weeks. Vitamin A levels were monitored every 4 weeks. Behavioural function was assessed at 12th and 18th weeks. After 20 weeks, rats were euthanised, and serum, cecal contents, liver, duodenum, hippocampus, and visceral white adipose tissue (vWAT) were collected for assessment of vitamin A metabolites, physiological and morphological changes, gut microbiome, and serum metabolome. Data were analysed using Student's t-test or the Mann-Whitney U test, as appropriate, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction. Females and males reach the deficiency threshold (<0.7 μmol/L) at 12 and 16 weeks, respectively. At week 12, females showed a 2-fold reduction in serum vitamin A levels (VAS, 1.1 vs VAD, 0.5 μmol/L;p = 0.012), despite unchanged body weight and feed intake. Microbial responses were sex-divergent; the Bacillota/Bacteroidota ratio increased only in females (4.18 in VAS vs 7.0 in VAD; p = 0.008). The virome shifted in both sexes, with distinct signatures. Anxiety-like behaviour appears by 12 weeks in females but not in males. Systemic responses (reduced gut barrier, increased immune gene expression, and adipocyte hypertrophy) were largely shared. This study provides evidence that adult-onset VAD in rats may be associated with sex-specific alterations in the microbiome, but with more generalised systemic outcomes.

papers.title: FABP4 drives gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis by inhibiting ferroptosis via UBR4/ALOX15-mediated arachidonic acid metabolism.
papers.abstract: Peritoneal metastasis (PM) significantly contributes to the high mortality rate in patients with advanced gastric cancer (GC) and indicates a poor prognosis. A hallmark of cancer is dysregulated lipid metabolism, and gastric cancer peritoneal metastasis (GCPM) is specifically associated with these metabolic alterations. While fatty acid binding protein 4 (FABP4) is a known crucial regulator of fatty acid metabolism in tumor cells, its precise role in GCPM remains unclear. In this study, we found that adipocytes induced FABP4 upregulation in GC cells through PPARγ-dependent signaling, and FABP4 was highly expressed in PM tissues from GCPM patients. FABP4 cooperated with CD36 to facilitate adipocyte-derived arachidonic acid (AA) acquisition while simultaneously limiting the peroxidation of AA that drives ferroptosis. Mechanistically, FABP4 stabilized UBR4 by limiting its lysosome-dependent degradation, thereby promoting UBR4-mediated ubiquitination and degradation of ALOX15, suppressing AA peroxidation and ferroptosis. Collectively, our findings reveal a FABP4-UBR4-ALOX15 axis that links adipocyte-derived lipid metabolism to ferroptosis resistance and peritoneal metastasis in GC cells, and identify FABP4 as a potential therapeutic target for GCPM.

papers.title: Shortening of the Zfp143 3'UTR by alternative polyadenylation alters ZFP36L1-mediated regulation and promotes adipogenesis.
papers.abstract: Understanding the molecular mechanisms governing adipogenesis is essential for elucidating adipose tissue development and metabolic disorders. Alternative polyadenylation (APA) of the 3' untranslated region (3'UTR) has emerged as an important regulatory layer in adipogenesis; however, the functional significance of APA-induced 3'UTR shortening in individual genes remains to be elucidated. This study aimed to investigate the roles and mechanisms of APA-generated zinc-finger protein 143 (Zfp143) isoforms in adipogenesis. The expression pattern of Zfp143 during adipogenesis was characterized, and functional analyses revealed the involvement of Zfp143 in adipogenic differentiation. Using 3'RACE, two Zfp143 isoforms with long and short 3'UTRs were identified. To evaluate the functional differences between APA-generated isoforms, isoform-specific expression constructs containing the identical Zfp143 coding sequence fused with either the short or long 3'UTR were generated. The short 3'UTR isoform exhibited higher Zfp143 expression levels and stronger adipogenic capacity than the long isoform.
