Dual-luciferase reporter assays, RNA immunoprecipitation assays, and molecular analyses demonstrated differential post-transcriptional regulation between the two isoforms. Mechanistically, the long 3'UTR isoform was negatively regulated by ZFP36L1 binding to AREs within its 3'UTR, whereas the short isoform escaped ZFP36L1-mediated regulation due to the absence of AREs in its 3'UTR. Collectively, these findings reveal an APA-dependent post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism in which ZFP36L1 differentially regulates Zfp143 3'UTR isoforms, thereby fine-tuning Zfp143 expression and adipogenic differentiation during adipogenesis.

papers.title: Molecular triage and isoform protection safeguard ubiquitin chain editing on DNA.
papers.abstract: In an accompanying study, we identify the RPA-ZUP1 complex as a ubiquitin chain-editing machine that promotes removal of RPA from ssDNA. Because loss of ZUP1 causes pathological RPA trapping on ssDNA, cells must preserve a functional RPA-ZUP1 pool to sustain RPA turnover. How this homeostasis is achieved is unknown. Here, we show that ZUP1 is subject to ubiquitin-dependent fate control. ZUP1 ubiquitination promotes recruitment of p97/VCP and ATXN3, defining a molecular triage pathway that protects ZUP1 from premature proteasomal degradation. Opposing this, the E3 ligases UBR5 and HUWE1 define a degradative branch that limits ZUP1 abundance, with HUWE1 restricting its accumulation on damaged chromatin. We further show that cells express a naturally occurring ZUP1 isoform resistant to efficient ubiquitination and turnover, suggesting that isoform diversity provides a protected pool of chain-editing activity. Together, these findings define a homeostatic system that preserves ZUP1 while limiting its persistence on damaged chromatin.

papers.title: Integrative Transcriptomic Analysis of Obesity-Associated Candidate Genes in Pediatric Adipose Tissue.
papers.abstract: Tryptophan metabolism has been linked to pediatric obesity, although the transcriptomic evidence connecting obesity-associated genes with this pathway remains limited. Two public subcutaneous adipose tissue datasets, GSE205668 and GSE104815, were analyzed. GSE205668 included 26 obesity and 35 control samples, and GSE104815 included 4 obesity and 4 control samples. Differential expression screening, weighted gene coexpression network analysis (WGCNA), exploratory coexpression enrichment, immune score analysis, and regulatory network prediction were performed. Four candidate genes, APOL4, FASN, KRT79, and MACROD1, emerged from the exploratory intersection analysis. Their expression was higher in control samples than in obesity samples in both public datasets. Results derived from nominal p-value screens are interpreted as exploratory. The literature-derived tryptophan-related WGCNA score is considered separately from the canonical Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) tryptophan-metabolism pathway. These findings define obesity-associated transcriptomic candidates in pediatric adipose tissue and do not establish direct participation of the four genes in tryptophan metabolism or a causal role in obesity.

papers.title: Probiotics-derived postbiotics improve host metabolic syndrome by activating the adipocyte thermogenic signaling pathway in high-fat diet-fed mice.
papers.abstract: Metabolic syndrome, including type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity, represents a global health challenge. While probiotics can modulate host metabolism, postbiotics (inanimate microbial preparations) have emerged as potentially safer and more stable therapeutic alternatives. The current study investigates the effects of postbiotics derived from five human-origin bacterial strains in mice model with high-fat diet-induced metabolic syndrome. Using multi-omics profiling, we demonstrate that supplementation of postbiotics significantly ameliorates weight gain, improves glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity, and alleviates hepatic steatosis. Transcriptomic analysis indicates that the treatment upregulated adipocyte genes related to thermogenesis and fatty acid oxidation while downregulating hepatic lipid synthesis. Most importantly, the intervention reshapes the gut microbiota structure. Target metabolomics reveals that this microbial remodeling is accompanied by a significant elevation of indole-3-acetic acid (IAA), a tryptophan-derived microbial metabolite, in the host serum. Functional studies in primary adipocytes confirm that IAA is sufficient to trigger thermogenic gene expression and activate AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) signaling. These findings suggest a mechanism where postbiotics improve metabolic health by modulating the gut ecosystem to enrich beneficial metabolites like IAA, which in turn ameliorates the metabolic syndrome and promotes adipocyte thermogenesis and lipolysis. The present research supports postbiotics as a promising therapeutic strategy for metabolic syndrome and highlights the importance of the gut microbiota-metabolite axis.

papers.title: Glycosylated extracellular vesicles drive a metabolic interplay between gastric cancer cells and adipocytes.
papers.abstract: Aim: Tumor cells and extracellular vesicles (EVs) dynamically interact with adipocytes, contributing to tumor progression and systemic metabolic dysfunctions. While the role of glycosylation in this process remains unclear, glycans facilitate communication between tumors and their surrounding environment. Here, we aimed to elucidate the pivotal role of sialyl-Tn (STn), a tumor-associated glycan, in driving a bidirectional metabolic reprogramming between gastric cancer cells and adipocytes. Methods: EVs were isolated from gastric cancer cells with distinct glycosylation profiles by ultracentrifugation and characterized by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and western blotting. Flow cytometry was used to quantify EV uptake by adipocytes. EV-mediated adipocyte browning and lipolysis were measured by real-time quantitative polymerase chain reaction, glycerol and fatty acid release, perilipin immunofluorescence, and western blotting analysis of lipid synthesis and hydrolysis enzymes. The reciprocal effects of beige adipocytes on tumor cells were evaluated using fatty acid uptake assays, metabolomics, RNA sequencing, Seahorse metabolic flux, organelle number, proliferation, and migration assays. Results: STn-positive gastric cancer cells and EVs induced white-into-beige transdifferentiation. These cells exhibited an enhanced capacity to release glycerol and fatty acids, which were predominantly taken up by gastric cancer cells displaying STn. As a feedback mechanism, gastric cancer cells shift their metabolism towards fatty acid oxidation, concomitant with increased mitochondrial and endosomal biogenesis, and enhanced motility. Conclusion: Our findings reveal a key role for the tumor-associated glycan STn in metabolic reprogramming of adipocytes by tumor cells and EVs, opening new avenues for targeted therapies in cancer patients experiencing metabolic dysfunctions, such as cancer cachexia.

papers.title: Chrononutritional regulation of metabolic homeostasis: intermittent fasting through gut microbiota, circadian rhythms, and autophagy.
papers.abstract: The global obesity epidemic has increased the burden of metabolic diseases. Dietary interventions are key to managing obesity and improving metabolic health. Intermittent fasting (IF) has emerged as a promising chrononutritional intervention that may modulate metabolic metabolic homeostasis through timed eating-fasting cycles. This review examines four main IF patterns:time-restricted feeding (TRF), alternate day fasting (ADF), the 5:2 fasting, and the 4:3 fasting, and evaluates their effects on body weight, glucose homeostasis, insulin sensitivity, and lipid profiles. Furthermore, it delineates the mechanistic pathways through which IF confers metabolic benefits beyond caloric restriction alone: (1) alleviating insulin resistance by enhancing the intestinal mucosal barrier and upregulating GLP-1 expression suppressing endotoxemia-related inflammation; (2) restoring circadian rhythmicity in the expression of metabolism-related genes to correct metabolic dysregulation; (3) increasing energy expenditure and lipid oxidation via short-chain fatty acid-mediated browning of white adipose tissue (WAT); and (4) enhancing cellular autophagy through activation of the SIRT3-AMPK-mTOR signaling pathway, thereby improving overall metabolic function. Evidence supports IF as a potentially effective alternative for obesity and metabolic disorders through chronobiological mechanisms. However, potential adverse effects like hypoglycemia and adherence challenges highlight the need for individualized approaches in clinical practice.

papers.title: A repurposing screen of 29 media mixtures derived from 15 commercial serum-free media products identifies potential cost reductions for industrial animal cell cultivation.
papers.abstract: We performed a repurposing screen of 15 commercial serum-free products, across 29 different media mix options, in Nunc™ EasYFlask™ cell culture flasks/CELLBIND® 6-well plates, agnostic of their recommended application or cell type. 20% v/v FBS DMEM was replaced with a given serum-free mix in a single step, and growth monitored over 6 days for the mouse muscle cell line, Sol8. 20 serum-free media mixes reduced or failed to increase growth, while 9 increased cell growth. 'Mix D', Fishers base medium containing 2% v/v Ultroser G serum alternative, showed the best combination of cell number increase and volumetric media cost reduction: 33% lower than 20% v/v FBS DMEM. Further Nunc™ EasYFlask™ cell culture flasks/CELLBIND® 6-well plates experiments showed that Mix D supported levels of Sol8 cell growth comparable to 20% v/v FBS DMEM, but with lower levels of metabolic activity. Comparable growth in Mix D was observed for Sol8 cells that had undergone a period of adaptation to the serum-free medium, and clonally-derived Sol8 sub-populations. Mix D also matched serum-containing media performance in supporting growth of the porcine muscle cell line, pMYOSC, the porcine pre-adipocyte fat cell line, pADSC and the mouse pre-adipocyte cell line, 3T3 L1 in Nunc™ EasYFlask™ cell culture flasks/CELLBIND® 6-well plates. 3T3 L1 cells cultivated in Mix D retained their capacity to differentiate into adipocytes, a cell type important for animal fat cultivation. The observation that Mix D supported growth of four different animal cell types at levels comparable to serum-containing medium recommends this formulation, and this repurposing screen approach, to researchers seeking serum alternatives.

papers.title: Lipedema in a male patient: familial evidence and clinical response to nutritional intervention - case report.
papers.abstract: Lipedema is a chronic adipose tissue disorder that predominantly affects women, although some rare cases do occur in men. We report the case of a 32-year-old man with symmetrical, lower-limb fat accumulation, foot sparing, pain, easy bruising, and a positive family history of lipedema. His first-degree female cousin exhibited the classic phenotype. Dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry demonstrated greater fat accumulation in the gynoid than in the android and visceral regions, reinforcing a predominantly gluteofemoral adiposity pattern. The patient underwent a 7-month personalized nutritional intervention consisting of a moderately hypocaloric, high-protein, low-glycemic diet with vitamin D supplementation and regular physical activity. This intervention was associated with reductions in anthropometric measurements and decreased pain scores on a Visual Analogue Scale. Laboratory tests revealed a preserved hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis, except for mild idiopathic hyperprolactinemia that normalized during follow-up. This case highlights lipedema in men and the potential benefits of early lifestyle-based interventions. O lipedema é um distúrbio crônico do tecido adiposo que afeta predominantemente mulheres, embora ocorram casos raros em homens. Relatamos o caso de um homem de 32 anos com acúmulo simétrico de gordura nos membros inferiores, dor, preservação dos pés, tendência a equimoses e histórico familiar positivo para lipedema. Sua prima de primeiro grau apresentava fenótipo clássico. A absorciometria por dupla emissão de raios X demonstrou maior acúmulo de gordura na região ginoide do que nas regiões androide e visceral, reforçando um padrão de adiposidade predominantemente gluteofemoral. O paciente foi submetido a intervenção nutricional personalizada por sete meses, baseada em dieta hipocalórica moderada, hiperproteica e de baixo índice glicêmico, associada à suplementação de vitamina D e à prática regular de atividade física. Essa intervenção resultou em redução das medidas antropométricas e diminuição dos escores de dor na Escala Visual Analógica. Os exames laboratoriais revelaram preservação do eixo hipotálamo-hipófise-gônadas, exceto por uma hiperprolactinemia idiopática leve, que se normalizou durante o acompanhamento. Este caso destaca a ocorrência de lipedema em homens e os potenciais benefícios de intervenções precoces baseadas em mudanças no estilo de vida.

papers.title: Targeting host ferroptosis in cancer cachexia: Tumor-immune triggers, tissue wasting, and the therapeutic paradox.
papers.abstract: Cancer cachexia is a systemic wasting syndrome driven by tumor burden, chronic inflammation, disrupted nutrient handling, and neuroendocrine stress. Supportive nutrition, exercise, and symptom management rarely restore lean mass, function, or treatment tolerance once wasting is established. Ferroptosis, iron-dependent cell death caused by phospholipid peroxidation, may connect inflammatory iron redistribution, lipid remodeling, mitochondrial stress, and impaired antioxidant defenses. This review critically evaluates ferroptosis in cachexia from a tumor-host pharmacology perspective, distinguishing causal evidence from associated oxidative signatures. We highlight two experimentally supported mechanisms: neutrophil-derived lipocalin-2 in lung cancer cachexia and tumor exosomal miR-203a-3p in pancreatic cancer-associated muscle wasting. We also examine the paradox that tumor ferroptosis induction may weaken host-tissue resistance and worsen muscle and adipose loss. We propose a "split-ferroptosis" strategy combining tumor sensitization with host-protective iron modulation, lipid peroxide scavenging, endogenous defense reinforcement, and biomarker-guided patient selection to expand the tumor-host therapeutic index.

papers.title: Multi-site metabolomics reveals one-carbon and placental steroid disruption in maternal pre-pregnancy obesity linked to adverse pregnancy outcomes.
papers.abstract: This study characterized metabolomic profiles of maternal adipose tissue, placenta, and cord blood in pre-pregnancy obesity and explored links to adverse pregnancy outcomes (APOs). From a prospective cohort (Oct 2024-Oct 2025, n  = 1,335), 25 obese (pre-pregnancy BMI ≥ 28 kg/m 2 ) and 25 control women undergoing cesarean section were included. Visceral adipose, placenta, and umbilical vein plasma were analyzed using UHPLC-MS/MS. Metabolite differences were analyzed using Random Forest modeling, OPLS-DA, KEGG pathway enrichment analysis, and correlation analysis with clinical indicators, including gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP), preterm birth, macrosomia, postpartum hemorrhage (PPH), and various laboratory parameters. In an independent external cohort, mRNA expression levels of key steroidogenic enzymes in placental tissues were verified by qRT-PCR. The obesity group showed significantly higher incidences of GDM, HDP, PPH and higher neonatal weight. Vitamin B12 and folic acid were key discriminators across all compartments. Adipose tissue metabolites were enriched in arginine/proline, pentose phosphate, and cysteine/methionine metabolism. Placenta was enriched in steroid hormone biosynthesis pathways. Cord blood additionally showed enrichment in TCA cycle, glutamatergic and serotonergic synapses. Key compartment-specific metabolites included etiocholanolone (adipose), 16-glucuronide-estriol (placenta), and 5 α -androstan-3-one (cord blood), all of which correlated with clinical indicators. The mRNA expression changes of key steroidogenic enzymes in placental tissues paralleled the alterations in their corresponding metabolite abundances. Pre-pregnancy obesity-related adverse pregnancy outcomes are driven by a disrupted maternal-fetal metabolic axis characterized by three core features: global dysfunction of one-carbon metabolism exemplified by vitamin B12 and folic acid abnormalities, placental steroid hormone biosynthesis abnormalities as the central hub, and disturbances in fetal energy and neurotransmitter metabolism as the downstream consequence. Monitoring these metabolites may enable early risk identification and guide targeted interventions for placental steroid metabolism.

papers.title: Amelioration of chronic inflammation, insulin resistance, and gut microbiota homeostasis by a combination of Bifidobacterium , Lactobacillus , Enterococcus , and Bacillus in obese type 2 diabetic mice.
papers.abstract: To examine the effects of a combination of live Bifidobacterium , Lactobacillus , Enterococcus , and Bacillus (CBLEB) on glucose/lipid metabolism, inflammation, gut microbiota, and related mechanisms in obese type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) mice. Obese T2DM mice were established by feeding mice a high-fat diet for four weeks, followed by a single intraperitoneal injection of streptozotocin (100 mg/kg). The mice were then divided randomly into 5 groups (n = 8/group): normal control (NC), T2DM model, CBLEB (585 mg/kg/d, by gavage), dimethylbiguanide (DMBG, 200 mg/kg/d, by gavage), and CBLEB+DMBG combination. All treatments were administered daily for four weeks. The body weight and fasting blood glucose were monitored weekly. An oral glucose tolerance test was performed to assess the glucose tolerance. The serum levels of lipids (triglycerides, total cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and low-density lipoprotein cholesterol), insulin, and inflammatory factors (tumor necrosis factor [TNF]-α, interleukin [IL]-1β, IL-6, IL-10, and lipopolysaccharide) were measured by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay. Pancreatic IL-6 and TNF-α expression was detected by immunohistochemistry. The histopathological changes in the pancreas, colon, and adipose tissues were evaluated by hematoxylin and eosin staining. The protein expression of insulin receptor substrate 1 (IRS-1)/p-IRS-1 (Ser307), Toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4)/MyD88, tight junction proteins (zonula occludens protein 1 [ZO-1]/claudin 1 [CLDN1]/occludin), and B-cell lymphoma/leukemia-2 (Bcl-2)-associated X protein A (BAX)/Bcl-2 was analyzed by Western blot. The gut microbiota composition was profiled by 16S rRNA gene sequencing. CBLEB significantly improved the weight gain, hyperglycemia, insulin resistance (IR), dyslipidemia, reduced adipocyte size, suppressed systemic inflammation, and alleviated pancreatic and colonic damage in T2DM mice. The combination of CBLEB and DMBG showed the most pronounced improvements in metabolic and inflammatory parameters. Western blot showed that CBLEB inhibited TLR4/MyD88 signaling, enhanced insulin signaling (IRS-1/p-IRS-1), repaired the intestinal barrier (ZO-1/CLDN1/occludin), and regulated the apoptotic balance (BAX/Bcl-2). Gut microbiota analysis suggested that CBLEB remodeled the gut microbiota, with a functional prediction suggesting shifts in the metabolic pathways and a decrease in the abundance of Escherichia spp. CBLEB ameliorated systemic inflammation and IR in obese T2DM mice through gut microbiota modulation, intestinal barrier restoration, and suppression of inflammatory pathways.

papers.title: Exosomal microRNAs as biomarkers of multimorbidity risk in lean and obese women with polycystic ovary syndrome.
papers.abstract: Polycystic ovarian syndrome (PCOS) is a multifactorial endocrine disorder that is characterised by reproductive, metabolic and cardiometabolic abnormalities. Besides typical hormonal abnormalities, inter-organ communication has a crucial role in the development of PCOS-associated multimorbidity. PCOS causes early changes in the insulin signalling pathway, inflammatory pathways, androgen synthesis genes, and ovarian theca cell activity even before the appearance of regular symptoms such as irregular periods, polycystic ovaries, weight gain, and hyperandrogenism. Exosomes are tiny extracellular vesicles discharged into the circulation. It transports molecular cargoes such as microRNAs (miRNAs), proteins that influence gene expression and reflect the underlying pathophysiological condition of target tissues. Exosomes facilitate early disease detection by carrying stable, selectively packaged gene-regulatory molecules that reflect early cellular and molecular alterations before phenotypic manifestations occur. Although exosomal miRNAs (ExomiR) are stable, non-invasive, and easily detectable in body fluids, they serve as a potent biomarkers. These circulating ExomiR have contributed to multiple organ dysfunctions, including the ovary, adipose tissue, liver, cardiovascular system, and brain, thereby raising the risk of comorbid conditions like endometrial disorder, insulin resistance, type 2 diabetes, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, and cardiovascular disease. In obese PCOS, circulating ExomiR influences pathways related to steroidogenesis, insulin signalling, inflammation, oxidative stress, and lipolysis. However, its role in lean PCOS is not well studied. This review summarises the potential roles of ExomiR as novel biomarkers that bridge reproductive and non-reproductive facets of PCOS, indicating new paths for precision medicine and tailored treatment interventions in both lean and obese PCOS phenotypes.

papers.title: CRISPR screens identify ACSL4 as a key regulator in macrophage activation and metabolic inflammation.
papers.abstract: Pro-inflammatory macrophages drive obesity-associated metabolic inflammation. Identifying key regulators of their activation is crucial for new therapies. This study aimed to identify novel regulators of pro-inflammatory adipose tissue macrophage (ATM) activation and assess their therapeutic potential. We combined genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 screening with scRNA-seq data from human adipose tissue and identified long-chain acyl-CoA synthetase 4 (ACSL4) as critical for pro-inflammatory ATM activation. Validation used myeloid-specific Acsl4 knockout mice (Acsl4 fl/fl Lyz2 Cre ) and shRNA-mediated knockdown in macrophage cell lines (RAW264.7, THP-1, and iBMDM). Mechanisms were explored via mutagenesis, immunostaining, co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP), bimolecular fluorescence complementation (BiFC), and transcriptional activity assays. A high-throughput screen of 8,685 DrugBank compounds was performed to identify candidates targeting ACSL4. ACSL4 deficiency markedly reduced pro-inflammatory factor expression (Tnfα, Il1β, and Il6). Myeloid ACSL4 deletion protected against high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obesity, correlated with reduced pro-inflammatory ATMs and enhanced adipocyte lipolysis and thermogenesis, without affecting food intake, water intake, or locomotor activity in mice. However, glucose tolerance and insulin sensitivity were not significantly affected. Mechanistically, ACSL4 contributed to inflammation independent of its enzymatic/ferroptotic functions (Thr328 mutation, troglitazone insensitivity). Instead, ACSL4 translocated to the nucleus in a karyopherin β1 (KPNB1)-dependent manner. DrugBank screening identified abemaciclib as a potential inhibitor of the ACSL4-KPNB1 interaction. Notably, abemaciclib treatment reduced macrophage inflammation and attenuated HFD-induced obesity in mice. ACSL4 promotes pro-inflammatory macrophage activation through its KPNB1-dependent nuclear translocation and cooperation with IRF5. Targeting the ACSL4-KPNB1 interaction may represent a potential therapeutic strategy for metabolic inflammation.

papers.title: Adipose tissue transcriptome before and after surgery: effects on genes driving lipid metabolism, inflammation, and RNA processing.
papers.abstract: Obesity, marked by excess adipose tissue, is strongly associated with increased cardiometabolic risk. Metabolic bariatric surgery (MBS) leads to significant and sustained weight loss and improves metabolic profiles in persons with severe obesity. However, how MBS induces persistent transcriptional changes in adipose tissue and their contributions to cardiometabolic improvements remain unclear. This study examined subcutaneous (SAT) and visceral (VAT) adipose tissue transcriptome profiles in people with severe obesity, tracking changes in SAT after MBS, with a focus on lipid metabolism, inflammation, RNA processing, and cholesterol handling. This study included 42 women with severe obesity undergoing MBS and 15 sex-matched healthy people without obesity as controls. Targeted RNA expression profiling was performed on SAT and VAT samples. In people with obesity, SAT showed higher expression of genes related to adipocyte function, anti-inflammatory markers, extracellular matrix remodeling, lipid metabolism, cell-death regulation, oxidative stress protection, mRNA processing, and cholesterol handling compared to VAT. In contrast, VAT showed elevated expression of genes linked to inflammation, complement activation, stress signaling, cell death, lipid biosynthesis, and mRNA processing. Compared with controls, SAT in obesity showed increased inflammatory and stress-response gene expression and upregulation of RNA processing regulators, but reduced de novo lipogenesis and cholesterol synthesis. Following MBS, SAT showed restored expression of lipogenic and adipogenic genes alongside downregulation of inflammatory, cholesterol biosynthesis, and splicing-factor genes. These findings demonstrate SAT and VAT remodeling in obesity and show that MBS partially reverses transcriptional changes in SAT, providing mechanistic insight into its metabolic benefits. They also highlight the need for targeted therapeutic strategies to more fully restore adipose tissue function and improve long-term metabolic outcomes. NCT00793143 and NCT01373892.

papers.title: Understanding pathophysiology of gallstone disease: a multi-omic analysis focused on adult women with obesity.
papers.abstract: Gallstone disease has a complex, multifactorial pathophysiology. Both the gut microbiome and the liver have been implicated as potential contributors. Because obesity is associated with alterations in gut microbial composition and is itself a risk factor for gallstone formation, we investigated the relative roles of the gut microbiome, the liver, and adipose tissue in gallstone disease in female patients with obesity. From the BARIA cohort, 108 consecutive female patients with obesity were included, of whom at baseline 39 had ultrasound proven gallstones (cases), whereas 69 did not have gallstones (controls). Fecal shotgun metagenomics, untargeted fasting plasma metabolomic analysis, and bulkRNAseq transcriptome analyses of liver, visceral (VAT), and subcutaneous (SAT) biopsies (taken during surgery) were analyzed. Especially VAT showed differences in expression of 57 genes, whereas liver gene expression revealed differences only after secondary analysis. In contrast to other publications, in liver "classic" ABC transporter gallstone genes were not identified in this cohort. Instead, the cholesterol transporter ABCG1 emerged, and expression was decreased in patients with gallstone disease. Plasma metabolomic profiling demonstrated increased levels of primary and secondary bile acids in the gallstone group. In contrast, gut microbiome differences between groups were limited. This integrated multi-omics analysis suggests that visceral adipose tissue may play a more prominent role in gallstone disease pathophysiology in women with obesity than previously appreciated. The observed selective molecular alterations and persistent bile acid differences highlight the complex metabolic interplay underlying gallstone formation and provide insight into tissue-specific mechanisms associated with obesity-related gallstone disease.

papers.title: Associations of body shape, visceral adiposity, and metabolic function indices with risk of major noncommunicable diseases: evidence from a nationwide population cohort.
papers.abstract: Comparative data evaluating the predictive performance of various obesity and metabolic indices for multiple noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) remain limited. We used the data sourced from the Health Evaluation and risk Reduction through nationwide Teamwork cohort (ChinaHEART), a national population-based study that enrolled 4,258,033 Chinese adults and followed them for more than 20 million person-years between November 2014 and December 2023. Fifteen obesity and metabolic indices were categorized into three groups: (1) body shape-related indices, including body mass index (BMI), body roundness index (BRI), waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), a body shape index (ABSI), weight-adjusted waist index (WWI), and conicity index (CI); (2) visceral fat-related indices, including lipid accumulation product (LAP) and Chinese visceral adiposity index (CVAI); and (3) metabolic function-related indices, including triglyceride-glucose index (TyG), TyG-BMI, TyG-BRI, TyG-WHtR, TyG-ABSI, TyG-WWI, and TyG-CI. The study outcomes comprised composite events of death or first hospitalization attributable to each of cardiovascular diseases (CVD), diabetes mellitus (DM), cancers, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) individually. Composite obesity and metabolic indices reflecting visceral adiposity accumulation and insulin resistance, respectively exhibited enhanced predictive accuracy for cardiovascular and diabetic risk, whereas their performance for cancer and COPD was comparatively limited. These findings support the paradigm that weight management strategies should be guided by risk assessments rather than relying solely on body weight or body shape. Furthermore, the development of diverse definitions for obesity measurement and management tailored to different population subgroups is warranted.

papers.title: Metabolic Reprogramming by Time-Restricted Feeding Confers Resistance to PM 2.5 -Induced Metabolic Disturbances in Adipose Tissue.
papers.abstract: Recent research indicates that exposure to fine particulate matter (PM 2.5 ) not only impairs the respiratory system but also disturbs adipose tissue homeostasis, contributing to rising obesity rates and systemic metabolic disturbances. Time-restricted feeding (TRF), a dietary approach that confines daily food consumption to specific time windows, has demonstrated significant potential in preventing and managing metabolic disorders. However, it remains unclear if TRF can alleviate PM 2.5 -induced adipose tissue dysfunction, and the mechanisms involved require investigation. We established a PM 2.5 -exposed male mouse model and randomly assigned the animals to four groups: filtered air (FA), PM 2.5 exposure, TRF+FA, and TRF+PM 2.5 . The PM 2.5 and TRF+PM 2.5 groups underwent whole-body PM 2.5 exposure in inhalation chambers, while the remaining groups were maintained under FA conditions. Mice in the TRF+FA and TRF+PM 2.5 groups were subjected to an 8-hour feeding window during the active phase (ZT16-ZT24). Our results indicated that PM 2.5 exposure induced systemic energy metabolism dysregulation and obesity, characterized by reduced heat production and metabolic rate, along with adipocyte hypertrophy, lipid droplet expansion, adipokine dysregulation, and inflammatory activation in both inguinal white adipose tissue (iWAT) and brown adipose tissue (BAT). Furthermore, PM 2.5 significantly suppressed thermogenesis, impaired oxidative phosphorylation, disrupted mitochondrial quality control networks, and downregulated the AMPK/SIRT1/PGC-1α signaling pathway. Notably, TRF intervention reactivated these signaling pathways, systematically reversed the multi-level pathological alterations, and restored mitochondrial homeostasis and energy metabolic balance. This study suggests for the first time that TRF counteracts adipose tissue dysfunction caused by PM 2.5 , offering a promising lifestyle intervention strategy against environment-related metabolic diseases.

papers.title: Exploring the role of histone deacetylases and histone deacetylase inhibitors in obesity and emerging evidence from Anorexia Nervosa.
papers.abstract: Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are key epigenetic regulators that modulate chromatin accessibility and transcriptional programs controlling metabolism, energy balance, and reward-related behaviors. Aberrant HDACs activity contributes to metabolic dysfunction by altering adipogenesis, thermogenic capacity, lipid profile, and hypothalamic circuits governing appetite. In obesity, specific HDAC isoforms promote adipocyte hypertrophy, impair browning of white adipose tissue, disrupt mitochondrial function, and exacerbate inflammation and insulin resistance. HDAC inhibitors (HDACi) counteract these effects by enhancing oxidative metabolism, stimulating thermogenesis, reducing adipocyte size, and improving systemic glucose and lipid homeostasis in preclinical models. Beyond peripheral metabolism, HDACi can also modulate neural pathways implicated in food intake, highlighting their potential influence in eating disorders, an area of research currently largely limited to anorexia nervosa. Research on HDACs, HDACi, and eating disorders is relatively recent; therefore, the characterization of potential molecular alterations and the identification of specific HDAC targets remain areas of ongoing development. Collectively, current evidence suggests that selective targeting of HDACs may offer a promising therapeutic strategy to correct epigenetic dysfunctions underlying both obesity and maladaptive feeding behaviors; however, translating these findings into clinical practice will require overcoming key challenges, including achieving isoform-specific selectivity, minimizing central nervous system-related side effects, and establishing efficacy and safety in human studies.

papers.title: Multiorgan metabolic reprogramming induced by chiglitazar in a letrozole-induced PMOS mouse model: Insights from integrated omics analyses.
papers.abstract: Polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS), formerly named polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), is a common endocrine-metabolic disorder with limited treatments. Chiglitazar, a novel pan-PPAR agonist, shows multitarget potential, but its systemic mechanisms in PMOS remain unclear. To compare chiglitazar with metformin and pioglitazone in a PMOS-like mouse model and elucidate its multiorgan mechanisms via integrated omics. A letrozole-induced PMOS-like mouse model was established. Mice were divided into five groups: normal control, PMOS model, and PMOS treated with metformin, pioglitazone, or chiglitazar. Phenotypic assessments included glucose tolerance, hormone levels, ovarian morphology, and estrous cycle. Multiomics analyses comprised DIA proteomics of liver, skeletal muscle, and visceral adipose tissue (VAT); ovarian transcriptomics; and 16S rRNA gut microbiota sequencing. Chiglitazar significantly improved insulin resistance (IR), reduced testosterone, restored estrous cyclicity, and ameliorated polycystic ovarian morphology. Proteomics revealed tissue-specific remodeling, with the VAT showing the most extensive proteomic remodeling. In the liver, chiglitazar downregulated mitochondrial OXPHOS proteins (Uqcrb, Ndufs4, Cox6a1) and upregulated insulin-degrading enzymes (Ide, Apeh). In adipose tissue, it inhibited OXPHOS pathways. In skeletal muscle, it modulated ubiquitin-mediated proteolysis. Ovarian transcriptomics indicated regulation of MAPK/GnRH signaling. Gut microbiota diversity was restored with enriched metabolic pathways. Chiglitazar induces metabolic reprogramming across multiple organs in PMOS-like mice, targeting IR, hyperandrogenism, ovarian dysfunction, and gut dysbiosis through distinct yet convergent pathways. These integrated mechanisms support its potential as a novel multitarget therapy for PMOS.

papers.title: VPS13C regulates triglyceride homeostasis and adipocyte differentiation.
papers.abstract: Hypertriglyceridemia is a major risk factor for cardiometabolic diseases. VPS13C is a genome-wide significant locus for triglyceride with an incomplete understanding of its functional role in triglyceride biology. In this study, we investigated the transcriptomic associations and functional roles of VPS13C in triglyceride metabolism. We analyzed VPS13C expression in subcutaneous adipose tissue and assessed fasting serum lipid levels (including total cholesterol and triglycerides) in participants from the Africa America Diabetes Mellitus (AADM) study. In parallel, we conducted functional studies in 3T3-L1 mouse adipocytes, where Vps13c was knocked down using siRNA. We then evaluated markers of adipogenesis, lipogenesis, and triglyceride metabolism. In human subjects, VPS13C expression in subcutaneous adipose tissue was inversely associated with fasting triglyceride levels but showed non-significant correlation with total cholesterol. In 3T3-L1 cells, Vps13c knockdown impaired adipocyte differentiation, evidenced by reduced lipid droplet formation and lower intracellular levels of triglycerides, glycerol, and fatty acids. This knockdown also led to significant downregulation of Pparg expression and suppression of PPARγ-mediated pathways, as well as genes involved in adipogenesis and lipogenesis. VPS13C is associated with circulating triglyceride levels and plays a critical role in adipocyte differentiation, adipogenesis and lipogenesis. These findings suggest that VPS13C may play an important role in triglyceride-related metabolic disorders.

papers.title: E3 Ubiquitin Ligase RNF126 Contributes to Pathogenesis of Obesity by Induction Mitophagy Mediated by PINK1/Parkin Pathway.
papers.abstract: Obesity and its associated metabolic disorders have become major global public health challenges. Increasing evidence indicates that mitophagy plays a pivotal role in the pathogenesis of obesity and related metabolic diseases. This study aimed to investigate the role and underlying mechanisms of E3 ubiquitin ligase RNF126 in obesity and non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Using Rnf126 + / - mice fed a high-fat diet (HFD), we found RNF126 deficiency markedly exacerbated body weight gain, elevated serum ALT and AST levels, inflammatory responses, apoptosis, and insulin resistance. Histological analysis with H&E and Oil Red O staining revealed that RNF126 deficiency aggravated hepatic inflammatory cell infiltration, lipid droplet accumulation, and adipocyte hypertrophy in HFD-fed mice. HFD feeding significantly inhibited RNF126 expression in liver and muscle. Moreover, Rnf126 + / - mice exhibited reduced oxygen consumption, carbon dioxide production and heat generation without changes in food intake. Mechanistically, qPCR and Western blot analyses demonstrated that RNF126 deficiency suppressed the mRNA and protein expression of UCP-1, SIRT1, and PGC-1α in the liver and white adipose tissue, indicating impaired mitochondrial biogenesis. Moreover, the protein levels of cleaved PINK1, Parkin, and LC3 were reduced, while p62 expression was increased in the liver of Rnf126 + / - mice, indicating inhibited autophagic activity. Consistently, oxidative stress was significantly elevated, as evidenced by increased MDA levels and decreased SOD and GSH contents. Rnf126 + / - mice livers displayed obvious mitochondrial swelling and partial cristae disorganization with an increase of mtDNA expression. Mitochondrial complex-III enzymatic activity, hepatic ATP, TOM20 protein expression and complex-III subunit UQCRFS1 expression were substantially decreased in HFD-fed Rnf126 + / - mice. At the cellular level, RNF126 overexpression in palmitic acid-treated HepG2 cells restored cleaved PINK1, Parkin, and LC3 protein levels, while reducing p62 expression, indicating that RNF126 promotes mitophagy. Furthermore, ROS fluorescence assays showed that RNF126 overexpression attenuated intracellular ROS accumulation. Rescue experiments demonstrated that the protective effects of RNF126 on mitochondrial membrane potential, lipid accumulation, and mitophagy marker expression are dependent on its ubiquitin ligase activity. Overall, RNF126 alleviates HFD-induced lipid accumulation and hepatic injury by promoting mitophagy and maintaining redox homeostasis, suggesting its potential as a novel therapeutic target for NAFLD.

papers.title: Early-Life Betaine Supplementation Drives Sex-Specific Metabolic Programming in Rats, Affecting FGF21 Signaling and Energy Balance.
papers.abstract: We aimed to evaluate the effects of maternal diet and betaine supplementation during the suckling period on Fgf21 expression and metabolic pathways related to FGF21 signaling and metabolic programming. Offspring of Wistar rats fed either a chow diet (CD) or a Western diet (WD) were studied at postnatal day 22 and at 7 months. During suckling, pups received betaine at a physiological dose corresponding to twice the average intake estimated from milk consumption, or a vehicle. After weaning onto a CD, all animals were switched to a WD from months four to seven. Biometric parameters, circulating markers, and gene expression in hypothalamus, retroperitoneal white adipose tissue (rWAT), and liver were analyzed, together with cecal Akkermansia muciniphila abundance. At day 22, a maternal WD reduced hepatic Fgf21 expression in both sexes; however, only males showed decreased Klb expression in rWAT, consistent with impaired FGF21 signaling. A maternal WD also reduced A. muciniphila abundance. Betaine increased Fgfr1 expression in rWAT of female offspring from control dams. By seven months, betaine supplementation in males born to WD dams increased adiposity, and insulin and leptin levels, whereas females exhibited an improved plasma lipid profile (lower NEFA and TG). Hypothalamic Drd2 and Fgfr1 expression further showed sex-specific modulation by the maternal diet and betaine. In conclusion, betaine supplementation during suckling exerts sex-specific long-term effects on metabolic programming. Females showed an improved lipid profile, whereas males, particularly those exposed to a maternal WD, developed increased adiposity and altered endocrine profiles. The findings suggest that early-life betaine supplementation can modulate long-term metabolic outcomes through sex-specific effects on FGF21-related pathways.

papers.title: Protocol for the isolation, enrichment, and culture of murine adipose progenitor cells.
papers.abstract: We present a protocol for isolating and culturing murine adipose progenitor cells (APCs) from adipose tissue. We describe steps for tissue dissection, unit-normalized enzymatic digestion, stromal vascular fraction (SVF) isolation, APC enrichment, and cell culture. We then detail quality control procedures that maximize cell yield, viability, and purity. This protocol combines enzymatic SVF isolation with magnetic-activated cell sorting enrichment to obtain a highly enriched APC population. It emphasizes reproducibility through unit-normalized digestion, controlled processing conditions, and standardized quality control metrics.

papers.title: Sirt3 deficiency impairs AMPK-Acc1 antilipogenic signaling in female adipocytes.
papers.abstract: Background: Biological sex influences adipose tissue function, while impaired adipogenesis contributes to adipose dysfunction. Sirtuin 3 (Sirt3), a mitochondrial NAD+-dependent deacetylase involved in oxidative metabolism and stress adaptation, remains insufficiently defined in adipogenic differentiation. We investigated how Sirt3 and sex shape adipogenic phenotype in mouse embryonic fibroblast (MEF)-derived adipocytes. Male and female Sirt3 wild-type (WT) and knockout (KO) mouse MEFs were differentiated into adipocyte-like cells and analyzed by Oil Red O staining, confocal microscopy, lipid droplet morphometry, adipogenic gene expression, fatty acid profiling, LC-MS metabolomics, immunoblotting, and transmission electron microscopy (n = 3-5 biological replicates per group). All groups induced adipogenic marker expression and formed lipid rich adipocyte-like cells, with female KO adipocytes showing the strongest lipid storage phenotype. In females, bortezomib (BTZ) increased AMPK and Acc1 phosphorylation in WT adipocytes, whereas KO cells showed reduced basal pAMPK/AMPK and failed to mount a comparable AMPK-Acc1 response. AICAR failed to restore AMPK-Acc1 signaling in KO adipocytes. Sirt3 deficiency increased Scd1 abundance and the C16:1/C16:0 desaturation index. BTZ reduced Scd1 in KO cells without normalizing the elevated desaturation ratio. Metabolomics indicated predominantly BTZ-associated glycerophospholipid and lysophospholipid remodeling. Qualitative ultrastructural analysis revealed BTZ-associated organelle stress, most evident in KO adipocytes. Sirt3 deficiency promotes a female biased lipid storage phenotype linked to impaired AMPK-Acc1 antilipogenic signaling, reduced lipid turnover, and persistent Scd1-associated fatty acid desaturation, supporting a model in which female adipocytes rely on Sirt3-dependent metabolic control during adipogenesis.

papers.title: Adrenal hormones in the maintenance of glucose homeostasis during prolonged fasting in male glucagon-deficient mice.
papers.abstract: Glucagon is a key regulator of fasting glucose homeostasis, but the contribution of adrenal hormones during prolonged fasting remains unclear. We investigated the complementary roles of glucagon and adrenal hormones in hepatic glucose metabolism during prolonged fasting. Male proglucagon-deficient (GCGKO) mice and adrenalectomized (ADX) mice were studied after a 36-h fast. Metabolic parameters, hepatic glycogen and lipid contents, gene expression, and liver metabolomic profiles were analyzed. GCGKO mice exhibited markedly elevated plasma corticosterone levels and only mildly reduced blood glucose levels despite preserved hepatic glycogen stores after a 36-h fast. Hepatic triglyceride and free fatty acid contents were significantly lower in GCGKO mice. Fasting increased the expression of genes involved in amino acid metabolism and the urea cycle in both control and GCGKO mice, but the magnitude of the response was attenuated in GCGKO mice. Hepatic amino acid levels were broadly reduced in control mice but largely preserved in GCGKO mice. In contrast, adrenalectomy in GCGKO mice resulted in severe hypoglycemia accompanied by reduced adipose tissue lipolysis and impaired hormone-sensitive lipase phosphorylation. Adrenalectomy had minimal effects on blood glucose and hepatic metabolic responses in control mice. Glucagon-dependent glycogen utilization, adrenal hormone-dependent adipose lipolysis, and cooperative regulation of hepatic amino acid metabolism by glucagon and adrenal hormones contribute to the maintenance of blood glucose during prolonged fasting. Adrenal hormones provide an important compensatory mechanism that preserves glucose homeostasis when glucagon signaling is impaired.

papers.title: Adipose Mesenchymal Stem Cells Secreted Exosomal miR-26a-5p Ameliorate Renal Fibrosis via Inhibiting Glycolysis and Ferroptosis in Renal Interstitial Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: Renal fibrosis, a defining feature of chronic kidney disease, involves a metabolic shift toward aerobic glycolysis and is frequently accompanied by ferroptosis, a form of iron-dependent cell death. This study investigated the therapeutic potential of adipose mesenchymal stem cell-derived exosomes (AMSC-exo) in renal fibrosis. Using a unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) mouse model and hypoxia-treated HK-2 cells, we assessed fibrosis, glycolysis, mitochondrial morphology, and ferroptosis. miRNA sequencing, dual-luciferase reporter assays, and transcriptome sequencing were performed to identify key exosomal miRNAs and downstream pathways. AMSC-exo significantly attenuated UUO-induced fibrosis and suppressed glycolysis and ferroptosis in tubular epithelial cells. miR-26a-5p was highly enriched in AMSC-exo and downregulated 6-phosphofructo-2-kinase/fructose-2,6-bisphosphatase 3 (Pfkfb3), a key regulator of glycolysis and ferroptosis. Knockdown of miR-26a-5p markedly weakened the renoprotective effects of AMSC-exo, whereas Pfkfb3 inhibition reversed the effects induced by miR-26a-5p deficiency. These findings indicate that AMSC-exo alleviate renal fibrosis by delivering miR-26a-5p to suppress Pfkfb3, thereby inhibiting glycolytic reprogramming and ferroptosis, and suggest the miR-26a-5p/Pfkfb3 axis as a potential therapeutic target for renal fibrosis.

papers.title: Dietary anthocyanins as multifunctional bioactives targeting obesity across experimental and clinical models.
papers.abstract: Obesity has emerged as a critical global health issue, contributing to cardiometabolic and other chronic diseases. Current management strategies, including diet, lifestyle modification, and pharmacotherapy, often lack sustainable efficacy and carry side effects. The search for safe, natural interventions has drawn attention to plant-based bioactives, particularly anthocyanins, which are abundant in dark-pigmented fruits and exhibit antioxidant and anti-obesogenic effects. This review critically evaluates the anti-obesogenic potential of anthocyanins, drawing on in vitro , preclinical, and clinical studies. Preclinical evidence demonstrates that anthocyanins improve lipid and glycemic profiles and insulin sensitivity, while reducing body weight, adiposity, hepatic steatosis, and systemic inflammation. Clinical trials generally support beneficial effects of anthocyanin-rich foods and supplements on selected cardiometabolic parameters ( e.g. , lipids, glycemic control, and inflammation) in individuals with overweight or obesity, while effects on body weight and adiposity are modest or inconsistent. Mechanistically, anthocyanins inhibit pancreatic lipase, adipogenesis, and lipogenesis; promote fatty acid β-oxidation through AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) driven peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPARα) signaling; enhance thermogenesis via upregulation of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1) and PR domain-containing 16 (PRDM16); and stimulate mitochondrial biogenesis in adipose tissue. In addition, anthocyanins attenuate oxidative stress and chronic inflammation by reducing reactive oxygen species, pro-inflammatory cytokines such as interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α), and by modulating nuclear factor kappa-light-chain-enhancer of activated B cell (NF-κB) and mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) pathways. Furthermore, anthocyanins beneficially modulate the gut microbiota, enriching species such as Akkermansia muciniphila , increasing short-chain fatty acid production, and improving intestinal barrier integrity. Overall, anthocyanins represent a compelling, multi-targeted natural intervention for obesity and its metabolic complications. These natural strategies may complement established pharmacotherapies and, when embedded in plant-forward dietary patterns and sustainable food systems, contribute to a more holistic approach to planetary health.

papers.title: 12,13-diHOME Is Increased During Targeted Temperature Management And Correlates With Survival After Cardiac Arrest Resuscitation.
papers.abstract: Trials of targeted temperature management (TTM) after cardiac arrest (CA) have had conflicting results. Brown adipose tissue (BAT) is a thermogenic organ activated by cold temperature to regulate body temperature, systemic metabolism and the immune system. Approximately 10-30% of adult patients have BAT and this heterogeneity may explain variable treatment to TTM. This study sought to measure differences in outcome, metabolic and immune activation between patients treated with TTM following CA with varying BAT activity, measured through BAT-associated lipid 12,13-diHOME concentrations in circulation. BAT biomarker 12,13-diHOME was quantified using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) on plasma from 74 patients at various time points starting at 6 hours and up until 7 days after return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC). Additionally, circulating glucose, C-peptide and fatty acids were measured by glucometer, ELISA and LC-MS, respectively. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells were analyzed by flow cytometry. 12,13-diHOME was increased in patients treated with TTM at 33°C and positively correlated with favorable outcomes. 12,13-diHOME levels peaked in the first 12 to 48 hours and decreased below the first post-ROSC level by 7 days. Glucose homeostasis was not associated with 12,13-diHOME levels. In a subset of patients, we could detect a specific phospholipid signature in patients with higher 12,13-diHOME. Patients with higher 12,13-diHOME also had increased mature neutrophils and lower immature neutrophils. Circulating 12,13-diHOME levels are increased in some patients undergoing targeted temperature management after cardiac arrest, which may be indicative of increased BAT activity. 12,13-diHOME is associated with survival, alterations of phospholipid metabolism, and a profile of less activated immune system. BAT may mediate the effects of temperature management on outcome after cardiac arrest.

papers.title: The Gut Microbiota as a Mediator of the Metabolic Benefits of Fungi and Their Polysaccharides: A Review of Evidence Addressing Causality.
papers.abstract: Prebiotic supplementation has emerged as a promising strategy to ameliorate metabolic disorders through beneficial reshaping of the gut microbiota. Accumulating evidence suggests that fungi and their polysaccharides (e.g., those from Auricularia auricula-judae , Boletus edulis , Hirsutella sinensis , Isaria cicadae , Ramaria botrytoides , and Wolfiporia cocos ) possess considerable potential in this context. The present review summarizes studies providing data relevant to the potential involvement of the gut microbiota in mediating the metabolic benefits of fungal interventions. Observed outcomes, potentially linked to the gut microbiota, included reductions in body, visceral fat, and liver weights, improved lipid and glycemic profiles, enhanced insulin sensitivity, and decreased circulating lipopolysaccharide, leptin, and proinflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6). Upregulation of tight junction proteins in the colon implied strengthened gut barrier function. Histological analyses revealed smaller adipocytes and attenuation of hepatic steatosis. Additional effects included stimulation of white adipose tissue browning and enhanced hepatic thermogenesis. Alterations in gut microbiota composition were diverse; however, a reduction in the Firmicutes/Bacteroidetes ratio was commonly reported. Furthermore, oral administration of bacterial species enriched by fungal interventions, such as Papillibacter cinnamivorans , Parabacteroides goldsteinii , Bacteroides intestinalis , Lactobacillus johnsonii , and Enterococcus casseliflavus , reproduced the metabolic improvements, supporting their possible mediating role. Collectively, current evidence indicates that fungi and their polysaccharides may exert metabolic benefits, at least in part, through gut microbiota modulation; however, further investigation is needed to determine the extent to which the gut microbiota contributes causally to these benefits.

papers.title: Nutrition, Circadian Regulation, and the Gut-Melatonin-Visceral Adipose Tissue Axis: An Integrative Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Visceral adipose tissue (VAT) dysfunction is a major determinant of obesity-related metabolic disorders, including insulin resistance, metabolic syndrome, cardiovascular disease, and chronic low-grade inflammation. Growing evidence indicates that VAT function is regulated by a complex interplay between nutrition, circadian rhythms, intestinal melatonin secretion, and the gut microbiota rather than by isolated metabolic pathways. The gastrointestinal tract represents an important interface between dietary exposures, microbial activity, immune signaling, and host metabolic regulation. Melatonin is a potential component of this network because it participates in circadian regulation and has been detected in gastrointestinal tissues, while experimental studies suggest that intestinal melatonin signaling may interact with gut microbial and metabolic processes. However, the cellular sources, quantitative contribution, local dynamics, and physiological significance of intestinal melatonin remain incompletely established, particularly in humans. This narrative review integrates current evidence regarding the interactions between nutrition, circadian regulation, intestinal melatonin, gut microbiota, and visceral adipose tissue. Rather than proposing a validated causal pathway, we introduce the Gut-Melatonin-Visceral Adipose Tissue (Gut-Melatonin-VAT) Axis as an integrative, hypothesis-generating conceptual framework that organizes established interactions together with candidate mechanisms requiring further experimental validation. Particular attention is given to the bidirectional relationships among dietary composition, meal timing, microbial rhythmicity, intestinal signaling, immune regulation, and VAT dysfunction. The framework may provide a basis for generating testable hypotheses concerning nutritional, chrononutritional, microbiota-targeted, and melatonin-related interventions, while recognizing that direct human evidence validating the complete pathway is currently lacking.

papers.title: Do Nutritional Status and Dietary Intake Influence the Ghrelin Response?
papers.abstract: Ghrelin is a key orexigenic hormone involved in the regulation of appetite and energy homeostasis, and its fasting circulating concentrations may reflect long-term energy balance and nutritional status. The aim of the study was to assess the associations between habitual daily energy and macronutrient intake from a conventional diet and the fasting total ghrelin concentrations in individuals with different nutritional status and to evaluate the postprandial ghrelin response following consumption of a standardized meal. An additional aim was to identify body composition parameters predictive of ghrelin concentrations. The prospective study included 76 individuals aged 40-60 years, classified into four body mass index (BMI) groups. Body composition was assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DXA). Energy and macronutrient intake was evaluated based on standardized 3-day food records. Ghrelin concentrations were measured in the fasting state and at 60, 120, 180, and 240 min after consumption of a standardized mix liquid meal (Nutridrink Protein, 459 kcal). Fasting total ghrelin concentrations were not associated with recent energy or macronutrient intake. In women, changes from the baseline differed across BMI groups at 60 and 120 min, whereas no between-group differences were observed in men. In the regression analyses, BMI and gynoid region fat showed significant coefficients in women, although the overall model was not significant, while gynoid region fat was significantly associated with fasting ghrelin in men. Fasting total ghrelin appears to reflect longer-term metabolic phenotype and adipose tissue distribution rather than short-term variation in habitual energy or macronutrient intake. The BMI-dependent differences in the early postprandial response observed in women further suggest that nutritional status may modify dynamic ghrelin regulation in a sex-specific manner. These findings indicate that ghrelin should not be interpreted solely as an acute marker of dietary intake, but rather within the broader context of body composition, fat distribution, and sex-related metabolic regulation.

papers.title: Dietary Fructooligosaccharide Is Associated with Improved Insulin Resistance, Reduced Romboutsia ilealis Abundance, and Modulation of GLP-1 Production in High-Fat Diet-Induced Obese Mice.
papers.abstract: Obesity disrupts glucose homeostasis and insulin signaling, partly through altered gut hormone secretion and intestinal inflammation. Our previous work demonstrated that fructooligosaccharides (FOS), a prebiotic fiber, suppressed colonic inflammation, and modulated gut microbiota when administered with vitamin D supplementation. However, the effects of FOS on metabolic alterations, glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) production under obesogenic stimulation remains unclear. Here, we examined the effects of FOS on insulin resistance and GLP-1 production in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mice. Six-week-old male and female C57BL/6J mice were assigned to control or HFDs ± 5% FOS for 10 weeks. Body weight, visceral fat, fasting glucose, insulin, triglycerides, and insulin resistance index (HOMA-IR) were assessed. Serum GLP-1 was quantified by ELISA. Colonic expressions of Glp1r , Pi3k , and Akt were evaluated by qRT-PCR and western blotting, respectively. Cecal abundance of Akkermansia muciniphila (AM), Dubosiella newyorkensis (DN), and Romboutsia ilealis (RI) was quantified by qPCR. FOS attenuated HFD-induced metabolic dysfunction, lowering serum insulin and HOMA-IR in both sexes. Notably, FOS elicited sex-dependent physical improvements of which it suppressed body weight gain by 10% in male mice and reduced visceral fat accumulation by 36% in female mice. The phenotypic changes in male mice were associated with an increase in GLP-1. Further, FOS modulated colonic PI3K/Akt signaling in a sex-dependent manner and downregulated HFD-associated increases in Glp1r mRNA expression. Consistent with our previous work, FOS suppressed RI abundance, and this reduction was associated with lower colonic Tlr4 mRNA expression and improved insulin-resistance index. FOS improves insulin sensitivity in HFD-induced obesity and specifically enhanced GLP-1 production in male mice. Though the mechanism remained elucidated, the observed phenotype changes may be attributed to a combination of altered colonic PI3K/Akt pathways and targeted bacterial shifts. These effects appear to be sex-dependent and support FOS as a promising dietary strategy for maintenance of metabolic health.

papers.title: Small-Nerve Fibre Pathology in Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease Is Associated with Liver Fat/Inflammation and Improves with Weight Loss.
papers.abstract: Background: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is associated with multiple extrahepatic complications, but its relationship with peripheral neuropathy, even without co-existing type 2 diabetes (T2D), remains poorly understood. Furthermore, to what extent addressing liver and metabolic health would be associated with improvements in small nerve fibre morphology (that mediate neuropathy) is unknown. We investigated the relationship between liver health and small nerve fibre morphology in adults with MASLD before and after diet-induced weight loss and improvements in liver health. Methods: Adults with MASLD (n = 12) and controls without MASLD or T2D (n = 16) underwent anthropometry, biochemistry, transient elastography (TE) and corneal confocal microscopy (CCM). Participants with MASLD then completed a 12-week low-calorie diet (LCD; Counterweight-Plus, ~850 kcal/day) with repeat assessments including multi-organ magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). TE quantified hepatic steatosis (controlled attenuation parameter, CAP), while MRI measured hepatic and pancreatic fat (proton density fat fraction, PDFF) and fibroinflammation (iron-corrected T1, cT1). Neuropathy was assessed using validated questionnaires and CCM-derived corneal nerve fibre density (CNFD), branch density (CNBD) and fibre length (CNFL). The primary outcome measure was change in liver PDFF. Associations between hepatic and neuropathy measures were assessed using correlation and multivariable linear regression. Results: Compared with controls, MASLD participants had higher liver fat and metabolic dysfunction, with reduced CNFD (25.7 vs. 28.4 fibres/mm 2 , p = 0.03) and CNFL (14.1 vs. 17.1 mm/mm 2 , p = 0.02). In multivariable regression, TE-derived CAP was independently associated with CNFD (β -0.03 (95% CI -0.06, -0.01), p < 0.05), while total cholesterol was associated with CNFL (β -1.54 (95% CI -2.81, -0.27), p < 0.02). After LCD, participants lost 12.5 kg with reductions in metabolic syndrome components ( p = 0.04) and liver fat (ΔPDFF -5.0%, p = 0.03). Neuropathic symptoms improved and CNFD increased (+1.87 fibres/mm 2 , p = 0.05). Reduction in liver fat correlated with increased CNFL (r = -0.63, p = 0.03), while change in hepatic fibroinflammation (ΔcT1) correlated with neuropathy disability (r = 0.62, p = 0.04) and small-fibre symptom scores (r = 0.47, p = 0.05). Conclusions: These exploratory findings suggest that MASLD, even without T2D, may be associated with small nerve fibre abnormalities and neuropathic symptoms. Diet-induced weight loss improved liver, metabolic and neural health in parallel. Larger prospective confirmatory studies are required to more precisely establish this relationship both at baseline and with interventions.

papers.title: Ultra-Processed Foods in Early Life: Biological Mechanisms, Developmental Programming and Childhood Obesity-A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Childhood obesity now affects more than 160 million children and adolescents worldwide, and over the same period ultra-processed foods have come to dominate the early-life diet. This review sets out a single argument: that the effect of ultra-processed foods on childhood obesity is better read developmentally, and that the digestive tract is the organ through which much of that effect is transmitted. Exposure begins before birth and continues through the first 1000 days and complementary feeding, the period in which the gut microbiota assembles and the intestinal barrier matures. We show how ultra-processed foods perturb these two systems in particular: a low-fibre, additive-rich, energy-dense diet reshapes microbial community structure and depletes short-chain fatty acid production, while emulsifiers and other additives thin the mucus layer and raise intestinal permeability, admitting microbial products that sustain low-grade inflammation. We trace how these gut-level changes feed forward into altered appetite regulation, adipocyte biology and, ultimately, excess adiposity, and we situate the other proposed mechanisms (matrix disruption, hyperpalatability, accelerated eating rate, endocrine-disrupting additives and central reward signalling) around this digestive core, marking at each step where the evidence is paediatric and where it rests on adult or animal data. The epidemiological literature is appraised by study design, and the constraints on causal inference are stated plainly: NOVA misclassification, residual confounding, reverse causation, dietary misreporting and the scarcity of paediatric trials. The practical implication is that prevention framed around early-life gut health, rather than around cumulative adult-style exposure, is where intervention is most plausibly effective. We are explicit throughout that most of the mechanistic evidence derives from animal or adult studies and that a causal role for ultra-processed foods in childhood adiposity, though biologically plausible, is not yet established in paediatric populations; the developmental reading we advance is the most coherent interpretation of an associational evidence base, not a demonstrated causal chain.
keywords: Developmental Origins of Health and Disease

papers.title: Molecular Biomarkers Linking Psoriasis and Cardiovascular Disease: Current Evidence and Clinical Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic, immune-mediated inflammatory disease affecting the skin, nails, and joints. Its complex pathogenesis results from interactions between genetic susceptibility and environmental factors and is accompanied by an increased risk of multiple systemic comorbidities, particularly cardiovascular disease. Growing evidence indicates that both conditions share common molecular pathways driven by chronic inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, metabolic disturbances, and immune dysregulation. Among the emerging molecular biomarkers, chemerin, endocan, and growth differentiation factor-15 (GDF-15) have attracted considerable attention due to their role in vascular homeostasis, adipose tissue biology, glucose metabolism, and inflammatory signaling. This review summarizes current evidence on the involvement of these biomarkers in psoriasis and cardiovascular disease, highlighting their contribution to the molecular mechanisms underlying the psoriasis-cardiovascular disease axis. Furthermore, we discussed their potential usefulness as candidate biomarkers for cardiovascular risk. However, prospective validation is strictly required to confirm their clinical utility and establish their incremental predictive value beyond conventional risk factors.
